context.text:
SHIPPED AND HARDWARE-VERIFIED. 24 kHz superwideband runs end to end today; treat it as a constraint you build on, not an open question.

Downlink: the model's own 24 kHz PCM goes straight to Opus with NO resampling anywhere. 12 kHz of delivered bandwidth. 9 kHz sibilance arrives at -22.6 dB where it was previously folded onto 7 kHz.

Framing, not sample rate, was the thing that failed before. The earlier 24 kHz attempt used 20 ms frames = 50 packets/s against a chip that can start about 48.8 decodes/s. At 60 ms frames it is 16.7/s and fits. A second cause was that libopus had been compiling -Os the whole time: target_compile_options put -O3 before Zephyr's flags so the command line read "-O3 -Os" and the last -O won. Applied as a source property it wins; text 255K -> 316K, encode 20.4 -> 16.4 ms.

Costs are MEASURED on-device with a 32.768 kHz counter around each call, not estimated: decode 8.8 ms/packet at 16 kHz, 25.2 ms at 24 kHz, encode 15.0 ms/call. That is about 87% of one 64 MHz core, which is why the uplink encoder runs at complexity 0 — uplink audio only has to be understood by speech-to-text, while the decoded downlink is what the owner actually hears. mic_drops went 29 -> 7 of 931.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, all of them numbers you can re-measure rather than judgements:
- Alias rejection on any resampling stage >= 60 dB. The 16 kHz path's 2-tap average gave 3.2 dB; the polyphase windowed-sinc FIR that replaced it gives 67.5 dB. Measure with scripts/audio-quality-probe.mjs.
- Codec cost under 100% of one 64 MHz core, with the measurement taken on-device.
- mic_drops under about 1% of blocks.
- tx_starved at or near zero. Last hardware run: "agent 24 kHz down", 284 packets decoded, tx_starved 3.
- No audible content before the agent speaks. The sync preamble used to be played as audio — 4 bursts of 16 samples at 0x6C6C (~85% of full scale) 20 ms apart, i.e. loud clicks at the start of every conversation. Post-fix the same press-moment capture is peak 0, 0 nonzero samples of 22050.

Do not propose work premised on 24 kHz being unavailable, on the SoC being too slow for it, or on needing a resampler in the downlink path. If you want to change the audio path, the bar is a measurement from scripts/audio-quality-probe.mjs or an on-device counter, not an argument.

America/New_York. That is this Mac's system zone, read from /etc/localtime, currently EDT (UTC-4).

Scope this correctly, because it is the part that has been getting confused: it is authoritative for anything RESOLVED ON THIS MAC — routine firing times, quiet hours, "this morning", file timestamps, calendar reads. It is not a claim about where the owner is standing. The pendant has never been given a zone: NITZ was never captured, no GNSS receiver is started (CONFIG_LOCATION and CONFIG_GNSS are unset and nrf_modem_gnss appears zero times in the firmware), and the device clock arrives as zoneless digits. Code that parses those digits must return a null instant rather than borrowing this zone — catchupSources.js and voiceNotes.js both already refuse it, and that refusal is correct.

If you need the owner's own timezone as distinct from the machine's, that is still an open question for the owner and you should say so rather than substituting this value for it.

context.topic: current pendant hardware revision and button count
context.text:
AUTHORITATIVE, from the owner's purchase invoices rather than from the firmware.

WHAT PHYSICALLY EXISTS TODAY (bought, on the bench):
- nRF9160-DK development kit
- Adafruit HUZZAH32 ESP32 Feather — the AirPods bridge, PROTOTYPE ONLY
- microSD breakout (Adafruit #254) + 64 GB card
- Adafruit DRV2605L Haptic Motor Controller (STEMMA QT/Qwiic, I2C 0x5A)
- Vibrating Mini Motor Disc — the actuator the DRV2605L drives
- Adafruit LSM6DSOX 6-DoF accelerometer + gyroscope (I2C)
- Adafruit MAX98357A I2S 3W Class D amplifier
- Adafruit PDM MEMS microphone breakout
- Lithium-ion polymer battery, 3.7 V 500 mAh

BUTTONS: the DK exposes sw0 and sw1 and the firmware uses BOTH — sw0 starts/ends recording (main.c:27), sw1 is the moment bookmark (main.c:39). Earlier guidance in this record said "exactly one user button" and that was wrong; it described an intended product, not the bench. Design for two today.

THE CORRECTION THAT MATTERS MOST: haptics and an IMU were previously reported here as hardware that does not exist, and a batch of device-skill requests was denied on that basis. That was wrong. Both are owned. They are not WIRED — the devicetree has `&i2c2 { status = "disabled" }` and haptic_test.c is not in CMakeLists.txt — so the gap is firmware integration, not procurement. A proposal that needs haptic feedback or motion sensing is buildable; say that it needs i2c2 enabled rather than that it needs new hardware.

WHAT IS GENUINELY ABSENT: no secure element, no fuel gauge, no RGB or multi-colour LED (one LED, led0), no display, no rotary input yet, no GNSS started (CONFIG_LOCATION and CONFIG_GNSS unset; nrf_modem_gnss appears zero times).

OWNER'S STATED DIRECTION FOR THE PRODUCT: a scroll wheel or rotary encoder, plus another button; and the enclosure should look like real jewellery — a gold pendant, not a gadget. Weigh proposals against that. A visible multi-colour status LED is a poor fit; haptic patterns are an excellent one, and the parts are already here. A rotary encoder is the answer to the crowding problem this committee kept hitting: roughly twenty distinct meanings were proposed for "long press" because there is a way to trigger and no way to SELECT among options. A wheel adds that axis.

USB IS NOT A PRODUCT TRANSPORT. Flashing and bench testing only.

tools.name: verify_operation_step
tools.why: The proposed commit protocol cannot honestly close an operation from executor receipts alone. faculty-action needs a read-only verifier call to faculty-perception that independently checks a specific step's postconditions against fresh Mac/browser state and returns provenance, without opening a microphone or performing mutations.

tools.name: audio_path_probe
tools.why: I need to execute the owner’s explicit 24 kHz end-to-end audio goal rather than merely propose it. Existing Mac/browser action tools cannot measure I2S sample clocks, Opus frame metadata, LTE jitter, or round-trip playback, and success cannot be claimed from configuration labels.

deviceSkills.name: tactile_action_outcome_beacon
deviceSkills.what_it_does: When the relay sends a signed operation outcome, the pendant renders a short haptic pattern for verified success, safe-to-retry, unknown, or cancelled. A press acknowledges the pattern; it never approves or executes an action. If several outcomes arrive offline, it queues only compact event IDs and presents them oldest-first.

proposals.user_asks: If I give you an instruction from the pendant while my Mac or browser is temporarily unavailable, remember it safely, tell me exactly what is waiting, and carry it out automatically when the required device comes back—without repeating an action or acting on stale information.
proposals.why_useful: Today an owner can issue an intent while walking away, but a disconnected browser or unready Mac turns it into an opaque failure. This makes the pendant a reliable front door: capture once, show pending state, resume only against a fresh readiness snapshot, and provide a completion receipt. It is not merely background Mac work because the pendant is the only always-with-owner capture and confirmation surface, while the relay survives device absence and authenticated browser state supplies the action reach.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for the short pendant capture/acknowledgment; use a cheaper background model for intent normalization, readiness checks, and resume planning. Use the action model only when execution begins or an ambiguity is found.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate local acknowledgment under 300 ms; relay persistence under 2 s when connected. Resume on next qualifying heartbeat, with a visible/prompted delay if the action is consequential. Completion or blocked receipt within 10 s of the device becoming ready.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.02 per queued instruction depending on background extraction and any browser reasoning; storage/heartbeat traffic dominates at scale, not realtime inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Commands and authenticated-page results must be encrypted in transit and at rest, with short retention and device-bound ownership. Never replay an irreversible step: require an idempotency key, a precondition hash/readiness snapshot, expiry, and renewed approval for changed or consequential targets. Pendant should store only a bounded encrypted audio/text envelope and purge after relay acknowledgment or expiry.
missing: A pendant offline-intent buffer and sync protocol with local receipt/expiry
Relay durable intent escrow with idempotency, TTL, encrypted payloads, and wake-on-readiness scheduling
Typed readiness/precondition snapshots that distinguish Mac GUI readiness from browser-extension/session readiness
Resume cursor and exactly-once/reconciliation semantics across Mac and authenticated browser
Pendant status/confirmation UX for queued, blocked, resumed, and completed states
End-to-end conformance tests for disconnect, retry, stale page, duplicate delivery, and power loss

proposals.user_asks: When a task you are carrying out breaks because a website, app layout, or login state changed, diagnose the break across the browser, Mac, and relay, repair the plan, and continue from the last verified step—telling me what changed instead of making me start over.
proposals.why_useful: Today a long-running action can fail after spending time navigating, leaving the owner with an opaque error and lost progress. Automatic recovery would turn brittle computer use into a service that can adapt to ordinary UI drift while preserving a precise boundary around what was and was not done. This is different from merely queuing, watching, or undoing work: it repairs an execution strategy after reality diverges.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to classify failures and compare prior/current page or UI structure. Use mac-vision/browser reasoning only for localized repair. Realtime is limited to the pendant explanation or a short approval request when the repaired target is consequential.
proposals.latency_budget: Detect and classify within 5 seconds of a failed step; attempt one bounded repair within 30 seconds. Pause and report rather than loop after two failed repairs or any changed consequential target.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.10 per recovered task, dominated by screenshots/DOM extraction and localized computer-use inference; normal successful tasks incur no extra model call beyond lightweight failure classification.
proposals.security_concerns: A visually similar control could be the wrong control, and a changed login or recipient could cause an unintended action. Keep the last verified state, compare target identity and semantic labels, require renewed approval for irreversible or materially changed actions, retain before/after evidence, and never silently broaden the task. Screenshots and authenticated DOM data need encrypted, short-lived storage with redacted logs.
missing: A cross-surface failure envelope carrying step ID, intent, preconditions, DOM/UI evidence, and side-effect status
A repair planner that can propose an alternate locator or interaction while preserving the original goal and scope
Mac-vision and browser-extension support for bounded alternative inspection without committing changes
A verified-step ledger and reconciliation protocol for unknown side effects
Policy classification for when repaired execution may continue automatically versus requiring pendant approval
Fault-injection and UI-drift conformance tests across browser offline, permission loss, login renewal, and partial submission

proposals.user_asks: “Do this everywhere it needs doing, and only tell me it’s done when you can prove each part succeeded.”
proposals.why_useful: Today judgement can decide a multi-surface plan and Mac/browser can return action receipts, but there is no shared commit protocol. A browser mutation can succeed while the Mac-side follow-up fails, or a stale page can make a receipt look successful. This capability turns a goal into a durable execution manifest: relay assigns one operation ID; Mac and authenticated browser steps acquire leases and report typed results; faculty-perception independently checks each postcondition from fresh UI/state; the relay records a dependency graph and compensating actions; the pendant gives one concise outcome, with the exact failed step and a safe retry/resume option. The owner gets truth rather than optimistic “done,” and a dropped Mac connection does not lose the operation.
surfaces: faculty-judgement emits a versioned manifest containing steps, dependencies, preconditions, postconditions, sensitivity, approval checkpoints, and compensation hints
relay persists the manifest, leases, event log, and resumable state; routes Mac and authenticated browser work and de-duplicates retries by operation/step IDs
mac-planner/mac-vision executes typed Mac actions and returns before/after evidence; browser-extension performs private-tab actions with URL/tab affinity and evidence
faculty-perception independently re-reads the relevant Mac state or browser page after each mutation and marks postconditions proven/unproven/unknown

relay-realtime speaks a short success or failure receipt through the pendant; on unknown or high-risk divergence it requests an owner decision, with the single button serving as approve-retry/cancel while the full evidence remains in dashboard
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheaper background model for manifest compilation, event reconciliation, and postcondition extraction; reserve realtime only for the owner's spoken request, ambiguity, and the final exception/approval exchange. Use deterministic validators for hashes, URLs, file existence, and typed browser fields rather than spending model tokens.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1 second from relay; reversible local steps usually complete in 2–10 seconds; verification adds one fresh read per mutation (roughly 1–3 seconds). Long jobs continue in the relay and surface a completion or exception later, without requiring the owner to stay connected.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.01–$0.08 per ordinary multi-step operation using background extraction/validation; dominant costs are browser/Mac round trips and occasional vision or realtime turns, not the durable event log. Deterministic checks are near-zero model cost.
proposals.security_concerns: The manifest must be capability-scoped and signed/bound to the requesting session, with step-level sensitivity and explicit approval for irreversible sends, purchases, deletes, or external messages. Evidence may contain private page text or file contents, so retain only hashes/snippets by default and encrypt sensitive evidence; expire it separately from the operation record. Never infer success from an executor HTTP 200 alone. On lease expiry, stale precondition, conflicting external change, or unverifiable postcondition, stop rather than retry blindly. Provide an append-only audit trail and compensating undo where valid.
missing: A shared operation/step event schema and durable state machine spanning relay, Mac harness, browser bridge, perception, and judgement
A relay lease/heartbeat and idempotency protocol with resume-after-disconnect semantics
A first-class postcondition verifier API that can request fresh browser snapshots, Mac state reads, or typed filesystem/app checks
Manifest-level approval checkpoints and a pendant button/server-push result path, including explicit unknown/needs-owner states
Evidence normalization (before/after references, provenance, timestamps, hashes) and a dashboard timeline that presents dependency failures and safe recovery options

proposals.user_asks: “When I arrive at [place], have everything ready for me—but don’t change or send anything until I confirm on the pendant.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot currently have a trustworthy physical-context handoff. The pendant is always with them, the phone can know location, the relay can wait while the Mac sleeps, and the Mac/browser can prepare private work—but there is no shared trigger, staged preparation, or local confirmation boundary. This would let a real-world event start useful work without prematurely sending messages, submitting forms, or exposing private content. For example, arrival at an airport could cause the relay to ask the Mac to collect the owner’s itinerary and open the relevant private tabs, while the pendant announces only that a ready packet exists; a deliberate button press releases the final action.
surfaces: iOS/phone location service detects a user-defined geofence or Bluetooth/Wi-Fi place identity and sends a signed arrival event to the relay
relay applies quiet hours, freshness, privacy, and rate-limit policy; starts a staged job and retains it durably if the Mac or browser is offline
Mac planner and browser bridge gather the allowed private context, prepare reversible drafts/open tabs/files, and return evidence without submitting or sending
faculty-judgement evaluates the staged packet against the trigger and asks for approval only for the final side effect

pendant receives a minimal local prompt such as 'Airport packet ready'; button press approves the named operation, while timeout, departure, or a second press cancels/locks it; relay then dispatches the approved Mac/browser action and reports outcome
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic geofence/event policy and a cheap background model for packet preparation and summarization. Use the realtime tier only if the owner asks a follow-up question or the trigger requires spoken disambiguation; do not spend realtime tokens on routine arrival events.
proposals.latency_budget: Arrival event to a ready packet in 10–60 seconds depending on Mac/browser availability. Pendant confirmation must be local and immediate; final dispatch acknowledgement under 2 seconds, with long work continuing asynchronously.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per triggered packet, dominated by private-page extraction and any vision step; geofence events, relay persistence, and deterministic policy are negligible. A daily rate limit and deduplication prevent location chatter from becoming API spend.
proposals.security_concerns: Location history is highly sensitive: keep only coarse place IDs and event timestamps, encrypt them, and expire raw coordinates immediately. Each geofence must be explicitly configured with permitted data sources and actions; never trigger external sends, purchases, deletes, or unlocks automatically. Bind the approval token to the exact staged manifest, expire it quickly, prevent replay, and require a visible spoken/LED indication of what will happen. If location is uncertain, the phone is spoofed, the owner departs, or private sessions are unavailable, do nothing and say why.
missing: A privacy-preserving iOS location/geofence client and signed arrival-event protocol
Relay-side staged-job and expiring approval-token state, with deduplication and quiet hours
A pendant local confirmation/result protocol that survives a transient network drop and clearly distinguishes ready, approved, cancelled, and failed
Cross-surface policy tying each place trigger to an allowlisted data scope and action manifest
Mac/browser preparation mode that can collect evidence and draft/open reversible artifacts without accidentally committing side effects

proposals.user_asks: "Carry this out, but if anything important changes while you're working, stop and tell me exactly what changed before continuing."
proposals.why_useful: Today judgement can decide an action, but execution can outlive the evidence it was based on. This gives the owner a real safety boundary across Mac, authenticated browser, relay, and pendant: long jobs continue when the owner leaves, yet stale or materially changed facts cannot silently produce a send, purchase, deletion, or submission.
surfaces: faculty-judgement emits a signed action manifest with assumptions, field hashes, expiry, reversibility, and required confirmation
faculty-perception watches source tabs/files and emits invalidation events when assumptions or page state change
relay persists the manifest, checkpoints, and cancellation/invalidation state while the Mac/browser are disconnected
mac-planner routes reversible steps to mac_run_actions and multi-step work to mac_delegate
browser-extension executes authenticated tab steps with before/after evidence and idempotency keys
pendant receives a terse pause reason and offers local confirm/cancel via button/voice when the owner returns
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheaper background model for manifest compilation, polling, diffing, and receipt summarization; reserve realtime only for the pendant's brief spoken interruption and confirmation. Use faculty-judgement for the initial policy decision, not on every checkpoint.
proposals.latency_budget: Reversible checkpoints under 2 seconds after a detected change; browser/file watches can poll or subscribe in the background. A stale irreversible step must wait for an explicit pendant confirmation, with no more than one short spoken sentence and a detailed receipt on Mac.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per long-running job depending on checkpoint count; dominated by browser/Mac observation and background model calls, not realtime voice. Storage is small: manifests, hashes, and receipts rather than page contents.
proposals.security_concerns: Private URLs, snippets, and file metadata stay on the Mac/bridge where possible; relay stores redacted hashes and minimum fields. Never auto-send mail, buy, delete, or submit after invalidation. Require explicit confirmation on the pendant for any irreversible action or changed recipient/amount/destination.
missing: A shared action-manifest schema and signature/expiry verifier
Perception-to-executor invalidation events for browser tabs and Mac files
Durable checkpoint/cancel state in the relay job runner
A pendant push message plus button confirmation path
Browser and Mac adapters that report typed before/after evidence at each checkpoint

proposals.user_asks: "If that task got halfway done, figure out what actually happened and finish only the missing parts—don't repeat anything."
proposals.why_useful: Long Mac/browser work can lose connectivity after some steps succeed. Without reconciliation, retrying can duplicate calendar events, create duplicate files, or send twice. A cross-surface recovery capability turns partial failure into a trustworthy outcome and gives the owner a concise completion receipt.
surfaces: relay records per-step idempotency keys, attempts, and durable receipts even across disconnects
mac-planner/mac-terminal queries local artifacts and command receipts to establish what completed
browser-extension reattaches to the same authenticated tab/session and checks page state, confirmation banners, and submitted-record IDs
faculty-perception compares the intended manifest with current Mac/browser state and labels each step complete, missing, ambiguous, or divergent
faculty-judgement decides whether a divergent state is safe to compensate or needs owner approval
pendant speaks only the ambiguity requiring attention and accepts confirm/cancel; Mac leaves a full reconciliation report
proposals.model_tier: Cheaper background model for receipt normalization and state comparison; faculty-judgement for ambiguous compensation policy; realtime only for the short owner-facing question.
proposals.latency_budget: Resume/reconcile within 5 seconds for local actions and 10–30 seconds for browser reattachment and page verification. Never retry an ambiguous externally visible action automatically.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.02–$0.10 per recovered job, dominated by browser/Mac verification calls; model use is limited to summarization and ambiguous-state classification.
proposals.security_concerns: Read only the minimum artifacts/pages needed to establish state. Treat submitted IDs and confirmation banners as sensitive evidence; redact them in spoken output. Require confirmation before compensating actions that could send, purchase, delete, or alter an external record.
missing: A durable per-step receipt ledger with idempotency keys and typed outcome states
Mac adapters for artifact/command reconciliation
Browser adapters for post-submit record lookup and session reattachment
A compensation-policy interface from faculty-judgement
A unified reconciliation report and pendant prompt

proposals.user_asks: "Give this task permission to do only what I just approved, across my Mac and logged-in browser, and let me revoke that permission from the pendant at any time."
proposals.why_useful: The owner can approve an individual action today, but approval is not yet a portable, independently enforceable authority shared by relay, Mac, and browser. A narrowly scoped capability token would let long-running work proceed without broad standing access while giving the owner an immediate physical revoke switch.
surfaces: pendant creates a one-time signed grant after the owner's button/voice approval, bound to task, device, destination, allowed verbs, limits, and expiry; a second button press revokes it locally and queues revocation if offline
relay is the authority registry and fan-out point, storing only token metadata and revocation state; it denies requests outside the grant and distributes revocations
mac-planner/mac-terminal present the token to action adapters, which enforce verb/path/app scope before acting and emit signed receipts
browser-extension binds the grant to an authenticated browser session/tab and enforces URL, form-field, recipient, and amount constraints before every mutation
faculty-judgement defines the grant's scope and whether a proposed step fits it; faculty-perception supplies current device/session identity and detects scope drift
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheaper background tier to compile and validate grants and to audit receipts. Use realtime only to explain the requested scope and receive the owner's short approval/revocation interaction.
proposals.latency_budget: Grant issuance under 1 second locally; relay propagation under 2 seconds; revocation must block new actions within 2 seconds and force a final local re-check immediately before any irreversible step.
proposals.cost_estimate: Less than $0.01 per grant in relay storage/signature operations; model cost only when translating natural language into a constrained scope, typically $0.01–$0.05. Dominant cost is verification calls for browser/Mac steps.
proposals.security_concerns: This is an authority system, so fail closed on unknown, expired, replayed, or offline-revoked tokens. Never place raw secrets in the token; use opaque IDs and hashes. Bind grants to the specific owner account, Mac, browser session, and task. Require a fresh physical confirmation for send, purchase, delete, or submit even if the grant appears to allow it. Keep a complete audit trail and provide emergency revoke-all from the pendant.
missing: A signed capability-token format with verb/resource/field constraints and expiry
Relay-side grant registry, replay protection, and revocation fan-out
Mac and browser enforcement middleware that checks grants before every mutation
Pendant-local key storage and offline revoke queue
A judgement policy compiler that turns approval language into a least-privilege scope
Cross-device audit receipts proving which grant authorized each step

proposals.user_asks: When I press the pendant button offline to bookmark a moment, bring it back later, figure out what it relates to, and leave me a ready-to-review follow-up on my Mac.
proposals.why_useful: The pendant already records offline moments, and the relay already surfaces held alerts, but today a bookmark is only an isolated event. This would turn a fleeting thought captured without connectivity into a grounded, actionable thread without requiring the owner to remember it later. It is inherently multi-node: pendant capture, relay durability, Mac/private-app context, browser session evidence when available, and faculty judgement/action for a safe follow-up.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic pendant/relay code for capture, deduplication, ordering, and delivery. Use a cheap background text model on the Mac for clustering/transcription summarization; use faculty-perception for evidence gathering and faculty-judgement for intent classification. Reserve realtime only for the eventual short spoken receipt or a focused clarification.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture must be immediate and offline. On reconnect, durable delivery and an initial receipt should complete within 2 seconds; enrichment may run in the background for up to 2 minutes. If private browser evidence is unavailable, leave the item pending rather than guessing or acting.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per reconciled bookmark, dominated by background model/context extraction; near-zero relay/storage cost. Realtime cost is avoided unless the owner asks a follow-up question.
proposals.security_concerns: Bookmark audio/transcript and matched private context may contain sensitive data. Encrypt the pendant spool and relay payload, minimize context to candidate snippets, retain provenance and expiry, and keep browser content on the Mac. Never send email, submit a form, or alter a calendar item automatically; create a reviewable draft/reminder with before/after evidence. Require explicit confirmation for any irreversible action.
missing: A durable bookmark envelope with monotonic device sequence, capture timestamp, link state, audio/transcript hash, and idempotency key across pendant→relay→Mac
A reconnect reconciler that acknowledges each envelope exactly once and reports late/duplicate/out-of-order delivery back to the pendant
A Mac enrichment worker that searches permitted local apps and authenticated browser tabs, records evidence versions/provenance, and expires stale matches
A decision-window/action-manifest bridge so judgement can request one clarification and action can create a review item or reversible reminder
A dashboard queue showing bookmark, transcript, matched evidence, confidence, expiry, and approve/edit/dismiss controls; current browser is offline and Mac readiness is false

proposals.user_asks: Remember this for the next place I arrive: when my pendant detects that I have reached a chosen place, give me the relevant note or open the exact Mac/browser workbench I need there—without me having to remember to ask.
proposals.why_useful: A wearable can capture intent at the moment it occurs, while the Mac and browser can prepare the private, concrete material needed later. The owner gets a just-in-time handoff instead of a generic reminder that arrives too early or too late. This requires the pendant's physical continuity, an always-awake relay, the Mac's local files/apps, and authenticated browser sessions together; no single node can provide it safely.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic geofence/proximity events, encrypted queueing, and scheduled delivery for the control plane. Use a background economical model to turn the captured note into a compact context card and choose the relevant workbench. Use faculty-perception to verify current place/session evidence and faculty-judgement to resolve ambiguity. Use realtime only for the short spoken handoff when the pendant is worn.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture is immediate and offline. Place arrival should trigger a local acknowledgement in under 1 second; the prepared card/workbench should be ready within 10 seconds online. If location confidence or browser freshness is inadequate, defer and ask one concise question rather than guessing.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.04 per handoff, mostly background context matching; deterministic relay and local Mac work are negligible. Realtime speech is only a few cents when used.
proposals.security_concerns: Location and private account data are highly sensitive. Keep raw location on the paired iOS/pendant path, send only a place pseudonym and intent ID to the relay, and keep authenticated page contents on the Mac. Require per-place opt-in, visible active-place state, expiration, revocation, and an audit trail. Opening a prepared workbench is reversible; sending, purchasing, deleting, or submitting anything still requires explicit confirmation.
missing: A product pendant with BLE/UWB or another reliable proximity/location signal and encrypted offline intent records; the current prototype has one button/LED and no location sensor
A paired iOS companion that resolves places locally, manages consent, and forwards signed arrival/absence events
Relay support for delayed, ordered intent envelopes keyed to place policies and expiry, including deduplication across reconnects
Mac/browser workbench generation that can stage private evidence without mutating accounts and can revalidate sessions at arrival time
A dashboard policy editor and audit view for place triggers, quiet hours, retention, and revoke/delete controls

proposals.user_asks: “Do this, but only go as far as you can prove; if it needs my approval, buzz me and let me confirm on the pendant.”
proposals.why_useful: The mind can decide a multi-step action today but cannot reliably distinguish a queued receipt from a real-world effect: the Mac currently reports UI success while Accessibility is denied, and the browser can be offline with commands pending. This makes execution honest and recoverable across the wearable, always-awake relay, Mac, and authenticated browser.
surfaces: faculty-judgement emits a typed plan with risk, preconditions, and the exact final side effect
relay persists a short-lived action lease, correlates request/action IDs, and survives the Mac or browser reconnecting
Mac agent runs a capability preflight (Accessibility, Screen Recording, focused app, filesystem/app state), executes only steps whose preconditions pass, then observes postconditions
browser extension reports online/session/tab affinity and returns evidence for private-page steps; public steps may use relay browser only when appropriate
pendant receives blocked/approval states, speaks a concise explanation, and uses the existing physical button for explicit confirmation of the final irreversible step
faculty-action compiles a truthful completion receipt: observed effect, evidence source/timestamp, or blocked reason; never infer success from queue acceptance
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only for the live spoken approval and brief status. Use a cheaper background model for plan validation, receipt summarization, retries, and reconnect reconciliation.
proposals.latency_budget: Preflight 1–2 seconds; approval prompt under 1 second after the plan reaches a checkpoint; reconnect reconciliation in background. A blocked result should be immediate rather than waiting for permissions.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 in model/API work: most steps are typed checks and local observations; realtime cost is only the short approval exchange. Relay D1/storage and a few telemetry requests dominate operational cost, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Leases must be single-use, short TTL, bound to the intended Mac/browser session and action hash, and reject stale/replayed button presses. Never send private page contents to the relay unless required; keep evidence local where possible. Require explicit pendant confirmation for send/submit/delete/payment/account changes. Report missing permissions and private-session unavailability without pretending the action happened.
missing: Typed action-plan/lease protocol shared by judgement, relay, Mac, and browser
Mac preflight and postcondition observers whose verdicts gate execution (not merely annotate receipts)
Pendant protocol/UI for blocked, awaiting-confirmation, and completed-with-evidence states
Browser online/pending-command reconciliation with durable job IDs
Tests covering denied Accessibility, offline browser, reconnect, duplicate button press, and partial multi-step completion

proposals.user_asks: “Do the same thing as last time, but show me what is different before you apply it.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can repeat real workflows without remembering every click or restating context: the system would recover the prior successful action as a reusable, evidence-backed recipe, adapt it to today’s data, and expose only the differences for approval. This is more useful than merely keeping an action log because it turns past work into a safe, personal operating procedure across private browser sessions and the Mac.
surfaces: pendant captures the spoken reference (“last time”) and presents a short spoken summary of the proposed differences
relay resolves the reference to a prior completed action graph, retains its provenance and sensitivity boundaries, and coordinates the run if the Mac disconnects
Mac agent re-observes the current filesystem, apps, and permissions, then maps the old recipe to current targets without replaying stale coordinates
browser extension reattaches the authenticated tab/session used by the prior recipe and extracts current values, while refusing to reuse a recipe against a different account or origin
faculty-perception compares prior evidence with current evidence and identifies changed fields, missing preconditions, and uncertainty

faculty-judgement decides whether the delta is safe, asks for approval only when the owner-visible effect differs, and faculty-action executes the approved typed steps with a new receipt linked to the original
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model to canonicalize old receipts into recipes and compute diffs. Use the realtime tier only to resolve the owner’s spoken reference and explain the final delta during the live interaction.
proposals.latency_budget: Recipe lookup under 500 ms; current-state collection 2–5 seconds; spoken diff under 10 seconds for a normal workflow. If a surface is unavailable, return the saved recipe and an explicit pause point rather than pretending it ran.
proposals.cost_estimate: Typically <$0.02 per invocation. Local observation and receipt comparison dominate; background model tokens are needed only for ambiguous semantic mapping, while realtime usage is limited to the short voice exchange.
proposals.security_concerns: Recipes must be scoped to account, origin, device, and action class; never store passwords, tokens, or unrestricted page text. Any change to recipient, amount, destination, permissions, deletion, or submission requires fresh physical confirmation. A recipe must expire or require revalidation when the source page or app changes materially. Keep sensitive evidence local and send only hashes/field-level diffs to the relay.
missing: A versioned action-recipe format derived from receipts, with provenance and sensitivity labels
Semantic target mapping that can replace stale coordinates/selectors with current evidence
Cross-surface identity and origin binding for private browser sessions
A diff renderer shared by relay voice, Mac dashboard, and pendant speech
Policy for recipe expiry, changed high-risk fields, and mandatory physical re-approval

proposals.user_asks: “If you can’t do that because the Mac is blocked, walk me through fixing it and retry automatically when I’m done.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can detect that UI automation is impossible but leaves the owner to diagnose permissions and remember to retry. This turns a dead end into a recoverable handoff: the Mac opens the relevant settings pane, the pendant explains the one missing step, the relay waits for the permission state to change, and the original action resumes exactly once.
surfaces: faculty-action detects and classifies the block
mac-planner opens the exact macOS Privacy & Security pane and polls permission state
relay-realtime keeps the pending job and sends a concise spoken instruction/retry status
pendant speaks the instruction and a button confirms the owner is ready
faculty-perception verifies input reachability and post-action evidence
browser-extension is used only if the owner must toggle a browser extension; otherwise it remains untouched
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic local code for permission classification, settings deep links, polling, and retry; use the realtime model only for the spoken explanation and ambiguity. No background LLM is needed.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate blocked response under 1 second; settings handoff under 2 seconds; poll every 2 seconds for up to 5 minutes, then leave a durable pending job and stop.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero API cost for local polling and Mac settings navigation; at most one short realtime turn for explanation. Dominant cost is the existing voice session, not the recovery logic.
proposals.security_concerns: Never grant permissions or alter security settings automatically. The owner must perform the toggle. Do not capture screen contents while Screen Recording is missing. Persist only job ID, missing permission, host bundle identity, and timestamps; retry is idempotent and only after perception verifies reachability.
missing: Mandatory UI-action preflight and typed blocked receipts
A local permission-state change watcher or short-poll endpoint
macOS deep links for the exact Accessibility and Screen Recording panes
Relay state machine for blocked->ready->single retry
Pendant button event routed to the pending job
Browser extension heartbeat/online state if browser recovery is requested

proposals.user_asks: “If the first way fails, finish the task another way without making me start over—and tell me exactly what was completed.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a task that hits an offline browser, a locked UI, or a sleeping Mac becomes a dead end or a misleading partial success. The owner should be able to hand the goal to the whole hive once; the action facet should preserve completed work, select a different reachable surface, and return one clear account of what happened rather than duplicate or abandon the task.
surfaces: pendant captures the single spoken goal and reads back the final state
relay holds the durable execution lease and receives heartbeats while devices disappear and return
faculty-judgement defines completion invariants and which substitutions are acceptable
faculty-perception verifies each claimed state transition with fresh evidence
faculty-action executes through Mac typed APIs, terminal, browser session, or relay fallback and records a shared task ledger
mac-planner and mac-terminal perform local alternatives when GUI/browser control is unavailable
browser-extension supplies authenticated-page actions when it is online, otherwise the task pauses at the exact browser-dependent boundary
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic orchestration, action IDs, preconditions, and evidence matching for execution and fallback. Use the cheaper background model to translate a failed step into candidate alternatives. Use realtime only for the owner's live explanation or a genuinely ambiguous spoken goal.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1 second; fallback selection in under 3 seconds; asynchronous work may continue for minutes or hours with heartbeat updates. Never retry an unknown side effect until its prior outcome is reconciled.
proposals.cost_estimate: Mostly local/relay orchestration with low background-model cost. The dominant cost is only the occasional reasoning turn to map an unavailable operation to an equivalent alternative; no screenshot or voice token cost is needed for silent retries.
proposals.security_concerns: Fallbacks must preserve the original authorization scope and must not silently downgrade a private browser operation to a public/cloud route. Sensitive data stays on the Mac/browser session. Unknown outcomes become a stopped, inspectable state—not a blind retry. The owner sees which surface acted, what evidence supports it, and which portion remains undone.
missing: A cross-surface task ledger with semantic completion invariants, dependency boundaries, and idempotent step identities
A failure taxonomy that distinguishes blocked, offline, rejected, timed out, and unknown-outcome actions
A planner that can generate and rank proof-equivalent fallback paths without widening data access
Evidence reconciliation across pendant, relay, Mac, and browser receipts
A resumable lease protocol that hands work between surfaces without replaying completed side effects
A compact spoken and dashboard receipt showing completed, substituted, blocked, and unknown steps

proposals.user_asks: After you change something on my Mac or in a logged-in website, prove that it actually took effect and tell me if it didn't.
proposals.why_useful: A successful API response is not proof that a click reached the screen or that a private web transaction persisted. This gives the owner a trustworthy outcome instead of a misleading completion message, especially when Accessibility or the browser bridge is unavailable.
surfaces: faculty-judgement plans the intended reversible change and its expected postcondition
faculty-action dispatches to mac-planner/mac-vision or browser-extension with an idempotency key
faculty-perception independently re-reads the relevant Mac state or authenticated page and compares it with the expected postcondition
relay-realtime delivers a concise spoken result on the pendant; the Mac keeps the cited evidence and retryable job record
proposals.model_tier: background for planning and evidence comparison; deterministic checks first (receipt status, file hashes, UI accessibility state, page extraction), escalating to planner only when the postcondition is semantic or ambiguous. Realtime is used only to converse with the owner.
proposals.latency_budget: For local reversible actions, 1–3 seconds. For authenticated browser verification, up to 10 seconds; if the bridge is offline, say queued/unverified rather than spending repeated calls.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually no model call for deterministic checks; about $0.001–$0.01 for an ambiguous background comparison, dominated by page/UI evidence tokens. No screenshot upload unless the owner explicitly allows it.
proposals.security_concerns: Verification must use the same scoped tab/session and avoid exposing private page content in relay speech. Never claim verified from an API acknowledgement alone. Irreversible actions still require the existing owner approval policy; this capability verifies effects, it does not authorize them.
missing: A typed postcondition/verification contract attached to each action plan
A faculty-perception verification endpoint that can read Mac state and authenticated browser evidence
Cross-node correlation of action idempotency key, before/after evidence, and final receipt
The browser bridge must return stable extraction evidence when it comes back online

proposals.user_asks: Prepare the change, and when I press the button on my pendant, carry it out—even if the voice connection has dropped.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can currently prepare work conversationally but cannot provide a reliable, local final authorization when the network or voice session disappears. A physical pendant press gives a clear last-mile signal without opening a microphone, while preventing a stale or replayed request from executing later.
surfaces: faculty-judgement creates a bounded, reversible transaction with an exact action hash, expiry, and expected target
relay stores the encrypted pending transaction and delivers a one-time challenge to the pendant
pendant firmware displays a short confirmation cue and turns the button press into a locally signed nonce response
relay validates the nonce and forwards the transaction to mac-planner or browser-extension
faculty-action executes with idempotency, then faculty-perception verifies the resulting state and sends a compact success/failure receipt back to the pendant
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic protocol and action execution; use the background tier only to summarize the prepared transaction or resolve an ambiguous postcondition. Realtime is not required once the transaction is prepared.
proposals.latency_budget: Button acknowledgement under 250 ms locally; relay-to-Mac execution normally under 5 seconds. An expired or disconnected transaction should fail closed and remain visibly pending rather than execute later.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for the protocol; approximately $0.001–$0.01 only when semantic postcondition verification needs a background model. Storage and relay traffic are negligible per transaction.
proposals.security_concerns: The signed response must bind to transaction hash, target session/tab, expiry, and a single-use nonce. Do not put private page contents on the pendant. Require a deliberate long-press or two-step button gesture for high-impact actions, and show a distinct failure cue when the relay cannot confirm execution.
missing: Pendant firmware support for a local confirmation challenge and signed one-time response
A relay transaction escrow with expiry, nonce replay protection, and delivery receipts
A shared transaction hash/idempotency protocol accepted by Mac and browser executors
A pendant-to-relay authenticated pairing key and a user-visible pending/expired state

proposals.user_asks: When you say “send it,” “buy it,” or “change it,” show me a concise description and the exact final values; I can approve that specific action with one deliberate pendant press, and you carry it out wherever it belongs, even if I leave the Mac before completion.
proposals.why_useful: The mind can judge and prepare a consequential action, but today approval is conversational and can be detached from the exact browser/Mac state. This binds the owner's physical, deliberate gesture to a hash of the reviewed action, then lets relay, Mac, and authenticated browser execute it and return an auditable receipt. It is useful precisely because no single node has both the private session, the durable queue, and the owner's physical confirmation.
proposals.model_tier: Use realtime only to explain the pending action and hear a short verbal review; use a cheaper background planner to normalize fields and compute the action digest; deterministic relay/Mac/browser executors perform the action, with no model deciding after approval.
proposals.latency_budget: Preview in under 2 seconds when state is available; pendant confirmation is immediate; execution may take seconds to minutes after the owner walks away, with a durable spoken/status receipt and retry/undo where supported.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per invocation: one short realtime turn for preview/confirmation, then mostly D1/R2 metadata and deterministic Mac/browser calls. Cost is dominated by any required private-page extraction or vision step, not the confirmation protocol.
proposals.security_concerns: Never include cookies or full private page contents in the digest. Store a redacted canonical action summary, target origin/session identifier, before-state hash, final-value hash, expiry, and nonce. Reject replay, stale tab state, changed totals, changed recipients, or scope expansion; require a fresh confirmation. Destructive or financial actions need explicit category policy and a visible cancel window. The pendant's button is proof of physical presence, not identity against an attacker with device access.
missing: A relay endpoint for pending-action envelopes, nonce/expiry, atomic consume, and receipt streaming
A pendant firmware confirmation mode (preview token, one deliberate press, cancel/timeout, offline queue)
A shared canonical action schema/digest library used by judgement, relay, Mac, and browser
Browser bridge online/reliable tab affinity and Mac Accessibility/Screen Recording grants for execution
Dashboard and spoken receipt UI showing exactly what was approved and what actually changed

proposals.user_asks: If something I asked you to do starts going wrong, let me say “stop” or hold the pendant button and have every participating hand halt immediately, quarantine the job, and tell me exactly what already happened and what did not.
proposals.why_useful: Today a queued Mac/browser job can continue after the owner leaves, while the pendant is the only continuously present control surface. An undo is too late for an email, purchase, deletion, or partial multi-step workflow. A relay-coordinated abort lets the owner interrupt in-flight work across the private browser, Mac automation, and durable worker, then produces a truthful partial-execution report.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime handles only the low-latency stop phrase and acknowledgement. Deterministic cancellation tokens, executor checkpoints, and receipt assembly do the safety-critical work; a cheaper background model may summarize the partial result after all executors report.
proposals.latency_budget: A local pendant stop acknowledgement should be immediate; relay propagation target under 500 ms when connected and best-effort delivery after reconnection. Each executor must checkpoint before every side-effecting step and report cancellation within one step.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low API cost: mostly signed control messages and D1 job state. Cost is dominated by any post-abort evidence extraction or screenshot, which should be optional and background.
proposals.security_concerns: The stop command must be authenticated to the paired pendant, signed, nonce-protected, and scoped to one job or action family. Cancellation must be fail-closed for unstarted side effects but honest that an already-committed external action cannot be recalled. Never claim rollback; show per-step committed/skipped/unknown states. Browser and Mac adapters need idempotent cancellation and a quarantine state that blocks retries until the owner resumes or discards the job.
missing: A relay control plane with signed abort tokens, fan-out delivery, replay protection, and durable quarantine state
A common executor protocol with step checkpoints, cancellation acknowledgements, and committed/unknown/skipped receipts
Mac and browser adapters that check cancellation before each side effect and stop computer-use loops safely
Pendant firmware support for a distinct stop gesture that works offline and flushes on reconnect
Dashboard/spoken status for partial execution, plus an explicit resume/discard operation

proposals.user_asks: When I ask you to do something, check that the right hand is actually available first; if it isn't, tell me exactly what is blocking it, keep the request safely resumable, and finish it automatically when that hand comes back—then tell me only when there is proof it happened.
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can report a receipt for a failed browser command while the Mac is not ready and the browser is offline. The owner needs one trustworthy contract: no false success, no lost intent, and no need to repeat a request after reopening Safari or granting access.
surfaces: pendant: speaks a concise blocked/queued/completed status and can receive an explicit cancel or retry command
relay: owns the durable intent, idempotency key, retry policy, handoff state, and reconnect-triggered resume
mac-planner: performs a preflight of bridge health, Accessibility/Screen Recording, app authorization, and task-specific reachability
mac-vision: supplies screenshot/DOM evidence only when the task requires UI interaction and only after permissions are confirmed
browser-extension: reports polling, session/tab affinity, page identity, and typed completion evidence; never accepts work while offline
dashboard: shows blocker, queued plan, attempts, evidence, and cancel/approve controls
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for routing, retry classification, and evidence reconciliation; reserve gpt-realtime for the spoken status and any owner clarification.
proposals.latency_budget: Preflight under 2 seconds when hands are online; queue immediately when offline; resume within 10 seconds of a reconnect event; speak a blocker in under 1 second and completion only after verified evidence.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.002–$0.02 per action lifecycle depending on whether evidence needs vision; most retries and state transitions are deterministic, with occasional cheap text reconciliation. Realtime cost is limited to owner-facing turns.
proposals.security_concerns: Private URLs, page text, screenshots, and permission state may cross relay boundaries; keep sensitive payloads on Mac/browser where possible and send hashes/typed evidence. Never retry irreversible sends, purchases, deletions, or submissions without a fresh approval lease. Bind retries to the original tab/session and idempotency key; expire queued intents and provide cancel.
missing: A typed cross-surface preflight schema and capability lease (online, permission, session, tab, and evidence requirements)
A durable intent state machine separate from action receipts: blocked, queued, running, verified, failed, cancelled, expired
Reconnect events from the Mac bridge and browser extension to wake the relay runner
Evidence requirements per action type and a verifier that distinguishes attempted from completed
A safe retry/approval policy for irreversible actions
Pendant-visible status and cancellation for queued intents

proposals.user_asks: When I’m physically with my Mac, let me approve a prepared action from the pendant with one button or a spoken phrase, and make sure the approval is bound to this device, this computer, and this exact preview—so the action cannot run later from an old request or on the wrong machine.
proposals.why_useful: The owner gets a practical, trustworthy bridge between their physical presence and high-impact digital actions. A prepared browser submission, local file change, or message can be approved while wearing the pendant, but a stale queued request, replayed voice command, or action on another Mac cannot silently execute.
surfaces: pendant: captures the short approval phrase or button gesture, displays a preview hash/status, and emits a device-bound approval token
relay: issues short-lived approval challenges, binds them to the pendant identity, Mac identity, exact action hash, and expiry, and records an auditable decision
mac-planner: assembles the exact action preview and refuses execution unless the challenge matches the current machine and unchanged plan
mac-vision: supplies visual confirmation of the final target when a GUI action is involved
browser-extension: confirms the exact tab/session/page identity and verifies that the submitted fields still match the approved preview
dashboard: displays pending approval challenges, target machine, preview digest, expiry, and revocation history
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic cryptographic checks and a cheap background model for preview summarization; use realtime only to conduct the short spoken approval interaction.
proposals.latency_budget: Preview preparation can take seconds; approval acknowledgement should be under 1 second, with execution beginning within 3 seconds after a valid token. Expire challenges after 60 seconds by default.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost for most actions, approximately $0.0005–$0.005 for a generated preview summary; cryptographic checks and audit records dominate neither latency nor cost.
proposals.security_concerns: The pendant becomes an approval credential, so loss or theft requires revocation and re-pairing. Never include secrets in spoken previews. Bind approvals to a nonce, action digest, tab/session identity, Mac host fingerprint, and narrow expiry; require a stronger confirmation for financial, deletion, publication, or message-send actions. Store audit metadata, not full private page contents, in the relay.
missing: Secure pendant identity and challenge-response signing or equivalent paired-device attestation
A canonical action-preview digest shared by judgement, relay, Mac, and browser
A Mac host fingerprint and browser tab/session identity in the approval verifier
Pendant-side approval interaction and revocation flow
A final pre-execution comparison that rejects any plan changed after approval

proposals.user_asks: When I tell you to do something, start it from the pendant and finish it on whichever device becomes available—if Safari is closed or the Mac is locked, keep the intent queued, retry safely, and tell me exactly what completed, what is waiting, and what still needs my approval.
proposals.why_useful: Today a decided action can simply burn 45 seconds and fail because the browser bridge is offline, while the owner receives no useful handoff. This makes the hive act as one reliable hand: capture intent on the wearable, execute on Mac/browser when reachable, and deliver a truthful receipt back to the pendant.
proposals.model_tier: background for queue classification, retry summaries, and receipts; planner only for ambiguous recovery; realtime only to acknowledge the owner's live request.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate pendant acknowledgement under 1 second; preflight health decision under 2 seconds; retries in the background with exponential backoff and a quiet-hours policy; spoken completion within 5 seconds of terminal result.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: deterministic health checks and state transitions dominate; roughly one background-model call (1–3k input tokens) only for ambiguous failure/recovery summaries, not per retry.
proposals.security_concerns: Private browser work must remain in the authenticated local extension; relay stores only encrypted job metadata and receipts. Never retry irreversible submit/send/purchase steps automatically; require explicit approval and re-check the target tab, URL, and before-state immediately before execution.
missing: A cross-surface durable job state machine with idempotency keys and lease ownership
Preflight health/readiness checks for Mac permissions, bridge online state, browser tab affinity, and network
Safe retry policy distinguishing reversible/idempotent steps from irreversible approval gates
Pendant-visible pending/completed/blocked receipt queue and a wake-up push path
A recovery protocol when a device reconnects after a dropped link

proposals.user_asks: Before you act across my Mac and logged-in browser, show me a trustworthy preview of the exact outcome—what files, messages, appointments, or web fields would change—and then carry it out only if the live state still matches that preview; if it changed, stop and explain the difference.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can currently approve an abstract plan, but cannot reliably know whether the world has changed between planning and execution. A cross-surface state-matched preview would make complex actions understandable and prevent stale plans from editing the wrong document, tab, account, or appointment.
proposals.model_tier: Background model for extracting and summarizing predicted diffs; planner tier only when the preview is ambiguous. Realtime should speak only the concise approval prompt and final result.
proposals.latency_budget: Generate a preview in under 8 seconds for ordinary Mac/browser tasks; approval prompt under 2 seconds after preview is ready; live-state revalidation under 2 seconds before execution.
proposals.cost_estimate: Typically one background call of about 2–5k input tokens plus deterministic local diffing; pixel comparison and DOM/file hashing dominate latency, not model cost.
proposals.security_concerns: Private page contents and local file metadata stay on the Mac/browser bridge where possible; relay receives only redacted diff summaries and hashes. Never claim a preview is complete when a surface is inaccessible. Require explicit approval for external communication, purchases, deletion, or permission changes.
missing: A read-only shadow executor that resolves every planned target without mutating it
Canonical before-state snapshots for files, DOM regions, app records, and selected pixels
A typed predicted-diff format with confidence, omitted fields, and irreversible-effect classification
Atomic compare-and-execute semantics across Mac and browser surfaces
A pendant/dashboard diff viewer that supports approve, edit, reject, and inspect-source actions

proposals.user_asks: “Do this wherever you can; if a device is unavailable, keep going and tell me exactly what is blocked.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can decide an action but execution fails late and opaquely: the browser has three pending commands while offline, and the Mac agent reports ready:false because Accessibility and Screen Recording are missing. A cross-surface preflight would test reachability, permissions, session/tab affinity, and relay/pendant connectivity before acting; route safe steps to another surface, durably queue blocked steps, and return a compact owner-facing receipt naming completed, queued, and blocked work. This avoids 45-second dead-end browser attempts and makes unattended work trustworthy.
surfaces: faculty-judgement emits an action graph with required capabilities and reversibility
faculty-action runs a preflight against Mac agent /ops/status, browser heartbeat/status, relay job state, and pendant pipeline
browser-extension executes authenticated browser steps when online; mac-vision or mac-terminal handles equivalent Mac-local work when permitted
relay persists queued steps and wakes the pendant with a short status/receipt
pendant displays or speaks completed/blocked/needs-owner-attention summary
proposals.model_tier: Background planner for graph validation and recovery; realtime only for the owner's live clarification or confirmation. Deterministic health checks and routing should be code, not model calls.
proposals.latency_budget: Preflight under 1 second for local/relay health; if blocked, report immediately rather than waiting 45 seconds. Queue retries with exponential backoff and quiet hours; wake pendant only for urgent or completed outcomes.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost for deterministic preflight; roughly one background planning call only for ambiguous fallback routing. Dominant cost is durable storage and occasional TTS/audio delivery.
proposals.security_concerns: Health metadata must not include page contents or secrets. Authenticated browser actions remain on the paired extension. Never bypass missing Accessibility/Screen Recording or confirmation gates; irreversible actions stay queued pending owner approval. Persist an audit receipt with required capability, route chosen, evidence, and retry history.
missing: A shared action-graph schema carrying prerequisites, fallback routes, urgency, expiry, and approval state
A single preflight endpoint/SDK aggregating Mac readiness, browser online/session state, relay reachability, and pendant delivery
Durable queue with retry/dead-letter and dependency-aware resume (not just a browser command queue)
Owner-visible blocked/queued receipt and pendant notification protocol
Automatic cleanup/reconciliation of the existing three stale browser commands

proposals.user_asks: “Make this change everywhere it needs to happen, but leave my world consistent if one part fails.”
proposals.why_useful: The mind can currently perform separate actions on the Mac, in authenticated browser sessions, and through the relay, but it cannot guarantee consistency across them. A single request such as updating a local project note, preparing a logged-in form, and recording the resulting reference can leave half-finished state when a surface disappears. The owner should get a cross-surface transaction: preview the complete change set, execute reversible steps under one transaction ID, verify postconditions on every surface, compensate completed steps when a later step fails, and report any genuinely non-compensable residue explicitly.
surfaces: faculty-judgement compiles the intended change into a typed transaction with invariants and compensation rules
faculty-action coordinates Mac file/note/reminder changes, authenticated browser mutations, and relay persistence under one transaction ID
browser-extension supplies before/after evidence and idempotent mutation handles for private pages
mac-vision or mac-terminal performs local changes with snapshots and restores when compensation is safe
relay stores the transaction journal and wakes the pendant with commit, compensated, or partial-failure status
pendant presents a terse completion state and offers owner confirmation for any residual irreversible step
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model only to translate an ambiguous goal into candidate steps and compensation plans; use deterministic code for transaction state, invariant checks, idempotency, and rollback. Realtime is only for live approval or clarification.
proposals.latency_budget: Preview in under 2 seconds for known actions; execute asynchronously when multi-step. The pendant should receive immediate accepted/running state and a final receipt when committed, compensated, or irreversibly partial.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low model cost after planning; storage and evidence journaling dominate. A background planner call is needed only when step dependencies or compensations are ambiguous.
proposals.security_concerns: Never claim atomicity for irreversible external effects such as sent mail, purchases, or submitted forms. Require explicit approval at the irreversible boundary, isolate secrets to their owning surface, encrypt the journal, redact page contents from relay receipts, and make compensation opt-in per action type. The owner must see exactly which effects are and are not reversible.
missing: A cross-surface transaction/saga protocol with typed invariants, idempotency keys, leases, and compensation handlers
Snapshot/restore adapters for Mac files, notes, reminders, and browser fields
Postcondition verification primitives that can cite evidence from each surface
A durable encrypted transaction journal and reconciliation worker on the relay
UI and pendant vocabulary distinguishing committed, compensated, and irreversibly partial outcomes

proposals.user_asks: When I say “take care of this when you can,” keep the task with you across disconnected devices: capture it on the pendant, do the work on my Mac and logged-in browser when they become available, and tell me on the pendant exactly what happened, what is waiting for approval, and how to undo it.
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can decide a task but loses the handoff when the owner walks away, the Mac sleeps, or the browser bridge is offline. This creates one durable action thread spanning the always-on relay, wearable capture, Mac execution, and private browser session—without silently sending irreversible actions.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to capture/clarify the short spoken intent and announce completion; use a cheaper background model for decomposition, retries, and receipt summarization. The relay persists a typed intent envelope; Mac planner selects the executor; browser extension handles authenticated pages; pendant is the notification/approval endpoint.
proposals.latency_budget: Pendant acknowledgement under 1 second, even offline (local queued receipt). Start execution within 30 seconds of Mac/browser availability. Each reversible step may retry in the background; irreversible browser submission pauses for explicit pendant or dashboard approval. Completion announcement should arrive within 2 seconds of a verified receipt.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per task for background planning and summarization, plus negligible relay/storage; realtime cost is limited to the initial utterance and final short announcement. Browser and Mac work dominate wall-clock time, not tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: Private page content must stay on the Mac/browser path and only extracted fields needed for the task may reach the relay. Bind the intent to the owner's device key, target account/session, and an expiry; never treat a reconnect as approval. Show before/after evidence for sends, purchases, deletions, or external submissions; require explicit approval and provide an idempotent undo where possible. If a device disappears, retain the task state but do not broaden permissions.
missing: A durable cross-surface action envelope with idempotency key, expiry, owner approval state, and executor lease
Pendant-local offline intent spool and a reconnect/push protocol for task state and approval prompts
Relay scheduler that resumes jobs when Mac and browser bridge return, with per-step typed receipts and retry policy
Mac/browser executor handshake exposing availability, authenticated session identity, and safe pause points
A unified owner-facing action timeline on the pendant and dashboard, including approve/reject/undo
End-to-end tests for sleep, network loss, duplicate reconnects, stale browser tabs, and partially completed workflows

proposals.user_asks: If a condition I care about happens, prepare the whole action and reach me wherever I am: for example, “if this flight drops below $800, check my calendar, hold the best option, and ask me on the pendant before buying.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot currently turn an intention about the future into a coordinated, bounded action. A relay can notice a public change, the Mac can reconcile local calendar and preferences, and the authenticated browser can prepare a private transaction—but no single node can safely carry the plan from trigger through a just-in-time approval.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for scheduled/trigger evaluation, option ranking, and preparation. Use realtime only when the pendant asks the owner for a concise final decision. Deterministic code should enforce thresholds, expiry, budget, and approval gates; the model must not be the authority for purchase or submission.
proposals.latency_budget: Trigger evaluation can run every 5–15 minutes or on a provider webhook. Prepare an option within 60 seconds of a qualifying event. The pendant approval prompt should arrive within 2 seconds once the private browser transaction is ready; expire the offer after a short owner-defined window.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.10 per triggered evaluation depending on option count; public polling/provider webhooks and browser/Mac execution dominate cost. Most non-triggered checks should use deterministic comparisons and no model call.
proposals.security_concerns: Never grant standing permission to buy or submit. Store the rule, threshold, maximum spend, allowed accounts, and expiry as structured policy; require fresh pendant approval tied to the exact displayed option and amount. Keep calendar and account data on the Mac/browser path, redact it from relay logs, and revoke a prepared hold if approval expires. Handle stale prices, duplicate triggers, timezone changes, and provider errors as safe pauses.
missing: A durable conditional-plan schema with trigger source, predicate, evaluation history, expiry, and bounded action graph
Provider adapters or signed webhook/polling inputs for public conditions, with freshness and anti-spoof checks
A cross-surface planner that can query Mac-local state and prepare—but not submit—an authenticated browser transaction
A pendant push prompt that displays a compact, exact option/price and binds approval to its hash
A reservation/hold lifecycle with timeout cancellation, duplicate-trigger suppression, and clear owner receipts
Dashboard controls for creating, testing, pausing, and deleting conditional plans without exposing private credentials

proposals.user_asks: “For this project, make the routine decisions yourself: you may carry out changes that satisfy my standing rules, but stop and ask me whenever the actual result would violate one of them.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner must re-authorize a stream of individually safe actions, or risk giving a broad instruction that cannot express nuanced limits. This would let the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser act as one bounded delegate: ordinary work proceeds while exceptions, ambiguity, and policy violations reach the owner with the exact evidence needed to decide.
proposals.model_tier: A cheaper background planner compiles the owner's natural-language rules into a typed policy; local Mac/browser executors enforce the deterministic checks; faculty-judgement handles ambiguous exceptions; realtime is used only to ask the owner a short clarification or approval through the pendant.
proposals.latency_budget: No added latency for actions that match a cached local policy (milliseconds). An exception should produce a pendant prompt within a few seconds; background policy compilation can take seconds to minutes.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per action after compilation: deterministic local checks dominate, with an inexpensive model call only when a new rule or ambiguous exception needs interpretation. Realtime cost is limited to exception conversations.
proposals.security_concerns: Policies can grant meaningful autonomy, so scope them by project, surface, data class, action type, amount, and expiry; never infer permission from silence. Private browser data should remain on the Mac bridge except for minimized evidence. Every automatic action needs a human-readable reason and an immediate pause/revoke control from the pendant or dashboard.
missing: A versioned policy language with explicit allow/deny/escalate predicates and conservative defaults
A policy compiler that turns owner rules into deterministic checks and tests them against proposed action bundles
Enforcement hooks shared by Mac, browser, relay jobs, and pendant prompts
A durable policy version/decision record attached to each action receipt
A fast owner-facing pause and revoke channel that works while a delegated job is running

proposals.user_asks: “Do it, and tell me only when you can prove it happened.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can decide an action and a hand can queue it, but completion is often inferred from the executor's acknowledgement. This gives the owner a genuinely closed loop: the pendant captures the intent, judgement chooses Mac/browser, faculty-action performs it, faculty-perception re-reads the resulting state, and the always-on relay retries and speaks a short proof or a precise failure. It is especially useful for reminders, edits, and browser workflows where 'queued' is not the same as 'done'.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only for the spoken intent and final concise result; use a cheaper background worker for retries, polling, and evidence normalization. faculty-judgement plans the operation; faculty-action executes; faculty-perception verifies against a declared postcondition.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate reversible actions should return an acknowledgement in 1–2 seconds, then a verified result within 10 seconds. Long browser or offline jobs may take minutes, with one spoken completion/failure notification and no repeated chatter.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per completed workflow depending on verification reads and model use; most retries and field comparison should be deterministic, with model calls only for ambiguous page changes.
