Mac Accessibility/Screen Recording permissions
live authenticated browser extension bridge

changes.change: Add an Action Lease Coordinator between judgement and all execution surfaces. Persist a lease record keyed by jobId/actionHash with owner approval timestamp, exact action scope, target surface/session, expiry (default 10 minutes), one-use nonce, risk class, and state (issued/claimed/running/committed/succeeded/failed/expired/revoked). Require Mac and browser workers to claim with a readiness attestation; reject claims when the bridge is offline or Mac permissions are not ready. Stream state transitions to the pendant and dashboard, and make every transition idempotent.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: An action they approved will either finish predictably or stop safely with a clear reason instead of timing out after 45 seconds, sitting in a stale browser queue, or being retried after circumstances changed.
changes.effort: Medium: D1 schema/API and relay tests; adapters in local-agent job runner and browser bridge; pendant notification messages; dashboard timeline. Add fault-injection tests for disconnects, duplicate claims, expired leases, and commit/retry races.
changes.risk: A too-short lease could interrupt a legitimate long task; use progress heartbeats without extending the absolute deadline. A lost completion packet could make the pendant say 'unknown'; receipts remain queryable and the relay replays terminal state. Never treat a worker heartbeat as owner reapproval.
changes.cost_impact: No recurring model cost; a few D1 writes per action and tiny telemetry payloads. Optional background summarization remains bounded.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one deterministic claim/preflight round (typically <200 ms locally, <1 s relay round trip) but avoids long doomed execution attempts.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by binding execution to the approved action hash, target session, nonce, and deadline; lease records must avoid storing secrets and support owner revocation.
depends_on: Structured readiness endpoint from Mac agent (Accessibility, Screen Recording, browser bridge polling, and target session)
Shared action/receipt schema across Mac, browser, relay, and pendant
Pendant firmware notification and offline approval event support

changes.change: Introduce a resumable Human-in-the-loop Checkpoint protocol spanning local-agent jobs, browser sessions, relay, and pendant. A worker can emit a checkpoint containing a stable job/action hash, bounded question, typed choices or a redacted input schema, evidence capsule, continuation token, deadline, and safe rollback point. Relay persists and delivers it; pendant returns a nonce-bound response; the worker resumes only if the checkpoint hash and target session still match. Add crash recovery, duplicate-response handling, expiry, cancellation, and a dashboard timeline.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can leave the Mac during a difficult task and answer only the one decision that genuinely requires them, rather than babysitting the screen or restarting the entire workflow after a harmless ambiguity.
changes.effort: High: define a serializable continuation contract for shell, GUI, and browser steps; implement relay storage and pendant transport; add resume adapters and fault-injection tests for worker/relay/device disconnects.
changes.risk: Some actions cannot safely resume after a crash; those checkpoints must be marked non-resumable and restart from a verified boundary. A malformed or stale response must fail closed. Never expose raw passwords or page contents in a prompt unless explicitly classified and encrypted.
changes.cost_impact: No recurring cost while waiting; one compact background-model call per checkpoint to phrase choices, plus small durable storage. Reusing evidence capsules avoids resending full context.
changes.latency_impact: Adds sub-second deterministic checkpoint persistence and response validation; resumption depends on the worker's next preflight, typically a few seconds.
changes.security_impact: Responses are scoped to a checkpoint nonce, action hash, target browser session, and expiry. The relay stores redacted prompt metadata and encrypted sensitive input only when required; every pause, response, and resume is auditable.
depends_on: A common typed job/evidence schema shared by Mac and browser workers
Pendant transport supporting push notifications and compact response events
Relay durable state and replay of pending checkpoints
Worker-specific safe-boundary and continuation adapters

changes.change: Add a cross-surface execution-readiness handshake and lease. Before any approved action, the relay asks Mac agent for a signed preflight containing Accessibility/Screen Recording readiness, browser-heartbeat freshness, target tab/session affinity, and current queue capacity. If a required surface is unavailable, persist the approved intent as a paused job with an expiry and cancellation token; the relay retries on heartbeat recovery, while the pendant announces 'waiting for browser' and a long-press cancels. Emit one terminal receipt with preflight failures, retry timestamps, and the exact action outcome—never a client-side timeout masquerading as failure.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A spoken request will either complete across the Mac and private browser or clearly wait and recover when the missing surface comes back. The owner no longer has to guess whether an action happened, repeat it after a timeout, or discover stale browser commands later; they can cancel from the pendant.
changes.effort: Medium: shared preflight schema and signed lease in relay/Mac agent, heartbeat-triggered retry worker, pending-job UI/status, pendant notification/cancel mapping, and failure-injection tests for permissions/browser dropouts.
changes.risk: A paused approved action could execute later than expected; enforce short leases, action-class expiry, idempotency keys, and require reconfirmation for destructive actions after any suspension. Recover by cancellation and receipt audit; never auto-retry send/delete/purchase classes.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing API cost: deterministic checks and retry orchestration; only invoke a model for ambiguous recovery messaging. Small D1/JSON state growth per pending job and heartbeat.
changes.latency_impact: Adds sub-second preflight when healthy; unavailable surfaces return immediately as paused instead of waiting ~45s for a browser timeout. Recovery latency is heartbeat cadence plus action execution.
changes.security_impact: Signed, scoped leases prevent replay and bind intent to a specific Mac/browser session; receipts must avoid page secrets. Requires explicit owner policy for which reversible classes may resume automatically.
depends_on: Enable Accessibility and Screen Recording for AI Pendant Agent
Bring Browser Bridge extension online and polling
Durable job runner and receipt/undo storage

changes.change: Add a durable deferred-action envelope and reconnect executor spanning pendant→relay→Mac/browser. Envelope fields: jobId, idempotencyKey, origin, typed steps, required capabilities, confirmation class, lease/deadline, dependency IDs, redacted target fingerprint, and status. Relay claims exactly once, Mac bridge heartbeats capability readiness, local agent executes only when prerequisites are true, and each step emits proof-of-effect or an explicit unverifiable result. Reconnect drains in dependency order; expired or capability-blocked jobs remain visible rather than being silently retried.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A request made while wearing the pendant no longer disappears when LTE drops, the Mac sleeps, or Safari is unavailable—and the owner hears the difference between completed, skipped, and merely attempted.
changes.effort: Medium-high: relay D1 schema/worker, local-agent queue and typed proof adapters, pendant compact spool protocol, dashboard state UI, and end-to-end fault-injection tests for duplicate delivery and sleep/reconnect.
changes.risk: A retry could duplicate a side effect; prevent this with idempotency keys, per-step leases, and no automatic execution of confirmation-class actions. If proof fails, stop and report unverified. Recover by exposing cancel/undo where supported and retaining receipts.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible relay storage/compute; background planner calls only for ambiguous plans. Optional vision verification adds screenshot/model cost per difficult step.
changes.latency_impact: No impact on live conversation; offline capture is immediate. Reconnect adds queue polling (target <30 s) and proof latency (typically <10 s).
changes.security_impact: Encrypted paired-device transport, least-privilege capability claims, redacted targets, short retention for proof artifacts, and confirmation gates for send/delete/purchase.
depends_on: durable browser runner and authenticated session reattachment
Mac bridge heartbeat exposing readiness/permission state
typed action receipts plus proof adapters
pendant offline envelope storage

changes.change: Implement a cross-surface Action Lease + Attestation protocol. Relay creates a nonce-bound lease containing plan hash, target surface/session, allowed effect class, expiry, and approval transcript hash. Before every write, Mac/browser return signed (or HMAC-authenticated) preflight evidence: online heartbeat, entitlement state, target identity, and expected-state digest. Executor refuses on stale/mismatched evidence. After execution, faculty-perception submits independent postcondition evidence; receipts become succeeded, refused, or unknown rather than treating dispatch as success. Pendant announces the exact reason and offers retry only after readiness changes.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can safely say “do it” while walking away and trust that the system either changed the intended thing or clearly said it could not. It prevents today's known failure mode where GUI actions are dispatched while Accessibility/Screen Recording are off and the browser is offline.
changes.effort: Medium-high: protocol schema and durable lease store, relay propagation, browser heartbeat/result changes, Mac preflight adapters, verifier library, dashboard states, and integration tests for stale leases, wrong tabs, offline devices, and ambiguous outcomes.
changes.risk: A false negative may refuse a legitimate action, which is recoverable by refreshing readiness and asking again. A false positive is more serious; mitigate with nonce binding, short TTLs, target hashes, independent read-back, and default unknown on missing proof. Roll out read-only/preflight telemetry first, then reversible writes, then irreversible actions behind explicit confirmation.
changes.cost_impact: Small storage/compute overhead; deterministic checks dominate. Background reconciliation is cheap; no extra realtime model call beyond the owner's approval.
changes.latency_impact: Adds ~100–500 ms for preflight and ~1–3 s for postcondition read-back, preferable to silent incorrect execution.
changes.security_impact: Improves least privilege and replay resistance. Do not store raw approval audio or secrets; store transcript hash, lease metadata, and redacted evidence. HMAC keys must remain device-specific and rotate.
depends_on: Fresh readiness/entitlement state from faculty-perception
A relay-visible durable lease/approval record
Browser bridge heartbeat and typed result support
Mac action receipts (already implemented, but currently lack gates/preconditions)

changes.change: Add a low-power coin vibration motor (or piezo haptic actuator) with a dedicated GPIO driver and a simple three-pattern status vocabulary: short pulse = lease accepted, double pulse = blocked/refused, long pulse = verified completion. Keep the existing LED/audio semantics, expose patterns as a tiny device command so relay can push them even when audio is unavailable. Add a physical silent-mode toggle or firmware setting, rate limits, and watchdog-safe driver behavior.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can know whether a remote action was accepted, blocked, or truly completed without looking at a screen or opening the microphone. That is especially valuable while the Mac/browser is offline or GUI entitlements are missing: the pendant gives an unmistakable refusal instead of leaving them guessing.
changes.effort: Low-medium hardware revision and firmware work: actuator, transistor/driver if needed, GPIO allocation, sealed enclosure test, and three short patterns. Validate comfort and accidental activation in daily wear; simulator can test event sequencing before hardware.
changes.risk: Vibration may disturb or drain the battery, or be mistaken for a notification. Make silent mode explicit, cap duty cycle, never use haptics for safety-critical claims without the server receipt, and fall back to LED/audio. Prototype board has provisional I/O, so confirm pin budget and power rail before layout.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $0.20–$2 actuator plus <$1 driver/passives per unit; tens of milliwatts only during brief pulses, near-zero idle. No model/API cost.
changes.latency_impact: Local acknowledgement can be under 100 ms after relay command; completion pulse waits for verified postcondition.
changes.security_impact: Haptic patterns must never imply success before cryptographically or otherwise authenticated receipt; commands need the same device/session binding as action leases. Silent mode state should not leak sensitive task content.
depends_on: Cross-surface Action Lease/Attestation protocol
Pendant firmware command channel and local event queue
Power-rail and enclosure validation for the eventual wearable design

changes.change: Add a fail-closed action reachability adapter shared by mac_run_actions, mac-vision, and browser routing. Before any UI action, verify the running host binary (bundle identity/path) is Accessibility-trusted and the browser bridge has a live heartbeat; if not, mark the step blocked rather than successful. After each reversible UI step, require an independent postcondition observation (frontmost app/title, file/reminder existence, or browser result) and classify outcomes as applied, blocked, or unknown. Persist the reason and a concrete recovery instruction in the receipt, and prevent dependent steps from running after blocked/unknown.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner currently receives success-shaped receipts for clicks and typing that did nothing, and browser jobs can spend 45 seconds before discovering the extension is offline. This makes actions trustworthy: either the requested change happened and is evidenced, or the owner gets an honest, immediately actionable failure.
changes.effort: Medium: central adapter plus adapters for common action types, tests against the current untrusted Accessibility state and offline browser state.
changes.risk: Some legitimate actions may be reported unknown and stop earlier until a postcondition observer exists; recover by allowing explicit retry or a manually confirmed override. No action should be silently repeated.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; small local observation overhead per step.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms per UI step; saves tens of seconds on offline-browser failures.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by failing closed and avoiding duplicate retries; does not broaden permissions or exfiltrate screen data.
depends_on: A correct Accessibility grant for the actual AI Pendant Agent binary
Browser bridge heartbeat/polling in the selected browser
Typed postcondition observers for each action family

changes.change: Make the uplink genuinely 24 kHz end to end: configure the I2S microphone/clock and DMA for 24,000 Hz capture, encode Opus at 24 kHz (or perform a documented high-quality 15.625→24 kHz resample before encoding), and carry the sample-rate contract through relay transcoding, pipeline telemetry, and Mac STT. Add a loopback/impulse and speech fixture that verifies timestamps, frame duration, no drift, and intelligibility over a 10-minute LTE-M run.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The current path advertises 24 kHz playback but captures at 15,625 Hz and uplinks Opus at 16 kHz, so the owner cannot actually use a superwideband voice path. Correcting the contract should make spoken commands clearer and reduce resampling artifacts.
changes.effort: High: clock/DMA and Opus changes, relay format negotiation, memory/performance profiling, and hardware validation on the current DK before choosing production audio hardware.
changes.risk: The nRF9160 prototype has only 211,608 B application RAM and audio already consumes roughly 87% of one core when encode and decode overlap; overruns or battery/radio cost may rise. Recover with 20/16 kHz negotiated fallback, bounded jitter buffering, and explicit telemetry rather than silently downsampling.
changes.cost_impact: No per-request API increase; possible production BOM increase for a 24 kHz-capable mic/clock and modest higher LTE payload. Prototype power draw may increase during simultaneous encode/decode.
changes.latency_impact: Target unchanged 60 ms frames; initial firmware profiling may add buffering while tuning DMA and Opus complexity.
changes.security_impact: No new data class; higher-fidelity audio increases sensitivity, so retain short-lived buffers and expose negotiated sample rate in receipts.
depends_on: A 24 kHz-capable microphone and stable I2S clock on the product design
Relay and Mac pipeline sample-rate negotiation
Acceptance tests for 24 kHz audio quality and CPU/RAM headroom

changes.change: Build a 24 kHz duplex audio conformance harness spanning all four bodies: inject deterministic swept-tone and speech fixtures at the pendant I2S/UART test point, tag every Opus frame with a monotonic sample counter, collect relay packet/jitter telemetry, capture the Mac/ESP32 output, and compare end-to-end sample rate, drift, loss concealment, latency, and spectral error. Emit a signed receipt with per-stage timestamps and automatically quarantine/revert the last audio firmware or relay codec change when thresholds fail; keep raw audio local and upload only hashes/metrics.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets speech that stays intelligible and in sync after real reconnects, instead of discovering a broken 24 kHz path during a conversation. A concise pass/fail receipt makes “audio is fixed” trustworthy and catches regressions across the pendant, network relay, and headphone bridge—not just in one node.
changes.effort: Medium-high: firmware test instrumentation and sample counters, relay telemetry schema, Mac/ESP32 capture adapter, golden fixtures, CI/nightly runner, and rollback integration. Requires a safe UART/J-Link test mode and a small hardware loopback fixture.
changes.risk: Test mode must be impossible to enter from normal button presses and must never transmit fixture audio as owner speech. Clock-counter bugs could falsely fail builds; gate rollout on a known-good baseline and retain the previous codec config for one-click rollback. No raw owner audio leaves the Mac; fixtures and aggregate metrics only.
changes.cost_impact: Low recurring API cost (local DSP and deterministic fixtures; occasional cheap background analysis). Rough hardware fixture cost $20–50, negligible power outside tests.
changes.latency_impact: No production latency when instrumentation is disabled; frame counters add 4–8 bytes per packet and telemetry is sampled asynchronously.
changes.security_impact: Counters and hashes are non-sensitive, but UART logs can contain transcripts; redact payloads before storage and require local pairing/authentication for test control.
depends_on: 24 kHz codec path implementation and explicit acceptance thresholds
durable pipeline telemetry at pendant, relay, and Mac/bridge
a safe firmware test-mode trigger and rollback-capable deployment

changes.change: For the product pendant, add a low-power haptic actuator and a fuel-gauge IC with an interrupt line, while retaining the single button and LED. Expose signed battery and haptic-event state to the relay so a pending Mac/browser action can be acknowledged, rejected, or timed out without relying on an ambiguous LED-only signal.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can approve or cancel an action confidently while walking, in a pocket, or in bright sunlight, and can be warned before a conversation dies from an empty battery. This makes the wearable a dependable hand for the Mac rather than a remote microphone with an unreliable visual indicator.
changes.effort: Moderate hardware revision, enclosure/acoustic redesign, driver and power-management work, haptic patterns, battery calibration, and relay protocol integration. Prototype on the current dev kit with an external actuator and gauge before committing a board spin.
changes.risk: Haptics could be distracting or drain the battery; provide quiet hours, intensity limits, and LED fallback. Incorrect fuel-gauge calibration could report false charge, so retain voltage-based fallback and calibration diagnostics. Never treat a haptic event as approval without a button edge and nonce match.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $2–6 in added components and PCB area at prototype volume, plus roughly 5–20 mA only during short haptic pulses and under 100 µA for the gauge. No meaningful API cost.
changes.latency_impact: A local approval acknowledgement can be immediate; the gauge interrupt adds no conversation-path latency.
changes.security_impact: Battery state is low sensitivity. Approval events must remain authenticated and nonce-bound; actuator patterns must not encode secrets or serve as the sole authorization signal.
depends_on: The relay-mediated approval protocol and short-lived action lease
A product-board revision beyond the current nRF9160 development kit
Firmware power and GPIO budget review

changes.change: Introduce a cross-surface ActionIntent/ActionReceipt protocol and executor coordinator. An intent contains an immutable canonical payload hash, target surface, permitted effect class, idempotency key, deadline, and machine-checkable postcondition. The relay owns a durable state machine (queued→leased→attempted→applied→verified or uncertain), renews leases, and emits compact progress events. Mac and browser adapters must return typed accepted/applied evidence plus a verification query; the coordinator retries only steps marked idempotent and never silently replays an unknown irreversible step. Keep a redacted receipt/evidence manifest for the owner and allow cancellation/retry of safe steps.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets one reliable answer to “did it happen?” even when the Mac sleeps, Safari is private, or the network drops. It prevents duplicate submissions and makes failures recoverable instead of requiring the owner to inspect several logs or guess whether a click took effect.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and migrations, relay worker/state machine, Mac/browser adapter changes, postcondition verifier hooks, pendant event mapping, and fault-injection tests for disconnects and duplicate delivery.
changes.risk: A verifier may read stale UI or misclassify a legitimate result; show verified versus uncertain explicitly and retain evidence. A crash between remote commit and receipt can still be ambiguous, so irreversible actions need endpoint-specific idempotency or a human-readable reconciliation path. Recover by querying the authoritative page/API before retrying.
changes.cost_impact: Small durable storage and polling overhead; background model calls only for ambiguous reconciliation. No new per-action realtime generation beyond short status utterances.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one authoritative verification read, typically 1–5 seconds, but makes long actions resumable and avoids unsafe blind retries.
changes.security_impact: Payload hashes and scoped capability tokens reduce confused-deputy risk. Redact page content and secrets from receipts; bind browser steps to the intended session/tab and reject scope changes.
depends_on: A typed browser result contract with tab/session affinity
Durable relay jobs with resumable polling
A Mac executor result schema and authoritative postcondition reads
A pendant progress/cancel event protocol

changes.change: Add a cross-surface execution coordinator backed by D1: an immutable action_graph (graphId, approvalReceipt, parentId, intentHash, policyVersion), action_step rows with unique (graphId, stepKey), leaseOwner/leaseExpiry, preconditionHash, state, attempt, and typed receipt; expose claim/renew/complete/fail/reconcile endpoints. Executors must atomically claim a step, reject duplicate keys, and on reconnect reconcile leases before accepting new work. Emit one ordered event stream consumed by pendant and dashboard.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A single approval would survive LTE drops, Mac sleep, and browser reconnects without repeating a reminder, purchase, message, or other side effect; the owner can see precisely what happened and resume only the safe remainder.
changes.effort: Medium-high: D1 schema/API plus relay tests, then adapter changes in Mac bridge and browser extension; staged read-only reconciliation first, mutations behind feature flag.
changes.risk: A lease timeout can falsely look abandoned while an executor is still acting, or a receipt can be lost after the side effect. Use idempotency keys at every adapter, short transactional claim windows, explicit unknown outcome state, and require judgement confirmation before retrying unknown irreversible steps. Roll back by disabling coordinator and treating existing jobs as legacy.
changes.cost_impact: Low edge/D1 cost (a few rows/events per step); no extra model call during execution. Dashboard and receipt storage increase modestly with retention TTL.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-500 ms claim/ack on relay; each device action remains bounded by its local executor. Reconnect reconciliation adds up to ~5 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Approval receipt and policy version are cryptographically bound to the graph; stale or altered plans are rejected. Browser auth stays local; receipts redact values and expire evidence.
depends_on: ActionIntent/receipt schema must be standardized across existing Mac and browser action paths
Mac bridge and browser extension must accept and persist idempotency keys
Judgement must expose preconditions and irreversible-step policy
Pendant needs a compact state/confirmation display

changes.change: Add a hard-priority delegation-stop event to the pendant firmware: a long press (distinct from conversation press) sets a local stop latch, gives immediate red/amber LED feedback, sends a tiny authenticated cancel frame when LTE is available, and persists the stop generation counter on microSD so a reconnect cannot resume an older delegated objective. The relay must treat that generation as authoritative until the owner explicitly clears it with a deliberate two-press gesture or spoken confirmation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a trustworthy physical kill switch for an agent that is acting across the Mac and logged-in browser, including when speech recognition fails or the Mac is busy. They can stop future actions immediately and know that reconnecting will not silently restart the task.
changes.effort: Medium: firmware button state machine and persisted counter, relay cancel-generation handling, and executor cancellation tests. Do not flash until bench-tested against the simulator and a disconnected/reconnected modem.
changes.risk: False long presses could pause a task; use a hold threshold and unmistakable LED/audio acknowledgement. A stop frame can be delayed by LTE half-duplex, so the relay also needs the persisted generation and executors need short leases. Recovery is explicit owner clearance; no automatic resume.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost. Firmware storage is a few bytes; no new hardware required. LTE stop packets are tiny. Battery impact is negligible except during transmission.
changes.latency_impact: Local stop feedback is immediate; relay propagation depends on LTE, targeted under 2 seconds when connected. Pending steps stop at the next lease boundary.
changes.security_impact: Authenticate and monotonically validate the stop generation to prevent replay or forged cancellation. Persist only the counter and task identifier hash, never task content or credentials.
depends_on: Relay-resident long-lived objective supervisor and cancellation protocol
Mac and browser executors honoring cancellation at step boundaries
A clearly specified owner confirmation gesture for clearing the stop latch

changes.change: Add a Proof-Carrying Action protocol shared by relay, Mac/browser harnesses, and faculty-perception. Every executable action is serialized as {actionId, idempotencyKey, targetSurface, precondition, effect, postcondition predicate, verification recipe, settleMs, expiry}. Executors return dispatch evidence only. A separate verifier performs the recipe after settle and appends a signed ProofRecord {actionId, observedAt, predicate, result: confirmed|failed|unknown, source, locator/tab/session or file/pipeline reference, evidenceHash}. Relay state transitions are queued→leased→dispatched→verifying→confirmed/failed/unknown, with duplicate dispatch coalesced and stale proofs rejected. Expose GET /jobs/:id/proof and a compact pendant result packet.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an honest answer about whether something changed in the world, not merely whether our software ran. This is especially useful for reminders, browser form fills, volume/app changes, and queued work after the Mac wakes; it prevents silent false success.
changes.effort: Medium: typed schema and D1/job state migration, verifier adapters for Mac and browser, relay result packet, and a fault-injection test matrix.
changes.risk: A verifier may observe stale UI or the wrong tab and falsely pass; bind evidence to session/tab identity, freshness, and content hash, and return unknown on ambiguity. Verification can time out after a real-world success, so retain evidence and offer a reconcile action rather than retrying blindly.
changes.cost_impact: Low relay storage/compute; approximately one extra model call only for ambiguous semantic predicates. Browser screenshots or vision dominate optional cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds a settle-and-probe delay: typically 1–3 seconds for local state and 3–10 seconds for browser state.
changes.security_impact: Reduces data exposure by transmitting typed predicates/evidence hashes instead of private page contents. Proof records may still reveal sensitive facts, so encrypt at rest and apply short retention.
depends_on: A typed action/postcondition contract
Independent Mac accessibility/file probes and authenticated browser DOM/session probes
Durable idempotent job runner and result correlation
Owner confirmation gate for irreversible actions

changes.change: Create an egress-closed Private Data Projection channel. The Mac/browser bridge sends relay requests only through a local policy broker that validates a versioned schema, strips raw DOM/file bodies and credentials, replaces permitted values with typed claims plus keyed hashes, and signs the exact field list. The relay rejects unsigned or out-of-schema payloads. Add an append-only local release ledger with source origin, field names, sensitivity class, recipient, and expiry; retries reuse the same release ID and cannot widen the payload.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can ask the whole hive to work across private accounts and local documents without having to trust that a model prompt remembered not to leak their data. They get useful answers while secrets remain on the Mac, and can inspect what was released afterward.
changes.effort: High: local broker integrated into both browser and Mac harnesses, schema/redaction library, relay rejection path, signed release ledger, and adversarial retry/failure tests.
changes.risk: Over-redaction may make tasks less useful; return a clear blocked-field explanation and let the owner explicitly authorize a narrowly scoped excerpt. A compromised local agent could still misuse its own access, so keep the broker separate from the planner and require OS keychain-backed signing.
changes.cost_impact: Low relay cost; modest local CPU and disk for classification, hashing, and ledger writes. No extra model call for deterministic fields; semantic extraction may add one local/background call.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms for policy and signing, plus local extraction time for complex pages/files.
changes.security_impact: Strongly reduces private-data egress and makes release auditable. It does not protect data already displayed on the Mac or defend against a compromised OS; those limits must be explicit.
depends_on: Browser and Mac bridges exposing source-origin metadata
A versioned sensitivity taxonomy and allowed claim schemas
Relay request authentication and durable request IDs
Owner-facing release-ledger viewer

changes.change: Add a cross-surface action contract and verifier. Every planned Mac/browser step carries risk class, lease ID, preconditions, typed expected postconditions, observation recipe, timeout, and undo strategy. The executor must re-observe after each mutating step, compare typed fields (not screenshots alone), append before/after evidence to the receipt, and halt with an explicit mismatch state. Relay, Mac bridge, and browser bridge share the same lease and cancellation token so a stale or revoked plan cannot continue.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask the mind to make real changes without silently drifting when a page, focused app, or UI state changes. They get an honest answer—completed, safely stopped, or uncertain—with evidence and a recovery path instead of a misleading success chime.
changes.effort: Medium-high: define contract/versioning, implement Mac and browser adapters, add observation recipes and mismatch states, then integration-test crashes, retries, stale tabs, and dropped pendant links.
changes.risk: A strict verifier will stop some actions that would have worked; recover by exposing the mismatch evidence and allowing a fresh re-plan. Never auto-retry an irreversible step after an ambiguous result. Existing legacy actions need an explicit unverified compatibility mode.
changes.cost_impact: Small per-step storage and observation overhead; background validation can use a cheap model, while deterministic field comparison avoids inference cost. No new hardware required.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms per step for observation; much less than recovering from a silent bad action.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety: leases, replay protection, scoped cancellation, and provenance. Screenshots/DOM snippets should be redacted and retained only under the existing short evidence TTL.
depends_on: Mac Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions being correctly granted to the running binary
Browser bridge online with request IDs and tab/session affinity
Durable job receipts and undo endpoints
A pendant-originated cancellation/revocation event

changes.change: Create a relay-owned exactly-once intent ledger spanning voice turns, Mac jobs, browser commands, and reconnects. Normalize each approved intent into a canonical target/action hash, issue one transaction ID and lease, and require every surface to carry it. Retries return the existing receipt; only a verified commit advances the ledger, while ambiguous external outcomes enter reconciliation instead of being replayed. Expiry and explicit target changes create a new transaction.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can repeat themselves or lose connectivity without wondering whether a message was sent twice, a form submitted twice, or a reminder duplicated. They receive one durable outcome tied to one request.
changes.effort: Medium: relay schema/state machine, adapters in Mac and browser executors, commit/reconciliation protocol, and failure-injection tests across dropped links and process restarts.
changes.risk: Over-aggressive normalization could merge two actions the owner intended separately. Mitigate with short intent windows, target/account scoping, and a spoken confirmation when confidence is below threshold. Unknown external outcomes must remain visibly unresolved.
changes.cost_impact: Tiny D1/storage and hashing overhead; no new model call for ordinary requests.
changes.latency_impact: One durable ledger round trip, typically tens to hundreds of milliseconds; retries become faster because they return the prior receipt.
changes.security_impact: Reduces duplicate side effects but makes the relay authoritative for transaction metadata. Encrypt sensitive target identifiers, scope keys per paired owner, and enforce retention/erasure.
depends_on: A shared transaction ID accepted by Mac and browser action APIs
Durable relay storage and authenticated pairing
Typed external postcondition/commit reporting from each executor

changes.change: Add a shared approval-intent envelope and atomic commit gate between faculty-judgement, Mac planner, browser bridge, and relay. On preview, each executor emits a canonical action manifest (surface, account identity, tab/session, URL, action type, field-level normalized values, DOM/source hashes, and expiry). The pendant confirmation signs/references the manifest nonce. Immediately before execution, the same executor reacquires the live state and compares the manifest; only an exact match can enter the existing execute/browser command queue. On mismatch, cancel the queued command, emit a typed stale-approval event with changed fields and a fresh preview, and make retries idempotent. Persist the manifest and final comparison in the existing job receipt/journal so undo and audit refer to the exact approved state.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: An approval will mean what the owner actually saw, not merely “yes to the last description.” A changed price, recipient, appointment, account, or page cannot silently receive an old approval; the pendant tells them precisely what changed and asks again.
changes.effort: Medium: shared schema and canonicalization library, adapters in planner and browser bridge, atomic gate in the durable job runner, pendant event rendering, and end-to-end race tests (refresh, navigation, account switch, duplicate delivery, reconnect).
changes.risk: Overly strict canonicalization may reject harmless dynamic fields and annoy the owner; field policies need volatile-field exclusions and a clear diff. If the bridge dies after approval, the action stays pending and expires rather than executing blindly. Recovery is a fresh preview/approval; existing cancel/undo handles actions that already committed.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage (manifest and hashes per job) and CPU; no extra model call for exact fields. Optional semantic normalization costs <$0.01 and should not be used for critical equality.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one live read/hash pass, typically 100–500 ms locally and up to 1–2 s for a browser round trip; mismatch path is slower because it requires a new preview.
changes.security_impact: Improves authorization by binding approval to account/tab/state and short-lived nonce. Keep raw sensitive values local; receipts store hashes plus redacted diffs. Prevent replay with nonce, expiry, and idempotency key.
depends_on: Durable browser job runner and command queue must expose a pre-commit hook (chg-16bc5dee, chg-14accc01 backlog).
Existing receipt/undo path must accept the manifest and comparison result (chg-5fc73ce3).
Pendant confirmation event and action-lease indicator need to be available (previously requested device skills).

changes.change: Create a read-only counterfactual impact layer between perception and action. It accepts a normalized proposed action plus source evidence, clones only the affected typed entities/relations into an ephemeral sandbox, runs deterministic dependency queries against Mac calendar/tasks/files and authenticated browser state, and returns confirmed/inferred/unknown consequences with provenance. The sandbox must be discarded after the report and be unable to call execution routes. Add adapters for browser form fields, calendar events, subscriptions, tasks, and local project metadata, with sensitivity-aware redaction before results reach relay or judgement.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can make informed decisions about changes that ripple beyond the page currently visible—without trusting a vague warning and without risking an accidental commit. They see conflicts and follow-up work before approving anything.
changes.effort: Medium-high: typed action schema, ephemeral graph fork, dependency rules, browser/Mac adapters, provenance and redaction, plus a hard read-only boundary and adversarial tests proving no execution side effect.
changes.risk: Dependency inference can be incomplete or over-alert. Every result must distinguish confirmed from inferred and unknown, show sources, and allow the owner to proceed only with explicit acknowledgement. Sensitive unrelated entities could leak unless graph traversal is scoped to action-relevant identities and time windows.
changes.cost_impact: Small temporary graph storage and local computation; approximately $0.01–$0.05 for explanation when a background model is needed. Raw browser content should not leave the browser/Mac surfaces.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 3–8 seconds for a normal action and up to 20 seconds for multi-source analysis; stream progress through the existing pipeline so the pendant does not appear stuck.
changes.security_impact: Strengthens safety by making the analysis sandbox technically incapable of committing actions. Provenance, sensitivity labels, and redaction reduce cross-surface data exposure. The sandbox must use separate credentials or no credentials for execution routes.
depends_on: A typed action manifest shared by browser and Mac surfaces.
Scoped context-graph queries with provenance, TTL, and sensitivity filtering.
Read-only adapters for authenticated browser state and Mac calendar/tasks/files.
A separate non-executable planning path; do not reuse POST /execute as a side effect of analysis.

changes.change: Add a cross-surface Action Checkpoint Protocol shared by relay, Mac agent, and browser bridge. Each step emits an append-only record {jobId, stepId, surface, idempotencyKey, preconditionHash, evidenceRef, outcome, committedAt}; the relay owns a durable state machine and leases, Mac/browser heartbeats renew leases, and reconnecting workers ask for the next uncommitted step. Resume logic must classify outcomes as committed, safely retryable, or unknown; unknown steps pause rather than repeat. Expose checkpoint progress and a resume/cancel control through the existing jobs, journal, browser poll/result, and pipeline event routes.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped connection or sleeping Mac would no longer leave the owner guessing whether a form was filled, a file was moved, or a reversible step needs repeating. Work would continue safely and the spoken receipt would distinguish completed, skipped, and owner-required steps.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and durable relay state machine, adapters in local-agent executor and browserBridge, reconnect tests across process restart, and dashboard/pendant receipt plumbing.
changes.risk: A false committed classification could skip needed work; a false retry could duplicate a side effect. Default unknown to pause, require evidence hashes for commit, and retain cancel/undo. Recover by replaying the append-only log and expiring leases.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and inference cost; roughly a few hundred bytes per step plus existing job/receipt writes. Background model only for human-readable receipts.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one local checkpoint write per step (typically <50 ms); reconnect resume begins on heartbeat, target under 10 s.
changes.security_impact: Metadata-only records with redacted evidence references; private page content remains on Mac. Encrypt relay state, scope leases to job and surface, and avoid persisting credentials or raw form values.
depends_on: Durable browser job runner and non-blocking progress polling (chg-16bc5dee / chg-14accc01 gaps)
Existing /jobs, /journal, browser poll/result, and pipeline event plumbing
A relay heartbeat/wake path to notify the Mac agent when a queued job can resume

changes.change: Introduce revisioned live-plan splicing across relay and local-agent workers. Add a job revision and optimistic compare-and-swap endpoint/state: the relay marks a running job paused, accepts a typed delta (skip, replace target, change account, reorder), asks perception for affected-state evidence, and commits a new plan revision only if the worker’s last-seen revision still matches. Workers must reject superseded revisions before every side effect and emit a plan-diff receipt. Deliver pendant interrupt events through the live pipeline rather than waiting for the next voice turn.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can correct an active task naturally instead of cancelling and restarting it. The system will change only future work, preserve completed progress, and prevent an old worker from acting on the plan the owner just replaced.
changes.effort: High: relay state-machine and event protocol, local-agent executor guards, browser command cancellation/renewal, planner delta generation, and dashboard/pendant controls; requires fault-injection tests for races and reconnects.
changes.risk: A pause race could allow one extra side effect or a malformed delta could target the wrong account. Enforce revision checks immediately before dispatch, pause at the next safe boundary, require affected-state evidence, and fail closed on ambiguity. Recover with existing receipts and undo where available.
changes.cost_impact: Small persistent metadata and event overhead; one inexpensive planning/verification call per correction, with no ongoing realtime inference after acknowledgment.
changes.latency_impact: Pause signal target under 2 seconds; revision validation adds tens of milliseconds per step; replanning target under 5 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Job-scoped signed interrupt tokens, no raw private page data in relay events, account identity included in the diff, and existing irreversible-action confirmation remains mandatory.
depends_on: A durable job state machine with worker leases
Typed plan-diff and affected-state evidence schemas
Pendant interrupt transport over the live pipeline
Atomic revision checks in Mac and browser executors

changes.change: Build a durable cross-surface action saga runner. Compile a judged plan into typed steps spanning Mac, authenticated browser, and pendant; persist a per-step idempotency key, precondition fingerprint, attempt count, evidence receipt, and compensating action. Before retry/resume, faculty-perception must re-check the precondition (Accessibility/Screen Recording/input reachability, browser heartbeat/tab identity, and focused-app/UI fingerprint); a receipt is not success unless it includes typed proof. If the Mac disappears, relay keeps the saga and wakes the Mac bridge; if a step is irreversible, the pendant's one-button action lease must be explicitly armed and expires on timeout. Expose resume-from-checkpoint and safe-abort, never replay completed side effects.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A long request like “move this reservation into my calendar and prepare the confirmation” will not duplicate events or silently claim success after the laptop/browser goes offline. The owner can leave, return, and receive a concise pendant prompt only for the one consequential step, with evidence of what already happened.
changes.effort: Medium-high: durable job schema/state machine and resume endpoint in local agent/relay; idempotency adapters for Mac and browser commands; perception proof contract; pendant lease event and timeout; dashboard timeline and tests for crash/offline/reconnect races.
changes.risk: A stale fingerprint could incorrectly permit a step, or a lost receipt could cause a conservative duplicate-prevention halt. Recover by requiring proof for every side effect, treating uncertain steps as needs-review, and retaining cancel/undo where available. Never auto-resume irreversible actions without a fresh pendant lease.
changes.cost_impact: Low incremental API cost: state transitions and verification are local/relay; occasional perception model call only on resume or mismatch, not every step. Storage is small JSON/D1 metadata plus bounded evidence snippets.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.2–1.5 s for local precondition/proof checks; resume after reconnect is slower but safe. No extra latency for already verified reversible steps.
changes.security_impact: Private browser evidence remains on the Mac/paired relay; redact field values in relay state, encrypt job metadata, bind leases to pendant/session, and expire them. Cross-surface correlation IDs must not expose account secrets.
depends_on: Durable browser job runner and planner result stream (chg-16bc5dee)
Typed action receipts with real UI proof; current receipts alone are insufficient while permissions.ready=false
Pendant action-lease indicator/confirmation firmware skill
Permission remediation for Accessibility and Screen Recording before claiming Mac UI success

changes.change: Replace the prototype's single-button/single-LED interaction with a production pendant interaction module: retain the talk button, add a distinct guarded confirm/cancel button (or capacitive confirm strip), a low-power haptic motor, and a multicolor status LED driven by a tiny I2C GPIO/LED controller. Define a physical two-step affordance: short talk press is never approval; a distinct confirm press/chord arms one expiring action lease, while cancel/haptic double-pulse aborts it. Include a hardware watchdog path that can cancel an active lease even when the link is down.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can safely approve a prepared payment, message, booking, or browser submission from the pendant without touching the Mac, and can feel an unmistakable cancel/timeout signal in a pocket or noisy room. Accidental talk-button presses stop being ambiguous approval.
changes.effort: High for the prototype spin: enclosure/PCB redesign, button debounce and haptic driver, battery characterization, firmware event protocol, accessibility testing, and relay/Mac lease integration. Keep current DK firmware as a compatibility mode during bring-up.
changes.risk: More controls can confuse users or cause false confirms; use guarded geometry, long-press/chord confirmation, haptic+LED acknowledgement, and an always-available cancel. Added motor noise and power draw need testing; if the new module fails, fall back to talk-only with all consequential actions blocked.
changes.cost_impact: Rough prototype BOM increment: about $3–8 (momentary switch/capacitive pad, ERM/LRA motor, driver, RGB LED controller, enclosure changes), with short haptic events drawing tens of mA and negligible standby. Production cost depends on enclosure/assembly.
changes.latency_impact: Local confirmation feedback under 100 ms; no network round trip required to cancel. Approval still waits for relay acknowledgement before execution.
changes.security_impact: Physical approval becomes a possession factor, not sole authorization: bind each lease to job hash, display/announce a short spoken summary, expire quickly, and require server-side policy checks. Never transmit raw secrets through the pendant.
depends_on: Action-lease protocol shared by faculty-judgement, faculty-action, relay, and Mac/browser runners
Durable checkpointed saga runner with typed proof receipts
A production pendant PCB/enclosure revision; current nRF9160 DK has only one button and one LED

changes.change: Add a locality-aware private-data execution plane. Before a job crosses the Mac/relay boundary, classify each field and task segment locally; keep authenticated-page DOM, credentials, message bodies, and screenshots on the Mac/browser, run extraction/redaction there, and send the relay only a typed minimal projection (or an encrypted model request when local inference is insufficient). Return a provenance map so faculty-action can still act on the original private tab without copying its contents into shared prompts or logs. Make the policy explicit per task and fail closed when classification is uncertain.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner could ask the system to work across logged-in accounts without having private emails, financial details, or page screenshots silently become relay context. They would get the same useful recommendation or prepared action, but sensitive source material would remain on the machine that already holds the session.
changes.effort: High: field-level sensitivity classifier and redaction engine on the Mac/browser, typed projection schema, relay payload enforcement, encrypted ephemeral exceptions, provenance references, audit/redaction tests, and model-routing fallback for cases local processing cannot handle.
changes.risk: Over-redaction can make a task fail or lose necessary context; under-redaction is a privacy incident. Recover by showing which fields were withheld, requiring explicit approval for an exceptional encrypted relay request, and retaining only short-lived hashes/references. Never allow raw browser DOM or screenshots into generic logs.
changes.cost_impact: Slightly higher local CPU and storage; lower relay token cost because prompts contain projections rather than full pages. A small classifier can run locally; expensive inference is reserved for ambiguous fields.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms for local classification/redaction. Large private-page tasks may become faster because less context crosses the network.
changes.security_impact: Meaningfully reduces exposure and cross-surface context leakage, but introduces a high-value local policy boundary. Use per-job keys, memory-only sensitive buffers where possible, strict log scrubbing, and explicit provenance labels.
depends_on: A typed cross-surface task/projection schema
Local browser and Mac execution hooks that can return references instead of raw page contents
Relay enforcement that rejects unclassified sensitive payloads
Dashboard/audit display of what data stayed local versus what was transmitted

changes.change: Add a hardware-backed identity and key store to the production pendant (for example a secure element on the currently free I2C bus), with per-device keys, monotonic anti-replay counter, and tamper-aware pairing state. The pendant signs action-lease approvals, cancellation tombstones, and offline voice/event spools; the relay and Mac bridge verify signatures before accepting them. Keep private task content out of the secure element—only hashes, counters, and keys live there—and provide a physical re-pair/revoke procedure.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant becomes a trustworthy possession rather than merely an authenticated network client: an approval or emergency cancel made from the device remains attributable to that device even after a reconnect, queued offline events cannot be replayed, and replacing a lost pendant does not require trusting an old session forever.
changes.effort: Medium-high hardware/firmware/security effort: secure-element selection and PCB integration over free I2C, manufacturing provisioning, TF-M/Zephyr driver, relay and Mac verification, key rotation/revocation UX, and recovery testing.
changes.risk: Lost-device recovery or provisioning mistakes could lock the owner out; a compromised relay could still misuse a currently valid lease if policy is weak. Mitigate with short-lived signed leases, server-side job hashes and expiry, a second recovery factor, revocation records, and a factory-reset procedure that invalidates old keys.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $0.80–$2.50 component cost in volume plus provisioning/assembly work; negligible standby power and a few milliseconds per signature.
changes.latency_impact: Tens of milliseconds for local signing; no meaningful impact on ordinary conversation. Offline approval remains available and verifies on reconnect.
changes.security_impact: Improves authenticity and replay resistance substantially, while creating manufacturing-key custody obligations. Provisioning keys must never be shipped in firmware or logs; audit all key lifecycle operations.
depends_on: A production pendant PCB revision with secure-element footprint and protected provisioning flow
Signed action-lease/cancellation protocol shared by pendant, relay, Mac, and browser
Owner recovery and revocation UX
Privacy-preserving payload/projection policy so signatures cover hashes rather than sensitive content

changes.change: Add a cross-surface Action Witness Contract and saga coordinator between existing /plan→/execute→/jobs routes and the Mac/browser bridges. Each step must declare target surface, idempotency key, precondition witness requirements, effect class (reversible/irreversible), timeout, and compensation. Before dispatch, coordinator validates a fresh witness bundle: Mac /observe inputReachability=ready plus stateWitnessId, and browser heartbeat/session epoch plus tabId. It atomically leases the step, records dispatch, and transitions outcomes to succeeded, failed, blocked, or unknown. Unknown (disconnect after dispatch) is never retried automatically; it triggers read-only reconciliation against receipt/evidence, then either resumes or asks the owner. Browser commands with stale epochs are quarantined rather than consumed. Expose saga status, step evidence, and an approval/reconcile endpoint, reusing existing job receipts and undo routes.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the Mac or browser drops during a real task, the owner gets an honest paused state and a safe way to continue or undo instead of duplicate sends, phantom success, or lost work. It turns the existing action pieces into dependable hands across devices.
changes.effort: Medium-high: relay state machine + durable storage, Mac witness emission, browser epoch/quarantine changes, typed receipt adapters, and pendant progress/approval rendering; integration tests for crash/disconnect at every transition.
changes.risk: A strict witness gate may pause work more often until permissions are fixed; stale queued commands could appear delayed. Recover by retaining all evidence, allowing explicit owner-approved override for low-risk reversible steps, and providing cancellation/compensation. Never mark success from transport acknowledgment alone.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible relay storage/CPU; 1–3 cheap background reconciliation calls per interrupted saga. No additional per-step realtime calls.
changes.latency_impact: Adds tens to hundreds of milliseconds for witness validation and lease persistence; avoids costly duplicate actions and can run long work asynchronously.
changes.security_impact: Reduces replay and confused-deputy risk; stores only hashes/IDs in relay where possible. Requires strict binding of witness to tab/session and expiry, and approval for irreversible effects.
depends_on: Mac local state witness and browser reconnect quarantine (mac-planner contribution)
A durable relay job/saga store rather than in-memory /execute orchestration
Typed action receipts with provenance and compensation metadata
Pendant progress and approval UI/event channel

changes.change: Add a cross-surface execution lease. When faculty-judgement creates an action with an irreversible boundary, relay issues a short-lived lease containing plan hash, destination, evidence hash, and required pendant presence. Mac/browser may prepare and pause, but cannot cross the boundary unless the pendant has recently attested the lease nonce; disappearance, expiry, browser-session change, or plan mutation revokes it. Relay deduplicates lease consumption and fans cancellation to the Mac job and browser command queue. Receipts record lease issuance, attestation, consumption, and revocation separately.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A task can be prepared while the owner is away, yet a sleeping/reconnected Mac or stale browser tab cannot send, delete, or buy just because an old approval exists. The owner gets a dependable physical stop/start control from the thing they are wearing, without opening the Mac or exposing credentials.
changes.effort: Medium-high: relay D1 schema and atomic consume, Mac job gate, browser queue gate, pendant attestation protocol/UI, and failure-injection tests for reconnects and duplicate delivery.
changes.risk: A lost pendant or dropped radio could strand a task; recover by explicit cancel/replan from Mac or voice. Clock skew and reconnect races require server-issued monotonic expiry and idempotency. Never treat mere BLE proximity as authorization; use a button gesture plus nonce and show the exact effect.
changes.cost_impact: Low recurring API cost (<$0.01/task for storage/events); engineering cost is protocol and test work. No new pendant hardware required, though secure element support would strengthen attestation.
changes.latency_impact: Adds ~100–300 ms for attestation on a live link and up to 2 s for a spoken/button prompt; no impact on read-only preparation.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by binding authorization to wearer-held hardware, but introduces a new credential. Store only rotating device keys/lease hashes; rotate and revoke keys, rate-limit attempts, and fail closed on any mismatch.
depends_on: durable relay action escrow (the queued cross-surface task primitive)
physical_action_confirmation pendant skill
browser stale-command quarantine and reconnect handshake
signed action receipts with plan/evidence provenance

changes.change: Add an end-to-end 24 kHz audio conformance runner that uses a deterministic PCM/I2S test fixture on the pendant (not the Mac microphone), sends the exact production Opus uplink through the relay, decodes the 24 kHz/60 ms downlink, and measures sample-rate tags, packet loss concealment, round-trip latency, drift, clipping, and weighted SNR against the golden vector. Have the Mac harness start/stop the run, collect /pipeline events and audio artifacts, and publish a signed pass/fail receipt with firmware, relay, codec, and wire-clock versions. Fail closed when capture is still 15,625 Hz or when any stage silently resamples to 16 kHz.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can hear a genuinely superwideband pendant conversation instead of trusting a green build or a claimed 24 kHz decoder. A single repeatable test catches the current split (15,625 Hz capture versus 24 kHz playback) before it reaches their daily wearable, without opening the Mac microphone.
changes.effort: Medium: add a firmware test mode and PCM fixture, relay-side vector/metrics code, and a Mac command that runs the test and stores a compact receipt. No production audio behavior changes until the receipt passes.
changes.risk: A test fixture can mask real microphone/I2S clock problems; include a second run using the physical mic with a local speaker/loopback jig, and label synthetic versus physical results. Keep the test mode gated and never enabled in release firmware. Recover by retaining the current 16 kHz uplink fallback when conformance fails.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one background verification job and bounded audio artifacts. Hardware fixture is roughly $20–$60 (I2S DAC/ADC or loopback board), powered only during tests.
changes.latency_impact: No production latency impact. The test takes roughly 1–3 minutes per firmware/relay build and measures, rather than adds to, the 60 ms frame path.
changes.security_impact: Synthetic vectors and aggregate metrics stay local or in short-retention job storage; do not upload owner speech. The physical-mic run must explicitly use a test tone or discard raw samples immediately.
depends_on: A firmware-accessible I2S/PCM injection or loopback test mode
A Mac-side build/device runner (the requested mac_read_build_and_devices capability)
/pipeline/audio and /pipeline/:pipelineId/audio/:direction artifact access
A defined 24 kHz acceptance threshold and clock-drift budget

changes.change: Build a cross-surface transaction coordinator between the existing /plan, /execute, browser command queue, Mac jobs, and relay. It should issue a planHash-bound transaction with explicit prepare/commit/abort states, per-step idempotency keys, leases, precondition snapshots, and one merged receipt. A pendant approval event commits only the exact still-valid hash; disconnect, stale tab, changed page, or lease expiry aborts safely. Keep browser and Mac evidence local/redacted and persist only hashes, statuses, and receipt pointers.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets one trustworthy answer to “did it happen?” and cannot accidentally approve a stale or duplicated action. Walking out of range or losing the browser no longer leaves an ambiguous half-completed task.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared transaction schema and durable state machine, adapters for Mac jobs and browser commands, relay lease/watchdog, and a small pendant event protocol; integration tests for reconnect, duplicate delivery, stale evidence, and undo.
changes.risk: A coordinator bug could block legitimate work or falsely report completion. Default all unknown states to abort/needs-review, retain the existing per-surface receipts, and provide an operator recovery endpoint that never retries irreversible steps blindly.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing storage and compute; one small durable record plus hashes per transaction. Model cost should fall because receipts and evidence are structured rather than re-summarized from full context.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–300 ms bookkeeping before prepare/commit; lease heartbeats run asynchronously. Commit remains bounded by the slowest Mac/browser step.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by binding approval to target, plan hash, evidence version, and expiry; reduces sensitive data copied into relay. Requires careful nonce/idempotency-key handling and authenticated pendant events.
depends_on: Owner-defined risk classes and which require physical approval
A relay-to-pendant approval/cancel event path
Browser and Mac adapters exposing prepare/commit boundaries
Durable job runner (the existing browser durable-runner backlog item must be completed)

changes.change: Route the existing Mac job approval gate into the relay/pipeline as a typed approval challenge instead of emitting only 'Waiting for your approval on the dashboard'. The challenge carries jobId, action type, concise spoken summary, expiry, and nonce; the pendant can approve/cancel with its single button, while the dashboard remains a secondary view. On reconnect, replay the challenge once, suppress duplicates, and update the same job receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can approve a safe action while wearing the pendant, without being at the Mac or opening the dashboard. A command that currently stalls silently becomes a clear, bounded interaction that either completes or expires safely.
changes.effort: Medium: add approval challenge/result events to the relay schema, bridge local approval-gated jobs to those events, add pendant button handling and replay/nonce tests.
changes.risk: A spoken prompt could be misunderstood, and duplicate button delivery could double-run an action. Show the action class and target in the prompt, require a deliberate second press for irreversible classes, bind the nonce to the job, and default timeout/reconnect to cancel.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible relay storage and bandwidth; avoids expensive realtime turns by using a compact event. One short TTS prompt costs only a few cents or less depending on the existing speech path.
changes.latency_impact: Approval delivery should be sub-second when LTE is live; commit follows existing job latency. Reconnect adds bounded delay and never auto-commits.
changes.security_impact: Improves security only if approval events are authenticated and nonce-bound; do not put page contents or secrets in the spoken prompt. Keep dashboard approval and pendant approval mutually exclusive.
depends_on: Relay approval event route and authenticated pendant event
The pending physical_action_confirmation/action_lease_indicator device skills (already requested)
Existing local approval gate and job receipt plumbing
Owner's manual Accessibility/Screen Recording grants remain needed for GUI-only actions

changes.change: Add a cross-node capability-token firewall for actions. Before faculty-action hands work to the Mac or authenticated browser, the relay mints a short-lived, single-use token scoped to an exact operation, target (app/tab/account), fields or files allowed, maximum side effects, and expiry. Mac and browser adapters must present that token for every mutation; they return a signed receipt containing the token hash, target identity, and before/after evidence. A token cannot be replayed on another tab, job, or surface, and relay logs contain only the scope and hashes—not credentials or page contents.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can let the hive act on private accounts without giving every node broad, permanent control. A prompt injection, stale browser tab, duplicate retry, or compromised relay worker is contained to one narrowly authorized action instead of becoming permission to send mail, move money, or alter unrelated files.
changes.effort: High: define a shared token/receipt format, add enforcement middleware to Mac jobs and browser commands, bind tokens to session/tab identity and idempotency keys, implement revocation and expiry, and test confused-deputy, replay, reconnect, and partial-failure cases.
changes.risk: Strict scopes may reject a legitimate multi-step task or strand an in-flight job. Start in audit-only mode, provide explicit scope expansion as a new approval, preserve existing receipts for recovery, and fail closed for mutations while allowing read-only work to continue.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1 and local-agent overhead per action; no additional model call is required. Token and hash storage is tiny compared with browser evidence or audio.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one local verification and usually one relay lookup per mutation (target under 50 ms when connected); cache only the single-use token at the executing surface, never broad credentials.
changes.security_impact: Substantially reduces blast radius and secret propagation. Requires secure randomness, authenticated transport, replay protection, clock-skew tolerance, careful redaction, and a recovery path for token revocation. This is intentionally distinct from an approval UI: approval says yes, while the token says exactly what yes permits.
depends_on: A shared identity for relay, Mac agent, browser bridge, and pendant events
Browser bridge online heartbeat and durable command IDs
Mac job receipts with target metadata
Owner-defined operation classes and maximum side-effect scopes

changes.change: Add a postcondition-verification stage to every irreversible Mac/browser job. The planner must emit a typed expected invariant (for example, appointment status=confirmed, draft remains unsent, reminder exists with exact time). After execution, a separate perception pass re-reads the authoritative surface—browser tab/session for web state, AppleScript/read-only route for Mac state—and stores a signed verification record alongside the existing receipt. If the invariant is false, ambiguous, or the tab/session changed, mark the job “unverified” rather than successful, stop retries, push a pendant alert with the observed value, and offer an explicit recovery/undo job. Use the same operation key for retries and require compare-before-commit when possible.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops hearing “done” when a click timed out, a site rejected a field, or the wrong tab was active. They get a truthful result grounded in the resulting state, plus the exact observed discrepancy and a recovery choice. This works without Accessibility for AppleScript/browser-readable surfaces and degrades honestly for GUI-only actions.
changes.effort: Medium: define invariant and verification schemas, add read-only adapters for existing Mac and browser surfaces, extend receipt storage/UI, and add pendant result states. One or two weeks for a narrow set of actions; broader semantic verification is incremental.
changes.risk: A site may update asynchronously or expose stale cached text, causing a false unverified result; use bounded polling with timestamps and show evidence. Verification must never itself mutate state. If the verifier crashes, preserve the receipt as executed-but-unverified and allow manual inspection; do not automatically retry irreversible work.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly one cheap read/verification model call only for semantic invariants ($0.001–$0.02), otherwise deterministic selectors/AppleScript. Additional browser/Mac round trips add modest bandwidth and relay storage.
changes.latency_impact: Adds approximately 0.5–5 s after execution depending on eventual consistency; pendant can say “checking” immediately. No added latency before approval or before the action starts.
changes.security_impact: Store hashes and minimal redacted evidence rather than full page contents; bind verification to URL/tab/session and plan hash. Read-only verification can inspect private data on the Mac but must not export secrets. Access failures become unverified, never success.
depends_on: A typed action plan with expected postconditions
Existing job receipts and undo routes
Browser session/tab affinity and typed browser results
Mac read-only AppleScript or equivalent route coverage
A pending pendant result state; GUI-only verification remains blocked until the owner grants Accessibility/Screen Recording

changes.change: Introduce a durable cross-surface saga coordinator rather than treating each Mac/browser action as an independent job. Persist a DAG of typed nodes with dependency barriers, commit markers, idempotency keys, expected postconditions, and explicit compensation policies. On reconnect, resume only the first uncommitted node; after each node, run a read-only verifier before releasing dependents. Expose partial-success and paused-for-owner states through the existing job and receipt APIs, and make unsafe compensation impossible to auto-run.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can ask for an outcome that crosses a private website and their Mac without manually checking whether half the work happened. A site rejection will not leave a misleading calendar reminder, and a dropped connection will not duplicate a booking or reminder. When full rollback is impossible, the owner gets an honest partial result and a precise next choice.
changes.effort: High integration effort: schema and durable worker first, then browser and Calendar adapters, verifier contracts, recovery tests, and pendant progress states. Start with browser-booking-to-Calendar/reminder as a narrow vertical slice.
changes.risk: Some external actions cannot be undone; the coordinator must stop before those nodes unless separately approved and must surface partial completion. Eventual consistency can make a successful node look absent, so use bounded verification and never retry an ambiguous irreversible node. Recover by leaving the graph paused with its evidence and operation key.
changes.cost_impact: Small durable storage and queue cost; one cheap planning or recovery call per graph ($0.002–$0.03), with deterministic steps otherwise. Verification adds browser/Mac requests but prevents duplicate side effects.
changes.latency_impact: Adds verification latency between dependent steps (typically 1–5 seconds, longer for eventually consistent sites); disconnect recovery becomes reliable rather than immediate. The pendant can stream node status so the owner is not left guessing.
changes.security_impact: Keep credentials and full private content on the Mac/browser surfaces. Relay stores only encrypted/redacted plan values, hashes, state transitions, and receipts. Bind every node to the owner's approval, session/tab identity, and idempotency key; require fresh approval for any compensation or newly discovered irreversible node.
depends_on: A versioned plan/receipt schema that supports dependency graphs and postconditions
Durable relay job execution across Mac sleep and reconnect
Browser command queue with stable tab/session affinity
Read-only Calendar/reminder verification adapters
Pendant progress and partial-success states
Owner Accessibility/Screen Recording only where no AppleScript or browser-readable adapter exists

changes.change: Build an end-to-end audio acceptance transaction that creates a local tagged test stream, correlates relay pipeline events with pendant decode/I2S counters and ESP32/A2DP telemetry, computes per-hop latency/jitter/loss/underruns, stores a signed receipt, and automatically tears down the test. It must fail closed when telemetry is missing rather than infer success from HTTP 200.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner asks whether the 24 kHz path works, they get a defensible answer naming the failing hop—or a verified pass—instead of a vague queued-job success. It prevents shipping a path that sounds acceptable in one segment but drops frames at the bridge.
changes.effort: Medium-high: a relay correlation schema, a Mac diagnostic runner, firmware/bridge counters, and a receipt renderer. No Accessibility grant is needed; shell/AppleScript and existing pipeline routes suffice for orchestration.
changes.risk: Diagnostics could generate audible output, consume radio/battery, or mis-correlate reused packet IDs. Use a unique run nonce, bounded duration, local-only synthetic audio, explicit teardown, and mark incomplete on any missing counter. Recovery is deleting the run receipt and stopping the pipeline; never flash automatically.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost for local tests; roughly $0.01–$0.05 if a model summarizes the receipt. Firmware flash/storage impact is small if counters are compact, but must be budgeted against 211,608 B application RAM and 1 MB flash.
changes.latency_impact: Adds no production voice latency. Test startup under 2 s and test duration 10–20 s; receipt available within 3 s of teardown.
changes.security_impact: Synthetic audio avoids microphone leakage. Receipts may reveal Bluetooth device identity and network timing; keep local by default and redact identifiers before relay upload. Require confirmation before pairing changes, firmware writes, or prolonged playback.
depends_on: An authoritative 24 kHz acceptance spec
A diagnostic counter/event schema on pendant, relay, and ESP32 bridge
A local Mac runner using existing run_shell/run_applescript and pipeline routes
Durable receipt storage and a dashboard/voice summary path

changes.change: Replace the provisional ESP32 classic-A2DP bridge with a BLE Audio-capable bridge (or a production codec module) whose transport and sink can preserve a 24 kHz mono path, while retaining a compatibility SBC output mode. Keep the pendant's 24 kHz decode as the canonical sample rate and move any unavoidable conversion to one explicitly measured boundary.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The current bridge hard-locks classic A2DP to 44.1 kHz stereo, forcing an extra 31,250→44,100 resample after the pendant's 24 kHz decode. A 24 kHz-capable sink would reduce avoidable conversion artifacts and make the owner's request for a true 24 kHz path physically achievable, not just true inside the codec.
