changes.effort: High: select a supported BLE Audio/LC3 chipset and headphones, redesign the bridge firmware and power/audio board, then validate coexistence with the nRF9160 link. Keep the existing ESP32 as a fallback during migration.
changes.risk: BLE Audio interoperability, pairing UX, and battery draw may regress; some headphones will only support SBC. Mitigate with dual-mode fallback, an A/B hardware harness, and the proposed tagged acceptance transaction before changing the daily path.
changes.cost_impact: Prototype bridge roughly $20–$60 in parts plus new headphones if needed; modest additional power versus the current ESP32 bridge, exact draw requires measurement. No per-run API cost.
changes.latency_impact: Potentially lower buffering than the current SBC/A2DP path, but BLE Audio scheduling may add 10–30 ms; require measured p50/p95 latency in acceptance receipts.
changes.security_impact: New pairing keys and Bluetooth identifiers must remain local and be resettable. Do not auto-pair or replace the current sink without confirmation.
depends_on: The end-to-end acceptance transaction and per-hop telemetry
A written 24 kHz acceptance criterion
Hardware/audio compatibility study for the chosen BLE Audio sink

changes.change: Add a provenance-preserving browser-to-reminder handoff transaction: browser extraction must return a cited source (tab/session, URL, timestamp, quote, normalized date and timezone, confidence); the Mac reminder creator must accept that typed payload and return the reminder ID; the relay stores one receipt linking source evidence to the created reminder; the pendant speaks only the minimal result. Reject the handoff when the date is ambiguous or the source tab changed between extraction and creation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a reliable reminder from a private page without copying details by hand, while being able to answer “which page and text caused this reminder?” later. Ambiguous dates become a clear stop instead of a silently wrong calendar entry.
changes.effort: Medium integration work across the existing browser result, reminder, job receipt, and spoken-summary paths; no new model or Accessibility grant is required for the basic version.
changes.risk: A stale page or timezone conversion could create a wrong reminder. Use source hashes, explicit timezone normalization, confidence thresholds, and automatic undo of the just-created reminder if post-verification fails. Do not retain unrelated page content.
changes.cost_impact: Low API cost, approximately $0.01–$0.04 per handoff for extraction and summary; local browser/Mac operations dominate latency.
changes.latency_impact: One extra verification round adds about 1–3 seconds, keeping total completion under 7 seconds in normal conditions.
changes.security_impact: Private page evidence stays scoped to the job and expires quickly; receipts retain only the minimal quote, URL, and source hash. No message sending or form submission is permitted by this transaction.
depends_on: A typed browser extraction result with stable citation and source hash
A reminder endpoint accepting normalized timezone and provenance metadata
A receipt schema that links browser evidence to the created Mac object
A spoken-summary renderer that redacts private page text

changes.change: Make the 24 kHz playback path deadline-aware: add a bounded 60 ms-frame jitter buffer with sequence numbers, concealment on a missing frame, and a cooperative audio scheduler that reserves decode time before uplink encoding. Keep the existing SD policy (write only failed uploads), expose underrun/late/decode timing counters, and have the relay stamp end-to-end frame sequence and playout timestamps so acceptance tests can distinguish network loss from local starvation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Speech and briefings stay intelligible through ordinary cellular jitter instead of clicking, stalling, or silently dropping audio; failures become diagnosable without storing routine recordings.
changes.effort: Medium firmware + relay work: ring-buffer and scheduler changes, relay metadata, and an automated 24 kHz acceptance harness across clean, jittered, and loss traces. Requires profiling on the actual board before tuning buffer size.
changes.risk: A larger buffer adds conversational delay; concealment can mask severe loss; scheduler bugs could starve uplink capture. Recover with a compile-time buffer cap, watchdog reset of the audio task, and counters/telemetry rather than indefinite buffering.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; roughly 4–12 kB RAM depending on buffer depth and under 1% flash growth. No additional hardware required.
changes.latency_impact: Adds configurable 60–180 ms playout latency, but prevents much longer stalls; interactive mode can use the smallest safe depth.
changes.security_impact: Telemetry contains timing and packet IDs only, not audio. Ensure counters are authenticated with the existing session and do not retain payloads.
depends_on: 24 kHz audio-path acceptance criteria
A relay audio probe or test harness that can inject delay/loss
End-to-end sequence/timestamp fields in POST /pipeline/audio and GET /pipeline/:pipelineId/audio/:direction

changes.change: Add an end-to-end audio handoff watchdog and loss-tolerant frame contract: every 24 kHz/60 ms Opus frame carries a monotonically increasing stream sequence and presentation deadline; the nRF9160 records decode time, ring-buffer depth, underruns, and CRC/sequence gaps in a compact  telemetry record, while the ESP32 bridge reports resampler starvation and SBC queue depth. On a missed deadline, the pendant emits a bounded comfort tone/status event and requests only the missing frame range instead of silently continuing. The relay stores a short encrypted replay window keyed by stream ID and sequence, and the Mac TTS producer publishes the same contract. Add an offline fixture that feeds synthetic speech and verifies 24 kHz decode -> 31,250 Hz I2S -> 44.1 kHz SBC without gaps.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Briefings and replies would stop going mysteriously silent. If the owner walks between relay coverage and headphones, the system can recover a small gap, say that audio is degraded, and leave a diagnosable receipt instead of pretending the message played. This is grounded in the current prototype's 25.4 ms decode per 60 ms frame, 87% combined encode/decode CPU load, and the bridge's known 44 kB-buffer starvation failure.
changes.effort: Medium/high: define a versioned frame header, implement compact counters and replay-window lookup in firmware/relay, add bridge telemetry, and build a host-side deterministic fixture. No flash should occur until the owner approves and the fixture passes.
changes.risk: Extra headers and telemetry consume airtime, flash, and RAM; replay can increase latency if the window is too large. Keep the window to a few seconds, cap counters, and fall back to live playback after one bounded retry. If the contract version is unknown, fail closed with a status event. Recovery is a firmware rollback plus relay feature flag.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible inference cost; roughly 1–3% extra uplink/downlink bytes and small persistent relay storage per active stream. Hardware unchanged.
changes.latency_impact: Normal path adds under 5 ms bookkeeping; recovery adds at most one frame interval plus network RTT (target under 300 ms).
changes.security_impact: Stream IDs and replay objects must be opaque and encrypted/TTL-deleted; telemetry must contain no audio payload or transcript. Sequence metadata can reveal listening times, so retain briefly and restrict to the owner's job.
depends_on: 24 kHz acceptance criteria from the owner
audio_path_probe tool or an equivalent host/bridge loopback test
Permission to read/build the pendant simulator firmware (not yet granted)
A relay route for bounded encrypted frame replay and typed telemetry

changes.change: Implement a durable cross-surface execution checkpoint protocol. Before each Mac or browser step, write a checkpoint containing jobId, stepId, idempotency key, consequence class, precondition hash, and expected witness. After execution, append separate attempted and witnessed receipts; on disconnect, crash, timeout, or browser-session loss, mark the step interrupted rather than retrying. Add a resume endpoint that selects only the next unverified step after fresh precondition/readback checks, and publish compact pending/interrupted/disputed/resumable events to the pendant stream. Keep the full evidence local to the Mac/bridge and send the relay only a redacted status plus checkpoint id.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped connection will no longer make the owner wonder whether an external action happened or risk sending it twice. They can hear 'step 2 of 4 completed; step 3 needs confirmation' and safely continue later from the pendant.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and durable storage, wrappers around mac_run_actions/browser_run_actions, reconnect reconciliation, independent readback adapters, and pendant event plumbing. Build first for reminders/files/drafts, then add external sends and purchases behind stricter confirmation.
changes.risk: A bad witness adapter could falsely mark a side effect complete, or a stale precondition could block a legitimate resume. Fail closed on ambiguity, retain the interrupted state, expose evidence and an explicit repair path, and never auto-replay irreversible steps.
changes.cost_impact: Small persistent journal growth (roughly 1–3 KB per step plus bounded receipt metadata); background reconciliation is low-cost. Full screenshots/page dumps should be content-addressed and retained only under existing retention policy.
changes.latency_impact: Adds tens to hundreds of milliseconds before and after each step for checkpoint writes; reconnect reconciliation is asynchronous. High-consequence resume waits for readback and owner confirmation.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by separating intent, attempt, witness, and confirmation. Checkpoint records must redact secrets, encrypt private evidence at rest, bind browser checkpoints to tab/session identity, and expire resume authority after session or page changes.
depends_on: A shared typed witness/checkpoint schema and durable claim store (the evidence-quorum work proposed by faculty-judgement).
Mac/browser readback adapters for side effects.
Pendant pending/interrupted/disputed events and a confirmation control.
Existing /jobs receipts and /journal must become append-only and idempotent rather than inferred from final status.

changes.change: Add a divergence-aware execution interlock between planning and action. Compile every step into a semantic precondition snapshot (recipient, amount, URL/origin, selected account, target file, permission state, and stable field identifiers). Before committing a step, compare the live Mac/browser state to that snapshot. If it differs, atomically pause the job, invalidate its action lease, store a minimal redacted diff plus the last safe checkpoint, and emit a pendant decision event with approve-corrected-plan, edit, cancel, or owner-takeover options. On approval, generate a new plan revision linked to the old one; never mutate the old plan or replay prior steps.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Unexpected UI or data changes become a clear one-sentence question instead of a silent failure, wrong click, duplicate submission, or lost progress. The owner can safely approve the correction while away from the Mac and continue from where the task actually stopped.
changes.effort: High: semantic state adapters for browser DOM and AppleScript-accessible Mac apps, a diff/classification service, atomic job pause/lease invalidation, plan revision storage, and pendant event/response plumbing. Start with browser forms and Mail/Calendar before general GUI vision.
changes.risk: Over-sensitive diffs could interrupt harmless layout changes; under-sensitive diffs could miss a changed destination or amount. Default to pause on uncertainty, classify only from stable semantic fields, and retain a human-takeover path. Expire approvals when the page/session changes again.
changes.cost_impact: Small metadata storage per step; background diffs are cheap. Vision fallback for unstructured dialogs costs more and should be sampled only after structured adapters fail.
changes.latency_impact: Adds a pre-commit comparison, typically under 300 ms for structured state; an owner decision adds conversational latency only when divergence occurs.
changes.security_impact: Reduces accidental disclosure and misdirected actions by keeping diffs minimal and binding approvals to origin, session, and plan revision. MFA/CAPTCHA/security prompts remain owner takeover events, never automated.
depends_on: A typed semantic precondition snapshot and plan-revision format.
Stable browser and Mac semantic-state/readback adapters.
Pendant decision events and an authenticated response channel.
Durable job pause/lease invalidation and append-only receipt history.

changes.change: Add a durable cross-surface action-card coordinator between relay, Mac agent, and browser bridge. It accepts one request_id and fan-outs to native AppleScript adapters (Mail, Calendar, Finder/Notes, Messages, Safari/Chrome) plus authenticated browser tabs, normalizes each result into {source, subject, snippet, timestamp, URL/deep-link, confidence, suggested reversible action}, deduplicates by stable hash, writes a local ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace/workbench/<request_id> artifact, and emits progress/completion receipts consumable by the pendant. Each adapter checkpoints independently so a dropped browser bridge or Mac sleep resumes without repeating work.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: One short pendant request can reliably turn scattered private information into something actionable instead of failing separately on “read gmail,” “read github,” and “read calendar.” The owner gets a spoken digest immediately, a durable reviewable workbench later, and safe reminders/drafts without accidental sends.
changes.effort: Medium-high: define typed schema and D1/local persistence, implement native AppleScript adapters and browser result normalization, add fan-out/fan-in and retry/idempotency, then connect briefing/audio receipt generation. Test with bridge offline and Mac sleep.
changes.risk: A connector could expose more private text than intended or duplicate an action after retry. Mitigate with source-scoped least-context extraction, stable request/idempotency keys, local-only raw artifacts, redacted relay summaries, and explicit unsent/preview states. If one source fails, report partial completion rather than claiming success; resume from checkpoints.
changes.cost_impact: No new hardware. One background model pass for normalization/prioritization; cost scales with snippets, not full pages. Storage is small JSON/Markdown artifacts plus hashes; cleanup policy required.
changes.latency_impact: Initial acknowledgement remains realtime; native adapters can return in seconds, browser fan-out in 10–30 seconds. Async receipts prevent blocking voice and allow relay_job_status polling.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by making provenance and scope explicit, but introduces a central cross-source join. Keep raw private data on Mac, send only selected snippets, enforce source permissions and confirmation on irreversible actions.
depends_on: A typed action-card/workbench schema
Durable job checkpoint storage and resumable fan-out
Native AppleScript adapter allowlist for Mail/Calendar/GitHub/browser
Pendant status/audio queue packet format

changes.change: Insert a Mac-local privacy broker as the mandatory boundary between native/browser execution and relay/model calls. Adapters return structured fields rather than prose; the broker applies a per-task allowlist, secret/PII classification, purpose and TTL, performs joins locally, computes source hashes and a redacted preview, and emits only the approved projection plus an audit receipt. The relay rejects untyped/raw payloads, while action execution consumes the same approved projection so the preview and the eventual operation are cryptographically linked.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can delegate sensitive cross-app work without having to choose between usefulness and exposing entire inboxes, pages, or files. They get a clear proof of what information was used and exactly what will change, while credentials and unrelated private text stay on the Mac.
changes.effort: High: define field-level schemas and policy evaluation, implement Mail/Calendar/browser/file adapters, add local secret detection and encrypted audit records, enforce relay validation, and test failure/rollback paths across browser and Mac jobs.
changes.risk: Over-redaction may make a task fail; under-redaction could leak sensitive data. Fail closed, explain missing fields locally, allow owner-approved one-time field exceptions, expire projections quickly, and retain only hashes and policy decisions after completion.
changes.cost_impact: No hardware cost. Small local CPU/storage overhead; lower cloud token cost because raw content is not uploaded. Background model cost is limited to local extraction/redaction and typed-result prioritization.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–3 seconds for local classification and joining; avoids repeated cloud context transfer and can make total sensitive tasks faster. Long jobs remain asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: Materially improves confidentiality and auditability. The broker becomes a high-value local component and must be sandboxed, encrypted at rest, authenticated to the relay, and prevented from silently widening policy scope.
depends_on: A typed field-level privacy policy/schema
Mac-local adapter and secret-classification service
Relay schema validation that rejects raw untyped private payloads
Preview/receipt linkage and owner confirmation protocol

changes.change: Complete the missing safety half of transactional execution: make every write action carry a canonical plan hash, expected target state/precondition, approval requirement, and expiry; have executor.js evaluate observeBeforeAction and refuse on mismatch before dispatch. For browser actions, bind the same transaction hash to tab/session and require the bridge result to echo it. Add an atomic approval-consumption endpoint/relay record so one pendant press can authorize exactly one plan, with duplicate/replay rejection. After dispatch, run declared postcondition reads and mark the job succeeded, failed, or uncertain; expose all decisions and evidence in the existing action receipt and /jobs/:jobId/receipts. Keep old jobs in compatibility mode but never silently treat a missing gate as approved for new jobs.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can safely approve a prepared action from the pendant without worrying that a stale page, changed file, retry, or reconnect will apply the decision somewhere else. If execution cannot be proven, they hear “uncertain” with an undo option instead of a false success.
changes.effort: Medium: define a versioned transaction schema, add pure precondition evaluators for common file/app/browser targets, durable nonce consumption in relay, executor refusal paths, and integration tests for stale state, retry, reconnect, and postcondition mismatch.
changes.risk: A stricter executor may refuse currently working plans or leave jobs pending when an app changes. Recover by presenting the exact failed precondition, allowing the planner to re-observe and issue a new plan; never auto-reuse the old approval. Roll out behind a version flag and retain raw receipts.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one cheap verification/read per write. Small durable storage increase for hashes and redacted evidence.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms for local preconditions and up to several seconds for browser postcondition reads.
changes.security_impact: Strongly improves replay and confused-deputy resistance. Approval tokens must be single-use, short-lived, device-bound where possible, and must not include secrets in logs.
depends_on: Durable relay transaction/lease record
Pendant nonce-bound approval gesture
Typed action schema shared by planner, browser bridge, executor, and receipt code

changes.change: Add an owner-scoped emergency revocation epoch shared by relay, Mac executor, and browser bridge. Persist epoch and cancellation reason in D1; expose an authenticated stop endpoint that is callable from the pendant path without an LLM. Every worker must compare its leased job epoch immediately before each external side effect, atomically mark the step cancelled when stale, stop polling, and acknowledge the epoch. On reconnect, workers quarantine stale commands rather than replaying them. Emit a cancellation receipt listing completed, prevented, and uncertain steps; retain ordinary undo separately.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A single deliberate gesture on the pendant would let the owner stop queued automation even when the Mac screen is inaccessible or the browser reconnects later. They get a trustworthy boundary—what definitely did not happen versus what needs checking—instead of hoping cancellation reached every surface.
changes.effort: Medium: relay schema/endpoint, worker middleware in Mac and browser paths, pendant event forwarding, acknowledgement aggregation, timeout handling, and race-focused tests where cancellation arrives during dispatch.
changes.risk: A side effect can race the final check and remain uncertain; the receipt must say so and never claim reversal. Overly broad cancellation could interrupt useful work, so scope it to the owner and require a deliberate long press. Recover by issuing a new plan after the owner reviews the receipt.
changes.cost_impact: Tiny D1 write plus worker polling/broadcast overhead; no model calls. Existing hardware is reused.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one local epoch comparison before each side effect; stop propagation target under 2 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Improves containment and limits replay. Endpoint must authenticate the paired pendant, reject stale epochs, rate-limit gestures, and prevent cancellation records from deleting audit evidence.
depends_on: Pendant event path that works offline until link returns
Shared job lease/epoch schema across Mac and browser workers
Typed cancellation receipts

changes.change: Add a durable ActionBundle coordinator between faculty-judgement and the existing executors. It accepts an intent hash plus typed steps (surface, target/session, preconditions, irreversible flag, idempotency key, verifier, and optional compensator), persists a state machine (planned → approved → preflighted → applied/verified or compensated/blocked), dispatches existing Mac/browser actions, and emits one signed receipt containing each step's observed before/after evidence. Resume must never replay a verified idempotent step; any changed target/session invalidates approval.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask for one outcome spanning their Mac and logged-in browser without manually supervising each handoff, while getting an honest answer when only half completed and a safe path to retry or undo the completed reversible parts.
changes.effort: Medium-high: coordinator schema and worker, adapters around existing job/browser result records, verifier hooks, approval-token binding, and dashboard/pendant status rendering. Start with reversible AppleScript and browser field edits, then add irreversible steps.
changes.risk: A coordinator could accidentally duplicate sends or apply a stale decision. Mitigate with intent/target hashes, idempotency keys, expiry, preflight checks, explicit commit gates, and treating unknown executor outcomes as blocked rather than retrying. Recover by resuming from the ledger or invoking compensators; retain raw executor receipts for audit.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1/R2 storage and queue overhead; one cheap orchestration call per bundle and no extra model call per step. Evidence storage should be redacted and retention-limited.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–300 ms for ledger transitions; execution remains parallel where dependencies permit. Long operations become durable instead of tying up the voice turn.
changes.security_impact: Improves least-privilege and auditability, but approval tokens and private before/after evidence become sensitive. Encrypt or redact evidence, bind tokens to session/account and exact field values, and prevent relay logs from receiving page contents.
depends_on: A durable job runner (the existing browser runner backlog item is still only half-shipped)
Per-step postcondition verification and action-proof tools (already requested but not granted)
Pendant-local approval/lease indicator for offline or dropped-link safety (already requested but not granted)

changes.change: Add an Action Escrow state machine between /plan, /execute, the browser command queue, and job receipts rather than treating them as independent calls. Persist one escrow record with intent hash, idempotency key, bound surface/session/tab/account, preconditions, postcondition, owner-confirmation nonce, lease expiry, and evidence pointers. Transition atomically through proposed → target-verified → awaiting-pendant-confirmation → executing → independently-verified → committed, with expired/drifted/failed terminal states. Make /execute refuse an unconfirmed or drifted escrow; make browser/Mac results append evidence to the same record; make faculty-perception close only after a fresh read; expose the complete state through existing /jobs/:jobId and receipts and make undo reference the committed escrow, not merely the last action.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A spoken decision becomes a trustworthy real-world outcome instead of a best-effort chain of disconnected calls. If the owner walks away, a tab changes, Wi-Fi drops, or the wrong account is active, the action expires or stops visibly; if it proceeds, the owner gets proof tied to the exact target and before/after state.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and atomic transitions in relay/backend, adapters in Mac and browser agents, pendant confirmation transport, and a postcondition verifier. Start with Calendar/Mail/browser form submissions and filesystem changes before expanding to purchases or deletes.
changes.risk: A state-machine bug could block legitimate actions or duplicate an action. Use idempotency keys, compare-and-set transitions, dry-run simulation, replay tests, and retain the existing receipts/undo path as fallback. If verification times out, report unknown—not success—and leave the escrow open only until its explicit deadline.
changes.cost_impact: Small persistent metadata/evidence overhead per action; one extra verification request and occasional cheap model call. No continuous polling when the owner is absent.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–2 seconds for target/precondition verification and confirmation; postcondition verification can be asynchronous, with durable job status available immediately.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by binding actions to origin/session/account and requiring a fresh nonce. Evidence must be redacted and short-lived; bearer tokens never go to the pendant. Irreversible actions remain separately classified and confirmation-gated.
depends_on: Typed precondition/postcondition schema
Pendant confirmation transport (currently unavailable)
Faculty-perception readback endpoint
Atomic durable job/lease storage

changes.change: Introduce a Witness Quorum layer between execution and completion reporting. Every side effect gets an action hash and evidence envelope. The executor's receipt is only one witness; a separate observer must independently re-read the target or an independent confirmation channel. Correlate witnesses by action hash, target binding, and freshness; classify the outcome as witnessed, disputed, or unknown. Expose that classification through job status/receipts and prevent the relay from saying “done” when only the executor acknowledged. For safe operations, allow an explicitly classified retry; for non-idempotent operations, freeze and request owner review.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an honest answer about whether something actually happened, rather than a confident “done” that may mean only that a click or API call was attempted. Failures become actionable disputes with evidence, and silent partial completion stops being mistaken for success.
changes.effort: High integration effort: evidence envelope and correlation service, independent readback adapters, state/timeout handling, and pendant/dashboard language. Pilot with one browser form and one filesystem operation.
changes.risk: Independent observers can disagree or observe stale state; false disputes could annoy the owner, while weak independence could create false confidence. Enforce freshness windows, source independence metadata, explicit unknown outcomes, and never auto-retry irreversible actions.
changes.cost_impact: One additional readback per action and small durable evidence records; cheap compared with the risk of an unverified external side effect.
changes.latency_impact: Adds 1–10 seconds before declaring completion; the owner can hear “executor finished, verification pending” immediately.
changes.security_impact: Evidence must be scoped to the target and redacted. Independent observers need narrowly scoped read access, never broad credential export. Action hashes and nonces prevent replay or cross-job evidence substitution.
depends_on: Typed evidence envelope
Independent observer/readback adapters
A status vocabulary that distinguishes attempted, witnessed, disputed, and unknown
Idempotency classification for retry policy

changes.change: Implement a cross-surface saga coordinator rather than another surface-specific queue. Accept a typed plan whose nodes target Mac actions, authenticated browser commands, or relay/public-browser work; persist job graph, dependency state, idempotency key, lease/heartbeat, evidence references, and compensation status in relay storage. Dispatch only ready nodes through existing adapters, resume leased nodes after restart, emit progress events, and expose one causal receipt plus cancel/undo endpoints. Keep private page payloads on the Mac; relay stores redacted hashes and metadata. This fills the missing connective layer between existing /plan, /execute, browser queue, Mac job receipts, and relay status.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A single request that spans a logged-in tab and the Mac will finish reliably after leaving the house or losing a connection, without duplicate actions or an unexplained half-complete state. The owner gets one truthful result showing each step, evidence, retries, and any compensation.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and storage, adapter contracts for three executors, lease recovery, event stream, and integration tests for restart/duplicate/failure scenarios.
changes.risk: A coordinator bug could run a later step after an earlier step only appeared successful, or compensation could be incomplete. Mitigate with idempotency keys, explicit typed terminal states (never infer success from timeout), per-node evidence, bounded retries, and conservative dependency semantics. Recover by canceling the saga and exposing manual-repair steps; do not claim rollback when it did not occur.
changes.cost_impact: Small persistent metadata and event storage; roughly $0.01–$0.08 in background model usage per complex job, with deterministic action calls dominating no API cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms dispatch overhead per node; restart recovery is seconds, while long browser/Mac work remains asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: Reduces data movement by keeping authenticated content at the browser/Mac edge. Requires signed job/node identities, least-privilege adapter tokens, encrypted receipts, redaction of page text, and retention limits.
depends_on: Durable browser runner (chg-16bc5dee)
Browser progress/resumable polling (chg-14accc01 remaining gap)
Existing Mac job receipts/undo and relay job records
A typed action contract shared by faculty-judgement and faculty-action

changes.change: Add a conditional-intent engine distinct from ordinary routines and durable jobs. Store a typed predicate DAG (source, expression, freshness window, required confidence, expiry) plus a typed action DAG and an evidence-binding rule. Subscribe to browser-bridge changes and Mac/relay state events where available; use bounded polling only as fallback. Evaluate all predicates against one observation epoch, acquire a short execution lease, then dispatch the action graph through existing Mac/browser adapters. Persist trigger evidence, suppress duplicate firings with a content-addressed observation key, and expose pause/resume/cancel plus a concise pendant notification.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can leave a precise intention such as “when the approved invoice appears and the Mac is online, file it,” and trust that it will happen once at the correct moment—even after sleep, disconnects, or a stale near-match—rather than having to remember to ask again.
changes.effort: High: predicate DSL and compiler, event/poll adapters, durable evaluation state, observation-epoch consistency, leases, deduplication, and tests for stale data, source races, expiry, and restart.
changes.risk: A false predicate could trigger an unwanted action; a race could combine facts from different moments. Require explicit freshness/confidence bounds, same-epoch evaluation, immutable compiled predicates, dry-run inspection, expiry defaults, and a terminal receipt containing the exact evidence. If a source is unavailable, remain pending rather than infer false or true.
changes.cost_impact: Low storage/event cost; polling authenticated pages can consume browser budget and Mac power, so prefer bridge events and adaptive backoff. Background model cost is limited to initial compilation and exceptional ambiguity.
changes.latency_impact: Event-backed conditions trigger within seconds; fallback polling adds the configured cadence. Setup adds a few seconds, but no realtime model is needed while waiting.
changes.security_impact: Predicate evaluation of private page content remains on the Mac/browser edge; relay stores hashes and redacted outcomes. Encrypt intent definitions and bind execution to the owner's device/session. Never transmit credentials or raw page contents to the relay.
depends_on: A durable event/predicate store and wakeable scheduler
Browser bridge change/event feed (currently offline)
Mac state/file/app event adapters that do not require Accessibility for supported AppleScript intents
Typed action/receipt contracts shared by faculty-judgement and faculty-action

changes.change: Build an end-to-end 24 kHz audio conformance and recovery harness: firmware emits deterministic mic/speaker loopback vectors and sequence counters; relay validates Opus packet cadence, resampling, CRC/order, and jitter-buffer behavior; Mac harness runs long-duration fixtures and records MOS-adjacent underrun/latency metrics; failures become timestamped receipts and a UART-readable diagnostic bundle. Add negotiated fallback profiles (24 kHz primary, 16 kHz compatibility) rather than silently transcoding.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets voice that stays intelligible instead of randomly clipping, drifting, or going silent, and a concrete diagnosis when the prototype fails. It directly advances the stated 24 kHz audio-path goal.
changes.effort: Medium-high: firmware test mode and counters, Worker validation/metrics, Mac fixture runner, and dashboard report.
changes.risk: Test mode must be impossible to enter during ordinary wear; malformed packets or bad clock measurements could falsely trigger fallback. Recover by keeping the current path as a safe profile, gating diagnostics behind explicit maintenance mode, and retaining raw counters without raw audio.
changes.cost_impact: Small ongoing storage/CPU for counters and reports; no per-turn model cost. One-time engineering for fixture generation and validation.
changes.latency_impact: No added steady-state latency; negotiated fallback may add one handshake round at session start.
changes.security_impact: Diagnostics should contain packet metadata and hashes, not microphone contents; raw audio fixtures remain local unless explicitly uploaded.
depends_on: 24 kHz acceptance criteria from owner
A firmware build/flash or simulator access grant
audio_path_probe capability

changes.change: Add a pendant long-press emergency stop protocol distinct from conversation press: holding the sole button for ~1.5 s emits a signed cancel-all-active-jobs event, the relay atomically marks cancellable Mac/browser steps cancelled, and the bridge aborts queued/not-yet-started commands. The pendant gives a short haptic/LED acknowledgement if available (otherwise a distinct LED flash), and the dashboard shows which already-started steps could not be reversed. Require a second press only to resume, never to confirm a destructive action.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: With no microphone open, the owner can stop a runaway browser click loop, duplicate retry, or unexpectedly long Mac job instantly—even while the voice session is unavailable—without hunting for the Mac window or trusting speech recognition.
changes.effort: Medium: firmware button state machine and signed event; relay cancellation endpoint plus job-state transition; Mac/browser executors poll cancellation between steps and abort queued commands; dashboard and receipts add cancelled-by-owner reason. Test races between cancel and step commit.
changes.risk: A long press could cancel an important benign job, so distinguish it with a deliberate hold and announce the affected job IDs on the next available audio/status channel. Cancellation cannot retract an already-sent email or completed purchase; receipts must say that plainly. Recover by allowing resume only from a fresh plan, never automatic replay.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost and storage; one small firmware update. Hardware cost $0 on the prototype; production should add a tactile button with a clear long-press feel, roughly <$1 and no meaningful extra draw.
changes.latency_impact: Local event acknowledgement should be <200 ms; relay cancellation target <1 s, with executor polling at each action boundary.
changes.security_impact: Use a device-bound signing key and replay-protected event counter; cancellation is high-impact but not destructive, and must be accepted only for the owner's active device/session. Do not transmit microphone audio—button event and job IDs only.
depends_on: Durable job state transitions with atomic cancel-vs-commit ordering
Mac/browser executors honoring cancellation between typed actions
A relay route for signed pendant events and a common active-job index
Owner-facing receipts that distinguish cancelled, completed, and irreversible side effects

changes.change: Implement a shared ActionContract v1 and reducer between judgement and existing executors. Each run contains contractVersion, runId, owner-visible goal, ordered/parallel steps, target surface, idempotencyKey, preconditions (resource fingerprint + observedAt + expiry), effect class, approval requirement, timeout, and compensation. The relay persists a state machine (planned→ready→running→blocked/awaiting_approval→succeeded/failed/compensated), grants a short lease per step, and accepts exactly-once step receipts from Mac/browser. On reconnect it reconciles receipts by idempotencyKey before dispatching anything; a changed fingerprint becomes blocked, never retried blindly. Reduce all receipts, browser results, journal entries, and pipeline events into one final run report and pendant event.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped connection, changed webpage, or half-completed Mac job would no longer cause duplicate sends, stale edits, or an untruthful 'done'. The owner gets one actionable answer: completed steps, blocked step and reason, safe undo options, and the exact approval needed to continue.
changes.effort: Medium-high: schema, durable reducer, adapters for existing Mac/browser jobs, lease/reconciliation tests, and pendant event rendering.
changes.risk: A strict validator may block a task that could have succeeded; recover with an owner-visible 'update and retry' action, never silent fallback. Reducer bugs could misreport completion, so derive status only from signed/typed receipts and retain raw events.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage/compute; one small D1/R2 record per step and no extra model call on retries. Existing receipts and browser results are reused.
changes.latency_impact: Adds <100 ms local validation plus one persistence write per transition; reconnects become safer but may wait for fresh observation when fingerprints expire.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by keeping secrets out of contracts, binding actions to resource fingerprints, expiring leases, and enforcing approval classes. Contract and receipts must be access-controlled and redact page contents.
depends_on: Action receipt implementation chg-5fc73ce3 is present but currently has no enforced gates or preconditions
A durable browser job runner and authenticated session affinity
Pendant-visible approval/blocked event handling
Shared event IDs across /browser/result, /journal, /pipeline/events, and Mac job receipts

changes.change: Add an offline-command quarantine and reconnect watchdog around the existing browser queue. When heartbeat expires, stop accepting new mutating commands, mark the five currently pending commands as paused (not failed), notify the relay/pendant with count and oldest age, and require a fresh session/tab fingerprint before replay. On reconnect, reconcile each command by idempotency key and discard commands whose URL/session or precondition hash changed; retain safe read-only commands for bounded replay. Add a visible drain/clear action and TTL-based expiry so stale private-page work cannot execute days later.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The browser is offline right now with five queued commands. This prevents a later browser reconnect from unexpectedly submitting stale forms or repeating actions, while preserving harmless research so the owner does not lose work.
changes.effort: Medium: heartbeat state transitions, queue metadata, reconnect reconciliation, relay event, and dashboard/pendant status.
changes.risk: A legitimate command may expire or be quarantined; expose each paused command and allow explicit resume after re-observation. Never auto-replay writes after an offline interval.
changes.cost_impact: Minimal D1/local queue metadata; no model calls. One heartbeat request at the existing cadence.
changes.latency_impact: No effect while online; reconnect adds one observation round before replay.
changes.security_impact: Reduces stale-session and delayed-submit risk. Store only redacted URL/session identifiers and hashes, not page secrets.
depends_on: Existing /browser/heartbeat, /browser/poll, /browser/result/:commandId, /browser/sessions
Durable browser job runner proposal chg-16bc5dee
Pendant-visible blocked/approval events
Owner-controlled browser extension heartbeat

changes.change: Add a cryptographic presence-bound approval protocol spanning the pendant and relay: the relay creates a one-time commitment nonce over a canonical, redacted action manifest (targets, recipient/amount, expiry, and effect class); the pendant stores it locally, shows a compact confirmation phrase/hash, and accepts a long-press plus button sequence offline. It signs/derives an approval token with monotonic counter and nonce, queues it until link returns, and the relay atomically consumes it only for that exact manifest. Any changed precondition, deadline, or action set invalidates the token. Emit explicit waiting/approved/expired/blocked states and attach the token ID to every Mac/browser receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a trustworthy 'I approved this exact thing while holding my pendant' guarantee, even if the voice link drops. A stale conversation, replayed request, or changed webpage cannot silently become a purchase, submission, or account change.
changes.effort: Medium-high firmware + relay protocol work, plus receipt plumbing and a small pendant UI/state machine.
changes.risk: Button misfires or lost queued tokens could inconvenience the owner; use a cancellable local state, clear timeout, and a spoken/LED recovery path. If signing material is unavailable, fail closed rather than treating a voice acknowledgement as equivalent.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; small persistent token record and a few bytes of pendant flash/RAM. Hardware can use the existing button/LED if firmware access is granted.
changes.latency_impact: Immediate local acknowledgement; online dispatch adds one relay round trip. Offline approvals wait safely instead of expiring into execution.
changes.security_impact: Strongly improves anti-replay and confused-deputy resistance. The action manifest must redact secrets, tokens must be single-use and expiry-bound, and device keys must never leave the pendant.
depends_on: Pendant firmware access and a local approval state machine
Relay durable atomic consume/deadline storage
Canonical action-manifest and receipt schema
Existing Mac/browser action dispatch and undo/receipt routes

changes.change: Add a cross-surface transaction coordinator between faculty-judgement and the existing browser/Mac executors. It persists a versioned action plan with before/after evidence, idempotency key, approval nonce/expiry, and correlation ID; exposes prepare→approve→execute→verify→reconcile states; refuses writes when evidence hash or tab/session changes; serializes browser and Mac side effects; after disconnect polls receipts and the external page before classifying acknowledged/uncertain/failed. Emit compact state transitions to the relay/pipeline so the pendant can say exactly what is waiting without claiming success.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A booking, purchase, or submission either completes once with proof or is clearly waiting for review. The owner will not be charged twice or be left guessing whether a disconnected browser click worked.
changes.effort: Medium-high: durable state schema and state machine, executor adapters, crash/restart recovery, external-ack verifiers for common page patterns, and contract tests for duplicate delivery and disconnect at every step.
changes.risk: A verifier may misclassify a site’s confirmation or a stale page may block a valid action. Default to uncertain/needs-review, never automatic retry for irreversible writes; retain raw receipts and provide undo only where the target supports it. Roll out first to reversible reminders/drafts, then gated transactions.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost for the coordinator; background reconciliation adds roughly $0.01–$0.05 per uncertain job and small durable metadata/receipt storage.
changes.latency_impact: Preparation adds one evidence snapshot/hash (usually <1 s); normal execution is unchanged. Disconnect cases may wait up to a configured reconciliation window rather than immediately returning.
changes.security_impact: Approval nonce is scoped to exact payload, account/session, target, and short expiry. Store hashes and redacted evidence by default; encrypt receipts and avoid copying credentials or full private pages into relay logs.
depends_on: A durable job runner and browser command queue with idempotency/session affinity (chg-16bc5dee, chg-14accc01)
The existing receipt/undo plumbing (chg-5fc73ce3)
A shared typed context/correlation service (chg-a82e0b13 or equivalent)
Browser bridge heartbeat currently reports home-chrome offline; owner must bring the extension online for authenticated execution

changes.change: Add a secure authorization path to the pendant: a device-unique private key in protected storage (or a small secure element), monotonic anti-replay counter, and firmware support for signing a displayed/action-digest-bound nonce only after a deliberate physical button gesture. Add revocation and recovery metadata without storing the owner’s action contents.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can authorize a sensitive action with a deliberate physical gesture on the device they are wearing, without dictating a secret or trusting an ambient voice command. A stolen browser session or copied transcript cannot reuse the approval.
changes.effort: High: secure key provisioning and lifecycle, signed-message protocol, firmware UI/LED feedback, Mac/browser verification middleware, relay persistence and revocation, plus red-team tests for replay, relay compromise, clock skew, lost pendant, and target substitution.
changes.risk: A lost pendant could block approvals or, if key lifecycle is wrong, authorize unwanted actions. Default-deny on malformed/stale proofs, require a physical long-press for high-risk actions, maintain a server-side revocation list, and provide a recovery ceremony using the owner’s existing trusted Mac.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $1–$4 incremental secure-element/BOM cost if the current board lacks protected key storage, plus negligible per-action API/storage cost; firmware and verification engineering dominate.
changes.latency_impact: Local signing is sub-100 ms; network verification adds roughly 100–500 ms. Expiry and single-use checks may briefly delay actions when the relay is unreachable, so only pre-approved low-risk fallback behavior should exist.
changes.security_impact: Improves authorization security by requiring possession plus physical intent, but creates a new root of trust. Keys must never be exportable; relay logs should contain only hashes, counters, target IDs, and timestamps; revocation must work even if the pendant is offline.
depends_on: A pendant firmware signing/proof primitive and protected key storage
A relay nonce/verification/revocation protocol
Mac and browser executor middleware that checks proofs before side effects
An owner-approved lost-device recovery flow

changes.change: Add a resumable audio-delivery protocol for 24 kHz generated briefings: the Mac/relay emits an operation-scoped manifest (codec, sample rate, duration, chunk hashes), the relay sends numbered chunks with bounded backpressure, and the pendant ACKs the highest contiguous chunk plus a final playback receipt. Persist only the manifest and a short replay window; on reconnect resume from the last ACK instead of restarting or duplicating speech. Surface underruns, codec mismatch, and truncated playback as explicit job/briefing status.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A briefing that was generated successfully should actually be listenable later. The owner gets one spoken confirmation that audio was fully delivered and can resume after walking out of range, instead of discovering a silent, partial, or duplicated queue item.
changes.effort: Medium: protocol and relay integration, a small pendant transport/playback state machine, and end-to-end tests with dropped links, delayed ACKs, and power loss.
changes.risk: A stale ACK could skip audio or replay it. Prevent this with manifest IDs, monotonic chunk sequence numbers, hash checks, and bounded replay; discard an incomplete item rather than presenting it as complete. Recovery is retry from the last verified chunk or regenerate the item.
changes.cost_impact: No additional model cost; modest relay storage for manifests/replay windows and negligible device flash/RAM for state. Audio generation remains the dominant API cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds milliseconds of ACK/control overhead and may delay final completion until playback buffering is verified; initial playback can begin as soon as the first safe buffer is filled.
changes.security_impact: Use opaque briefing IDs and authenticated transport; do not put transcript text in chunk metadata. Expire manifests and replay buffers promptly.
depends_on: The 24 kHz path acceptance criteria already requested from the orchestrator
A firmware-local durable event/queue primitive (offline_intent_spool request is still unanswered)
An authenticated relay-to-pendant data channel with delivery acknowledgements
A canonical briefing/job ID shared by /research, /pipeline/audio, and the audio queue

changes.change: Add a cross-surface action transaction protocol. Before faculty-action executes a judged plan, each step must carry a typed target, precondition snapshot (device/session/tab, identity, relevant field values), intended effect, reversibility class, and verification query. The relay assigns an idempotency key and short action lease; the Mac/browser executor rechecks the precondition immediately before the mutation, refuses on drift or stale lease, then runs the verification query and emits a signed receipt containing before/after evidence. On link loss the relay keeps the transaction pending (never retries a mutation blindly), and the pendant can announce pending/succeeded/blocked when it reconnects. Extend existing receipts and undo records rather than creating a second history.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A judged instruction becomes dependable action instead of a hopeful click: the owner is told when the page, account, amount, or recipient changed underneath us, gets proof of what actually changed, and cannot suffer a duplicate or stale execution just because the Mac or voice link briefly disappeared.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared transaction schema and state machine in relay plus Mac/browser adapters; precondition/verification implementations for typed Mac actions and authenticated browser mutations; receipt signing and reconnect status delivery. Start with reminders, calendar edits, and browser form drafts before irreversible sends.
changes.risk: A conservative verifier will block legitimate actions when a page has harmless cosmetic drift; recover by presenting the exact failed precondition and allowing a fresh judged plan. Never auto-retry mutations. Signing-key loss or clock skew can mark receipts unverifiable, so retain local unsigned evidence and surface 'unverified' honestly. This does not bypass macOS Accessibility/Screen Recording; AppleScript and bridge paths remain usable, while GUI steps stay blocked when reachability is false.
changes.cost_impact: Small per-step relay/D1/R2 metadata and one cheap verification read; roughly 1–3 extra Mac/browser calls per mutation. No expensive model call required after judgement; use the realtime tier only to explain a block aloud.
changes.latency_impact: Adds about 0.5–2 seconds for precondition and postcondition reads on Mac, potentially more for browser round trips; safer than speculative retries. Pending state is immediate when the link drops.
changes.security_impact: Improves security: binds actions to tab/session/device and lease, prevents replay via idempotency keys, and records before/after provenance. Receipts must avoid storing page secrets; hash/redact sensitive values and require explicit confirmation for irreversible effects.
depends_on: A durable relay job record and receipt/undo store (extend the existing job and /jobs/:jobId/receipts paths)
Typed action schemas in mac_run_actions and browser_run_actions
Authenticated browser session/tab affinity from the browser bridge
A physical-action confirmation and action-lease indicator on the pendant for high-impact or irreversible steps

changes.change: Evolve the pendant from a single-button/LED prototype into an action-confirmation interface: retain the conversation button, add a low-profile tactile confirm/cancel pair (or a two-stage thumb rocker), a coin ERM haptic motor, and a distinct amber/red/green status LED or RGB LED. Firmware should expose a small local state machine—armed, awaiting approval, executing, succeeded, blocked—with a timeout and no network dependency for cancel. The relay/action lease protocol supplies the nonce and effect summary; only a matching physical confirm event can authorize a high-impact mutation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can approve a consequential action without opening the Mac or speaking a secret aloud, and can feel/see whether an action is waiting, running, completed, or blocked in a noisy room or while the phone is away. A physical cancel gives an immediate escape when the judged plan is wrong.
changes.effort: High for a product revision, moderate for a dev-kit experiment: add GPIO inputs, haptic driver, LED patterns, debounce/state persistence, enclosure changes, and relay nonce binding. Prototype first with the existing button as confirm and an external I2C GPIO expander/haptic breakout; migrate to a custom board after the interaction is validated.
changes.risk: Extra controls can cause accidental presses or confuse conversation start; require a deliberate long-press/double-action and audible/haptic distinction, and fail closed on ambiguous input. A lost link must leave the lease unapproved and expire it. Hardware changes are not needed for ordinary reversible actions, so retain the current path as fallback.
changes.cost_impact: Prototype breakout roughly $10–25, custom BOM increase about $3–8 per unit; haptic bursts are tens of milliamps and negligible average draw, while RGB LED current must be duty-limited. No per-call model cost.
changes.latency_impact: Local feedback under 100 ms; confirmation waits on the owner's deliberate gesture, while relay verification remains network-bound.
changes.security_impact: Strengthens authorization by requiring a local presence signal bound to a one-time lease nonce. Do not treat button presence alone as identity for financial or destructive operations; combine it with explicit spoken summary and server-side expiry.
depends_on: Cross-surface action lease/attestation transaction schema
Pendant firmware access and a final physical-action confirmation policy
A product-board revision; current nRF9160 DK has only one user button and one LED

changes.change: Add a cross-surface commit coordinator between judgement and faculty-action. It materializes a versioned action graph (Mac, browser, relay, pendant), assigns each step an idempotency key and pre/postcondition, and stores append-only checkpoints. Browser and Mac workers must return typed evidence (dispatch, observed-before, observed-after, or unknown). The coordinator retries only steps declared idempotent, pauses on unknown/non-idempotent outcomes, and emits one signed receipt stream consumed by relay-realtime, the pendant, and dashboard. On reconnect, the pendant receives the pending commit state and a concise spoken result rather than a duplicate command.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped call or flaky browser bridge will no longer leave the owner guessing whether an email/form/reminder happened. They get one safe approve-once workflow and an honest, auditable answer; ambiguous side effects stop instead of being repeated.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and state machine, adapters in Mac job runner and browser bridge, reconciliation probes, relay persistence, pendant event/audio client, and dashboard timeline; then fault-injection tests for disconnects and duplicate deliveries.
changes.risk: A coordinator bug could pause legitimate work or, worse, duplicate a non-idempotent action. Default-deny unknown outcomes, per-step idempotency declarations, short leases, explicit cancellation, and existing undo/receipt routes provide recovery. Roll out read-only shadow receipts before enabling execution.
changes.cost_impact: Small storage and relay overhead; roughly one compact record per checkpoint. Background reconciliation is inexpensive. No extra realtime model call except preview/final speech; ambiguous steps still incur existing local-agent/model costs.
changes.latency_impact: Adds tens of milliseconds to dispatch and durable writes; no added delay within a step. Final receipt may arrive later after reconnect or reconciliation.
changes.security_impact: Plan hashes, owner/session binding, expiry, least-privilege surface tokens, and redacted evidence prevent stale or cross-session approvals. Private DOM/content remains on the browser bridge/Mac; only hashes and typed facts leave.
depends_on: The existing Mac job/receipt and browser command/result paths must expose stable idempotency keys and typed evidence.
A durable relay job store (the current job runner backlog item is still open).
Pendant approval and pending-state transport; the owner’s requested physical confirmation/lease skills are still unavailable this round.
A reconnect route that queues the final spoken receipt and a dashboard view of the timeline.

changes.change: Add a bounded Contingency Case runtime, distinct from one-shot jobs and page watches. A case stores a goal, evidence assertions, expiry, stop conditions, and a finite set of owner-approved reversible branches. Each observation creates a versioned state transition; the runtime may execute only the branch whose preconditions match, records before/after evidence, and emits an exception event when no branch matches. Relay wakes the case on schedule or browser/Mac events, while the pendant receives a compact “decision needed” prompt with the relevant evidence and a one-button defer/stop response.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can delegate the ongoing management of a messy situation without granting open-ended autonomy. The system keeps working when websites or statuses change, takes safe next steps automatically, and asks exactly one focused question when reality leaves the approved plan.
changes.effort: High: new case schema and evaluator, event/schedule wakeups, branch authorization, browser/Mac observation adapters, durable state transitions, pendant notification/defer protocol, and adversarial tests for stale evidence and repeated events.
changes.risk: A faulty precondition could trigger an unintended branch or create notification loops. Require explicit finite branches, strict expiry, monotonic transition IDs, duplicate-event suppression, dry-run simulation, and default stop on disagreement or missing proof.
changes.cost_impact: Small persistent state per case and periodic observation costs; background model calls can be avoided for deterministic transitions. Novel exceptions may use a model call and authenticated browser/Mac reads.
changes.latency_impact: No impact on ordinary voice turns. Branches run on event/schedule latency; unresolved exceptions wait for the next pendant connection or relay wakeup.
changes.security_impact: Cases are scoped to named sessions/accounts and expire automatically. Secrets remain on the Mac/browser surface. Every branch carries an authorization class, and irreversible classes are unexecutable without fresh owner approval.
depends_on: A durable relay scheduler/event queue
Typed browser and Mac observation results with provenance and freshness
A branch authorization model separate from one-shot action approval
Pendant notification, defer, and stop events

changes.change: Add a cross-surface 24 kHz audio conformance sentinel: a pendant firmware test mode emits a short locally generated calibration chirp and captures a timestamped reference window; the relay tags each Opus packet with sequence, source sample-rate, encode/decode timestamps, and loss markers; the Mac harness runs the test on demand and stores a compact receipt (measured capture rate, decoded rate, jitter, packet loss, underruns, CPU headroom) in the job receipt. The relay rejects silently mislabelled 16 kHz packets and selects a safe fallback profile rather than claiming superwideband success. Expose the latest pass/fail and failure stage through the existing pipeline/job status surfaces.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask “is my pendant audio really 24 kHz?” and get a trustworthy answer instead of subjective audio quality or a green connection light. Regressions become actionable (mic clock, Opus profile, relay transcode, bridge playback, or underrun) and the system can preserve intelligible speech when the wideband path is unhealthy.
changes.effort: Medium-high: firmware test capture/generator and counters, relay packet metadata/validation, Mac test orchestration, and dashboard/receipt rendering. Requires one hardware-in-loop session for calibration.
changes.risk: A bad calibration threshold could report false failures or force an unnecessary fallback; keep test mode explicit, retain raw audio only in RAM, and make fallback reversible. No Accessibility or Screen Recording is required. Recover by rerunning the sentinel after link stabilization and keeping the last known-good profile.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one short test packet burst and a small D1 receipt. Engineering time is the main cost.
changes.latency_impact: No steady-state latency change. An explicit test takes roughly 2–5 seconds; packet tagging adds only a few bytes per frame.
changes.security_impact: Calibration audio should never leave the pendant; only numeric metrics and hashes cross the relay. Receipts must avoid retaining speech content or sensitive waveform data.
depends_on: 24 kHz acceptance criteria from the owner
permission to inspect/build the pendant firmware and connected serial/J-Link devices
an authenticated pendant-to-relay test trigger and a typed audio receipt schema

changes.change: Replace the prototype audio front end with a native 24 kHz-capable capture and playback clock domain: use a microphone/codec path whose actual sample clock supports 24 kHz (or an integer-related clock with verified low-jitter conversion), add an independent audio DMA clock rather than deriving capture from the current 15,625 Hz path, and give the bridge a negotiated clock/profile contract. The firmware, Opus configuration, relay, and acceptance tests must all advertise measured rates rather than hard-coded labels.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets genuinely superwideband speech instead of a 16 kHz uplink being relabeled or reconstructed as 24 kHz on playback. Voices, environmental cues, and transcription quality improve, and the pendant remains reliable when the network changes because both ends agree on the real clock and profile.
changes.effort: High: select and prototype a production audio codec or I2S microphone clocking scheme, revise the pendant/bridge PCB or carrier, update Zephyr drivers and DMA buffering, then requalify Opus, RF power, thermal behavior, and enclosure acoustics. This is a product-hardware change, not a simulator-only patch.
changes.risk: A new clock tree can introduce drift, buffer overruns, RF interference, or higher power draw; the development kit must remain supported as a compatibility profile during migration. Recover with a negotiated 16 kHz mode and hardware-in-loop drift tests before deployment.
changes.cost_impact: Prototype engineering plus roughly $8–$25 per production unit for codec/clock/audio components and PCB changes; likely tens of milliwatts additional draw depending on codec. API cost is negligible.
changes.latency_impact: Potentially neutral or slightly lower once DMA is correctly clocked; initial buffering and resampling tests may add 10–30 ms until tuned.
changes.security_impact: No new cloud data is required. Keep raw microphone samples local except during an explicitly active call; expose only negotiated profile and health metrics to the relay.
depends_on: Owner-defined 24 kHz acceptance criteria
Firmware inspection/build access and serial/J-Link hardware-in-loop testing
The previously proposed end-to-end conformance sentinel to prove the new clock path

changes.change: Add reconnect quarantine for pending browser commands: every queued command gets an expiry, session/tab fingerprint, and intended effect class; when the extension reconnects, do not replay stale or write/submit commands automatically. Move them to a reviewable queue, revalidate the tab/session fingerprint, and let the relay ask the pendant whether to discard, refresh evidence, or resume. Read-only idempotent commands may be auto-replayed only within a short TTL and unchanged session.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The browser is currently offline with seven pending commands. Without quarantine, reconnecting can cause old clicks, typing, or submissions to run against a changed tab and produce an action the owner no longer intended. The owner gets safe recovery instead of surprise browser mutations.
changes.effort: Medium: extend browser command persistence/schema, add reconnect reconciliation and dashboard/pendant status, and test stale, duplicate, and tab-changed cases.
changes.risk: A command may remain pending until the owner reviews it; that is safer than replay. Recovery is explicit discard or re-plan. Read-only commands can expire harmlessly.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and model cost; one deterministic reconciliation per reconnect.
changes.latency_impact: Adds under 1 second for queue inspection; owner confirmation adds human latency only for stale/irreversible work.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by binding commands to session/tab fingerprints and preventing stale authenticated actions. Do not persist page contents beyond existing evidence retention.
depends_on: browser bridge reconnect/heartbeat path
typed effect class and idempotency metadata on browser commands
owner-visible pending-command review via existing jobs/receipts or dashboard

changes.change: Add a persistent, resumable alert envelope protocol to the pendant: relay-delivered alerts are stored with alertId, urgency, expiry, redacted display/audio payload, retry schedule, and acknowledgment nonce. The firmware renders and repeats active alerts without server contact, queues an acknowledgment event durably, and uploads it exactly once after reconnect; duplicate envelopes are idempotent and expired alerts are visibly marked rather than silently discarded.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: An urgent alert will not vanish because the pendant briefly loses Wi‑Fi or the relay is restarting. The owner can acknowledge it on the device and later see proof that the acknowledgment reached the system, instead of wondering whether a critical reminder was delivered.
changes.effort: Medium firmware and relay protocol work, plus power-loss/reconnect tests and a small dashboard status view.
changes.risk: Persistent alerts could annoy the owner or survive after they are no longer relevant; enforce expiry, bounded repetition, quiet-hours policy, and a physical dismiss action. If flash writes fail, keep the alert in RAM and report unacknowledged rather than claiming durability.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost. Small flash journal and under roughly 8 KB RAM for a bounded active-alert queue; modest battery use while repeating audio/LED.
changes.latency_impact: Local rendering is immediate; reconnect acknowledgment delivery is bounded by the next network opportunity.
changes.security_impact: Use per-alert authenticated envelopes and nonces; persist only redacted payloads and metadata, never raw conversation audio. Acknowledgment proves device interaction, not identity of a third party holding it.
depends_on: relay alert envelope and escalation scheduler
pendant/server acknowledgment event schema
owner-configurable urgency, expiry, and quiet-hours policy

changes.change: Introduce a signed, append-only operation envelope shared by relay, Mac agent, and browser bridge. Each envelope carries operationId, parent decisionId, target invariant, preconditions, approval state, idempotency key, per-step lease, typed result, evidence reference, and terminal outcome (proven/failed/unknown). Require every surface to echo the operationId; have the relay reconcile late/out-of-order events and expose one causal timeline to the pendant. This is a protocol change, not another action endpoint, and it must cover browser commands and Mac jobs uniformly.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets one trustworthy answer about a real-world request instead of disconnected Mac job IDs, browser command IDs, and spoken claims. If the link drops or a step partially succeeds, they can resume safely without duplicate purchases/messages or wondering which device acted.
changes.effort: Medium-high: define schema/state machine, add persistence and signing at relay, adapt Mac job and browser bridge adapters, add replay/idempotency tests, and render a compact timeline plus proof state in the pendant/dashboard.
changes.risk: Schema bugs could strand jobs or cause duplicate execution. Roll out read-only correlation first, then enforce idempotency for reversible actions; retain compatibility with existing job receipts and provide a migration/replay tool. Never infer success from missing events.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible per-request storage/compute; roughly 1–3 KB of metadata per step plus short-lived evidence hashes. No model cost except optional reconciliation.
changes.latency_impact: Adds under 100 ms for envelope persistence and event correlation; no extra model round trip on the happy path.
changes.security_impact: Operation envelopes and evidence references must be authenticated and scoped to the owner; redact page text and local paths, sign cross-surface events, and expire evidence according to retention policy. Approval tokens must be single-use and bound to operationId plus exact mutation.
depends_on: Durable job runner and browser command queue must preserve operationId/idempotency keys.
A verifier endpoint/tool (currently requested but unavailable) to classify postconditions as proven/failed/ambiguous.
Pendant confirmation and action-lease indicators for irreversible steps.
Relay storage/retention policy for evidence references.

changes.change: Add a browser-bridge liveness gate and queue reconciler: when heartbeat is absent, stop retrying commands, mark them waiting-for-device (not failed), coalesce duplicate idempotent requests, and notify the relay with the exact pending count. On reconnect, perform a read-only tab/session handshake, replay only commands whose lease and idempotency key are still valid, and expire stale commands with a pendant-readable explanation. Expose a one-click/dashboard drain or cancel operation rather than leaving seven opaque pending commands.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner will not get repeated timeouts or accidentally replayed browser actions after reopening Safari. They will know what is waiting, what expired, and what can safely resume—even when the browser extension disappears while they are away.
changes.effort: Medium: heartbeat state machine, durable queue metadata, idempotency/coalescing, reconnect handshake, and dashboard/relay notification.
changes.risk: A reconnect race could duplicate an action or incorrectly discard a valid one. Default to no replay for writes, replay reads only, and require explicit approval to resume any mutation; preserve existing receipts.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1/local JSON metadata overhead; no additional model calls in the normal path.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one handshake round trip on reconnect; prevents 45-second per-command timeout delays while offline.
changes.security_impact: Keep session/tab identifiers scoped and do not expose URLs or private page text in notifications; authenticate heartbeats and bind replay leases to the owner/session.
depends_on: Browser extension heartbeat/polling endpoint already present (/browser/heartbeat, /browser/poll).
Durable browser command queue and idempotency keys (existing/partially implemented).
Pendant or relay event channel for waiting/expired status.

changes.change: Add a cross-surface shadow-execution engine that runs an approved action plan against captured, redacted state snapshots before touching the live Mac or browser. It should compute an expected diff and dependency impact (files, calendar entries, messages, account fields), detect conflicting concurrent changes, and attach the snapshot hash to the eventual live execution. The live executor must abort if the current state no longer matches the simulated basis, then request a fresh plan.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Before asking the system to do something consequential, the owner could see not merely the fields that will change but whether the whole multi-device plan is internally consistent. This catches stale tabs, changed prices, overwritten files, and contradictory steps before any real side effect.
changes.effort: High: normalize Mac and browser state into a common redacted model, implement adapters for read-only shadow actions, diff/impact rendering, snapshot hashing, and abort-on-drift enforcement.
changes.risk: A simulation can miss behavior that only occurs live, so it must be labeled predictive and never treated as proof. Snapshot capture could expose private data; redact aggressively and expire snapshots. If an adapter cannot model a step, mark it unknown and require a live confirmation rather than silently proceeding.
changes.cost_impact: Extra local storage and read-only adapter work; deterministic simulation is cheap, with planner escalation only when conflicts or unmodeled effects require interpretation.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 1–5 seconds for local plans and potentially longer for multi-tab reads, but avoids expensive failed or duplicated live actions.
changes.security_impact: Snapshots remain encrypted/local where possible; send only minimal structured diffs to the relay. Bind approval to the exact plan and snapshot hash, and invalidate it on any state drift.
depends_on: A common typed operation envelope and invariant/approval lease.
Read-only browser inspection and AppleScript adapters for Mac state.
A diff viewer and pendant-friendly summary of predicted effects.
A live executor that enforces snapshot-hash preconditions.

changes.change: Add a durable cross-surface transaction ledger and saga coordinator between the existing plan/execute/jobs/browser/pipeline paths. A transaction record contains ordered steps with dependency edges, idempotency keys, target surface/session/tab, precondition and postcondition descriptors, reversibility, compensation action, commit boundary, lease expiry, and evidence references. The relay dispatches one step at a time, persists acknowledgements before advancing, pauses at irreversible steps for a single owner confirmation, retries only idempotent steps, and runs compensations on reversible partial failure. Extend job receipts rather than replacing them, but require transactionId/stepId and evidence-envelope linkage; emit pipeline events and pendant audio for state transitions. Keep authoritative verification as a separate read-only worker so execution never self-certifies.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A request spanning the Mac and a private logged-in tab either finishes coherently or clearly tells the owner what remains; dropped links, browser delays, or a restarted Mac no longer create silent half-completed work. The owner gets one spoken pending/verified/partial result instead of guessing from unrelated receipts.
changes.effort: Medium-high: schema/migrations, relay state machine, idempotent dispatch adapters, compensation policy, and integration tests for crash/retry at every boundary.
changes.risk: Duplicate mutations if idempotency is missing, or harmful compensation if a supposedly reversible action has side effects. Default unknown actions to pause; use short leases, durable transition logs, and operator-visible recovery. Existing per-job undo remains the fallback.
