changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage/queue cost; background verification adds 2–6 cheap model or rule-based calls per multi-step transaction. Evidence should be hashes/deltas by default to avoid repeated token and storage cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds tens to hundreds of milliseconds for ledger writes per step and intentional waits at browser/verification boundaries; immediate spoken acknowledgement remains under one second.
changes.security_impact: Improves isolation by binding every command to an authenticated machine and browser session, redacting evidence, and making account identity/irreversible confirmation explicit. The ledger itself contains sensitive metadata and needs encryption, retention limits, and deletion controls.
depends_on: Existing receipt schema must accept transactionId/stepId/evidence references
A verified read-only postcondition probe (the requested verify_action_proof capability)
Durable action lease and pendant confirmation primitives (already requested, not yet observed as granted)
Browser extension must be online for private-tab steps; otherwise the saga must remain pending rather than claim success

changes.change: Add an end-to-end audio format contract enforced at every pipeline boundary. The contract must carry declared sample rate, actual PCM frame count, channels, codec, clock domain, and resampler stage; validate that capture (currently observed as 15,625 Hz), Opus uplink (16 kHz), relay transcode, TTS output (24 kHz), and pendant playback (24 kHz decoded / 31,250 Hz I2S wire clock) are not silently conflated. Reject or mark a run as format_mismatch when metadata and byte-derived duration disagree, and emit one machine-readable resampling manifest with the pipeline receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets speech that is intelligible and correctly timed instead of a system that can claim “24 kHz” while an earlier stage is actually 15,625 or 16 kHz. Failures become diagnosable from one receipt rather than requiring UART archaeology, and acceptance of the requested 24 kHz path becomes measurable.
changes.effort: Medium: shared schema plus validators in relay and local pipeline, byte-duration checks, one fixture per boundary, and a dashboard/briefing display of the manifest. Firmware changes should follow only after the contract exposes the real clock mismatch.
changes.risk: Strict validation may temporarily reject existing prototype captures or surface clock drift as failures. Recover by retaining the raw artifact, labeling the failing boundary, and allowing an explicitly flagged compatibility mode during development; never silently resample twice.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few hundred bytes of metadata per run and modest CPU for arithmetic checks. No new hardware required for the contract.
changes.latency_impact: Under 1 ms for metadata and duration validation; no additional model call. A corrective resample, if required, adds only the existing codec/resampler latency.
changes.security_impact: Metadata is non-sensitive; raw audio retention remains governed by existing policy. Do not upload additional audio solely for validation—derive checks from headers, frame counts, and already-authorized payloads.
depends_on: Owner-provided 24 kHz acceptance criteria (still outstanding)
A real pendant/device connection for hardware verification (currently no pendant is connected)
An explicit choice whether the product contract is 24 kHz speech at the decoded playback boundary or 24 kHz capture, since current hardware reports 15,625 Hz capture

changes.change: Add a factory/service-mode audio clock calibration protocol spanning the nRF9160, relay, and ESP32 bridge. On request, the pendant emits a short deterministic PCM/Opus calibration sequence with monotonic sample counters; the bridge returns captured I2S edge counts and the relay compares declared versus measured duration across capture, uplink, decode, resampling, and playback. Persist only the resulting calibration coefficients and pass/fail record, not the calibration audio. Refuse to advertise the 24 kHz playback path as healthy when drift or an unexpected clock domain exceeds the configured tolerance.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can trust that speech will not slowly change pitch, timing, or truncate when the pendant is worn for a long conversation. When the path is wrong, the system can say exactly which device or clock is responsible instead of presenting a plausible but misleading 24 kHz status.
changes.effort: High: firmware test mode and monotonic counters, a bridge loopback/edge counter, relay comparison endpoint, persisted calibration record, and a service report in the dashboard. Requires a real pendant and bridge fixture for validation.
changes.risk: Calibration could interrupt an active conversation or falsely fail under radio loss. Restrict it to startup/service mode, keep the last known-good coefficients, distinguish transport loss from clock failure, and never overwrite a good calibration with an incomplete run.
changes.cost_impact: No per-request model cost. Small firmware and relay storage overhead; likely under 1 KiB per calibration record. Hardware cost is zero if the existing I2S bridge exposes measurable edges; otherwise a low-cost timer capture/GPIO instrumentation revision may be needed.
changes.latency_impact: No normal-path latency. Service calibration takes roughly 1–3 seconds when explicitly requested.
changes.security_impact: Calibration carries no owner content and should not upload conversational audio. Authenticate service-mode requests and require a physical button gesture or maintenance authorization before running diagnostics.
depends_on: A connected pendant and ESP32 bridge
An agreed tolerance and definition of acceptable 24 kHz playback
Firmware build/toolchain access controlled by the owner
A relay route for calibration manifests and dashboard rendering

changes.change: Implement a contract-bound action transaction that sits between /plan, /execute, the job queue, Mac/browser runners, and pipeline events. At plan time, canonicalize target, preconditions, permitted side effects, expiry, and confirmation requirement into contractHash. At execution, atomically acquire a short lease and emit lease/running/paused events; every Mac or browser step must include contractHash, requestId, tab/session affinity, and a before-state digest. Reject stale or mismatched steps. On completion, run postcondition checks against fresh reads, append a signed receipt containing evidence references and the exact contractHash, and only then emit completed for spoken playback. If the pendant playback predicate is absent, emit delivered-to-relay rather than falsely claiming the owner heard it. Reuse jobs/undo-last only for steps explicitly marked reversible.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can trust “done” or “stopped” in a way they cannot today: a changed webpage, lost tab, stale plan, dropped pendant, or partial Mac failure cannot silently turn into an unverified action. They also get a precise explanation and an undo path for the parts that are genuinely reversible.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and state machine in relay, adapters in Mac/browser runners, postcondition verifier, receipt format, and pipeline event vocabulary; then failure-injection tests for expiry, duplicate delivery, tab replacement, and link loss.
changes.risk: A strict verifier may pause work that would have succeeded, and old clients may omit contractHash. Roll out in shadow mode, accept legacy jobs as unverified, and provide an explicit retry with a newly compiled contract. Never auto-replay an irreversible step.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage/CPU for hashes and state; one extra lightweight verification/read per mutation. Background model cost remains low; no extra realtime call except the final concise status.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms for lease and local digest checks, plus native time for a postcondition read. Failures become earlier pauses instead of long silent retries.
changes.security_impact: Improves replay and confused-deputy resistance by binding every mutation to a short-lived, user-approved contract and tab/session. Keep evidence redacted/minimal and avoid storing private page bodies by default.
depends_on: A durable shared action-contract schema
A verifier for preconditions/postconditions (the pending verify_operation_step/verify_action_proof capability)
A real pendant playback acknowledgement predicate; until then, use the honest delivered-to-relay state
Existing receipt/undo implementation and browser request-id/tab affinity

changes.change: Add a compensating-recovery planner for partially completed cross-surface actions. When a job stops after step n, derive a bounded recovery graph from each completed step's declared compensation (for example, restore a draft field or move a file back), distinguish safe compensation from irreversible external effects, and present the owner a spoken/inspectable choice: leave as-is, compensate selected reversible steps, or resume from the exact checkpoint after a fresh precondition check. Store the partial-state snapshot and compensation result in the same receipt, rather than treating jobs/undo-last as a single global undo.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A failed multi-step request will not leave them guessing whether half the work happened or risk an indiscriminate undo. They can recover a draft or file operation safely while being warned clearly about the message, purchase, or submission that cannot be rolled back.
changes.effort: Medium: extend job step metadata with compensation descriptors and state snapshots, add recovery planning and explicit user choice, then test crashes between every pair of steps across Mac and browser adapters.
changes.risk: A compensation can itself fail or have side effects, and snapshots may contain private data. Permit only adapter-declared reversible operations, require fresh verification before compensation, encrypt/minimize snapshots, and mark the transaction unresolved if recovery cannot be proven.
changes.cost_impact: Small durable metadata overhead; one cheap background planning call only for failed multi-step jobs. No additional realtime model call beyond the status prompt.
changes.latency_impact: No cost on successful jobs; failed jobs gain seconds for recovery analysis, with immediate paused status first.
changes.security_impact: Prevents unsafe blanket replay/undo and limits recovery to the original contract scope, tab/session, and owner approval. Redact sensitive field values from receipts unless needed for recovery.
depends_on: The existing durable job/receipt and actionReceipt work
Per-step contractHash, idempotency key, and before-state evidence
Mac/browser adapters declaring which operations are compensatable
The pending verify_operation_step/verify_action_proof capability

changes.change: Implement a relay-owned Action Transaction Coordinator between the existing /execute, Mac jobs, and browser command queue. It should compile a goal into typed steps (surface, effect class, idempotency key, preconditions, approval requirement, lease expiry), dispatch one step at a time, correlate browser result or Mac receipt by the same step ID, and advance only after proof matches the precondition/postcondition. Persist a compact event log and expose GET /action-transactions/:id, POST /action-transactions/:id/approve, POST /action-transactions/:id/cancel, POST /action-transactions/:id/resume. On timeout or disconnect, freeze the lease and resume from the last proven checkpoint instead of replaying writes.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets reliable “it was done once” behavior instead of duplicated browser submissions, ambiguous Mac jobs, or a false completion after a timeout. They can leave home, reconnect later, and hear exactly which step is waiting, what evidence proves prior steps, and what can still be undone.
changes.effort: Medium-high: relay schema/state machine, adapters for existing Mac receipts and browser typed results, and tests for duplicate delivery, timeout, reconnect, approval expiry, and partial undo. No new model is required for enforcement.
changes.risk: A bad proof adapter could advance without real completion, or an overly strict one could strand work. Default closed on missing/contradictory evidence; retain receipts and offer manual resume. Never auto-retry effect=write unless the step declares an idempotency key and the target confirms it.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1 write/read overhead per step and one cheap background planning call; no material realtime cost. Evidence should be hashes/snippets with short retention, not full pages by default.
changes.latency_impact: Adds tens to hundreds of milliseconds per step for persistence and verification; avoids the much larger cost of blind 45-second browser retries.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by making approval scoped to an exact step and expiring it with the lease. Private evidence remains surface-local where possible; transaction IDs and hashes cross the relay, not secrets.
depends_on: Typed browser results and Mac action receipts must include stable step/action IDs and idempotency keys
An authenticated relay-to-pendant event path and a physical cancel/approval affordance
Owner enabling the browser bridge when private browser work is needed

changes.change: Add a tiny bistable 3-color status indicator and a vibration motor to the wearable, driven by a safety-isolated local action-state controller. The relay can publish only a compact signed state token (idle, working, waiting-for-owner, blocked, completed, failed); the pendant renders that state with color/pattern and a short vibration code, retaining the last state through LTE loss. The controller must fail closed: loss of link or an invalid/expired token can never authorize an action, and the existing user button remains a cancel/acknowledge input rather than an execution trigger.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can tell at a glance or by touch whether the system is still working, waiting for them, or stopped—even in a noisy room, while driving, or when speech cannot be heard. They stop wondering whether a request was lost, and can safely cancel a live operation without opening the Mac dashboard.
changes.effort: Moderate hardware revision and firmware protocol: add a low-power RGB LED, coin vibration motor, driver transistor, signed state-token parser, and persistence of one compact state record. Validate visibility, haptic distinguishability, and behavior across LTE reconnects before production enclosure work.
changes.risk: Extra power draw and accidental button interpretation could confuse the owner. Use distinct, documented patterns; require a deliberate long press for cancel/acknowledge; rate-limit vibration; and preserve the current LED-only fallback if the motor or token parser fails. This is an addition to the prototype, not a claim that the current DK can support it.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $2–6 in components and under 20 mA peak while indicating; negligible API cost because only a signed state token crosses the relay. Battery impact is dominated by vibration and should be duty-cycled.
changes.latency_impact: State changes reach the pendant on the next relay poll/push, typically sub-second online and eventually after reconnect; local rendering is immediate.
changes.security_impact: The indicator is intentionally non-authorizing. Signed, expiring state tokens prevent stale server state from being mistaken for approval, and no private page content is displayed or stored on the wearable.
depends_on: A relay action-state protocol that emits signed, expiring compact tokens
A pendant firmware event path that persists the last safe state and handles long-press cancel locally
A connected production pendant rather than the current unconnected development-kit situation

changes.change: Add an action-graph executor between judgement and the surface tools. Compile a decision into typed steps with required surface, fallback surfaces, preconditions, reversibility, and confirmation class. Execute ready steps independently; when a surface is offline, mark only dependent steps blocked, attempt explicitly allowlisted fallbacks (for example granted AppleScript instead of browser UI), persist step receipts and evidence, and resume when reachability changes. The final response must distinguish completed, skipped, blocked, and awaiting-confirmation steps.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A broken browser bridge or missing pendant would no longer make the whole request appear to fail—or worse, appear complete. The owner can safely say “handle it” and receive a precise partial result plus automatic continuation when the missing hand becomes available.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema, durable scheduler, surface capability registry, receipt aggregation, retry/backoff, and tests for partial completion and duplicate delivery.
changes.risk: Fallback could act in the wrong context if affinity is weak; require explicit account/tab/app identity and precondition hashes. Duplicate retries could repeat side effects; use idempotency keys and compensating undo where possible. Recover by pausing ambiguous or irreversible nodes and showing the exact blocked reason.
changes.cost_impact: Low incremental API cost; deterministic routing for most graphs, background model only when choosing among semantic fallbacks. Storage increases modestly for step receipts/evidence.
changes.latency_impact: Adds milliseconds for graph validation; offline steps return immediately as blocked/queued rather than waiting for timeout. Resume latency depends on bridge/device recovery.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by making least-privilege fallback and confirmation explicit, but requires careful redaction of receipts and strict surface/account affinity.
depends_on: Durable browser job runner (chg-16bc5dee) or equivalent step persistence
Action receipt/undo foundation (chg-5fc73ce3)
A live surface capability/health registry
Owner confirmation policy for irreversible actions

changes.change: Add an authenticated audio playback journal to the pendant: every response is addressed by pipelineId plus 20 ms frame sequence, with a 2–4 second ring buffer, CRC/underrun markers, and a single-button replay request. On reconnect it posts a compact missing-range event; the relay serves only those ranges and the Mac falls back to TTS when the source PCM has expired.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When speech drops out, the pendant repairs the sentence instead of leaving the owner guessing or forcing them to ask the whole question again. It also makes the 24 kHz path measurable in real use.
changes.effort: Medium firmware + relay integration; requires a real pendant for power/RAM testing and a simulator acceptance test first.
changes.risk: Ring-buffer pressure or replay loops could stall playback; cap retries, evict oldest frames, and expose a clear audible failure tone plus receipt. Do not flash until the owner approves and a device is connected.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible runtime/API cost; 2–4 seconds of mono s16le at 24 kHz is about 96–192 KiB, so storage should be external/streamed rather than consuming application RAM. Fallback TTS costs one speech call.
changes.latency_impact: Local repair is sub-second; network range fetch typically under 1 s; fallback regeneration several seconds.
changes.security_impact: Bind requests to authenticated pipeline/session IDs, expire audio quickly, and avoid logging PCM. Replay of sensitive audio after a delayed reconnect should be opt-in or require a button press.
depends_on: A connected pendant and measured RAM/storage budget
Relay range-fetch and idempotent audio-segment endpoint
Mac audio worker that can correlate pipeline receipts and regenerate expired PCM
24 kHz acceptance criteria and device-side audio-path probe

changes.change: Introduce a cross-surface Handoff Lease protocol. A pendant-originated handoff stores an immutable capture pointer plus a normalized goal and expiry; the relay waits for cryptographically attested Mac-bridge and browser-session presence, grants one short lease to the executor, and collects Mac receipts plus browser evidence into a single review packet. Leases expire and return to pending without duplicate execution.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can speak an unfinished task once while away and trust that it will resume at the right machine, with an understandable proof of what happened, rather than losing the request or accidentally running it twice.
changes.effort: Substantial relay/database integration, Mac and browser heartbeat changes, pendant pending-handoff controls, and dashboard review UI; requires protocol and failure-injection tests.
changes.risk: Stale or duplicated leases could perform an unintended action. Use idempotency keys, explicit expiry, surface identity binding, and stop before irreversible browser actions. If either presence attestation disappears, pause and report rather than continue.
changes.cost_impact: Small durable metadata storage and occasional background polling; no repeated realtime inference after capture. Evidence retention cost is bounded by packet TTL.
changes.latency_impact: Adds at most one presence/scheduling delay; execution itself is unchanged. Offline pendant acknowledgement remains immediate.
changes.security_impact: Raises security requirements because authenticated browser context is intentionally joined to wearable intent. Encrypt handoff payloads, minimize transcript retention, scope leases to named surfaces, and redact secrets from review packets.
depends_on: A durable handoff record and scheduler
Attested presence rather than simple online status
Typed cross-surface receipt/evidence schema
Offline pendant controls for cancel/expiry
Owner-defined policy for irreversible actions

changes.change: Install a hard preflight refusal in the executor: before dispatching any ui_click, ui_menu, type_text, press_keys, or vision step, read the live inputReachability/accessibility result from /observe. If uiActionsWillReachTheScreen is false or the probe is stale, do not invoke the action at all; return status=blocked with reason, required owner fix, and a receipt marked not-executed. Add the same gate to browser bridge writes when the extension is offline, while allowing explicitly read-only AppleScript/research actions. Make the gate decision part of the job journal so retries cannot silently turn a blocked step into a claimed success.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Right now the Mac reports UI actions as successful while doing nothing, and the browser has 9 queued commands while offline. The owner should never hear that an email was typed, a button was clicked, or a page changed when no physical action occurred. This turns silent false success into an immediate, actionable explanation and prevents unsafe retries.
changes.effort: Moderate: central executor preflight, freshness handling, typed blocked receipts, retry/journal integration, and tests for stale/failed probes across UI and browser writes.
changes.risk: A transient probe failure may block a legitimate action; recover by re-running observation and offering safe AppleScript/declarative alternatives. Never auto-bypass the gate. Existing read-only automation remains available.
changes.cost_impact: No model/API cost; one local observation per potentially interactive step and small journal entries.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 50–200 ms per interactive step; avoids 45-second browser hangs and misleading completion.
changes.security_impact: Strongly improves safety and auditability. No new data leaves the Mac; accessibility state and block reasons are already local operational metadata.
depends_on: Existing GET /observe inputReachability and uiActionsWillReachTheScreen fields
Existing actionReceipts.js and job journal
Existing browser status/queue state from GET /browser/status
A typed distinction between read-only and write actions

changes.change: Add a cross-surface causal ledger, separate from the existing per-job receipts: every action attempt must reference a predecessor evidence hash and publish a postcondition evidence hash containing the target surface, identity, timestamp, and observed state. The relay should accept a successor only when the predecessor is committed, reject duplicate effect IDs across Mac/browser/pendant, and mark the whole chain compensatable, abandoned, or needs-owner-review when a link disappears. Reconnection should reconcile by querying evidence, never by replaying the last command.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner could ask for one outcome that spans devices and leave without fearing a duplicate send, upload, or edit after a reconnect. They would receive a truthful chain such as “file created, attachment confirmed, message still unsent,” instead of a collection of locally successful receipts that cannot establish what actually happened end to end.
changes.effort: High: define signed typed evidence envelopes, durable relay state, idempotency namespace shared by local and browser executors, reconciliation, and dashboard/pendant rendering. This is protocol work between existing components, not another action queue.
changes.risk: A false postcondition or clock/identity mismatch could halt work unnecessarily; default recovery is stop and ask, never replay. Evidence retention must be bounded and redact sensitive values. Existing single-surface jobs continue using their current receipts if no causal chain is requested.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1/R2 and local journal overhead; no recurring model cost beyond optional background reconciliation.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one local ledger write and evidence validation per step (tens to hundreds of milliseconds); reconnect recovery becomes slower but deterministic.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability and prevents cross-surface duplicate side effects. Evidence must use hashes/redacted summaries rather than copying private page contents to the relay; approval scope and transaction identity must be authenticated.
depends_on: Existing action receipts and journal IDs
Relay durable state and Mac bridge connectivity
Typed observation/postcondition evidence from faculty-perception
Browser command IDs and tab/session affinity

changes.change: Add a durable DeferredIntent envelope and state machine shared by relay and Mac: intentId/idempotencyKey, normalized goal, allowed surfaces, explicit postcondition, approval class, lease expiry, retry budget, current job/command IDs, and verification state. On reconnect, resume only unexpired intents; after every completed action invoke faculty-perception through /observe or a typed inspection, then emit a signed success/failure/unknown receipt to the pendant. Keep command receipts as child records rather than treating transport completion as task success.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner says “do that later,” they get a trustworthy answer about the result—even if the browser was offline or the Mac slept—instead of silently duplicated work or a misleading “done.”
changes.effort: Medium: relay D1 schema/state machine, Mac adapter around /execute and browser command IDs, verifier callback, and pendant status rendering; add fault-injection tests for reconnect, expiry, duplicate delivery, and ambiguous verification.
changes.risk: A weak postcondition could falsely report success, and retries could duplicate side effects. Mitigate with explicit postconditions, idempotency keys, no automatic retry for irreversible actions, and an UNKNOWN result requiring review. Recover by cancelling the envelope and using existing job undo where available.
changes.cost_impact: Low storage and API overhead; roughly one background verification call per completed intent, much cheaper than realtime reasoning.
changes.latency_impact: Adds seconds after action completion for verification; immediate acknowledgement remains unchanged.
changes.security_impact: Lease and approval class prevent stale or unauthorized replay; evidence should be hashed/redacted in relay and detailed private state retained only on Mac.
depends_on: Owner pairing of a pendant so final receipts can be delivered
Browser extension online for browser-backed intents
A small verifier contract between faculty-perception and action receipts
Existing durable job/receipt and browser command IDs

changes.change: Add a pendant-first emergency stop protocol: a long press or two-button gesture emits a locally generated, replay-resistant stop nonce; relay immediately marks all active action leases for that owner as cancelled, forwards cancellation to Mac jobs and queued browser commands, and returns a terse LED/audio acknowledgement. Each affected job records whether it stopped before or after its last committed step. This is a kill switch, not an approval prompt and not dependent on speech, Accessibility, or the browser being online.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: If the owner hears an unexpected action, loses trust, or simply changes their mind, they can stop the hive from their body instantly—even while the Mac UI is stuck, the browser is unavailable, or the microphone is not open.
changes.effort: Medium: pendant firmware gesture and signed event, relay cancellation fan-out, Mac/browser cancellation adapters, and race-condition tests around already-committed steps.
changes.risk: A false trigger could cancel useful work; require a deliberate gesture and brief vibration/LED confirmation. Cancellation cannot undo an already-committed external side effect, so receipts must clearly distinguish stopped, completed, and unknown. Recover by allowing explicit resume from a checkpoint.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible per-action API cost; small firmware and relay implementation cost, with no added model calls.
changes.latency_impact: Relay cancellation should reach online Mac jobs in under 500 ms; offline browser commands are marked cancelled and prevented from later execution.
changes.security_impact: Use a device-bound key and monotonic nonce to prevent forged or replayed stops. Do not expose job contents in the pendant acknowledgement.
depends_on: A paired pendant with a working button and secure device identity
Relay fan-out cancellation for Mac jobs and browser command queues
An atomic cancelled-before-execution check in each executor

changes.change: Add a two-phase cross-surface action coordinator. Phase 1 (prepare) asks browser-extension and Mac executor to resolve each typed action against its current tab/app, capture a redacted before-state hash and proposed after-state, and reserve an idempotency key without mutating. Phase 2 (commit) executes steps in dependency order only if all required reservations are fresh; after every mutation it records proof and evaluates the postcondition. On partial failure it stops, marks the packet mixed, and invokes only declared compensations (or presents a precise manual recovery list).
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say one clear 'go' and avoid half-finished real-world tasks: no email sent from the wrong tab, no reminder duplicated after a reconnect, and no later claim of success without evidence. If one site changes while leaving, the system safely pauses instead of guessing.
changes.effort: Medium-high: typed action/precondition schema, prepare adapters for AppleScript and browser refs, coordinator state machine, durable proofs, and compensation tests across sleep/reconnect.
changes.risk: A reservation can become stale between prepare and commit; enforce short TTLs and revalidate immediately before each mutation. Compensation may itself fail, so never claim rollback without a receipt; expose mixed state and offer retry/manual recovery. Roll out read-only prepare first.
changes.cost_impact: Low API cost because prepare uses typed reads and hashes; background validation roughly $0.01–$0.04 per packet. Storage is small per step (IDs, hashes, receipts).
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–2 seconds for prepare before the first visible mutation, but reduces costly retries and duplicate actions.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety: least-privilege per surface, redacted proofs, exact tab/session binding, no irreversible commit without explicit step-level confirmation. Requires careful protection of before-state snippets and idempotency tokens.
depends_on: Shared DeparturePacket/ActionStep contract from faculty-judgement
Existing browser command queue and Mac action receipts
A durable job/coordinator store; owner-granted Accessibility remains optional for AppleScript/typed routes but GUI-only steps stay blocked

changes.change: Add a browser-bridge readiness gate and command watchdog before enqueue: require an online poll heartbeat newer than a short TTL, an attached tab/window identity, and zero stale pending commands; otherwise do not enqueue. Give each command a deadline shorter than the 45-second transport timeout, cancel/expire it explicitly, and surface a structured blocked receipt with the exact recovery (open Safari, enable bridge, dismiss dialog, or reattach tab). Add a sweeper for orphaned pendingCommands so failed browser work cannot accumulate and later run against a different tab.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner asks the mind to act, it will fail fast and explain what to fix instead of waiting nearly a minute, leaving nine queued commands, or potentially replaying an old action in a newly opened tab. This is especially important for private-account actions while the owner is away.
changes.effort: Medium: heartbeat/affinity preflight, deadline and cancellation states in the bridge queue, orphan sweeper, and tests for Safari dialogs, sleep/wake, extension restart, and tab replacement.
changes.risk: A transient heartbeat loss could reject a safe action; allow an explicit retry from the receipt, but never silently retry writes. Queue cleanup must preserve audit records while deleting executable commands. Keep the current behavior as fallback behind a feature flag.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible model/API cost; small relay storage for terminal receipts and periodic sweeper requests.
changes.latency_impact: Healthy actions start faster (sub-second preflight); blocked actions return in under 2 seconds instead of ~45 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Reduces stale-tab and replay risk by enforcing session/tab affinity and expiring commands. Do not include page contents in readiness logs.
depends_on: Existing browser command queue with request IDs and tab/session affinity
GET /browser/status
POST /browser/result/:commandId
Durable receipt storage and job cancellation semantics

changes.change: Implement a cross-surface Execution Envelope and fence coordinator. Every delegated job gets a compact signed envelope: job/thread id, monotonic checkpoint, target surface, preconditions/state hashes, idempotency key, reversible/undo handle, expiry, approval boundary, and receipt schema. Relay persists it and owns lease expiry; Mac/browser workers must validate the lease before each step and emit typed receipts. A pendant button/event or disconnect policy writes a signed pause fence; workers stop at the next safe boundary. Resume first runs reconciliation against current Mac/browser state and receipts, then advances only uncompleted idempotency keys. Dashboard and spoken status render the same envelope rather than inventing per-surface status.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: If the owner walks away or the link drops during a real task, it will stop safely and later continue without guessing or duplicating clicks, messages, or purchases. They can see one trustworthy timeline of what happened and what still needs approval.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema, relay durable storage, worker middleware in Mac/browser bridges, pendant event plumbing, reconciliation tests, and dashboard/status rendering.
changes.risk: A false pause or stale state hash could leave work unfinished; recover by preserving receipts, exposing manual resume, and allowing a fresh plan after lease expiry. A protocol bug must fail closed before irreversible steps.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage/CPU for envelopes and receipts; background reconciliation is cheap. Occasional screenshot/page extraction remains the dominant API cost.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-millisecond local fence checks; typically 1–5 seconds added on resume for state reconciliation, longer only when browser inspection is required.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by binding actions to a signed, expiring lease and explicit approval boundary. Encrypt envelopes/receipts, redact secrets and page contents, and prevent workers from accepting unsigned or cross-job replayed commands.
depends_on: Durable job runner and browser command queue must expose stable job ids and idempotency keys
Pendant must expose a pause/fence event and local indicator; currently no pendant is connected
A typed state-inspection/reconciliation operation for Mac and browser workers
Owner confirmation policy for irreversible actions

changes.change: Add a portable approval-token protocol for prepared external mutations. The planner creates a canonical redacted transaction digest plus evidence capsule and precondition snapshot; relay signs a short-lived token addressed to the paired pendant and target browser/Mac session. The pendant displays a bounded summary and offers approve/reject; approval can be queued offline but is accepted only once relay verifies pairing, expiry, nonce, and digest. Immediately before execution, the worker performs compare-and-swap against the snapshot and refuses any changed recipient, amount, destination, text, or account. Record the digest and approval in the receipt so the owner can prove exactly what they authorized.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can approve a carefully prepared real-world change from the pendant without being at the Mac, while stale pages, changed prices, altered recipients, or replayed approvals cannot silently turn into a different action.
changes.effort: Medium: canonical mutation normalization, evidence capsule storage, signed token verification in relay and workers, pendant UI/input, and compare-and-swap adapters for browser and Mac actions.
changes.risk: Over-redaction could make a summary ambiguous; fail closed and ask for a fresh preparation. Clock skew or a lost connection could delay approval; use relay-issued monotonic expiry and retain the pending transaction. Never treat a spoken 'yes' without the matching digest as authorization.
changes.cost_impact: Small relay storage/signature overhead; no additional model call for approval. Evidence capture and private-page extraction remain the main cost.
changes.latency_impact: Usually adds under 2 seconds for token delivery and one state verification before execution; changed state intentionally causes a re-preparation delay.
changes.security_impact: Reduces confused-deputy and replay risk by binding approval to exact content, session, nonce, and expiry. Requires encrypted evidence capsules, paired-device authentication, redaction, and audit retention controls.
depends_on: A normalized transaction/evidence representation across Mac and browser action types
Paired-pendant identity and reliable relay delivery
Worker compare-and-swap hooks before irreversible effects
Pendant-side approve/reject interaction and offline queue

changes.change: Add a durable cross-surface Intent Handoff protocol between pendant/relay and Mac/browser jobs. On voice capture, create an intent envelope {idempotencyKey, normalized goal, allowed read scopes, confirmation policy, createdAt, expiry}; persist only encrypted metadata in relay. When /browser/status reports the bridge online, claim the envelope exactly once, create or resume a /jobs task bound to the browser session, and stream state transitions queued→claimed→extracting→waiting-for-confirmation→completed/failed. Attach source URL/tab/timestamp/snippet hashes to the receipt, synthesize a short audio result, and let the pendant cancel or replay by intent ID. Do not auto-resubmit after ambiguous failures.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Their spoken 'read Gmail/GitHub/calendar' requests currently disappear as failures when the browser is offline. They would instead get an immediate queued acknowledgement and a reliable, cited answer later, without granting the relay access to account cookies or allowing accidental outbound actions.
changes.effort: Medium: relay envelope store and state machine, Mac bridge reconnect claimant, browser-session binding, receipt/audio callback, and pendant status/cancel UI; integration tests for duplicate delivery, expiry, reconnect, and confirmation boundaries.
changes.risk: A stale intent could run against changed page state or the wrong tab. Mitigate with session/account binding, short TTL, read-only scope, evidence snapshots, explicit re-authorization after long offline periods, and idempotency. Recover by canceling the intent and exposing the full receipt; never infer success from a lost callback.
changes.cost_impact: Small durable-storage and queue cost; approximately $0.01–$0.05 per completed read plus speech synthesis, with background-tier model usage. No credential replication to relay.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-second local acknowledgement; completion depends on bridge reconnection, then typically 30–120 seconds for three account reads.
changes.security_impact: Improves containment by keeping cookies/page bodies on Mac/browser. Encrypt intent metadata, minimize retention, redact logs, bind jobs to account/session IDs, and require pendant confirmation for any mutation.
depends_on: Owner must keep the Mac bridge and relevant browser extension online/authorized when work should resume.
Use existing job receipts and browser command idempotency rather than inventing a second action ledger.
Existing offline_intent_spool request remains unfulfilled; implement this as the relay/Mac integration rather than re-requesting the unavailable skill.

changes.change: Add a cross-surface temporal snapshot protocol. At the instant a spoken goal is accepted, the relay issues a snapshot nonce; the Mac agent records a manifest of relevant local files/apps, the browser bridge records tab URLs and bounded extraction hashes, and the perception layer records the pendant request plus timestamps. Judgement and action may reference only that nonce. The Mac review surface renders a replayable evidence bundle showing what was observed, what changed during preparation, and which facts are now stale; any mutation must revalidate the affected item immediately before execution.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner would be able to trust a preparation or recommendation even when pages, messages, or files change while the system works. They could see exactly what the mind saw, catch stale or mis-scoped evidence, and approve a result without wondering whether the action is based on an earlier tab state.
changes.effort: Medium-to-high: define a signed manifest format, capture bounded cross-surface evidence without copying secrets to the relay, persist bundles on the Mac, add freshness/revalidation checks to execution, and build a human-readable replay view.
changes.risk: Snapshots can contain sensitive content and may be mistaken for current truth. Encrypt and retain them briefly, store content locally with hashes in relay metadata, label every item with capture time and freshness, and force revalidation before any write. If capture is incomplete, the system must return an incomplete bundle rather than silently continue.
changes.cost_impact: Small relay metadata cost; local disk usage scales with bounded evidence bundles. Background extraction is cheaper than repeatedly invoking the realtime tier; replay adds negligible API cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 1–5 seconds to initial capture and a few seconds for pre-action revalidation; avoids expensive rework and unsafe retries.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability but creates a sensitive local artifact. Encrypt at rest, redact secrets from manifests, enforce per-session access, short retention, and owner deletion. Never place raw authenticated page contents in model prompts unless required.
depends_on: A shared typed evidence/manifest schema across perception, browser bridge, Mac agent, and action receipts.
A Mac-side review/replay surface and local encrypted evidence store.
Execution must accept and verify a snapshot nonce and perform last-mile revalidation before writes.

changes.change: Add a postcondition verifier between action receipts and perception: every reversible action may carry a typed expectedState (file hash/exists, app frontmost, reminder presence, browser URL/text fingerprint, volume level). After dispatch, the local agent runs a fresh independent observation, stores before/after evidence and observedAt in the receipt, and classifies verified, contradicted, or unknown. A durable retry worker re-observes delayed effects without replaying the action; relay_job_status and the pendant receive the classification rather than treating executor success as completion.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner says “do it,” they get an honest answer about the world, not merely that a command returned successfully. It prevents silent failures and duplicate side effects when an app is slow or a browser tab changes.
changes.effort: Medium: typed postcondition schema, observers for file/app/browser/reminder, receipt fields, retry state machine, and dashboard/spoken rendering; no Accessibility required for file, AppleScript, and browser-bridge observations.
changes.risk: A stale or overly broad postcondition could produce unknown/false contradiction; default to unknown and never retry the side effect. Recover by showing evidence and allowing a deliberate re-check. Browser/account reads remain private and authenticated.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage for bounded evidence and no meaningful API cost; semantic GUI verification may use one cheaper local-model call.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–800 ms for deterministic checks; delayed effects move to background verification.
changes.security_impact: Receipts may contain private URLs, snippets, and file hashes; redact content by default, retain only typed evidence unless the owner asks for detail.
depends_on: Existing actionReceipts.js and GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts
An implementation of the pending verify_operation_step tool or equivalent local-agent verifier
Perception contract defining evidence freshness and confidence

changes.change: Add a low-power BLE central/peripheral presence channel to the pendant product, with a locally authenticated rolling token and a small nonvolatile pending-intent journal. Firmware emits signed connect/disconnect/proximity events to the relay and uses the existing single LED plus button to expose waiting, ready, expired, and confirmation-required states. Keep the audio/I2S path unchanged; this is a separate control-plane feature, not an audio-path assumption.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant can tell the system that the owner is really back at the intended Mac or has deliberately returned to an action, so deferred work happens at the right moment instead of firing while they are away or silently expiring.
changes.effort: Hardware revision or validated BLE-capable radio firmware, secure pairing/token rotation, a small event protocol, and relay persistence; prototype first with the existing radio if its firmware supports authenticated advertising, otherwise add a sub-$5 BLE beacon/SoC.
changes.risk: False proximity could release an intent too early, and a lost pendant could leave work waiting. Use proximity only as a readiness signal, never sole authorization for irreversible actions; require the button for those. Expire journals and provide cancellation from the dashboard. Recover with explicit pending/expired state.
changes.cost_impact: Prototype firmware cost is low; a new beacon/radio component is roughly $3–8 in volume and tens of milliwatts only during brief scans/advertisements, with a small battery-life impact.
changes.latency_impact: Presence transitions can be detected in roughly 1–5 seconds depending on scan interval; no impact on conversational audio when scheduled outside I2S handling.
changes.security_impact: Pairing identifiers and intent metadata must be encrypted/authenticated; avoid broadcasting owner identity or task text. Rotate tokens and reject replayed events.
depends_on: Conditional-intent relay state machine
Authenticated pendant event ingestion
A cross-surface pending-intent display and explicit confirmation path

changes.change: Implement a resumable cross-surface approval envelope and job state machine between the existing planner/executor, browser queue, pipeline, and receipts. When an action reaches a declared gate, persist {jobId, actionId, target surface/tab, redacted preview, precondition hash, effect class, expiry, nonce}; emit a pipeline event and pendant prompt. Accept exactly one authenticated confirmation carrying the nonce, re-check the precondition, then resume the same actionId (never re-plan or replay completed IDs). On mismatch/expiry/disconnect, transition to held and require a fresh preview. Append the prompt, confirmation, re-check, and final receipt to the existing job and pipeline records.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can leave the Mac and still safely finish a real browser or desktop task from the pendant, without a stale dashboard approval silently authorizing changed content. Jobs become recoverable rather than abandoned when a bridge or browser session drops.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared state schema and migration, relay event/confirmation route, Mac executor gate/resume handling, browser command correlation, pendant UI/firmware event support, and end-to-end disconnect/replay tests.
changes.risk: A bug could resume the wrong action or duplicate a send. Mitigate with single-use nonces, action hashes, idempotent action IDs, expiry, precondition re-check, explicit irreversible confirmation, and default hold on uncertainty. Recovery is cancel/undo where available; otherwise preserve the held envelope and receipt for review.
changes.cost_impact: Small durable relay storage and a few pipeline events per gated action; one short realtime prompt. No continuous model cost while held.
changes.latency_impact: Adds approximately 100–500 ms for persistence and precondition re-check; resume target under 3 s after pendant confirmation.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by constraining approval to an exact redacted action and tab/session, but introduces a sensitive confirmation channel. Use bearer-authenticated device identity, nonce replay protection, encrypted transport, and avoid storing page contents in the envelope.
depends_on: A real precondition gate in the executor (the current actionReceipts implementation records receipts but explicitly does not gate)
Pendant online event/confirmation transport; otherwise dashboard-only fallback
Durable relay job runner and browser command correlation
Owner-defined confirmation policy for irreversible effects

changes.change: Add a deterministic contingency-policy engine that runs after every failed, timed-out, or partially completed Mac/browser step. Policies are compiled into an allowlisted decision table before execution (for example: browser timeout → capture current URL/title and save local draft; permission failure → notify and hold; changed precondition → discard draft and request review; network loss → retry once then cancel). The engine must atomically checkpoint safe artifacts, emit a typed pipeline event, and attach the selected rule plus evidence to the existing receipt. It must never infer permission for a new side effect from a natural-language failure summary.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Tasks stop failing ambiguously while the owner is away. Their chosen safe fallback happens predictably, unfinished work is preserved as a draft or cleanly canceled, and the owner can understand exactly why the system stopped or changed course.
changes.effort: Medium: policy schema and validator, failure taxonomy, checkpoint adapters for local files/browser drafts/relay alerts, receipt and dashboard rendering, plus fault-injection tests for duplicate delivery and partial completion.
changes.risk: An overly broad rule could create or retain sensitive drafts, or misclassify a partial action. Mitigate with deny-by-default scopes, per-site/app limits, expiration, dry-run simulation, immutable rule IDs in receipts, and a hold state whenever classification is uncertain. Recovery is cancel or existing undo.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and compute for deterministic rules; occasional background summarization only when the owner asks for a human-readable explanation.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 50–300 ms for policy lookup and checkpointing; network/browser recovery may take longer but is bounded by the selected rule.
changes.security_impact: Reduces unsafe retries and silent partial changes. Checkpoints must be encrypted or local-only by default, with redaction before relay notification; policies cannot authorize sends, purchases, deletion, or publication.
depends_on: A durable job/event store shared by Mac, browser, and relay
Typed failure and partial-completion evidence from executors
Atomic local/browser checkpoint adapters
Dashboard and pendant notification delivery

changes.change: Install a mandatory action-preflight gate between faculty-judgement plans and every mutating executor. For each step, require a fresh signed observation (<=15 s) proving the target surface is reachable: Mac inputReachability/uiActionsWillReachTheScreen for UI actions, browser extension online plus matching session/tab for browser actions, and a live lease for any pendant-triggered action. If the proof is absent, stale, or mismatched, do not dispatch; persist a blocked receipt with the exact missing precondition and wake/re-evaluate on the next device heartbeat. Include the observation hash and expiry in the final receipt so a later agent can tell whether the action really reached the world.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The system currently reports UI actions as successful while doing nothing and has nine browser commands pending against an offline bridge. This prevents silent no-ops, avoids replaying stale browser work, and tells the owner exactly what must recover before an action can safely happen.
changes.effort: Medium: shared executor middleware, signed observation schema, TTL/heartbeat watcher, blocked-receipt state and tests across Mac and browser backends.
changes.risk: A false-negative preflight may delay a harmless action; recover by allowing an explicit owner-approved override for a named step and recording it. Never auto-replay a mutating step after recovery without revalidation.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API/storage cost; one small observation record per attempted step and occasional heartbeat checks.
changes.latency_impact: Adds <100 ms when healthy; blocked work waits for recovery rather than consuming repeated 20–45 s browser timeouts.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by binding execution to fresh reachability proof; observation hashes reveal state metadata but no page contents or secrets.
depends_on: verify_operation_step tool or equivalent shared preflight API
action lease/receipt schema integration
browser bridge heartbeat and Mac inputReachability observation

changes.change: Add a cross-surface completion ledger and verifier: every judgement action carries an idempotency key, expected postcondition (typed entity/field/operator/value), evidence scope, deadline, and approval class. The relay persists state planned→dispatched→observed→verified|unverified|failed; the Mac executor/browser bridge reports dispatch receipts only, while faculty-perception (or a cheaper verifier worker) must attach fresh, redacted evidence from the target surface before the ledger emits completion. On timeout, retry only idempotent reads or surface a pending/unverified state; never replay a write merely because verification is late. Emit state transitions to /pipeline/events and expose a compact owner-facing receipt linked to existing job receipts and undo.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can trust 'done' again: a reminder, browser update, or message is confirmed at its destination instead of merely accepted by a local process. If the browser disappears or an action partially succeeds, they hear exactly that and get a safe next step rather than a false success or duplicate write.
changes.effort: Medium: shared JSON schema and D1/atomic-store state machine, adapters for existing /execute and browser command results, one verifier worker plus redaction tests, and pendant/dashboard event rendering. Start with Reminders and one browser read/write flow.
changes.risk: A stale or wrong verifier could falsely confirm; mitigate with source timestamps, expected-value comparisons, bounded freshness, and explicit unverified status. Duplicate writes remain possible for inherently non-idempotent actions, so those require approval and no automatic retry. Existing jobs must continue to parse their current receipts and be migrated as unknown/unverified rather than silently marked done.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and relay CPU; background verifier calls add roughly $0.005–$0.03 per task depending on browser extraction. No new hardware required.
changes.latency_impact: Immediate acknowledgement remains unchanged; final completion adds typically 1–10 seconds, with longer waits moved to durable background polling.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability but creates more evidence records. Store hashes/snippets and field names rather than raw private pages, encrypt/expire evidence, and keep credentials confined to the Mac/browser session.
depends_on: A typed postcondition schema and action idempotency key emitted by faculty-judgement
A relay event/push path to the pendant
A faculty-perception verifier that can read Mac and authenticated browser state
Owner approval policy for non-idempotent effects

changes.change: Build an evidence ledger and receipt reducer spanning Mac jobs, browser commands, relay pipeline events, and pendant telemetry. Every event gets a monotonic event ID, source/device identity, source timestamp plus ingestion timestamp, job/action/artifact linkage, and one of queued/accepted/executing/executed/delivered/played/failed/unknown. Reducer rules must never promote state from historical acceptance or timeout; stale or contradictory sources produce unknown with reasons. Expose a per-action timeline and freshness badge through the existing job receipts/ops snapshot, and let faculty-action request a retry only after faculty-judgement sees the explicit unknown state.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner will stop being told “done” when a command is merely queued, a browser is offline, Mac input cannot reach the UI, or speech was accepted by the relay but never played on the pendant. They get a truthful, actionable status and can safely retry or wait.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared event schema and persistence, reducer tests for contradictory/out-of-order events, adapters for four producers, dashboard and spoken summary formatting.
changes.risk: Clock skew, duplicate events, and partial outages can create unknown states; recover by using server ingestion ordering, idempotency keys, bounded reconciliation, and preserving raw evidence for audit. Never auto-retry irreversible actions.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1/JSON storage and background CPU; negligible model cost because summaries can be generated from typed state, with realtime model only for conversational explanation.
changes.latency_impact: Cached status is immediate; fresh reconciliation typically adds under 1–3 seconds and should not block an already completed local action.
changes.security_impact: Cross-surface evidence joins private URLs, paths, and audio metadata; encrypt or minimize payloads, hash content where possible, enforce per-owner job access, and redact secrets before relay/dashboard projection.
depends_on: Pendant-side authoritative delivery/playback acknowledgements
A durable browser command/result identity and tab affinity (existing queue is offline with pending commands)
Relay pipeline telemetry carrying device identity and source timestamps
Integration hooks in actionReceipts.js and browser result handlers

changes.change: Add a causal-state layer around each plan: capture a minimal, provenance-tagged read-only baseline immediately before execution; propagate one correlation ID through Mac action receipts, browser command/results, relay pipeline events, and device acknowledgements; capture the same typed fields afterward; and compute an expected-versus-observed delta. Mark fields as expected, incidental, unexplained, or unverifiable. For external services, use field hashes and stable identifiers rather than retaining page contents. Expose the preflight prediction and postflight delta as a signed artifact attached to the job, not as an inferred sentence in the model prompt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can see exactly what changed due to an instruction and spot duplicate sends, wrong targets, partial execution, or unexpected account/file changes—even when an application and the local executor both claim success.
changes.effort: High: define typed snapshot adapters, correlation propagation, field-level provenance, diff classification, retention limits, and adversarial tests for retries, concurrent changes, and stale browser tabs.
changes.risk: Unrelated changes may occur between snapshots, and external systems may hide state. Preserve uncertainty rather than attributing it; use narrow observation windows, stable IDs, server timestamps, and an explicit 'could not attribute' result. Never block emergency read-only actions on a complete baseline.
changes.cost_impact: Moderate local storage and API reads; compact hashes keep retention inexpensive. Occasional background reconciliation costs less than realtime inference.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 1–5 seconds around consequential actions; read-only actions can use asynchronous postflight diffing.
changes.security_impact: Baseline and delta artifacts can reveal sensitive account state. Minimize fields, hash content, encrypt artifacts, enforce per-job access, and automatically expire raw observation material.
depends_on: A shared correlation ID propagated across all surfaces
Read-only state adapters for Mac, browser, relay, and pendant
Authoritative device acknowledgements where physical output is claimed
A typed provenance and freshness policy

changes.change: Add a durable, idempotent action-bundle protocol spanning relay and Mac agent. Each bundle contains a requestId, normalized target, exact parameters hash, preconditions, postconditions, expiry, confirmation token (if needed), and preferred executor. Dispatch must first re-check readiness and preconditions; execution emits receipts; faculty-perception independently probes the postcondition through typed APIs/AppleScript/browser inspection. Only a verified postcondition transitions the bundle to completed. Offline browser, missing permissions, absent pendant, timeout, or ambiguous UI transitions to queued/blocked/unknown with a retry policy and never to done. Surface the same state and evidence capsule in relay speech and dashboard, and make retries/undo use the same idempotency key.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops having to guess whether “done” means done. Long or cross-device requests survive leaving the house, avoid duplicate sends, and explain exactly why work is waiting or unverifiable.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and D1/local persistence, executor adapters, postcondition probes, and dashboard/relay rendering; then fault-injection tests for offline and timeout cases.
changes.risk: A strict verifier may mark real work unknown when a site has no readable confirmation, so provide a safe “needs review” state and never auto-retry irreversible actions. Recovery is manual review or a bounded retry with the same idempotency key.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1/local storage and polling cost; background model only for ambiguous evidence. Vision calls are exceptional. No new hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one verification round trip after execution; fast typed probes remain under seconds, while browser verification may take tens of seconds.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by binding approval to exact parameters and expiry, minimizing replay and duplicate execution. Evidence should be redacted by sensitivity class before relay storage.
depends_on: A durable job runner and existing receipt/undo records
A typed verification/proof tool (currently requested but not yet available)
Browser extension recovery/online polling for private pages
Actual pendant connection before spoken delivery acknowledgements can be trusted

changes.change: Add a low-power haptic actuator and a three-color status LED (or an RGB LED) to the next pendant revision, with a tiny event protocol from relay: accepted, waiting-for-device, executing, verified, needs-owner, and failed. Keep the existing single button semantics. The firmware should render these states locally from signed short events and fall back to a distinct error pattern when the link drops; it must not imply completion until the relay sends the verified state.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can tell at a glance or by touch whether a request was merely heard, is waiting for the Mac/browser, or was actually verified—without opening a phone or trusting a possibly stale spoken response in a noisy place.
changes.effort: Low-to-medium hardware revision plus firmware event/state handling and relay mapping; validate visibility, haptic distinctness, and battery impact in real wear tests.
changes.risk: Extra notifications could become distracting or reveal sensitive activity in public. Make haptics opt-in per sensitivity class, use neutral patterns by default, and ensure loss of connectivity never freezes the device in a false success state. Recovery is a reboot-safe neutral/unknown pattern.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $1–4 BOM increase for actuator, driver/passives, and RGB LED; roughly 5–20 mA only during short haptic/LED pulses, near-zero idle draw. No model/API cost.
changes.latency_impact: Local indication is immediate after relay delivery; verified indication still waits on the real execution and probe path.
changes.security_impact: Use opaque patterns for sensitive jobs and do not encode message content. Signed event type plus expiry prevents spoofed completion indications.
depends_on: A real pendant hardware revision (current board is a prototype with one LED and no connected device)
Relay action-bundle states and authoritative postcondition verification
Firmware update path and power-budget measurement

changes.change: Implement an intent-drift firewall at the final-commit boundary. Faculty-judgement emits a canonical, expiring intent capsule with typed fields (actor, recipient, destination, amount, object, scope, attachments, side effects, and allowed alternatives). Every Mac, AppleScript, and browser executor must submit its final mutation capsule to the firewall before committing. The firewall performs deterministic field comparisons plus a policy-driven semantic comparison, invalidates stale approvals when tab/session/page identity or material fields change, and returns allow, block, or ask-owner-with-diff. Resume tokens must be single-use and parameter-bound; retries cannot bypass the firewall.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets protection against a subtle but costly failure: the system completes the workflow it inferred rather than the action the owner actually authorized. They see only a short exception when something materially changed, not repetitive approval prompts.
changes.effort: High integration effort: define the shared schema, instrument every executor, build field extractors and policy tests, then fault-test changed recipients, amounts, tabs, attachments, and partial retries.
changes.risk: Overly strict comparison may interrupt legitimate edits, while weak extraction may miss drift. Default uncertain cases to ask-owner for irreversible effects, allow only explicitly safe alternatives, and retain a human-readable before/after diff for recovery.
changes.cost_impact: Small persistent capsules and deterministic comparisons; occasional cheap semantic-model calls and rare realtime clarification. No hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-second for typed fields; roughly 1–3 seconds when semantic extraction is required, before an irreversible commit.
changes.security_impact: Reduces replay, confused-deputy, wrong-recipient, and stale-approval risk. Capsules must be encrypted or minimized, expire quickly, and exclude raw private page content unless needed for the diff.
depends_on: A shared action protocol across relay and local Mac agent
Typed final-value extraction from browser and app adapters
An owner confirmation/resume channel on the pendant or dashboard

changes.change: Add a cross-surface action transaction coordinator between /execute, the Mac action runner, and browser command queue. Before execution it assigns a transactionId and records each step's precondition, target surface, reversibility class, and expected proof. After every step it persists before/after evidence and a compensation recipe. On timeout or contradictory result, it freezes later steps, asks the Mac/browser surfaces for fresh state, runs only safe compensations in reverse order, and exposes a human-readable recovery packet through relay_job_status and job receipts. Irreversible steps become hard boundaries that require owner confirmation before continuation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a multi-step task half-completes, the owner will know exactly what changed and get the safe parts restored instead of manually investigating duplicate tabs, half-filled forms, or uncertain Mac state.
changes.effort: Medium-high: coordinator state machine, typed compensation metadata in both harnesses, fresh-state probes, and failure-injection tests.
changes.risk: A bad compensation could itself alter data or create duplicates. Default to no-op when proof is missing, use idempotency keys, and preserve receipts; recover by stopping and presenting the packet.
changes.cost_impact: Low persistent storage and a few deterministic Mac/browser calls; roughly $0.01–$0.05 only when a failure needs model-assisted classification.
changes.latency_impact: Adds ~1–3 seconds of receipt/state persistence per step; failure recovery takes 5–15 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability but stores more private before/after metadata. Encrypt sensitive values, store hashes/snippets by default, and never send private page contents to third-party services.
depends_on: A durable browser job runner and typed browser queue must expose step-level results.
Mac actions must return stable idempotency keys and before/after proof.
Owner approval policy must distinguish reversible compensation from irreversible continuation.

changes.change: Add a fast, non-mutating browser preflight gate before any browser_* step: verify the selected session/tab's bridge heartbeat, tab identity, and command-poll age within a short deadline (for example 2 seconds), then classify it as ready, stale, offline, or blocked-dialog. Do not enqueue a 45-second navigate when the bridge is known unavailable. For public URLs only, route a clearly labeled fallback to the server browser backend; for authenticated URLs, fail immediately with a one-line owner-repair instruction and preserve the intended action without retrying. Record the preflight result in the job receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The current failure mode wastes nearly a minute per attempt and leaves the owner guessing whether Safari changed. The owner gets an immediate, honest answer and public research can still proceed while private pages remain protected.
changes.effort: Low-medium: heartbeat endpoint/command, session classification, router branch, and tests for stale/offline/blocked-dialog states.
changes.risk: A false-ready result could still time out; use a hard deadline and retain the existing timeout. A public fallback must never receive private URLs, cookies, or page text; require explicit URL classification.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage; reduces failed realtime/model calls and Mac round trips.
changes.latency_impact: Healthy actions add <2 seconds; unhealthy actions return in ~2 seconds instead of ~45 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Positive if URL classification is deny-by-default and private session IDs cannot be sent to the public backend.
depends_on: A bridge heartbeat or last-poll timestamp exposed by the browser bridge.
The existing browser job router must distinguish authenticated session-bound work from public URL work.

changes.change: Add an Action Transaction Coordinator between /plan, /execute, the job queue, Mac/browser executors, and the reporting surfaces. Persist one transaction per owner-approved intent with an idempotency key, action lease expiry, ordered steps, preconditions, postconditions, and evidence references. Dispatch only leased steps; accept typed executor receipts; run read-only postcondition checks through AppleScript/typed Mac routes or the bound browser session; classify each step as verified, failed, blocked, or unknown. On bridge/browser recovery, resume only unexpired, uncommitted leases and never replay a verified step. Expose a compact status/evidence endpoint for relay-realtime and a durable event stream for the pendant when one exists.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner will stop hearing “done” when the Mac merely queued a command, and will not accidentally perform an action twice after a disconnect. They get a clear, evidence-backed answer—what changed, what did not, and what needs their decision—even when the browser or Mac disappears mid-task.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared transaction schema and migrations, coordinator worker, executor adapters, postcondition library for common Calendar/Mail/Finder/browser operations, recovery tests, and a small status projection.
changes.risk: A wrong postcondition could falsely report success or trigger an unsafe retry. Default to unknown and stop on ambiguity; require idempotency and explicit confirmation for irreversible steps. Recover by canceling expired leases and retaining immutable receipts.
changes.cost_impact: Small persistent D1/R2 metadata cost and background polling; model cost near zero for typed checks, with occasional cheap summarization. No hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one typed verification round trip (usually <2 s); asynchronous tasks are reported through status rather than blocking voice.
changes.security_impact: Store hashes, identifiers, timestamps, and minimal snippets instead of private page contents; enforce bearer auth and per-session affinity. Never export credentials or raw authenticated-page data to the relay by default.
depends_on: Durable job runner (chg-16bc5dee) or equivalent queue worker
Step verification/proof tools already requested but not yet delivered
Owner confirmation and action-lease policy
At least one online executor; current Mac bridge is online but browser and pendant are offline

changes.change: Implement a reconnect quarantine for pending browser commands. When the extension heartbeat returns, stop automatic execution, inventory all queued commands with request/idempotency key, target tab/session, age, and intended mutation, compare them with relay/Mac transaction records, and mark each as duplicate, stale, safe-to-resume, or requiring fresh approval. Resume only read-only or explicitly re-approved mutations; publish a reconciliation brief and preserve a per-command audit trail.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The browser is currently offline with nine pending commands. When it comes back, the owner should not face a burst of stale clicks, duplicate submissions, or actions against the wrong tab. They get one concise review of what survived the outage and safe continuation only where intent is still valid.
changes.effort: Medium: queue metadata and transaction lookup, heartbeat transition hook, quarantine state, reconciliation worker, and a review/status endpoint.
changes.risk: A classifier may misjudge whether a command is stale or duplicate. Fail closed for mutations, retain commands for explicit review, and allow cancellation without execution. Recovery is deterministic replay only after a new lease and approval.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and one background reconciliation pass; no extra model call for key/age/session checks, optional low-cost summary for the review brief.
changes.latency_impact: Adds a short inventory delay after reconnect; read-only commands can resume within seconds, while mutations wait for review.
changes.security_impact: Keep private URL/page details local to the browser/Mac; relay receives only command type, session fingerprint, timestamps, and hashes. Require bearer authentication and do not log form contents.
depends_on: Browser command queue with request IDs, idempotency keys, and tab/session affinity (chg-14accc01)
A durable transaction/lease record connecting browser commands to /jobs receipts
Browser heartbeat/poll/result routes
Owner confirmation policy for stale or irreversible commands

changes.change: Introduce a capability-token authority layer shared by faculty-judgement, relay, Mac, and browser executors. Judgement issues a signed, narrow token containing policy ID/version, permitted operation grammar, resource/account scope, quantitative limits, sensitive-field exclusions, expiry, max uses, and required confirmation levels. Before every concrete Mac or browser step, the executor verifies the token against the normalized step and consumes a nonce; a mismatch hard-stops without dispatch. The relay exposes revoke-all and token-status, while the Mac/browser surfaces return the exact failed predicate. Persist only token hashes and audit metadata, and support an offline revocation cache on the Mac so a stale grant cannot survive relay loss.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can delegate routine authority without handing the system a vague promise or permanent access. A mistaken interpretation becomes a blocked step with a precise explanation, not an accidental purchase, message, deletion, or account change. Revoking authority remains possible even during a network outage.
changes.effort: High: policy grammar, signed-token issuance/verification, normalization of Mac and browser actions, nonce/replay protection, revocation distribution/cache, UI for review/revoke, and adversarial boundary tests.
changes.risk: Normalization bugs could either over-block useful work or authorize a step that only appears equivalent. Fail closed, use conservative operation grammars, require explicit confirmation for unknown verbs, and ship test vectors for account, amount, recipient, time, and sensitive-field boundaries. Recovery is token revocation and manual one-time approval.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1 metadata and signature-verification overhead; no recurring model cost for in-scope checks. Engineering cost is substantial; no hardware purchase required, though an offline pendant revoke control would be a later enhancement.
