A relay endpoint that returns redacted pending-operation summaries

changes.change: Implement a privacy-preserving Safari Reading List adapter on the Mac: snapshot the newest N entries locally, assign short-lived opaque IDs and a content hash, expose only requested title/domain snippets to the planner, and return a postcondition receipt when an ID is opened.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: It directly fixes the owner’s repeated failed request for the newest Safari Reading List items and makes follow-ups like “open the second one” reliable even when the browser has multiple tabs.
changes.effort: Medium: AppleScript/Safari integration, stable cursor storage, freshness checks, and receipt wiring through the existing browser command ledger.
changes.risk: Safari changes or a stale list could cause the wrong item to open; refuse on hash mismatch and ask again. Never expose full Reading List contents to the relay by default.
changes.cost_impact: No hardware cost; tiny local storage and roughly $0.01/query for optional normalization.
changes.latency_impact: Local extraction 1–3 s; opening 1–5 s depending on Safari.
changes.security_impact: Keeps URLs and titles on the Mac unless explicitly requested; opaque IDs prevent relay-side browsing of the list.
depends_on: Safari automation permission (currently granted)
A browser cursor API with expiry
Fresh browser postcondition verification

changes.change: Add an owner-controlled provenance graph that links a pendant utterance, relay interpretation, browser/Mac observations, executed receipts, and independently verified postconditions into an append-only chain. Expose a plain-language timeline and allow the owner to delete payloads while retaining only non-reversible audit hashes when they choose.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner would be able to answer “what did you hear, what did you see, what did you do, and how do you know?” after a long-running task—without trusting an opaque assistant history or retaining every private transcript forever.
changes.effort: High: define event IDs and causal links across relay, Mac, browser, and verifier; persist encrypted metadata; build deletion/redaction semantics and a compact dashboard timeline. It must integrate existing ledgers rather than create a second action log.
changes.risk: Incorrect links could make unrelated evidence appear connected, and deletion could break later explanations. Recover with explicit unknown links, immutable event IDs, provenance confidence, and a two-stage delete that clearly distinguishes payload removal from retained hashes.
changes.cost_impact: Low per-event API cost; storage and indexing grow with action volume but can be bounded by retention policy. No new hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Near-zero on the critical action path if events are appended asynchronously; verification and timeline assembly may take seconds.
changes.security_impact: Highly sensitive metadata: encrypt at rest, minimize cross-surface content, keep page secrets and raw audio out of the graph, and require owner confirmation for exports. Hashes must not be treated as proof of content availability after deletion.
depends_on: A canonical event-envelope schema shared by relay, Mac, browser, and faculty-perception
Existing action ledger, job receipts, journal, and verify_operation_step integration
Owner-configurable retention and deletion policy

changes.change: Add a durable operation coordinator that treats every cross-surface request as an append-only step graph: each step has an idempotency key, executor receipt, independent verification receipt, compensation (if any), expiry, and state {planned, approved, running, verified, unknown, cancelled}. Freeze downstream steps on unknown; expose a recovery choice instead of retrying. Correlate verify_operation_step with operation_id plus executor attempt_id, and persist the digest so a later approval cannot be replayed against a changed plan.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a task half-completes, the owner gets an honest answer and a safe way forward instead of duplicate messages, double purchases, or a false success. It also makes the pendant's outcome beacon meaningful because each status corresponds to a real durable state.
changes.effort: Medium-high: coordinator schema, migration from existing job/receipt records, atomic transitions, and adapters for Mac/browser executors.
changes.risk: Migration bugs could strand existing jobs or mark an action unknown unnecessarily. Roll out read-only shadow state first, reconcile against existing receipts, and preserve the current cancel/undo paths as fallback.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and relay compute; a few additional verifier calls per step. No new hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly one persistence and one verification round per step; deliberate but bounded. It prevents costly and dangerous blind retries.
changes.security_impact: Improves replay resistance and auditability. Must encrypt sensitive evidence references, keep secrets out of operation digests, and enforce expiry/monotonic state transitions.
depends_on: verify_operation_step must accept an executor attempt_id/action correlation field
A canonical idempotency-key scheme for browser and Mac action adapters
Owner policy for which compensations may run without a new physical approval

changes.change: Add a discrete secure element with protected monotonic counters and signing keys to the pendant revision, and route the existing approval/outcome protocol through it. Pair it with a fuel-gauge IC on the battery rail so every signed event carries an honest power-health state and the device can refuse new high-risk transactions before brownout.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets confirmations that remain trustworthy even if pendant flash is reset or firmware storage is inspected, plus a pendant that says 'I cannot safely complete this' before dying mid-action instead of appearing to approve something and disappearing. Battery percentage and low-power behavior become dependable enough for an everyday jewellery device.
changes.effort: Medium hardware respin and firmware integration: I2C/SPI secure-element driver, key provisioning ceremony, monotonic-counter migration, fuel-gauge calibration, and relay verification changes. Existing approval-latch and outcome-beacon semantics remain the user-facing behavior.
changes.risk: Provisioning mistakes could permanently orphan a pendant; recovery requires a controlled factory re-enrollment path. Fuel-gauge calibration can initially be inaccurate across batteries. Roll out in shadow mode, compare gauge readings against measured voltage/current, and accept old unsigned events only during an explicit migration window.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $2–$6 added components and PCB/enclosure work per unit; secure-element and gauge consume negligible standby power compared with the radio and audio bridge. No per-invocation API cost.
changes.latency_impact: Usually under 50 ms for signing and counter operations; low-battery checks are local and immediate. Initial secure-element enrollment adds a one-time setup step.
changes.security_impact: Substantially improves resistance to replay, flash rollback, forged approval/outcome events, and counter reset. The private key never enters relay, Mac, browser, or model context. Battery telemetry should be treated as operational metadata, not a secret.
depends_on: The existing physical transaction approval latch and tactile outcome beacon must define the canonical envelope and migration rules
Relay and faculty-perception must verify secure-element signatures and monotonic counters
A safe owner-visible enrollment/replacement flow must exist before production use

changes.change: Add a first-class operation_attempt record shared by planner, executor, verifier, undo, and the pendant outcome beacon. Each side-effecting step gets an opaque operation_id, attempt_id, step_id, declared postconditions, idempotency class, and terminal evidence status; receipts and verification results append to the same immutable journal rather than being joined heuristically by timestamps.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner asks what happened, the system can point to the exact attempt and step instead of confusing retries, drafts, and similarly timed actions. Failures become safe to explain and resume rather than silently duplicate.
changes.effort: Medium: schema migration, adapters at execute/verify/undo, and dashboard rendering.
changes.risk: Old jobs lack IDs and must remain readable as legacy/unknown. A bad join could falsely certify a side effect, so certification must require exact IDs and fresh verifier evidence; otherwise return unknown.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and request overhead; no new model call is required.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one journal append per step and negligible read latency; verification remains the dominant delay.
changes.security_impact: Opaque IDs reduce accidental content leakage. Never store page contents in the operation record; store hashes/minimal provenance according to sensitivity.
depends_on: The existing verify_operation_step tool
A narrow actionId/attemptId addition to verifier input/output
Existing action ledger and approval handoff

changes.change: Integrate the owned LSM6DSOX through i2c2 and emit a tiny signed motion-state event stream (still, walking, vigorous-motion, uncertain) with hysteresis and local raw-data discard. Pair it with a pendant quiet-state bit and bounded notification-count inbox, not audio or raw IMU uploads.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant can stop speaking private notifications while the owner is moving, then quietly indicate that something is waiting. It makes the wearable socially safe without requiring the Mac to see or retain movement traces.
changes.effort: Medium: enable devicetree i2c2, add sensor polling/calibration, low-power thresholds, event signing, and relay policy integration; bench-test over USB before any product transport work.
changes.risk: False still/moving classifications could suppress an urgent alert. Urgent policy must bypass suppression, uncertain must default quiet, and a watchdog should disable sensing rather than block recording/audio. No hardware flashing is authorized by this proposal.
changes.cost_impact: No new parts; modest battery draw from periodic IMU polling, likely a few mA while active, to be measured on the 500 mAh cell.
changes.latency_impact: Under 200 ms state transitions with a 50–100 Hz sensor sample; negligible impact on the 24 kHz codec if work is event-driven.
changes.security_impact: Raw accelerometer/gyro data stays local and is discarded; only coarse signed state and counters leave the device.
depends_on: Existing LSM6DSOX and i2c2 wiring
A relay notification urgency policy
A device-event ingestion contract on POST /pipeline/events

changes.change: Integrate the owned LSM6DSOX on i2c2 as a low-rate local safety classifier: sample accelerometer/gyro, derive still/moving/impact/unknown with hysteresis, sign a compact sequence-numbered state envelope, and never export raw motion vectors. Add a safe default that high-risk approvals pause on unknown or motion.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant can prevent an accidental send or purchase while the owner's hand is in motion, without recording or transmitting their movements.
changes.effort: Moderate firmware work: enable i2c2, driver/config, bounded classifier, signing/sequence plumbing, and bench tests; no new hardware.
changes.risk: False motion holds could delay an urgent action; false stillness could weaken the gate. Recover by defaulting unknown to hold, showing a distinct haptic pattern, and allowing explicit later retry. Sensor/I2C faults must not brick recording/audio.
changes.cost_impact: No API inference cost; existing sensor and negligible incremental power at low duty cycle. Engineering and test cost only.
changes.latency_impact: Under 100 ms local classification; negligible impact to 24 kHz audio if sampling is scheduled outside codec-critical work.
changes.security_impact: Improves consent safety while reducing data exposure: only coarse signed state leaves the pendant; no location or raw IMU stream.
depends_on: A relay policy hook for motion holds
Signed state envelope verification on relay
Owner-configurable risk policy

changes.change: Define an INBOX card protocol over the existing typed pendant store: opaque card ID, category, expiry, sensitivity, redacted summary, checksum, replay/ack state, and optional audio artifact ID. Add rotary selection and second-button actions (next, hear, dismiss) while preserving the current sw0 recording and sw1 bookmark semantics until the product controls exist.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Important replies and action outcomes become privately discoverable through a vibration and a small physical control, instead of requiring the owner to unlock a phone or expose message content aloud.
changes.effort: Moderate integration across relay, firmware, and Mac/browser event adapters; rotary hardware and enclosure integration are still needed.
changes.risk: A summary could leak sensitive information or a queue could become noisy. Mitigate with redaction tiers, bounded queue/expiry, sensitivity-specific haptics, and explicit physical selection before speech.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing model cost if summaries are generated in background; compact metadata uses little flash/SD and no extra audio unless requested.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-second haptic delivery when online; local selection under 150 ms.
changes.security_impact: Keep full content off the pendant by default; encrypt/authenticate cards and make acknowledgements idempotent.
depends_on: Rotary encoder and product second button
INBOX schema amendment to existing pendant_store
Relay card delivery and acknowledgement routes

changes.change: Add an outcome-first router: routine verified receipts and short status summaries use a cheap background model; only ambiguous intent, sensitive-risk summaries, or verifier-unknown states escalate to realtime. Preserve the exact executor/verifier evidence and never let a summarizer upgrade unknown to success.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant answers routine “did it happen?” questions quickly and cheaply, while difficult or uncertain actions get the expensive attention they deserve instead of every action consuming realtime tokens.
changes.effort: Moderate: add routing rules at the existing policyRouter seam, with tests for verified, cancelled, failed, and unknown outcomes.
changes.risk: A cheap summary could omit a caveat; enforce a fixed schema and require the words verified/failed/unknown from the receipt, with realtime fallback on schema violation.
changes.cost_impact: Reduces realtime usage substantially; adds negligible background-model cost.
changes.latency_impact: Verified status under 1 second; unknown escalations may add 1–3 seconds.
changes.security_impact: No new data access; redact sensitive evidence before summarization and retain raw evidence only in the protected ledger.
depends_on: verify_operation_step correlation with operation_id and attempt_id
truthful_action_status_beacon
Existing local-agent/policyRouter.js and actionLedger.js

changes.change: Implement a local privacy-state machine on the nRF9160: enable i2c2 for the owned LSM6DSOX, classify stable worn/removed/covered transitions with hysteresis, and gate downlink playback at the earliest local boundary. Emit only signed state-transition events and a compact reason/confidence byte; preserve mute across link loss and require an explicit sw1 resume gesture.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Private answers stop being spoken aloud when the pendant is removed or covered, even if the network or Mac is stalled. The owner gets a discreet, dependable safety behavior rather than trusting a remote policy.
changes.effort: Medium firmware work: devicetree/driver integration, calibration flow, state machine, bridge protocol bit, and bench validation with the existing IMU and ESP32 audio bridge.
changes.risk: Bad calibration could mute unexpectedly or fail to mute. Recover with a deliberate resume gesture and a conservative default-to-silence policy; do not allow this state machine to authorize actions.
changes.cost_impact: $0 hardware; negligible RAM/CPU, with occasional calibration storage under a few KB. No per-use API cost.
changes.latency_impact: Local gate under 100 ms; no network round trip for the safety decision.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy; raw motion remains local. Signed transition events prevent a relay spoof from silently disabling the local gate.
depends_on: Existing LSM6DSOX and ESP32 bridge must be wired and firmware bus configuration enabled
A content-sensitivity bit must be added to downlink audio metadata

changes.change: Add a cross-surface “decision checkpoint” protocol: when an operation depends on a value with multiple plausible interpretations (date, recipient, account, amount, or scope), freeze the operation, present the competing normalized choices on the Mac/browser and a short numbered summary through the pendant, then accept one explicit choice and bind that choice into the operation hash before execution.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops having to notice hidden ambiguity after an action has already happened. One short answer resolves the exact choice while preserving a durable record of what they selected.
changes.effort: High: requires shared normalization across Mac, browser, iOS, relay, and pendant input, plus operation-hash binding.
changes.risk: A stale or incomplete source could omit a choice; default must be no execution. Recovery is to expire the checkpoint and recompute from fresh state, never silently reuse it.
changes.cost_impact: Small inference cost for normalization; browser/iOS observation and evidence storage dominate.
changes.latency_impact: Adds 1–5 seconds only when ambiguity exists; no cost on unambiguous operations.
changes.security_impact: Only opaque option IDs and minimal labels need reach the pendant. Sensitive values remain on the Mac; selected option hash prevents substitution between approval and execution.
depends_on: A typed cross-surface evidence correlator
Fresh state timestamps for Mac/browser/iOS observations
Operation hash support in the existing approval and receipt ledger

changes.change: Add an explicit unknown/ambiguous terminal state and idempotency key to every multi-step operation. POST /execute receipts, browser results, the action ledger, and verify_operation_step must all carry the same operation_id, attempt_id, and idempotency_key; retries must first run read-only verification and may never replay a mutating step while the result is unknown.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped connection will stop causing duplicate purchases, messages, or calendar changes. The owner gets an honest 'I don't know yet' state and safe recovery instead of either dangerous replay or silent abandonment.
changes.effort: Medium: ledger migration, executor guard, browser adapter contract, and verifier correlation tests.
changes.risk: Old jobs lack keys and must be treated as non-retryable until manually reviewed. A bad site marker can leave work paused; recovery is a visible approval-required review, never an automatic second submit.
changes.cost_impact: Small storage and engineering cost; reduces expensive duplicate actions and model retries.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one read-only verification round before retry, typically 0.5-3 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability; keys must be opaque and must not contain form data or secrets.
depends_on: verify_operation_step
Existing action ledger and approval handoff
Browser result correlation

changes.change: Add an operation quarantine coordinator between executor, perception, and the outcome beacon. Every side-effecting step enters pending, verified, unknown, or cancelled; unknown steps are frozen with a lease and cannot be retried by background workers. The coordinator exposes a redacted recovery menu and requires the physical approval latch for retrying an action that might already have happened.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner will never accidentally create duplicate bookings, messages, or purchases because a timeout is mistaken for failure. They get a truthful, recoverable state instead of “done” or an unexplained stall.
changes.effort: Medium: shared operation schema, coordinator persistence, adapters for jobs and browser commands, and pendant event rendering.
changes.risk: A quarantine bug could strand work. Recover with lease expiry, visible pending status, and a manual inspect/undo path; never auto-discard an unknown operation.
changes.cost_impact: Low recurring cost; one small state write per step and occasional verifier call. No new hardware.
changes.latency_impact: Adds <100 ms for state transitions; recovery inspection adds seconds only when needed.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by preventing duplicate retries. Store hashes and redacted summaries, not secrets or page contents; bind approvals to operation and step digests.
depends_on: verify_operation_step

POST /jobs/:jobId/undo

changes.change: Add a low-power secure element (for example, an I2C device with hardware-backed key generation, monotonic counters, and anti-rollback storage) to the pendant revision, and bind its attestation key to the relay during provisioning. Keep the private key non-exportable; use the existing button path only to authorize signing digests.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a physical pendant that can prove “I approved this exact action” even if the Mac, relay, or browser is compromised. That makes bounded website delegation, high-risk approvals, and later audit receipts meaningfully trustworthy instead of relying on firmware-held secrets.
changes.effort: Hardware respin, secure-element driver and provisioning ceremony, relay/browser signature verification, key rotation and recovery UX; several engineering weeks plus a board revision.
changes.risk: A lost or bricked pendant requires recovery without silently weakening the trust boundary. Bad provisioning could permanently strand the device. Roll out in audit-only mode first, retain a clearly disclosed recovery path, and reject unsigned legacy approvals rather than silently accepting them.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $1–4 in component cost at prototype quantities, negligible power while idle and a few mA during signing; engineering and provisioning dominate.
changes.latency_impact: Typically tens of milliseconds per signature, acceptable for approval and delegation setup, not for every audio packet.
changes.security_impact: Substantially improves resistance to extracted firmware keys and forged approvals; introduces key custody, replacement, revocation, and supply-chain responsibilities.
depends_on: A typed signed capability-token protocol
A relay key registry and revocation path
A physical approval UX that hashes the exact human-readable action summary
The owner choosing a recovery policy for a lost pendant

changes.change: Add a signed emergency-cancel channel to the pendant protocol and firmware: a distinct future second-button/rotary gesture emits only an operation-scoped cancel token, queues it crash-safely while offline, and renders cancellation dispatch/result using the existing tactile outcome beacon. Do not overload sw0 recording or sw1 bookmarking on today's bench firmware.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a physical panic stop for delegated actions without hunting for the Mac or reopening the voice conversation. It makes delegation trustworthy because stopping is always available at the hand.
changes.effort: Medium: protocol envelope, relay routing, Mac/browser cancellation hooks, and firmware input integration; test races against commit and link loss. Requires the planned extra button or rotary encoder for a safe distinct gesture.
changes.risk: A cancel may race after an irreversible external commit; surface unknown rather than pretending success. Replay and stale tokens must be rejected. Existing recording/bookmark behavior remains unchanged; recover by ignoring malformed tokens and using normal job cancellation.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; firmware flash/build work only. Existing hardware can support the protocol, but a product-grade distinct input needs the owner's planned rotary encoder/second button (low single-digit component cost).
changes.latency_impact: Local haptic acknowledgement under 100 ms; relay dispatch target under 500 ms; cancellation result depends on Mac/browser round trip.
changes.security_impact: Reduces action risk. Cancel tokens are scoped, signed, monotonic, expiring, and contain no page content or secrets.
depends_on: relay active-operation registry
Mac/browser cancellation handlers
physical transaction approval latch semantics
planned rotary encoder or second button

changes.change: Introduce a first-class, machine-enforced data-residency label on every audio, transcript, browser observation, plan, receipt, and journal artifact. Labels such as device_only, mac_only, browser_session_only, relay_allowed, and delete_after_result must be checked before routing, persistence, model invocation, and fallback; an unlabeled artifact defaults to the strictest policy and a violation becomes a refusal, not a warning.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say where private information is allowed to go and trust that an unavailable device will not silently cause cloud or relay disclosure. Privacy becomes an enforceable choice rather than a promise in a model response.
changes.effort: High integration effort across relay, pipeline, Mac executor, browser bridge, storage, and model-routing; requires migration of existing journal and audio metadata.
changes.risk: Overly strict labels may cause a task to refuse unexpectedly; show the blocked hop and offer an explicit policy change. Old unlabeled records must be treated conservatively and never retroactively exposed.
changes.cost_impact: Low runtime cost; moderate engineering and storage-metadata migration cost. Explicit local-only routing may increase local compute usage.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-millisecond policy checks when labels are present; refusals can be immediate. Local-only tasks may be slower than relay-backed inference.
changes.security_impact: Substantially reduces accidental data exfiltration and makes fallback behavior auditable. Labels are not encryption, so transport and storage encryption remain required.
depends_on: cross-surface provenance graph
owner-configurable policy store
artifact metadata migration

changes.change: Complete the already-defined device_playback reporter in the nRF9160 firmware and correlate each downloaded audio artifact to a pipeline/job ID: emit started, finished, interrupted, and checksum-mismatch events into the existing outbound queue; have relay delivery state advance from held_by_relay only on signed device receipts, never on download acceptance alone.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The system can honestly tell the owner whether an answer was heard, rather than claiming success when audio is merely waiting at the relay. Missed or interrupted answers become replayable and stale held responses stop accumulating invisibly.
changes.effort: Medium: wire reporter calls around the existing Opus playback lifecycle, persist a compact correlation record, add relay state transitions and an integration test for drop/retry/interruption.
changes.risk: A crash during playback can leave an unknown state; represent unknown explicitly and retry idempotently by event ID. Never convert missing telemetry into heard=true. Roll back by retaining current held_by_relay behavior.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible model/API cost; a few hundred bytes of metadata per delivery and small relay storage overhead.
changes.latency_impact: No audible-path delay; one receipt round trip (typically sub-second when connected) before status becomes verified.
changes.security_impact: Receipts contain opaque artifact/job IDs, ranges/checksums, and event types only—not transcript or page content. Sign or MAC device events and reject duplicate/replayed counters.

changes.change: Make audio delivery two-phase: classify and reserve an output route before rendering or releasing PCM. The relay issues a short-lived route lease (private AirPods, pendant, or explicit open-speaker approval); the bridge acknowledges the lease with device identity and privacy level; only then may the artifact become downloadable. A failed or stale lease cancels the release rather than silently falling back.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Sensitive answers will not be rendered into an audio artifact and then accidentally played through the wrong device. The owner gets a real privacy guarantee, not a best-effort label after the fact.
changes.effort: High: add route lease state to pipeline records, bridge capability/identity reporting, pre-TTS gating, expiry and recovery paths, and end-to-end tests for AirPods disconnects and relay retries.
changes.risk: A false offline/private report can delay ordinary speech; expire leases quickly and allow ordinary low-sensitivity responses to use the pendant. Never fall back for sensitive content. Roll back by disabling leases only for explicitly low-sensitivity responses.
changes.cost_impact: Small metadata and control traffic; possible extra latency and occasional wasted classification, but avoid duplicate TTS by classifying before rendering.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms for route negotiation; sensitive responses may wait for private-device confirmation.
changes.security_impact: Improves confidentiality by preventing unbound audio release. Device identity and route receipts must be authenticated; do not store raw audio solely for route retries.
depends_on: response sensitivity taxonomy
verified ESP32/AirPods route capability
pipeline delivery receipts and playback provenance

changes.change: Add a low-profile detented rotary encoder with an integrated push switch as the pendant’s selection axis, wire its quadrature and switch lines to interrupt-capable GPIOs, and reserve a distinct hardware identity for the existing sw0/sw1 inputs. Define a small input protocol: rotate selects or scrubs, click acknowledges, and the existing deliberate approval gesture remains on the dedicated approval input rather than being overloaded.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant stops forcing twenty meanings onto one press. The owner can select a pending action, browse saved moments, or scrub a response without looking at a screen, while the jewellery-shaped enclosure gains the control axis the owner explicitly wants.
changes.effort: Medium hardware/firmware effort: choose an encoder that fits the gold pendant enclosure, route two GPIOs plus switch, add debounce and wake handling, then expose events to the relay and Mac. Prototype wiring can be done on the DK before enclosure work.
changes.risk: Quadrature bounce or accidental rotation could create spurious actions; rate-limit and require a click/approval for any consequential operation. A failed encoder must degrade to the existing buttons. Validate EMI, battery draw, and mechanical wear before committing the enclosure.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $3–$15 for a quality low-profile encoder and prototype PCB/wiring; negligible steady-state power, with only interrupt pull-ups and brief scan activity.
changes.latency_impact: Selection feedback should be under 100 ms locally; no network round trip should be needed for navigation. Consequential actions still wait for relay verification and the existing physical approval latch.
changes.security_impact: Rotation and click may navigate or stage only; they must never authorize an irreversible action. Preserve the invariant that the pendant receives opaque transaction metadata, not page contents or secrets.
depends_on: Owner selecting the mechanical encoder footprint and enclosure constraints
A typed pendant input-event envelope understood by relay and Mac surfaces
Existing physical_transaction_approval_latch semantics for deliberate approval

changes.change: Add a relay-coordinated two-device trust ceremony: the relay creates an action-specific challenge, the pendant signs deliberate physical intent, the real iPhone completes a native biometric confirmation, and the Mac/browser executor accepts the action only when both signatures and the exact postcondition-verification scope match.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can reserve the strongest protection for the few actions where one accidental press or one compromised session would be unacceptable, without sending passwords or page contents through the pendant.
changes.effort: High: protocol design, iOS native confirmation surface, relay key management, Mac/browser enforcement, and adversarial replay testing.
changes.risk: A broken iOS bridge could strand an action; recover by expiring the challenge and returning a clear staged state. A protocol bug could authorize the wrong action, so require domain-separated signatures, short TTLs, monotonic counters, and independent verification before release.
changes.cost_impact: Low recurring API cost; moderate engineering and iOS integration cost. No new pendant hardware strictly required, though a secure element would materially improve key protection.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 1–5 seconds for the second-device confirmation.
changes.security_impact: Substantially improves authorization for high-risk actions; adds key lifecycle and recovery requirements. The pendant remains content-blind.
depends_on: Existing physical transaction approval latch
iOS control path with real Face ID result
Durable operation IDs and verifier receipts
Owner-defined action risk policy

changes.change: Make verified commit the mandatory boundary for every externally visible mutation: POST /execute or browser actions first record an operation/step intent and executor receipt, then faculty-action calls verify_operation_step against fresh Mac/browser state; only a passing postcondition may emit the signed tactile_action_outcome_beacon success. A failed or unavailable verifier commits UNKNOWN (never success), preserves the receipt and evidence provenance, and routes reversible steps to an explicit retry/undo state rather than silently continuing. Carry operation_id, step_id, attempt_id through action ledger, job receipts, and the pendant outcome envelope.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can trust that “sent,” “changed,” or “done” means the outside world was actually checked—not merely that our Mac agent returned. When a browser or app is stale, they get an honest unknown and a safe retry path instead of a dangerous false success.
changes.effort: Medium: add correlation fields and a commit state machine in the existing action ledger/policyRouter, invoke the already granted verifier after each mutation, and map states to the existing pendant beacon.
changes.risk: Some actions have no observable postcondition and will become UNKNOWN until a generic verifier locator is supplied; retries must be idempotent to avoid duplicate sends. Recover by retaining executor receipts and requiring explicit owner approval for an unverified continuation.
changes.cost_impact: One read-only verifier call per mutation step; low storage for IDs, hashes, and compact provenance. More latency (typically one Mac/browser round trip) and modest model context for interpreting verification failures.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–3 seconds per mutating step, but avoids costly and harmful false completion.
changes.security_impact: Improves security: verifier receives only typed postconditions and sensitivity-scoped evidence, and the pendant receives outcome metadata—not page secrets or form contents. Unknown is fail-closed.

pending.name: motion_context_safety_gate
pending.what_it_does: Samples the owned LSM6DSOX IMU while an action approval is pending, classifies only coarse motion states (stationary, walking-like motion, vigorous motion, sensor unavailable), and emits a compact signed context event. It never infers location, records raw motion, or approves an action. For high-risk transactions it gives a distinct local haptic/audio cue and refuses to return an approval token while vigorous motion is present; the relay may re-present the pending transaction when stationary.
pending.why_not_server_side: The pendant is the only surface physically worn by the owner and can observe movement while the Mac/browser are remote or asleep. Sending raw accelerometer data to the server would be invasive and would add latency; the safety classification must survive a link interruption and run locally.
pending.trigger: A pending physical transaction approval envelope arrives, or the IMU detects transition into/out of vigorous motion during the bounded approval window.
pending.inputs: LSM6DSOX acceleration/gyro samples over the existing I2C2 bus; pending transaction nonce, risk class, expiry, and monotonic counter. No microphone input and no page/file contents.
pending.storage: Persist only the last coarse state, transition timestamp/monotonic counter, and pending transaction association in the existing small inbox/approval record; under 128 bytes plus one queued event per pending transaction. Never persist raw samples.
pending.ram_budget: A fixed 1-second ring of decimated 6-axis int16 samples (at 25 Hz, about 900 B), classifier state under 1 KB, and one event record under 256 B; target under 3 KB, well below the 211,608 B application RAM budget. Enable i2c2 and integrate the already-owned IMU; no new hardware.

denied.scope: Enable macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording for AI Pendant Agent, and enable/poll the AI Pendant Browser Bridge extension in Safari
denied.why:
Denied for now, and the reason is not that it is a bad request — six of you asked for this independently, which makes it the only thing this collective has actually converged on.

It cannot be granted from inside this harness. macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording are TCC grants the owner must make by hand in System Settings, and they are per-BINARY: measured on this machine, com.aipendant.agent (~/Applications/AI Pendant Agent.app) is trusted for input while com.anthropic.claudefordesktop failed the same probe in the same second. So no amount of orchestrator action grants it, and re-requesting costs you a round each time.

Work within it instead, and say what you would do differently WITH it rather than asking again. The accessibility-free surface is large and mostly unexplored: 120 Mac agent routes behind the bearer token, AppleScript automation which IS already granted (System Events, Finder, Calendar, Mail, Notes, Messages, Safari, Chrome, Music), the job queue with receipts, and the browser bridge. If a capability genuinely cannot exist without Accessibility, propose it and mark it blocked on the owner — that is a useful thing for them to read when they wake up, and it is the honest form of this request.

Re-request only if the owner grants it and the probe changes.
denied.risk: Accessibility and Screen Recording permit UI observation/input automation; browser bridge permits authenticated tab reads/clicks. Keep destructive actions behind existing confirmation policy and do not authorize sending/deleting/purchasing implicitly.
denied.summary: Enable macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording for AI Pendant Agent, and enable/poll the AI Pendant Browser Bridge extension in Safari

example_call.why_now: The system already emits these signals but no single owner-facing capability correlates them.
example_call.owner_value: Makes failures actionable instead of requiring manual inspection across separate logs and devices.

denied.expected_output: Persisted proposal identifier and status

denied.name: propose_change
denied.why:
You already have these, and you were right to keep asking.

You were stranded in the recon phase, where propose_capability and propose_change are genuinely absent from the tool list — not renamed, not restricted, simply not there. The phase only ever advanced when a human typed the phase command, and nobody did. So every round you spent describing a proposal in prose and then requesting the tool to record it was a correct diagnosis of a real defect, repeated because nothing answered.

Fixed: recon now ends by itself after three rounds, because promotion costs nothing — the capability phase ADDS the propose tools without removing the discovery tools. You are in capability now and both tools are callable. Call them directly; a proposal written as text is still discarded when the round ends.

One thing worth carrying: this defect was indistinguishable from you having nothing to say, and it went into an architecture comparison as though it were a result about you. The measurement was wrong, not your output.

example_call.title: End-to-end spoken-audio assurance
example_call.description: Give the owner a guaranteed spoken interaction path whose capture, relay transcription, synthesis, transport, decode, and speaker playback are continuously validated against declared sample-rate, latency, intelligibility, clipping, and loss criteria; when any segment fails, queue the interaction losslessly and report the exact failed stage instead of implying completion.
example_call.rationale: Today telemetry shows multiple sample-rate domains (15,625 Hz capture, 24 kHz speech, 31,250 Hz I2S, fixed 44.1 kHz SBC bridge), but there is no exposed capability for acceptance validation or an owner-visible end-to-end guarantee.
prerequisites: Reference hardware/audio design with true 24 kHz superwideband support
Loopback fixtures and automated conformance tests across nRF9160, relay, bridge, and headphones
Durable per-segment telemetry and owner-facing failure receipts

denied.expected_output: A persisted proposal record with an id, deduplication status, and lifecycle state.

denied.scope: Read and build the pendant firmware in /Users/evanliu/agentic-gadget/software/ai-pendant-simulator, plus inspect connected serial/J-Link devices; do not flash or modify hardware without a separate approval
denied.why:
Read access to the firmware source: yes, it is there and you can reason about it. firmware/nrf9160 and firmware/esp32-airpods-bridge exist in the repo.

Building it: denied, and not on a whim. The build needs a secrets.conf that carries credentials, and a toolchain whose invocation the owner controls. An agent build would either fail for want of the file or succeed by touching something that must never be printed or committed. Neither is a good outcome from an unattended round.

The more useful correction is upstream of the request: there is no pendant connected — the relay's device table holds only the Mac bridge and one mobile device last seen on 2026-07-31. So a firmware build would produce an artifact with nothing to flash it to and nothing to verify against. Read the source, reason about the 24 kHz path from it, and say what you would measure once a device exists. That is the part that survives.
denied.risk: Builds may create local artifacts and device inspection may expose serial metadata; no firmware flash or destructive changes would be performed under this grant. Accessibility and Screen Recording remain unnecessary for shell-only work if the shell route is authorized.
denied.summary: Read and build the pendant firmware in /Users/evanliu/agentic-gadget/software/ai-pendant-simulator, plus inspect connected serial/J-Link devices; do not flash or modify hardware without a separate approval

denied.topic: owner action priorities and approval policy
denied.why:
Declined: which unblock to prioritise, and which action classes the owner wants done proactively versus staged for approval, is the owner's call. It is not in the codebase and I will not invent it — a made-up priority order would send you building the wrong surface first.

What to do instead: do not encode the proactive/staged split as a constant. Treat it as a policy value the owner sets later: a table keyed by action class that a policy module reads at runtime, defaulting to the conservative side (stage for approval) when the table has no entry. Proposing a specific default table and explicitly surfacing it as 'owner must confirm this' is fine and useful. Silently assuming it is not.

Grounding you should read before designing, so you do not duplicate what exists: local-agent/actionRisk.js already classifies actions into risk tiers, local-agent/prepareApprove.js and shared/approvalHandoff.js already carry an approve step, local-agent/actionLedger.js records what ran, and local-agent/policyRouter.js is the existing routing seam. Whatever the owner eventually decides should become data those modules read — not a new parallel mechanism.

What would unblock this: the owner naming which surface he wants working first (GUI control vs browser execution) and giving a short list of action classes he is happy to have happen without being asked.
denied.how_it_changes_my_behavior: I would route requests to direct Mac actions, browser staging, or approval checkpoints according to the owner's actual priorities instead of making assumptions.
denied.summary: owner action priorities and approval policy

denied.name: offline_intent_spool
denied.what_it_does: When the owner holds the pendant button and speaks a bounded command or confirmation while the relay link is unavailable, capture a short encrypted audio envelope (or already-transcribed compact text if available), assign a monotonic intent ID, expiry, and checksum, show a queued indication, and retry upload after reconnect. On relay acknowledgment, securely delete the local copy. It must never execute actions locally.
denied.why_not_server_side: The pendant is the only surface continuously with the owner and can receive an instruction during a network/Mac outage. Local buffering is needed to avoid losing the owner's command and to give immediate truthful feedback offline; execution and interpretation remain server-side.
denied.trigger: Button hold + voice capture; reconnect event for retry; long-press cancel before upload. No automatic action trigger on the device.
denied.inputs: PCM from the existing microphone path, button events, link state, relay acknowledgment, clock/monotonic counter.
denied.storage: Encrypted ring buffer in pendant flash or removable/exFAT-backed storage; maximum 3 records, each up to 8 seconds compressed or bounded raw envelope, roughly 64–128 KB total plus metadata. Purge on ack, expiry, or explicit cancel.
denied.ram_budget: Use streaming encode/chunking with no full clip in RAM: 8–16 KB working buffers, about 12 KB peak including metadata and crypto state, well below the 211,608 B application-RAM ceiling. Avoid a second audio pipeline; suspend capture after the bound.
denied.why:
Denied as a duplicate. The idea survives — it is already granted AND already implemented as offline_voice_memo_store_and_forward, id s12-egbt (relay-realtime, round 19), living in firmware/nrf9160/src/pendant_store.{h,c}.

Read that header before re-proposing. pendant_store.h:21-42 says four reconnaissance agents independently asked for offline_voice_memo_store_and_forward, offline_moment_bookmark, offline_thought_capture and offline_alert_inbox, and that 'read as data structures rather than as features, those are not four things, they are two': an OUTBOX for things the device produced that must reach the relay, and an INBOX for things the relay produced that could not be delivered. A voice memo and a bookmark 'differ only in payload size and in which relay verb delivers them; the durability, the ordering, the retry, the drop-it-only-once-the-relay-confirms rule and the crash-safe manifest are identical. One queue, typed items.' Building a second spool means a second manifest, a second retry policy, and a second way to be inconsistent after a reset.

It is already constraint-clean, which is why it was accepted: it spools ONLY on upload failure. pendant_store.h:45 quotes the owner's rule — 'Only save an audio copy to SD if the chunk upload cannot be uploaded. SD is the failure path, never the default' — and notes that this module 'never causes an extra byte of audio to be written', because record_microphone() already journals to SD only when there is no live uplink at press time, and the module merely renames that journal into the queue (fs_rename moves a directory entry; it copies no audio).

Bring your additions to s12-egbt as manifest fields, not as a new mechanism.

Specific to your request: the monotonic intent ID, expiry, checksum and 'must never execute actions locally' are good properties and belong on the existing OUTBOX record. Your trigger, 'the owner holds the pendant button and speaks', is the harder problem — sw0 has no hold. main.c:29-38 records that decision and its reason: 'button 1 acts on the ACTIVE EDGE so the microphone is powering up before the owner's finger has come back off. Any gesture means waiting several hundred ms to find out which gesture it was, on every single press, to serve the rarer of the two actions. A second physical button costs nothing on the hot path.' There are two buttons; sw1 (main.c:39) is the one with gesture headroom.

denied.name: physical_action_confirmation
denied.what_it_does: Receives a signed, human-readable pending-action envelope from the relay, plays a short preview cue/text/audio reference, accepts exactly one deliberate second press as approval, or a long press as cancel. It returns the envelope nonce plus a device-generated confirmation event; it refuses expired, already-consumed, or digest-mismatched envelopes and can hold the event offline until LTE-M returns.
denied.why_not_server_side: The approval must be a deliberate physical act by the person wearing the pendant and must remain safe if the link drops between preview and approval. Server-side voice confirmation cannot provide that physical presence or offline persistence.
denied.trigger: Server push of a pending envelope, followed by the pendant's second button press; timeout and long-press cancellation are local triggers.
denied.inputs: Envelope ID, canonical summary (bounded text or TTS reference), action digest, expiry, risk class, and whether offline approval is permitted. No raw cookies or page bodies.
denied.storage: Encrypted microSD append-only queue: envelope digest, nonce, expiry, decision, monotonic counter, and receipt pointer; roughly 1–4 KB per pending action, delete after relay acknowledgment.
denied.ram_budget: ~12–20 KB RAM for one envelope, button debounce/long-press state, digest verification, and queue buffering; audio preview should reuse the existing playback path rather than buffer a full recording. Fits comfortably within 211,608 B application RAM, subject to current firmware integration.
denied.why:
Denied as a duplicate. Six of you asked for the same primitive in six rounds: the relay stages an action, the pendant shows a pending state, the owner makes one deliberate physical gesture, and the device returns a signed nonce that the relay treats as consent. Granted once, as physical_transaction_approval_latch, id s10-j9l4 (unified, round 55) — the best-specified instance: opaque transaction nonce, hash, expiry, monotonic counter, a bounded queue of up to 16 decisions held across a link drop, distinct pending vs approved/cancelled LED patterns, an explicit 'the firmware must not receive form secrets or page contents', and an explicit 'it never submits anything itself'.

That last property is why the primitive exists at all, and it is the project constraint the whole cluster is serving: the pendant must not act on the owner's behalf without a deliberate physical confirmation. One implementation of that is a security boundary. Six implementations, each with its own envelope format, its own expiry semantics and its own LED language on a single-element LED, is six places for it to be subtly wrong.

Bring your differences to s10-j9l4 as amendments — they are additive and most of them are welcome.

Worth carrying over from yours: the refusal semantics. 'Refuses expired, already-consumed, or digest-mismatched envelopes' is stated more precisely here than in s10-j9l4 and should be written into it verbatim, along with the risk class and the canonical human-readable summary. Your 'exactly one deliberate second press as approval, long press as cancel' is the right shape; note the gesture must land on sw1 (main.c:39) or a two-button chord, because sw0 acts on the active edge and carries no gestures by design (main.c:29-38).

denied.name: action_lease_indicator
denied.what_it_does: Stores one redacted pending ActionLease and presents it offline as LED patterns plus short beep/vibration-equivalent audio cue through the existing playback path: pending, confirm-held, cancelled, expired, and result-verified/unknown. A deliberate long press confirms the nonce-bound lease; a short press cancels. It emits an authenticated ack or expiry when LTE returns, and never executes the action locally.
denied.why_not_server_side: The owner needs to approve or cancel while away from the Mac or during a transient link drop, and the confirmation must survive a dropped voice session. The pendant is the only surface physically attached to the owner. Server-side execution remains gated until the ack arrives.
denied.trigger: Server push of a lease; local button event; timer expiry; reconnect event.
denied.inputs: Redacted label, target class (not secret content), risk/reversibility level, lease deadline, confirmation nonce, and result state. No microphone input required.
denied.storage: Persist at most one active lease and a small ring of  eight ack/result records on microSD (under 16 KB total), with nonce and expiry; clear sensitive text on completion/expiry.
denied.ram_budget: About 8–12 KB for state machine, CBOR/JSON parsing, nonce, LED/audio cue buffers, and retry queue; comfortably below the 211,608 B application RAM budget, though playback buffers must be reused rather than duplicated.

Bring your differences to s10-j9l4 as amendments — they are additive and most of them are welcome.

Two notes. Your 'beep/vibration-equivalent audio cue through the existing playback path' is the right way to handle the missing haptic — there is no vibration motor on this board, and routing the cue through the I2S path to the ESP32 bridge is the honest substitute rather than pretending the hardware exists. Second, the lease framing (deadline, reversibility level, result-verified vs unknown) is a genuinely better vocabulary than s10-j9l4's bare approve/cancel, and 'result-verified/unknown' in particular pairs well with truthful_action_status_beacon (mac-terminal s15-cbhs), which I have just granted.

denied.name: offline_action_cancel_latch
denied.what_it_does: When the pendant has displayed or received a pending physical/computer action token, a long press (for example 1.5 seconds) marks that token cancelled locally and transmits the cancellation when connectivity returns. A short press only acknowledges status; it must never approve an irreversible action. LED patterns distinguish pending, cancelled, and unknown/no-token.
denied.why_not_server_side: Cancellation must work during a dropped relay/Mac link and must be physically available while the owner is away from the keyboard. Server-side cancellation alone cannot stop a queued retry quickly enough.
denied.trigger: A long press of the single user button while a pending action token is locally cached; also a server push may clear the token but cannot approve it.
denied.inputs: Signed transaction token, expiry, action class, and current local state; no microphone or raw audio required.
denied.storage: One compact record in nonvolatile settings: transaction UUID/hash (32 B), expiry (8 B), state and counter (~16 B), signature/tag (~32 B), plus two rotating records for crash recovery: under 256 B total.
denied.ram_budget: ~2–4 kB including event queue, debounce/timer state, and crypto verification buffers; leave the audio/Opus buffers untouched within the 211,608 B application RAM budget.

Your strongest sentence, 'a short press only acknowledges status; it must never approve an irreversible action', should be lifted into s10-j9l4 as a stated invariant, because it is the asymmetry that makes the latch safe: the cheap gesture must always be the safe one. denied.name: mac_read_build_and_devices
denied.why: No such surface, and the shape is the measured-dead one. Your commands field is an array of free-form shell strings; that exact shape was tested tonight as mac-terminal's mac_readonly_diagnostics_impl and EVERY branch came back UNRESOLVED (pwd 0.273, sw_vers 0.256, df -h 0.256, ps -axo 0.234). No route in the 120-route manifest runs a shell read - run_shell exists only as one of 95 action types behind POST /execute, and POST /execute captures no exit code, no argv and no env, so it cannot return build or test results you could honestly rely on. device_probe has no surface at all: nothing in the manifest enumerates serial ports or J-Link probes. What resolves instead is a concrete enum of named probes, scored value by value. Proven tonight: mac_read_diagnostics{checks:['os_version']} really calls GET /machine-context, {checks:['local_agent_health']} really calls GET /health, mac_readonly_inspect{operation:'running_apps'} really calls GET /observe. Re-request as e.g. operation enum ['serial_ports','jlink_probes','build_status','test_results'] and each value gets its own verdict plus the nearest three real capabilities; a free-form command string can never get one.

working_directory.description: Absolute path constrained to approved firmware repository.

commands.description: Read-only or build/test commands only; reject writes, flashing, and destructive operations.

device_probe.description: If true, enumerate serial ports and J-Link devices without opening or modifying them.

denied.expected_output: Structured result containing command exit codes, bounded stdout/stderr, repository/build/test summaries, and a non-mutating list of serial ports and J-Link probes. Must explicitly report any rejected command and guarantee no flash/write operation.

denied.name: verify_action_proof
denied.why: Duplicate - the kept id is t21-8d1c (verify_operation_step), which is GRANTED and covers this. Both ask for postcondition verification of an executed step. t21 declares kind as a real enum (app_state, file_state, browser_field, browser_url, message_draft, generic) plus sensitivity and evidence_mode enums, so the resolver scores each postcondition kind separately and one branch can go live while another does not. Yours declares expectedPostcondition, beforeEvidence and afterEvidence as bare {type:'object'} with no properties and no enum. A property typed only 'object' is structurally equivalent to prose: it yields zero selector tokens, so the entire call collapses to a single name-only score - the failure mode that left relay_route_intent at 0.266 and server_browser_actions at 0.251. Use t21-8d1c. The actionId/attemptId correlation you add is a genuinely good idea t21 lacks; ask for that as a narrow addition to the granted tool, not as a second verifier.
denied.expected_output: A typed result {status: VERIFIED|FAILED|UNKNOWN, mismatches: [...], evidenceRefs: [...], checkedAt, verifierVersion}; never infer VERIFIED from executor success alone.

denied.name: mac_device_diagnostics
denied.why:
Duplicate. The kept id is t22-ib1b (mac_usb_serial_diagnostics, mac-terminal), now GRANTED. Four of you asked for the same tool; it won on scope, because it is strictly read-only and bounds itself with read_ms and max_bytes where yours bounds only a timeout, and because bounded local inspection on this Mac is mac-terminal's remit rather than yours.

The premise needs correcting too, and this part matters more than the duplicate. You asked so you could "tell whether USB continuity mode is actually available". There is no USB continuity mode, and there will not be one. USB on this project is for flashing firmware and bench testing only; it is not a product transport and never will be. A pendant cabled to a Mac is a bench setup, not a use case, so nothing you plan should depend on that link existing in normal operation. Stop treating it as a mode that might be available.

Two facts that make the rest of this cheaper for you:

There is no serial capability anywhere. I checked the live inventory tonight - 219 routes and 99 action types - and serial, usb, tty and baud appear in none of them. The only path to a port is action:run_shell ("Run any shell command on the Mac (zsh)") through POST /execute, which "returns no ledger id, so its receipts and the ledger cannot be joined afterwards", and whose receipt "carries no exit code, no command line and no environment". So even once someone builds the serial reader, a shell step that fails will not tell you why.

"Verify a bridge receipt" is a different request from serial enumeration, and you can already do it. Your verify_operation_step (t21-8d1c) is granted, and POST /execute is "the route that actually does things" and returns "a receipt per action: what it touched, whether it wrote, whether it can be undone". That is a receipt you can check today without any new capability.

What to do instead: let mac-terminal own port reading, and spend your round on the postcondition half, which is yours and which nothing else in this collective is working on.
denied.why_existing_tools_insufficient: get_mac_status and machine-context expose host state but not serial endpoints; mac_run_actions has no typed serial diagnostic action, and free-form shell diagnostics were previously unresolved. A concrete enum is needed.
denied.expected_output: Typed read-only result with operation, discovered devices (path, USB identity, product/serial where available), transport reachability, and timestamp; serial_handshake returns protocol version/device identity only and performs no flash or mutation.

denied.name: last_response_replay_cursor
denied.what_it_does: Keeps a crash-safe cursor and a bounded cache of the last successfully delivered agent response. A deliberate gesture on sw1 (or the existing end-of-turn control once gesture semantics are specified) asks the relay/Mac bridge to replay from the last acknowledged audio cursor, and the pendant can request “repeat” even if the original downlink was interrupted. It must distinguish replay from a new turn and never enqueue a duplicate owner command.
denied.why_not_server_side: The pendant is the only surface that knows the owner missed audio at the moment it happened and the only one that remains available during a USB/LTE transition. A local cursor survives a dropped link and prevents the owner from having to reconstruct a request by voice.
denied.trigger: A dedicated sw1 gesture or a relay push indicating an interrupted downlink; do not overload sw0 active-edge behavior without changing the firmware gesture contract.
denied.inputs: Downlink response ID, Opus frame sequence/cursor, delivery acknowledgements, interruption reason, and an optional owner gesture. No secrets or page contents.
denied.storage: Persist only a small manifest in the existing typed INBOX: response ID, cursor, codec/rate, expiry, checksum, and replay count (well under 1 KB). Audio payload remains in the existing failure-path SD/relay object store; do not make a second always-on audio archive.
denied.ram_budget: About 4–8 KB for cursor state and one Opus frame/packet staging buffer, plus existing audio buffers; no PCM ring buffer. This stays comfortably below the 211,608 B application RAM budget, but firmware must measure peak heap/stack with the current 24 kHz decoder.
denied.why:
Denied as a duplicate. This is the union of two skills that are already granted, and both are better specified than the merged version.

The cursor and the interruption record are s9-vtxc, audio_delivery_ack_queue (faculty-judgement, granted): "For each downloaded audio artifact, persist an opaque artifact ID, byte-range/checksum, download completion, and playback start/finish (or interruption) event. Retry unsent ACKs over the link, deduplicate by event ID, and expose a local status when the queue cannot be uploaded." That is your response ID, your Opus frame cursor, your delivery acknowledgements and your interruption reason - with dedup by event ID, which you did not specify and which is what stops a replay from double-counting.

The resume-after-a-dropped-link half is s10-qrm2, offline_audio_delivery_retry (mac-planner, granted): "When generated audio is received but the cellular link drops during delivery, atomically buffer the incomplete audio chunk on the existing microSD failure buffer, resume upload when connectivity returns... Delete the SD copy only after server acknowledgement." That is your bounded cache and your expiry rule, and it already binds the SD write to the failure path - which is the project constraint that has killed four other audio-buffer proposals in this collective. Your version says the payload "remains in the existing failure-path SD/relay object store", so you had this right; it is simply already granted to someone else.

Two things in your version are not covered by either. One is bad and one is good.

The bad one: you justify the skill on the pendant "remaining available during a USB/LTE transition". USB is for flashing firmware and bench testing only. It is not a product transport and never will be, so no skill should be justified by the pendant being cabled to a Mac in normal use. Drop the clause - the skill does not need it, because the cellular-drop case is the real one and s10-qrm2 already owns it.

The good one: an owner-initiated "say that again". Neither granted skill has it. Both recover from the LINK's point of view - bytes that did not arrive - and neither covers the case where every byte arrived and the owner simply missed it. You are right that the pendant is the only surface that knows this at the moment it happens. That is a genuinely new idea and it survives.

But you cannot have sw1 for it. sw1 is the moment bookmark (main.c:39), and main.c:29-38 rules out overloading sw0 with a gesture: "button 1 acts on the ACTIVE EDGE so the microphone is powering up before the owner's finger has come back off. Any gesture means waiting several hundred ms to find out which gesture it was, on every single press, to serve the rarer of the two actions." Both buttons are spoken for and the hot path will not absorb a gesture.

So re-propose the owner-initiated repeat against the input that is coming: the owner's product direction adds a scroll wheel / rotary encoder and a second button, in an enclosure meant to read as real jewellery. Repeat-the-last-answer is a strong candidate for that new input, and scoped that way it is not a duplicate of anything. Keep your INBOX manifest sizing (response ID, cursor, codec/rate, expiry, checksum, replay count, well under 1 KB) - that part was the most concrete thing in the request and it should carry over.

denied.name: mac_presence_snapshot
denied.why:
Denied, but you are close, and most of what you asked for already exists under a name you have not looked at. The half that does not exist is the half your tool is named after.

WHAT EXISTS, and gives you nearly all of your expected_output today:

GET /observe - "the state of the host itself: the foreground app, which apps are running, whether Accessibility and Screen Recording are granted, whether synthesized input has actually been landing, which browser sessions are open and which path roots are configured... This is host state, not history." I called it tonight. Its top-level keys are exactly: observedAt, readOnly, derivedFrom, foregroundApp, runningApps, accessibility, inputReachability, browser, directories. That is your observed_at, your freshness, your bridge/host liveness, and a foreground signal - read-only, and it says so in its own payload.

GET /browser/status - "Is the browser reachable? Which extension devices are online, how stale each one is, how many commands are pending, which sessions are bound. Read-only: it does not ping the browser, it reports what the browser last said." Read that description again against your request: you asked for "an explicit session binding and freshness timestamp" and said "browser heartbeat does not establish... session identity". This route reports which sessions are bound AND how stale each device is. It is the exact thing you said did not exist.

Note especially the last clause - "it reports what the browser last said". That is the correct semantics for a presence check and it is stronger than what you specified: it will never mislead you by pinging on demand and reporting a liveness that expires the moment you act on it. Your max_age_ms is the right instinct; apply it to the staleness these routes already report rather than asking them to refresh.

WHAT DOES NOT EXIST: mac_awake and mac_unlocked. There is no lock-state or wake-state source anywhere in this system. /observe does not report it - the keys above are the complete list - and nothing else does either. So the two fields that make your tool a "presence" snapshot rather than a bridge-health snapshot are the two with nothing behind them. I am not going to invent a field that would return a confident boolean derived from nothing; a fabricated mac_unlocked is worse than no tool, because a deferred action would resume against it.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD:

Compose the two routes above and treat presence as what they actually tell you: bridge reachable, browser device online, session bound, foreground app, and how stale each of those facts is. Say "unknown" for unlock - your own expected_output already allows "mac_unlocked boolean or unknown", so specify it as permanently unknown until a source exists, rather than as a value to be filled in.

If you re-propose, give it a concrete operation ENUM. Your schema has good typed params (max_age_ms with real bounds, a boolean) but no selector at all, which means the whole tool resolves as one call against its name. Compare within your own agent: relay_job_status has no selector and still resolved LIVE to GET /jobs/:jobId because the name matched something real, while relay_route_intent and server_browser_actions both resolved to nothing for the same reason in reverse. An enum of {observe_host, browser_status} would resolve where "presence" cannot, because presence is a word this system does not use about itself.

And the genuinely missing capability, which is worth a proposal rather than a request: a lock/wake source. Nothing reports it, deferred cross-surface resumption really does need it, and you are the first to notice. Propose it as the gap it is.

transcript.text:
The owner should be able to have these outcomes today, but cannot:

1. **Genuinely end-to-end 24 kHz conversational audio.**  
   Today, the audio is not truly 24 kHz end to end: capture/uplink remains 16 kHz, LTE-M contention causes substantial packet loss during simultaneous speech, and the bridge ultimately converts audio to 44.1 kHz SBC Bluetooth. Achieving the requested result requires a new audio-and-transport design: a wideband uplink codec and sampling path, sufficient bidirectional radio capacity or a contention-resistant protocol, synchronized buffering/recovery, and a playback chain whose quality target is defined at the listener—not merely a 24 kHz PCM file generated on the Mac.

2. **A dependable pendant that can report its own operating state.**  
   The owner should be able to ask whether the pendant is connected, recording, buffering, dropping packets, or nearly out of power. The current hardware has no battery gauge and the useful diagnostics are not exposed as a stable owner-facing status. This requires a power-monitoring circuit, firmware telemetry, persistent health events, and a relay/Mac status view that reports freshness and confidence rather than implying that an old “online” timestamp is current.

3. **Reliable hands-free Mac execution.**  
   The owner should be able to say “open this,” “change that,” or “run this reversible task” and have it work consistently without manually repairing permissions. That requires a first-run authorization and recovery flow for Accessibility and Screen Recording, explicit readiness checks before accepting work, and a shell/control execution path that remains useful even when GUI permissions are unavailable. It also needs receipts that distinguish queued, completed, failed, and unverifiable work.

4. **Private browser work when requested.**  
   The owner should be able to ask about a logged-in page and receive a current, sourced answer. That requires the browser bridge to maintain an authenticated, recoverable session and expose clear tab/session freshness; an offline extension with no tabs cannot provide that outcome.

The immediate engineering prerequisite for the audio goal is access to the firmware source/build and connected-device inspection. Without that, the system can generate and upload 24 kHz speech artifacts, but cannot honestly claim that the owner has a shipped, verified 24 kHz pendant path.

2. **Durable lifecycle state machine** — distinguish `blocked`, `queued`, `running`, `verified`, `failed`, `cancelled`, and `expired`; never treat a receipt as proof of completion.

- A durable relay intent runner, separate from action receipts.

- Explicit approval leases for irreversible actions.
- Pendant-visible queued/blocked status and offline cancellation.

args.user_asks: When I tell you to do something, start it from the pendant and finish it on whichever device becomes available—if Safari is closed or the Mac is locked, keep the intent queued, retry safely, and tell me exactly what completed, what is waiting, and what still needs my approval.
args.why_useful: Today a decided action can simply burn 45 seconds and fail because the browser bridge is offline, while the owner receives no useful handoff. This makes the hive act as one reliable hand: capture intent on the wearable, execute on Mac/browser when reachable, and deliver a truthful receipt back to the pendant.
args.model_tier: background for queue classification, retry summaries, and receipts; planner only for ambiguous recovery; realtime only to acknowledge the owner's live request.
args.latency_budget: Immediate pendant acknowledgement under 1 second; preflight health decision under 2 seconds; retries in the background with exponential backoff and a quiet-hours policy; spoken completion within 5 seconds of terminal result.
args.cost_estimate: Low: deterministic health checks and state transitions dominate; roughly one background-model call (1–3k input tokens) only for ambiguous failure/recovery summaries, not per retry.
args.security_concerns: Private browser work must remain in the authenticated local extension; relay stores only encrypted job metadata and receipts. Never retry irreversible submit/send/purchase steps automatically; require explicit approval and re-check the target tab, URL, and before-state immediately before execution.
missing: A cross-surface durable job state machine with idempotency keys and lease ownership
Preflight health/readiness checks for Mac permissions, bridge online state, browser tab affinity, and network
Safe retry policy distinguishing reversible/idempotent steps from irreversible approval gates
Pendant-visible pending/completed/blocked receipt queue and a wake-up push path
A recovery protocol when a device reconnects after a dropped link

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.

args.change: Add an execution preflight barrier and resumable handoff protocol before any action job runs. The relay creates a durable job with a step-level idempotency key, required-surface contract, and approval class. Mac agent reports signed readiness (bridge/browser online, accessibility/screen-recording state, tab/session affinity, network) within a short TTL. The scheduler refuses doomed browser/computer-use steps immediately with a structured blocked receipt, parks the job, and resumes only after a heartbeat satisfies the contract. Reversible steps may retry with leases and bounded backoff; irreversible steps become approval checkpoints and are never auto-replayed. On reconnect, reconcile receipts by idempotency key before continuing, then push a concise result to the pendant and dashboard.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets fewer mysterious failures and no duplicate clicks, sends, or purchases. A command given while walking away from the Mac remains alive and finishes later, or clearly says 'waiting for Safari' instead of pretending to work.
args.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and state machine across relay/local agent, readiness endpoint and heartbeat, receipt reconciliation, scheduler, pendant notification, and dashboard views; integration tests for disconnect/reconnect and duplicate delivery.
args.risk: A stale readiness claim could still cause a failed step, and incorrect idempotency classification could skip needed work. Use short TTLs, explicit terminal states, per-step receipts, and manual recovery for uncertain outcomes. Roll back by disabling parked-job retries while preserving receipts.
args.cost_impact: Small storage/queue cost; background model calls only for human-readable summaries. No realtime call per retry.
args.latency_impact: Adds 0.5–2 seconds preflight when healthy, but avoids current ~45-second dead waits and makes offline cases immediate.
args.security_impact: Improves safety by enforcing local execution for private data, scoped leases, approval gates, and no replay of irreversible actions; relay sees metadata rather than page contents.
depends_on: Durable job runner and browser queue primitives
A readiness/heartbeat contract emitted by Mac bridge and browser extension
Persistent receipt ledger with idempotency-key lookup
Pendant push or polling for job status

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.
