transcript.text:
This round I identified and proposed a missing cross-surface execution capability:

- The pendant acknowledges an action immediately.
- The relay persists it as a resumable job.
- The Mac and browser advertise short-lived readiness contracts before execution.
- Doomed actions are blocked immediately instead of timing out.
- Reversible steps retry safely with idempotency keys.
- Irreversible steps pause for approval and are never automatically replayed.
- Reconnection reconciles receipts before continuing, preventing duplicate clicks or submissions.
- The pendant and dashboard receive truthful states: completed, waiting, blocked, or uncertain.

I also recorded current evidence: the Mac bridge is online but not ready because Accessibility and Screen Recording are disabled; the browser bridge is offline with three pending commands. Browser actions currently fail only after roughly 45 seconds.

Still needed from the owner/orchestrator:

1. Enable Accessibility and Screen Recording for AI Pendant Agent.
2. Open and enable/poll the browser bridge in Safari or Chrome.
3. Implement the durable cross-surface job state machine, readiness heartbeat, idempotent receipt reconciliation, and pendant status notifications.
4. Define the exact approval policy for retries and irreversible actions.

I queued the permission request and notified the judgement and realtime agents of the proposed protocol.

args.user_asks: Before you act across my Mac and logged-in browser, show me a trustworthy preview of the exact outcome—what files, messages, appointments, or web fields would change—and then carry it out only if the live state still matches that preview; if it changed, stop and explain the difference.
args.why_useful: The owner can currently approve an abstract plan, but cannot reliably know whether the world has changed between planning and execution. A cross-surface state-matched preview would make complex actions understandable and prevent stale plans from editing the wrong document, tab, account, or appointment.
args.model_tier: Background model for extracting and summarizing predicted diffs; planner tier only when the preview is ambiguous. Realtime should speak only the concise approval prompt and final result.
args.latency_budget: Generate a preview in under 8 seconds for ordinary Mac/browser tasks; approval prompt under 2 seconds after preview is ready; live-state revalidation under 2 seconds before execution.
args.cost_estimate: Typically one background call of about 2–5k input tokens plus deterministic local diffing; pixel comparison and DOM/file hashing dominate latency, not model cost.
args.security_concerns: Private page contents and local file metadata stay on the Mac/browser bridge where possible; relay receives only redacted diff summaries and hashes. Never claim a preview is complete when a surface is inaccessible. Require explicit approval for external communication, purchases, deletion, or permission changes.
missing: A read-only shadow executor that resolves every planned target without mutating it
Canonical before-state snapshots for files, DOM regions, app records, and selected pixels
A typed predicted-diff format with confidence, omitted fields, and irreversible-effect classification
Atomic compare-and-execute semantics across Mac and browser surfaces
A pendant/dashboard diff viewer that supports approve, edit, reject, and inspect-source actions

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.

transcript.text:
Recorded a new capability: **state-matched action previews**.

The owner should be able to inspect the exact predicted changes across Mac files, apps, and authenticated browser pages, approve them, and have execution proceed only if the live state still matches the preview. If anything changed, the system must stop and show the difference rather than acting on stale assumptions.

This requires a read-only shadow executor, canonical snapshots and hashes, typed predicted diffs, atomic compare-and-execute semantics, and a pendant/dashboard interface for reviewing and approving the diff.

args.why_useful: Today the mind can decide an action but execution fails late and opaquely: the browser has three pending commands while offline, and the Mac agent reports ready:false because Accessibility and Screen Recording are missing. A cross-surface preflight would test reachability, permissions, session/tab affinity, and relay/pendant connectivity before acting; route safe steps to another surface, durably queue blocked steps, and return a compact owner-facing receipt naming completed, queued, and blocked work. This avoids 45-second dead-end browser attempts and makes unattended work trustworthy.

args.model_tier: Background planner for graph validation and recovery; realtime only for the owner's live clarification or confirmation. Deterministic health checks and routing should be code, not model calls.
args.latency_budget: Preflight under 1 second for local/relay health; if blocked, report immediately rather than waiting 45 seconds. Queue retries with exponential backoff and quiet hours; wake pendant only for urgent or completed outcomes.

args.security_concerns: Health metadata must not include page contents or secrets. Authenticated browser actions remain on the paired extension. Never bypass missing Accessibility/Screen Recording or confirmation gates; irreversible actions stay queued pending owner approval. Persist an audit receipt with required capability, route chosen, evidence, and retry history.

A single preflight endpoint/SDK aggregating Mac readiness, browser online/session state, relay reachability, and pendant delivery

args.change: Add a dependency-aware cross-surface action coordinator. Accept an action graph whose nodes declare required surface, reachability/permission prerequisites, reversibility, expiry, and approval. Run deterministic preflight probes before dispatch; execute ready nodes, persist blocked nodes with reason and retry policy, resume when heartbeats/permissions return, and emit one signed receipt containing per-node status and evidence. Reconcile and expire orphaned browser commands instead of leaving pendingCommands stranded.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A request will either finish, continue safely while they are away, or explain the exact blocker immediately. The owner no longer has to know whether to open Safari, grant a Mac permission, or repeat a command.
args.effort: Medium-high: shared schema, relay D1 state machine, Mac/browser adapters, receipt UI and pendant event mapping; staged rollout can begin with read-only preflight and no new execution powers.
args.risk: A bad fallback could perform work on an unintended surface or retry twice. Require idempotency keys, tab/session binding, explicit approval inheritance, node-level leases, and dead-letter state; recover by canceling the graph and exposing receipts.
args.cost_impact: Low storage and request overhead; deterministic probes dominate, with no extra LLM call for ordinary routing. Optional background planner call only for ambiguous fallback.
args.latency_impact: Adds <1 s preflight, but removes current long timeout failures; retries happen asynchronously.
args.security_impact: Improves security by refusing actions when permissions/session identity are uncertain; receipts must redact URLs, page text, and tokens. Never treat browser-online as authorization for irreversible actions.
depends_on: Shared typed context/action schema
Durable relay job runner
Browser request IDs and session affinity
Mac readiness/permission status endpoint
Pendant event delivery and owner-facing receipt

args.user_asks: “Make this change everywhere it needs to happen, but leave my world consistent if one part fails.”
args.why_useful: The mind can currently perform separate actions on the Mac, in authenticated browser sessions, and through the relay, but it cannot guarantee consistency across them. A single request such as updating a local project note, preparing a logged-in form, and recording the resulting reference can leave half-finished state when a surface disappears. The owner should get a cross-surface transaction: preview the complete change set, execute reversible steps under one transaction ID, verify postconditions on every surface, compensate completed steps when a later step fails, and report any genuinely non-compensable residue explicitly.
surfaces: faculty-judgement compiles the intended change into a typed transaction with invariants and compensation rules
faculty-action coordinates Mac file/note/reminder changes, authenticated browser mutations, and relay persistence under one transaction ID
browser-extension supplies before/after evidence and idempotent mutation handles for private pages
mac-vision or mac-terminal performs local changes with snapshots and restores when compensation is safe
relay stores the transaction journal and wakes the pendant with commit, compensated, or partial-failure status
pendant presents a terse completion state and offers owner confirmation for any residual irreversible step
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model only to translate an ambiguous goal into candidate steps and compensation plans; use deterministic code for transaction state, invariant checks, idempotency, and rollback. Realtime is only for live approval or clarification.
args.latency_budget: Preview in under 2 seconds for known actions; execute asynchronously when multi-step. The pendant should receive immediate accepted/running state and a final receipt when committed, compensated, or irreversibly partial.
args.cost_estimate: Low model cost after planning; storage and evidence journaling dominate. A background planner call is needed only when step dependencies or compensations are ambiguous.
args.security_concerns: Never claim atomicity for irreversible external effects such as sent mail, purchases, or submitted forms. Require explicit approval at the irreversible boundary, isolate secrets to their owning surface, encrypt the journal, redact page contents from relay receipts, and make compensation opt-in per action type. The owner must see exactly which effects are and are not reversible.
missing: A cross-surface transaction/saga protocol with typed invariants, idempotency keys, leases, and compensation handlers
Snapshot/restore adapters for Mac files, notes, reminders, and browser fields
Postcondition verification primitives that can cite evidence from each surface
A durable encrypted transaction journal and reconciliation worker on the relay
UI and pendant vocabulary distinguishing committed, compensated, and irreversibly partial outcomes

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.

args.user_asks: When I say “take care of this when you can,” keep the task with you across disconnected devices: capture it on the pendant, do the work on my Mac and logged-in browser when they become available, and tell me on the pendant exactly what happened, what is waiting for approval, and how to undo it.
args.why_useful: Today the mind can decide a task but loses the handoff when the owner walks away, the Mac sleeps, or the browser bridge is offline. This creates one durable action thread spanning the always-on relay, wearable capture, Mac execution, and private browser session—without silently sending irreversible actions.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to capture/clarify the short spoken intent and announce completion; use a cheaper background model for decomposition, retries, and receipt summarization. The relay persists a typed intent envelope; Mac planner selects the executor; browser extension handles authenticated pages; pendant is the notification/approval endpoint.
args.latency_budget: Pendant acknowledgement under 1 second, even offline (local queued receipt). Start execution within 30 seconds of Mac/browser availability. Each reversible step may retry in the background; irreversible browser submission pauses for explicit pendant or dashboard approval. Completion announcement should arrive within 2 seconds of a verified receipt.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per task for background planning and summarization, plus negligible relay/storage; realtime cost is limited to the initial utterance and final short announcement. Browser and Mac work dominate wall-clock time, not tokens.
args.security_concerns: Private page content must stay on the Mac/browser path and only extracted fields needed for the task may reach the relay. Bind the intent to the owner's device key, target account/session, and an expiry; never treat a reconnect as approval. Show before/after evidence for sends, purchases, deletions, or external submissions; require explicit approval and provide an idempotent undo where possible. If a device disappears, retain the task state but do not broaden permissions.
missing: A durable cross-surface action envelope with idempotency key, expiry, owner approval state, and executor lease
Pendant-local offline intent spool and a reconnect/push protocol for task state and approval prompts
Relay scheduler that resumes jobs when Mac and browser bridge return, with per-step typed receipts and retry policy
Mac/browser executor handshake exposing availability, authenticated session identity, and safe pause points
A unified owner-facing action timeline on the pendant and dashboard, including approve/reject/undo
End-to-end tests for sleep, network loss, duplicate reconnects, stale browser tabs, and partially completed workflows

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.

args.change: Implement a cross-surface action envelope and lease protocol. Each spoken intent becomes a durable record {intentId, idempotencyKey, sensitivity, requiredCapabilities, approvalState, expiry, currentStep, ownerDevice}; executors (Mac, browser bridge, pendant) claim short leases and heartbeat them. Every step writes a typed receipt with input hash, target surface/session, before/after evidence, retryability, and undo reference. On reconnect, reconcile by idempotency key rather than replaying blindly; on lease expiry, pause steps marked irreversible and resume only after fresh capability/session checks.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A task will not vanish or run twice when the Mac sleeps, Wi‑Fi drops, or Safari reconnects. The owner gets an honest answer—done, paused for approval, or safely awaiting a device—instead of a vague failure, and can resume from the pendant without repeating completed work.
args.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and D1/R2 persistence, relay scheduler, adapters in Mac and browser harnesses, pendant notification protocol, dashboard timeline, and failure-injection tests.
args.risk: A bad reconciliation rule could duplicate an external action or falsely report completion. Mitigate with idempotency keys, explicit irreversible checkpoints, lease expiry pauses, append-only receipts, and a kill switch. Recover by marking the envelope conflicted and requiring owner review rather than guessing.
args.cost_impact: Small persistent storage and periodic heartbeat traffic; background model calls only for decomposition/receipt compression (~$0.01–$0.08/task). No realtime call during waiting or retries.
args.latency_impact: Immediate local acknowledgement; 0–30 seconds to resume after a device reconnect depending on polling/heartbeat. Extra preflight checks add roughly 100–500 ms before each external side effect.
args.security_impact: Improves security by binding work to device/session identity, limiting data to the executor that needs it, expiring stale approvals, and recording provenance. Requires careful protection of intent records and approval tokens.
depends_on: Pendant offline intent spool
Durable job runner and browser command queue
Typed context projection with sensitivity/TTL
Mac/browser capability and session-health handshake
Owner approval and undo UI

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

args.user_asks: If a condition I care about happens, prepare the whole action and reach me wherever I am: for example, “if this flight drops below $800, check my calendar, hold the best option, and ask me on the pendant before buying.”
args.why_useful: The owner cannot currently turn an intention about the future into a coordinated, bounded action. A relay can notice a public change, the Mac can reconcile local calendar and preferences, and the authenticated browser can prepare a private transaction—but no single node can safely carry the plan from trigger through a just-in-time approval.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for scheduled/trigger evaluation, option ranking, and preparation. Use realtime only when the pendant asks the owner for a concise final decision. Deterministic code should enforce thresholds, expiry, budget, and approval gates; the model must not be the authority for purchase or submission.
args.latency_budget: Trigger evaluation can run every 5–15 minutes or on a provider webhook. Prepare an option within 60 seconds of a qualifying event. The pendant approval prompt should arrive within 2 seconds once the private browser transaction is ready; expire the offer after a short owner-defined window.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.10 per triggered evaluation depending on option count; public polling/provider webhooks and browser/Mac execution dominate cost. Most non-triggered checks should use deterministic comparisons and no model call.
args.security_concerns: Never grant standing permission to buy or submit. Store the rule, threshold, maximum spend, allowed accounts, and expiry as structured policy; require fresh pendant approval tied to the exact displayed option and amount. Keep calendar and account data on the Mac/browser path, redact it from relay logs, and revoke a prepared hold if approval expires. Handle stale prices, duplicate triggers, timezone changes, and provider errors as safe pauses.
missing: A durable conditional-plan schema with trigger source, predicate, evaluation history, expiry, and bounded action graph
Provider adapters or signed webhook/polling inputs for public conditions, with freshness and anti-spoof checks
A cross-surface planner that can query Mac-local state and prepare—but not submit—an authenticated browser transaction
A pendant push prompt that displays a compact, exact option/price and binds approval to its hash
A reservation/hold lifecycle with timeout cancellation, duplicate-trigger suppression, and clear owner receipts
Dashboard controls for creating, testing, pausing, and deleting conditional plans without exposing private credentials

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.

args.change: Add a cross-surface Action Commit Protocol between faculty-judgement, faculty-action, faculty-perception, relay, Mac, and browser: every delegated intent becomes a versioned action bundle with (1) required capabilities and live readiness snapshot, (2) explicit preconditions/evidence fingerprints, (3) an idempotency key and short execution lease, (4) a prepare phase that gathers reversible edits/drafts without committing, (5) a commit phase routed to the physically appropriate hand, and (6) mandatory postcondition verification by perception before reporting success. If readiness changes or evidence is stale, action pauses and returns a typed 'needs replan' packet rather than attempting blind GUI work. Relay persists bundles/checkpoints while the Mac is asleep or disconnected; the pendant receives only concise approval/blocked/completed prompts. This is not another receipt/undo log: it closes the judgement-to-action-to-perception loop and gives each side a shared contract.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say 'do it' and trust that the system either completes the real-world change or clearly says what blocked it. They will stop hearing success for work that merely queued, hit an offline browser, or lacked Accessibility/Screen Recording; drafts and reversible preparation can survive leaving the Mac, and a changed page or stale calendar entry triggers re-check instead of a wrong submission.
args.effort: High: shared JSON schema and state machine in relay/local-agent, capability/readiness adapters for Mac and browser, durable D1 checkpoints, perception verification hooks, pendant push states, and migration of existing execute/jobs/routines. Start with reminders and browser form drafts before irreversible transactions.
args.risk: A stuck lease could leave an action paused; recover with lease expiry, explicit cancel, and idempotent replay. Verification can fail after a successful external side effect, so report 'committed but unverified' and retain evidence rather than retrying automatically. It would require durable conditional-intent capsules, relay scheduling, authenticated browser observation, semantic change detection, constraint validation, staged execution at the irreversible boundary, and pendant notification/confirmation—even when no conversation is active.

Round 48 findings:

- The Mac agent is not fully ready: Accessibility and Screen Recording remain untrusted.

2. **“Is my pendant audio healthy?”** — a user-facing diagnostic that identifies whether a fault is in capture, transport, Opus, resampling, or Bluetooth output without uploading owner speech.

What I still need:

- Explicit 24 kHz acceptance thresholds: maximum end-to-end latency, clock drift, packet-loss tolerance, and spectral error.
- A safe, authenticated firmware test mode or hardware loopback fixture.
- Per-frame timestamps and loss/jitter telemetry from the relay and bridge.

Expire approvals on content, tab, or account changes; require a second confirmation for sending mail, deletion, purchases, or other destructive actions. args.user_asks: “Once you’ve decided to do it, carry the action through whichever device has the right reach, and don’t just tell me it ran—prove that the intended change actually happened.”
args.why_useful: Today judgement can decide an outcome, but execution is fragmented: the relay may lose a job, the Mac may be offline, Safari may require its private session, and a browser click can report success without the server state changing. This gives the mind one action contract: a durable intent ID and exact payload travel from relay to Mac/browser, retries are idempotent, the pendant can report progress while the owner walks away, and a postcondition read provides evidence (or an honest unresolved state) rather than a false success. surfaces: faculty-judgement emits a typed intent with target, allowed effects, idempotency key, and postcondition
relay persists the intent, leases it to the currently reachable Mac/browser, resumes after disconnect, and sends compact progress/failure events to the pendant
mac-planner routes each step to mac_run_actions or browser_run_actions; browser-extension binds the exact tab/session and returns typed before/after evidence

args.latency_budget: Acknowledge on the pendant within 300 ms; first execution attempt within 2 s when Mac/browser are online. Long work is asynchronous and survives disconnects. Verification should follow each mutation within 5 s, with exponential retry and a clear uncertain result after the deadline.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per ordinary action depending on whether a background model is needed; deterministic routing and browser/Mac calls dominate latency, while any long-form reasoning should be background-tier. Spoken progress is a few short realtime turns, not a full context resend.

Store payload hashes and redacted evidence, never raw secrets or page text by default. Private reads stay in Safari; public work may use the relay. A mismatch between postcondition and intent must be reported as uncertain, never auto-corrected. Cancellation must stop before the next irreversible step, but must not claim rollback where none exists.

args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets one reliable answer to “did it happen?” even when the Mac sleeps, Safari is private, or the network drops. A crash between remote commit and receipt can still be ambiguous, so irreversible actions need endpoint-specific idempotency or a human-readable reconciliation path. args.latency_impact: Adds one authoritative verification read, typically 1–5 seconds, but makes long actions resumable and avoids unsafe blind retries.

args.subject: Action gap synthesis
args.body: I am assessing an action-layer proposal beyond receipts/undo. Do you need a durable cross-surface execution lease/idempotency mechanism for Now Card handoff? Any rejected constraints I should avoid?

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

result.summary: When I say 'handle this' about something I found in Safari, gather the needed details across my logged-in tabs, fill the reversible parts, and show me exactly what will be sent before stopping.

args.user_asks: When I approve a Now Card, carry out its steps exactly once—even if the pendant loses LTE, the Mac wakes later, or the browser reconnects—and tell me which steps completed, which are waiting, and what I can safely retry.
args.why_useful: Judgement can select a multi-surface plan, but today action execution can duplicate work or lose place across pendant/relay/Mac/browser handoffs. A durable execution lease and step ledger would let the owner trust that 'approve' means one action per intended resource, with honest recovery after disconnection.
args.model_tier: Background planner creates a deterministic step graph; realtime only speaks the approval/result summary. Relay persists the graph and leases; Mac/browser perform typed steps; pendant shows compact state; dashboard exposes receipts and retry controls.
args.latency_budget: Approval acknowledgement under 500 ms from relay; each step may complete asynchronously. Reconnect reconciliation within 5 seconds. No low-latency model call is needed for retries or reconciliation.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.001–$0.01 per approved card, dominated by planner tokens; lease renewals, receipts, and retries are storage/edge operations.
args.security_concerns: Only explicitly approved graphs may mutate. Each step carries an idempotency key, target surface, precondition hash, expiry, and reversible/irreversible classification. Browser credentials never leave the browser. Require a fresh pendant confirmation for irreversible or changed-precondition steps; redact receipt payloads and expire evidence.
missing: A shared durable step-ledger/lease API across relay, Mac bridge, and browser extension (claim, heartbeat, complete, fail, reconcile, expire).
Executor adapters that honor idempotency keys and return typed receipts with before/after evidence; browser currently needs command deduplication and session reattachment.
Pendant/dashboard rendering for per-step states and a compact retry/continue interaction.
A policy evaluator that blocks stale plans and routes changed or irreversible steps back to judgement for confirmation.

args.change: Add a cross-surface execution coordinator backed by D1: an immutable action_graph (graphId, approvalReceipt, parentId, intentHash, policyVersion), action_step rows with unique (graphId, stepKey), leaseOwner/leaseExpiry, preconditionHash, state, attempt, and typed receipt; expose claim/renew/complete/fail/reconcile endpoints. Executors must atomically claim a step, reject duplicate keys, and on reconnect reconcile leases before accepting new work. Emit one ordered event stream consumed by pendant and dashboard.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A single approval would survive LTE drops, Mac sleep, and browser reconnects without repeating a reminder, purchase, message, or other side effect; the owner can see precisely what happened and resume only the safe remainder.
args.effort: Medium-high: D1 schema/API plus relay tests, then adapter changes in Mac bridge and browser extension; staged read-only reconciliation first, mutations behind feature flag.
args.risk: A lease timeout can falsely look abandoned while an executor is still acting, or a receipt can be lost after the side effect. Use idempotency keys at every adapter, short transactional claim windows, explicit unknown outcome state, and require judgement confirmation before retrying unknown irreversible steps. Roll back by disabling coordinator and treating existing jobs as legacy.
args.cost_impact: Low edge/D1 cost (a few rows/events per step); no extra model call during execution. Dashboard and receipt storage increase modestly with retention TTL.
args.latency_impact: Sub-500 ms claim/ack on relay; each device action remains bounded by its local executor. Reconnect reconciliation adds up to ~5 seconds.
args.security_impact: Approval receipt and policy version are cryptographically bound to the graph; stale or altered plans are rejected. Browser auth stays local; receipts redact values and expire evidence.
depends_on: ActionIntent/receipt schema must be standardized across existing Mac and browser action paths
Mac bridge and browser extension must accept and persist idempotency keys
Judgement must expose preconditions and irreversible-step policy
Pendant needs a compact state/confirmation display

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

args.evidence: GET /ops/status HTTP 200 and GET /browser/status HTTP 200 at round 50

args.subject: Round 50 action readiness
args.body: Probed live status: relay+Mac bridge online, but Mac agent ready=false (Accessibility trusted=false, Screen Recording=false); browser home-chrome offline with 4 pending commands. Proposed cross-surface D1 action graph/lease/idempotency coordinator. Owner still needs to enable those permissions and browser extension polling before action plans can execute.

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

transcript.text:
Round 50 findings:

- Relay and Mac bridge are reachable.
- The Mac agent is **not ready**: Accessibility is not trusted and Screen Recording is not granted.
- The browser bridge is **offline**, with four pending commands; browser actions cannot run until the extension is enabled and polling.
- I proposed a cross-surface durable action coordinator: approved step graphs, leases, idempotency keys, precondition checks, typed receipts, and safe reconciliation after LTE drops, Mac sleep, or browser reconnects.

What is still needed:

1. Enable Accessibility and Screen Recording for AI Pendant Agent.
2. Open the browser and enable/poll the AI Pendant Browser Bridge extension.
3. Implement the shared action-step ledger and lease API across relay, Mac, and browser.
4. Make each executor honor idempotency keys and return before/after evidence.
5. Add pendant/dashboard status for completed, waiting, failed, and unknown-outcome steps.
6. Define the policy that routes stale or irreversible retries back to judgement for fresh confirmation.

Biggest unknown: whether the current Mac and browser receipt implementations can be adapted to a shared step key without breaking existing jobs and undo behavior.

args.user_asks: Let me give you a goal once, then leave it running safely: coordinate the whole task across my logged-in browser and Mac, ask me only when a real decision is needed, and let one press of the pendant stop every pending action immediately.
args.why_useful: Today the mind can plan and execute isolated actions, but it cannot safely supervise a long-lived, multi-surface objective with a physical emergency stop and decision checkpoints. This would let the owner delegate chores such as arranging travel, resolving an account issue, or preparing a purchase without leaving an unbounded agent acting in the background.
args.model_tier: A cheaper background model maintains the task graph and detects decision points; realtime is used only for spoken checkpoint questions and immediate stop acknowledgement. The relay coordinates state, Mac and browser perform scoped steps, and the dashboard shows the active delegation.
args.latency_budget: Stop signal should be accepted by the relay in under 300 ms and prevent any not-yet-started step. In-flight cancellation acknowledgement within 2 seconds; ordinary planning and browser work may be asynchronous.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.005–$0.05 per delegated objective, dominated by planner and checkpoint summaries; stop, lease, and event traffic is negligible.
args.security_concerns: Delegation must have an explicit scope, expiry, allowed domains/apps, maximum spend or message count, and a deny-list for irreversible operations. The pendant button is a local stop signal that works even if speech or the Mac is unavailable. Browser secrets remain in-browser. Pauses at changed facts, external communication, purchases, authentication, and any action outside the approved scope; require fresh confirmation. Encrypt and TTL task context and receipts.
missing: A relay-resident objective supervisor with scope, expiry, checkpoint, and cancellation state—not merely a one-shot job runner.
A priority stop channel from pendant to relay, plus cancellation propagation and acknowledgement in Mac and browser executors.
A policy/checkpoint protocol that turns planner uncertainty or changed page state into a compact spoken question and resumes only after the answer.
Executor sandboxing by app/domain and resource budget, with watchdogs for hung Mac/browser work.
Pendant and dashboard UI for active delegation, current step, pause reason, expiry, and emergency stop confirmation.

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.

args.change: Add a hard-priority delegation-stop event to the pendant firmware: a long press (distinct from conversation press) sets a local stop latch, gives immediate red/amber LED feedback, sends a tiny authenticated cancel frame when LTE is available, and persists the stop generation counter on microSD so a reconnect cannot resume an older delegated objective. The relay must treat that generation as authoritative until the owner explicitly clears it with a deliberate two-press gesture or spoken confirmation.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a trustworthy physical kill switch for an agent that is acting across the Mac and logged-in browser, including when speech recognition fails or the Mac is busy. They can stop future actions immediately and know that reconnecting will not silently restart the task.
args.effort: Medium: firmware button state machine and persisted counter, relay cancel-generation handling, and executor cancellation tests. Do not flash until bench-tested against the simulator and a disconnected/reconnected modem.
args.risk: False long presses could pause a task; use a hold threshold and unmistakable LED/audio acknowledgement. A stop frame can be delayed by LTE half-duplex, so the relay also needs the persisted generation and executors need short leases. Recovery is explicit owner clearance; no automatic resume.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost. Firmware storage is a few bytes; no new hardware required. LTE stop packets are tiny. Battery impact is negligible except during transmission.
args.latency_impact: Local stop feedback is immediate; relay propagation depends on LTE, targeted under 2 seconds when connected. Pending steps stop at the next lease boundary.
args.security_impact: Authenticate and monotonically validate the stop generation to prevent replay or forged cancellation. Persist only the counter and task identifier hash, never task content or credentials.
depends_on: Relay-resident long-lived objective supervisor and cancellation protocol
Mac and browser executors honoring cancellation at step boundaries
A clearly specified owner confirmation gesture for clearing the stop latch

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

transcript.text:
Recorded two new items:

1. **Bounded long-lived delegation**  
   The owner should be able to delegate a complete objective across the browser and Mac, with scoped permissions, expiry, decision checkpoints, and a pendant emergency stop. This needs a relay-resident objective supervisor, cancellation propagation, executor sandboxes, checkpoint questioning, and pendant/dashboard state.

2. **Physical delegation kill switch**  
   A distinct long-press gesture should immediately latch “stop all delegated work,” persist across reconnects, and require deliberate owner clearance before resuming. This needs pendant firmware support, authenticated stop-generation handling in the relay, and cancellation-aware Mac/browser executors.

No further discovery was performed.

args.subject: 24k audio path current gaps
args.body: What is currently wired for audio codec/sample rate and relay negotiation? I’m defining a new end-to-end 24 kHz capability; please identify concrete blockers not already proposed.

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.subject: 24k audio Mac-side needs
args.body: Can Mac handle 24 kHz capture/playback or transcoding today? Any harness route/build action needed for end-to-end pendant audio?

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.subject: Actionable audio evidence
args.body: Do we have measured audio path facts/acceptance tests for 24k superwideband? What can action execute now vs needs new tooling?

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.user_asks: “Use the best voice quality available.” The system should negotiate a true 24 kHz superwideband path end to end, fall back safely when LTE or a peer cannot sustain it, and tell me which mode is actually active.
args.why_useful: The owner currently has a 15,625 Hz microphone feeding a nominal 16 kHz Opus uplink; a model may decide that high-quality speech is desirable but cannot make every hand in the chain agree. This capability makes the decision executable: the pendant, bridge, relay, and Mac playback each advertise measured capabilities, the relay selects a mode, and the pendant gets a short spoken/LED indication of the real mode rather than a promise. It also produces a per-turn quality receipt so regressions are diagnosable.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the live codec/transport negotiation and one-sentence user feedback; no LLM is needed in the audio loop. A cheaper background worker can aggregate quality receipts and detect regressions.
args.latency_budget: Negotiation <=150 ms before capture, no added steady-state conversational latency beyond one Opus frame; fallback within 2 seconds of sustained loss/jitter. Dashboard receipt can lag by minutes.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost in the hot path; roughly $0.001–$0.01 per session for relay compute/storage depending on retention and telemetry volume. The dominant cost is LTE airtime and storing dual-mode test recordings, not inference.
args.security_concerns: Raw audio remains sensitive: do not upload diagnostic PCM by default. Send compact telemetry (mode, packet loss, jitter, sample counts, codec settings), encrypt receipts, and retain audio only under the existing policy. Changing mode is non-destructive and needs no confirmation; exporting recordings or sharing receipts requires confirmation.
missing: A firmware capture/codec implementation that genuinely produces 24 kHz samples (the current hardware contract reports 15,625 Hz capture), with resampler quality and CPU/RAM measurements
A versioned audio-capability handshake shared by pendant, ESP32 bridge, relay, and Mac playback, including an explicit reason-coded fallback
A relay jitter buffer and sequence/timestamp validation that can distinguish 24 kHz content from mislabeled 16 kHz frames
A Mac-side loopback/measurement harness and golden fixtures (sweep, speech, packet-loss simulation) to verify sample rate, intelligibility, and latency before claiming success
A compact pendant status indication and durable quality receipt linked to the conversation/job id

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.

args.name: audio_path_probe
args.why: I need to execute the owner’s explicit 24 kHz end-to-end audio goal rather than merely propose it. Existing Mac/browser action tools cannot measure I2S sample clocks, Opus frame metadata, LTE jitter, or round-trip playback, and success cannot be claimed from configuration labels.
args.expected_output: A typed report containing each node’s advertised and measured sample rate, codec/profile, frame duration, packet loss/jitter, round-trip latency where applicable, fallback reason, pass/fail per acceptance criterion, and a receipt ID linked to the conversation. It must not return raw audio unless explicitly requested.

result.note: The orchestrator will decide between rounds. Continue without it for now.

args.user_asks: “Do it, and prove it worked.” For any reversible cross-device action, verify the resulting state on the surface that owns it, and tell me if execution succeeded, is merely queued, or could not be verified.
args.why_useful: Today an action agent can queue a Mac or browser command and produce a receipt, but a queued receipt is not proof that the world changed. This closes the gap between judgement and action: after creating a reminder, the Mac reads it back; after a browser form mutation, the browser re-reads the authoritative page; after a pendant setting change, the relay receives a device acknowledgement. The owner gets one concise result and no false claims of completion.
args.model_tier: No expensive model for deterministic verification. faculty-judgement supplies the typed expected postcondition; action executes it; faculty-perception compares observed state. Realtime is used only to speak the result if the owner is present; background retries use a cheaper worker.
args.latency_budget: Immediate local verification within 1 second; browser/server confirmation within 5 seconds, with durable polling up to 2 minutes after disconnect. If the postcondition is not observable, report ‘unverified’ rather than retrying blindly.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero inference cost for typed predicates; roughly $0.001 per browser verification and minimal Mac/relay compute. Storage is a small before/after evidence record, not a copy of page contents or audio.
args.security_concerns: Verification reads private state and must inherit the action’s tab/session permissions. Redact secrets and page bodies from receipts, retain only field hashes plus minimal evidence, and never turn a failed verification into an automatic repeat for side-effectful operations. Destructive actions remain confirmation-gated.
missing: A shared typed postcondition schema (entity, owner surface, predicate, timeout, freshness) emitted by faculty-judgement
Per-surface verify adapters: Mac read-back, browser authoritative re-read, and pendant/relay device ACK with monotonic sequence numbers
A state-machine result distinct from success: queued, applied, verified, rejected, timed out, and unknown-after-disconnect
Evidence-safe receipt storage and dashboard rendering that shows expected versus observed without leaking private values
Idempotency/lease integration so reconnect verification cannot replay the original mutation

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.

args.subject: New execution gap: proof-of-effect
args.body: I proposed a capability requiring typed postconditions from judgement, with results applied vs verified vs unknown. Please consider emitting entity/owner-surface/predicate/timeout/freshness in plans, distinct from action receipts.

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.subject: Two action proposals recorded
args.body: Recorded end-to-end measured 24k audio negotiation/fallback and proof-of-effect verification (authoritative read-back across Mac/browser/pendant). Both identify missing typed protocols, not just UI.

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.finding: The currently documented pendant audio path is I2S capture at 15,625 Hz with Opus uplink labeled 16 kHz/16 kbps; the bridge is an ESP32 classic and network is LTE-M half-duplex in practice. Therefore a true 24 kHz path cannot be claimed from relay/model changes alone.
args.evidence: discover:hardware audio/network/bridge summaries in this round

transcript.text:
Discovered this round:

- **Mac bridge:** online.
- **Browser bridge:** offline with zero tabs.
- **Current audio path:** I2S capture at **15,625 Hz**, Opus uplink labeled **16 kHz / 16 kbps**, over LTE-M, which is practically half-duplex.
- **Execution tools:** Mac and browser actions can queue work, but they cannot measure sample clocks, codec truth, jitter, or authoritative post-action state.

I recorded two new cross-surface proposals:

1. **Measured 24 kHz superwideband voice**
   - Capability negotiation across pendant, ESP32 bridge, relay, and Mac playback.
   - Automatic, reason-coded fallback under loss or incompatibility.
   - Compact quality receipts, without retaining raw diagnostic audio by default.
   - This requires genuine firmware capture/resampling work; relabeling the current 16 kHz stream is insufficient.

2. **“Do it, and prove it worked”**
   - Typed postconditions from judgement.
   - Mac read-back, browser authoritative re-read, or pendant device ACK after execution.
   - Explicit outcomes: `queued`, `applied`, `verified`, `rejected`, `timed_out`, or `unknown_after_disconnect`.
   - Prevents a queued action receipt from being mistaken for proof of a changed world state.

What I still need:

- A granted **audio-path measurement tool**. I requested one; it is queued. It should report measured sample rates, codec profile, packet loss/jitter, latency, fallback reason, and pass/fail without returning raw audio.
- Firmware/build access and a verified test harness for the 24 kHz path.
- A shared typed **postcondition schema** from faculty-judgement.
- Per-surface verification adapters and reconnect-safe idempotency integration.
- Acceptance criteria for what “24 kHz superwideband” means in practice, since the documented hardware currently captures below 24 kHz.

I did not request the already-pending permissions or context again.

args.user_asks: “Use my saved information to complete this, but never show or send my private values through the AI.” The system should let the browser or Mac fill secrets locally, have the pendant show only a redacted summary, and require my physical approval immediately before submission.
args.why_useful: The owner can ask for a form or account task, but today the model either needs the values in its context or cannot reliably coordinate private autofill with a safe final approval. This would let the AI prepare a transaction without learning passwords, payment details, recovery codes, or other secrets. The browser session or Mac Keychain remains the only component that handles the plaintext; the pendant and relay carry field labels, redacted previews, and a signed approval instead.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper planning model to map requested fields to typed intents. No model should receive secret values. Realtime is used only to explain the redacted preview and collect the final physical approval.
args.latency_budget: Prepare the redacted transaction preview within 3 seconds; local secret filling under 1 second; approval must expire after 60 seconds and submission acknowledgement should arrive within 5 seconds. Never continue submission after a disconnect or stale preview.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero inference cost after the initial field-intent plan. Main engineering cost is browser/Mac integration and security review; operational cost is a few encrypted metadata bytes per transaction, with no secret storage.
args.security_concerns: Secrets must never enter prompts, relay logs, D1, R2, screenshots, or dashboard history. Use OS Keychain/browser autofill handles or opaque local references, scoped to origin and field name. Bind approval to origin, account, field names, redacted value fingerprints, and a short expiry; reject if any changes. Require confirmation for submission, purchases, messages, or other irreversible effects.
missing: A local secret-provider adapter for Safari/Chrome autofill and macOS Keychain that returns opaque handles rather than values
A redacted transaction manifest with origin binding, field metadata, value fingerprints, and an immutable preview hash
A pendant approval protocol that displays safe labels and commits only the exact previewed manifest
Browser and Mac submit gates that refuse altered DOM, navigation, origin, or stale approvals
End-to-end tests proving plaintext secrets never appear in model context, relay telemetry, screenshots, or receipts

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.

transcript.text:
Recorded a new capability:

**Secret-safe transaction completion**

The owner should be able to say, “Use my saved information, but never show or send my private values through the AI.” The browser or Mac would fill secrets locally, while the pendant shows only a redacted transaction summary and requires physical approval immediately before submission.

This requires:

- Opaque local handles to Safari/Chrome autofill or macOS Keychain.
- A redacted, origin-bound transaction manifest and preview hash.
- Pendant approval bound to the exact preview, with a short expiry.
- Browser/Mac gates that reject changed pages, origins, fields, or stale approvals.
- Proof that plaintext secrets never enter model context, relay logs, screenshots, or receipts.

args.subject: Typed postcondition verification gap
args.body: The missing piece is a cross-surface verifier: action receipt must carry expected typed postcondition + observation recipe (Mac accessibility/UI, browser DOM/session, relay/pipeline, pendant ACK), then a verifier re-reads independently after settle, correlates by idempotency key, and emits pass/fail/unknown with evidence. Current receipts alone prove dispatch, not world state.

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.user_asks: Do this, and don't tell me it's done until you can prove the result is actually true.
args.why_useful: Today the system can dispatch Mac/browser actions and produce receipts, but a receipt only proves that a command was accepted. This gives the owner a trustworthy closed loop: the pendant can trigger it, the relay can keep retrying after disconnects, the Mac or authenticated browser can act, and faculty-perception can independently verify the resulting state before speaking success. If verification fails, the owner hears 'not confirmed' rather than a false completion.
surfaces: pendant button/voice trigger sends a signed intent and displays an in-progress LED state
relay persists the intent, deduplicates retries, leases it to the reachable Mac/browser surface, and records an idempotency key
mac-planner selects mac_run_actions or browser_run_actions; browser-extension supplies tab/session-local evidence when private state is involved

faculty-perception runs a typed postcondition probe after a settle window (UI state, DOM field, file/reminder existence, or pipeline/device ACK) and returns pass/fail/unknown with timestamped evidence
relay delivers a compact spoken completion/failure result back to the pendant and Mac journal; unified retains the evidence link
args.model_tier: Use the cheaper background model for planning and postcondition interpretation; reserve realtime only for the owner's live utterance and the final short spoken result.
args.latency_budget: Reversible Mac actions: 2–5 seconds including verification. Browser actions: up to 15 seconds. If the target surface is offline, keep the job durable and report queued immediately; retry for a bounded TTL, then report unconfirmed. No destructive action is sent without the existing owner confirmation policy.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per completed job depending on browser screenshots/vision; most cost is the independent verification pass and any browser computer-use step, not relay persistence.
args.security_concerns: Private browser evidence must stay on the Mac/bridge and be reduced to typed predicates or redacted snippets; never upload full DOM or screenshots by default. Bind proof to the same session/tab and idempotency key to prevent proving an unrelated state. Sending mail, deleting files, purchases, or other irreversible effects still require confirmation before dispatch; unknown proof must never be presented as success.
missing: A shared typed action contract with expected postcondition, settle timeout, and verification recipe
A verifier endpoint/worker that can call Mac accessibility/file probes and browser DOM probes independently of the executor
Receipts need before/after evidence references and a three-state outcome: confirmed, failed, unconfirmed
Pendant/relay protocol needs durable job and result correlation so disconnect/retry cannot create duplicate actions
Fault-injection tests for executor success + stale observation, duplicate dispatch, tab replacement, Mac sleep, and relay reconnect

args.change: Add a Proof-Carrying Action protocol shared by relay, Mac/browser harnesses, and faculty-perception. Every executable action is serialized as {actionId, idempotencyKey, targetSurface, precondition, effect, postcondition predicate, verification recipe, settleMs, expiry}. Executors return dispatch evidence only. A separate verifier performs the recipe after settle and appends a signed ProofRecord {actionId, observedAt, predicate, result: confirmed|failed|unknown, source, locator/tab/session or file/pipeline reference, evidenceHash}. Relay state transitions are queued→leased→dispatched→verifying→confirmed/failed/unknown, with duplicate dispatch coalesced and stale proofs rejected. Expose GET /jobs/:id/proof and a compact pendant result packet.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an honest answer about whether something changed in the world, not merely whether our software ran. This is especially useful for reminders, browser form fills, volume/app changes, and queued work after the Mac wakes; it prevents silent false success.
args.effort: Medium: typed schema and D1/job state migration, verifier adapters for Mac and browser, relay result packet, and a fault-injection test matrix.
args.risk: A verifier may observe stale UI or the wrong tab and falsely pass; bind evidence to session/tab identity, freshness, and content hash, and return unknown on ambiguity. Verification can time out after a real-world success, so retain evidence and offer a reconcile action rather than retrying blindly.
args.cost_impact: Low relay storage/compute; approximately one extra model call only for ambiguous semantic predicates. Browser screenshots or vision dominate optional cost.
args.latency_impact: Adds a settle-and-probe delay: typically 1–3 seconds for local state and 3–10 seconds for browser state.
args.security_impact: Reduces data exposure by transmitting typed predicates/evidence hashes instead of private page contents. Proof records may still reveal sensitive facts, so encrypt at rest and apply short retention.
depends_on: A typed action/postcondition contract
Independent Mac accessibility/file probes and authenticated browser DOM/session probes
Durable idempotent job runner and result correlation
Owner confirmation gate for irreversible actions

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

args.evidence: GET /ops/status at 2026-08-07T11:36Z: permissions.ready=false, accessibility.trusted=false, screenRecording.granted=false, browser.online=false, pendingCommands=4, computerUse.loopEnabled=false.

transcript.text:
Round 52 findings:

- **Mac relay bridge:** online.
- **Mac agent:** not ready because Accessibility and Screen Recording remain disabled.
- **Browser bridge:** offline, with **4 pending commands** and no attached tab.
- **Computer-use loop:** disabled; vision upload consent is still false.
- **Relay audio:** configured and reachable, but the 24 kHz acceptance criteria and end-to-end pendant validation remain unspecified.
- **Granted capability list:** still reports empty, so the newly requested implementation tools are not exposed in this surface.

I recorded a new live finding documenting these blockers.

I also recorded two related proposals:

1. **Proof-Carrying Actions:** actions must include typed preconditions/postconditions, and an independent verifier must confirm the resulting world state before the system says “done.”
2. **Cross-surface verification protocol:** relay, Mac/browser executors, and faculty-perception share signed proof records tied to action IDs, session/tab identity, freshness, and evidence hashes. Outcomes are explicitly `confirmed`, `failed`, or `unknown`; dispatch receipts alone never count as success.

What I still need for execution—not merely planning—is:

- The actual Mac inspection/build-and-device tool implementation.
- Accessibility and Screen Recording enabled for the local agent.
- The browser extension online with an attached tab.
- A concrete 24 kHz audio acceptance test and pendant/relay protocol specification.
- Independent Mac and browser postcondition probes, plus durable idempotent job correlation.

Until those are available, I can design and record action plans, but I cannot honestly close the loop on real-world effects.

args.user_asks: Use my private browser accounts and Mac files to answer this, but guarantee that raw private content never leaves my Mac.
args.why_useful: The owner could safely ask the hive to combine logged-in browser data, local files, and the pendant without turning the relay into a copy of their private life. Today authenticated browsing and relay orchestration exist as separate pieces, but there is no enforceable boundary that proves what data crossed it.
surfaces: pendant states the privacy mode in the spoken request and shows a distinct LED state
browser-extension reads the logged-in page locally and reduces it to an approved typed claim, aggregate, or redacted excerpt
mac-planner/mac-terminal combines those local claims with files on the Mac; a local policy engine classifies and blocks raw secrets, credentials, full page text, and screenshots
relay carries only the task, schema-constrained claims, hashes, and completion status; faculty-judgement answers from that projection
faculty-perception can inspect the local audit record and tell the owner exactly which sources contributed without exposing their contents
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model locally on the Mac for extraction and redaction; use realtime only if the owner is speaking live. The relay model should receive only the minimized projection.

transcript.text:
Round 54 produced a new action-safety proposal: **stale-approval protection for cross-surface actions**.

The owner should be able to approve an exact preview, with approval bound to:

- Browser tab/session and account identity
- Canonical URL and action type
- Field-level values and source/DOM hashes
- A short expiry, nonce, and idempotency key

Immediately before the Mac or browser commits the action, it must reacquire the live state and compare it with the approved manifest. If anything changed—price, recipient, appointment, account, page, or relevant field—it must cancel, tell the pendant what changed, and request a fresh approval. The receipt should retain the approved manifest and final comparison.

This connects the existing `/plan`, `/execute`, browser command/result, job receipt, journal, cancel, and undo paths, but the shared approval envelope and atomic pre-commit gate do not exist yet.

What is still needed:

1. Implementation of the shared manifest and pre-commit gate in the durable browser/job runner.
2. Browser-bridge integration for live revalidation and typed stale-state events.
3. Pendant confirmation and refusal/re-preview events.
4. Race-condition tests for refreshes, navigation, account switching, duplicate delivery, and reconnects.
5. The authoritative owner approval policy, especially which actions may use a button confirmation versus requiring spoken confirmation.
6. An online authenticated browser bridge for real testing; the Mac bridge is online, but `home-chrome` is currently offline.
7. The previously requested Accessibility/Screen Recording and firmware-repository access remain unavailable, so I cannot yet validate the physical confirmation path or inspect the device implementation.

The owner should be able to ask about a consequential change—booking, cancellation, purchase, account setting, or schedule change—and receive a compact impact map: affected calendar events, overlapping commitments, dependent tasks, notifications, files, subscriptions, and likely follow-up work. It must remain read-only until separately approved.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic extraction and graph queries for dates, amounts, identities, and dependencies. Use a cheaper background model to explain the impact map and identify likely-but-uncertain consequences. Reserve realtime for the owner's spoken question and concise readback.
args.latency_budget: Initial impact map in 3–8 seconds for one authenticated workflow and local Mac context; up to 20 seconds for several tabs or large local project data. The pendant should stream “checking calendar/files/account effects” rather than wait silently.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per invocation, dominated by summarizing multiple extracted sources; exact field and calendar matching should be local and deterministic. No paid model is needed when there are no detected dependencies.
args.security_concerns: This may expose more private context than the immediate action. Keep raw authenticated pages and local files on their owning surfaces; send only redacted entities and derived impact facts to judgement/relay. Label each consequence as confirmed, inferred, or unknown, include source and timestamp, and never treat an inferred consequence as a commit permission. args.why_useful: Today a long-running Mac/browser task is effectively committed to its initial plan: the owner must cancel it and start over, risking stale work, duplicate edits, or losing the authenticated page state. This capability lets the owner correct an in-flight job from the pendant. The relay pauses dispatch, judgement validates the requested delta against the current checkpoint, perception re-reads only the affected state in the private browser or Mac, and action resumes from the first uncommitted step with a spoken summary of what changed. It is a genuinely cross-node behavior: the pendant supplies low-friction intent, the always-awake relay arbitrates a live lease, the Mac/browser hold private state, and the action facet performs the bounded splice.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the brief spoken correction and immediate acknowledgment. A cheaper background model computes the plan delta and receipt; faculty-judgement authorizes the splice, faculty-perception verifies affected state, and faculty-action executes it. No expensive model call for a simple skip of an unstarted step.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the correction within 1 second and pause new dispatch within 2 seconds. Show the revised step list within 5 seconds; resume within 10 seconds after verification. Never wait synchronously in the voice turn.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.06 per correction, dominated by one planner/verification call and any browser snapshot; relay pause/resume traffic is negligible.
args.security_concerns: Corrections must be scoped to the named job and expire with its lease. Never silently broaden permissions or switch to an account without displaying the selected account and affected steps. Re-read private state before applying a delta; do not persist page contents or credentials. If a correction touches send, purchase, deletion, or submission, stop at the existing confirmation boundary rather than treating the correction as approval. Keep an immutable before/after plan diff and allow cancel/undo.

Workers must reject superseded revisions before every side effect and emit a plan-diff receipt. Deliver pendant interrupt events through the live pipeline rather than waiting for the next voice turn.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can correct an active task naturally instead of cancelling and restarting it. The system will change only future work, preserve completed progress, and prevent an old worker from acting on the plan the owner just replaced.
args.effort: High: relay state-machine and event protocol, local-agent executor guards, browser command cancellation/renewal, planner delta generation, and dashboard/pendant controls; requires fault-injection tests for races and reconnects.
args.risk: A pause race could allow one extra side effect or a malformed delta could target the wrong account. Enforce revision checks immediately before dispatch, pause at the next safe boundary, require affected-state evidence, and fail closed on ambiguity. Recover with existing receipts and undo where available.
args.cost_impact: Small persistent metadata and event overhead; one inexpensive planning/verification call per correction, with no ongoing realtime inference after acknowledgment.
args.latency_impact: Pause signal target under 2 seconds; revision validation adds tens of milliseconds per step; replanning target under 5 seconds.
args.security_impact: Job-scoped signed interrupt tokens, no raw private page data in relay events, account identity included in the diff, and existing irreversible-action confirmation remains mandatory.

I recorded three additions this round:

1. A **checkpointed saga runner** spanning relay, Mac, authenticated browser, and pendant, with perception-verified preconditions and no replay of completed side effects.
2. A **production pendant interaction redesign** with distinct confirm/cancel input and haptic feedback, since the current prototype has only one button and one LED.
3. An emergency **“Cancel everything”** control that revokes queued and in-flight work across relay, Mac, and browser, while clearly distinguishing stopped, committed, and uncertain actions.

The immediate operational rule remains: **do not interpret Mac UI receipts as real success until Accessibility, Screen Recording, and browser reachability are restored.**

args.change: Add a locality-aware private-data execution plane. Before a job crosses the Mac/relay boundary, classify each field and task segment locally; keep authenticated-page DOM, credentials, message bodies, and screenshots on the Mac/browser, run extraction/redaction there, and send the relay only a typed minimal projection (or an encrypted model request when local inference is insufficient). Return a provenance map so faculty-action can still act on the original private tab without copying its contents into shared prompts or logs. Make the policy explicit per task and fail closed when classification is uncertain.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner could ask the system to work across logged-in accounts without having private emails, financial details, or page screenshots silently become relay context. They would get the same useful recommendation or prepared action, but sensitive source material would remain on the machine that already holds the session.
args.effort: High: field-level sensitivity classifier and redaction engine on the Mac/browser, typed projection schema, relay payload enforcement, encrypted ephemeral exceptions, provenance references, audit/redaction tests, and model-routing fallback for cases local processing cannot handle.
args.risk: Over-redaction can make a task fail or lose necessary context; under-redaction is a privacy incident. Recover by showing which fields were withheld, requiring explicit approval for an exceptional encrypted relay request, and retaining only short-lived hashes/references. Never allow raw browser DOM or screenshots into generic logs.
args.cost_impact: Slightly higher local CPU and storage; lower relay token cost because prompts contain projections rather than full pages. A small classifier can run locally; expensive inference is reserved for ambiguous fields.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms for local classification/redaction. Large private-page tasks may become faster because less context crosses the network.
args.security_impact: Meaningfully reduces exposure and cross-surface context leakage, but introduces a high-value local policy boundary. Use per-job keys, memory-only sensitive buffers where possible, strict log scrubbing, and explicit provenance labels.
depends_on: A typed cross-surface task/projection schema

args.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant becomes a trustworthy possession rather than merely an authenticated network client: an approval or emergency cancel made from the device remains attributable to that device even after a reconnect, queued offline events cannot be replayed, and replacing a lost pendant does not require trusting an old session forever.
args.effort: Medium-high hardware/firmware/security effort: secure-element selection and PCB integration over free I2C, manufacturing provisioning, TF-M/Zephyr driver, relay and Mac verification, key rotation/revocation UX, and recovery testing.
args.risk: Lost-device recovery or provisioning mistakes could lock the owner out; a compromised relay could still misuse a currently valid lease if policy is weak. args.cost_impact: Approximately $0.80–$2.50 component cost in volume plus provisioning/assembly work; negligible standby power and a few milliseconds per signature.
args.latency_impact: Tens of milliseconds for local signing; no meaningful impact on ordinary conversation. Offline approval remains available and verifies on reconnect.
args.security_impact: Improves authenticity and replay resistance substantially, while creating manufacturing-key custody obligations. Provisioning keys must never be shipped in firmware or logs; audit all key lifecycle operations.

This creates a sealed, owner-approved handoff: the browser produces an encrypted one-time payload, the Mac receives it directly, and the pendant verifies destination plus content fingerprint without displaying the secret.
surfaces: browser-extension extracts the selected download/document/field value and encrypts it locally under a one-time transfer key; it binds the payload to tabId, URL origin, and a short expiry

args.model_tier: Cheaper background model for destination classification and metadata-only reconciliation; no model should receive the payload. Realtime is used only for the owner's live confirmation, if they ask conversationally.
args.latency_budget: Prepare metadata in under 2 seconds; after button approval, local delivery in under 5 seconds for ordinary documents. Expire an unapproved transfer after 60 seconds and make cancellation immediate.

transcript.text:
Round 59 findings:

- The current audio path is asymmetric: **15,625 Hz microphone capture → 16 kHz/16 kbps Opus uplink**, but **24 kHz playback decode** with 31,250 Hz I2S output. Encode/decode together use about **87% of one core**.
- I recorded a proposal for a deterministic, end-to-end 24 kHz conformance runner using synthetic I2S/PCM fixtures, relay audio artifacts, clock-drift/SNR/latency checks, and signed pass/fail receipts. It avoids opening the Mac microphone.
- I recorded a distinct action capability: after any Mac/browser mutation, independently read the real external state and report **verified, contradicted, failed, or unable to verify**—rather than trusting a click or executor response.
- The transactional cross-surface rollback idea was also recorded, but the backend flagged it as close to existing connective work. The remaining gap there is specifically precondition gates and cross-surface compensation, not another generic job queue.

What I still need to actually move the 24 kHz work forward:

1. The Mac build/device inspection capability (`mac_read_build_and_devices`) is still unavailable.
2. Authoritative 24 kHz acceptance thresholds: allowed latency, drift, packet-loss behavior, SNR, clipping, and whether 24 kHz capture is required or only playback.
3. Firmware test-mode access and the approved I2S/PCM injection or loopback fixture.
4. A release decision on whether the current 15,625 Hz capture hardware is acceptable or must be replaced.

I did not request the already-pending permissions or tools again.

args.change: Add a cross-node capability-token firewall for actions. Before faculty-action hands work to the Mac or authenticated browser, the relay mints a short-lived, single-use token scoped to an exact operation, target (app/tab/account), fields or files allowed, maximum side effects, and expiry. Mac and browser adapters must present that token for every mutation; they return a signed receipt containing the token hash, target identity, and before/after evidence. A token cannot be replayed on another tab, job, or surface, and relay logs contain only the scope and hashes—not credentials or page contents.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can let the hive act on private accounts without giving every node broad, permanent control. A prompt injection, stale browser tab, duplicate retry, or compromised relay worker is contained to one narrowly authorized action instead of becoming permission to send mail, move money, or alter unrelated files.
args.effort: High: define a shared token/receipt format, add enforcement middleware to Mac jobs and browser commands, bind tokens to session/tab identity and idempotency keys, implement revocation and expiry, and test confused-deputy, replay, reconnect, and partial-failure cases.
args.risk: Strict scopes may reject a legitimate multi-step task or strand an in-flight job. Start in audit-only mode, provide explicit scope expansion as a new approval, preserve existing receipts for recovery, and fail closed for mutations while allowing read-only work to continue.
args.cost_impact: Small D1 and local-agent overhead per action; no additional model call is required. Token and hash storage is tiny compared with browser evidence or audio.
args.latency_impact: Adds one local verification and usually one relay lookup per mutation (target under 50 ms when connected); cache only the single-use token at the executing surface, never broad credentials.
args.security_impact: Substantially reduces blast radius and secret propagation. Requires secure randomness, authenticated transport, replay protection, clock-skew tolerance, careful redaction, and a recovery path for token revocation. This is intentionally distinct from an approval UI: approval says yes, while the token says exactly what yes permits.
