args.subject: Action gap search
args.body: I am looking for new cross-surface action capability beyond backlog. Any decisions you can make that currently lack execution path?

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.user_asks: “When I approve a prepared change on the pendant, carry it out even if the connection briefly drops—but never twice—and tell me exactly what happened.”
args.why_useful: Today judgement can prepare an action and the Mac/browser can execute one, but a real-world approval is split across unreliable links and there is no end-to-end guarantee that the approval, execution, and receipt refer to the same one-time change. This gives the owner a safe commit protocol: the pendant shows the final before/after summary, the owner's button press or spoken approval creates a short-lived one-time authorization, the relay holds it through a reconnect, the Mac/browser performs the idempotent step, and the pendant gets a concise success/failure/expired result. It is useful specifically because no single surface can both authenticate the human's physical approval, reach private browser state, survive disconnects, and report a durable receipt.
surfaces: faculty-judgement creates a normalized action plan and irreversible-step boundary
relay-realtime assigns a one-time nonce, expiry, and durable delivery state
pendant displays a compact diff and records a local approval event (or cancellation)
mac-planner dispatches the approved plan through mac_run_actions or the job queue
browser-extension executes authenticated tab steps and returns typed before/after evidence
relay records the receipt and pushes the outcome back to the pendant; faculty-action can report or undo
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background/deterministic executor for queue delivery, idempotency and receipt validation; use the realtime tier only for the short approval conversation and spoken result. No expensive model call is needed to replay or verify a known plan.
args.latency_budget: Preview should reach the pendant in under 1 s; approval acknowledgement under 300 ms when online. Reconnect delivery may take seconds. The authorization should expire after 60 s (configurable), and every retry must be safe because the same operation key is reused.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per invocation, dominated by the initial judgement/preview model call; retries, relay storage, Mac execution, and browser bridge traffic are negligible. A receipt/undo path avoids paying for a second model call in the common case.
args.security_concerns: Never send credentials or page contents to the pendant; show only a redacted diff and origin/tab identity. Bind the nonce to plan hash, account/session, exact irreversible step, device identity, and expiry; reject replay, altered plans, stale tabs, and duplicate operation keys. Require a fresh physical button hold for irreversible actions, with spoken approval as non-authorizing. Persist an audit receipt and provide undo where the operation supports it. Data leaves the Mac only as the minimum redacted preview and result.
missing: A durable one-time approval envelope shared by pendant, relay, Mac, and browser bridge
Offline pendant approval spool with replay protection and a visible pending/expired state
An executor-side idempotency/compare-before-commit check for browser and Mac actions
A unified receipt schema linking plan hash, approval nonce, tab/session, before/after evidence, and undo token
The owner must still grant Accessibility/Screen Recording if a step requires GUI-only control; AppleScript and existing browser routes remain usable without it

args.change: Add a postcondition-verification stage to every irreversible Mac/browser job. The planner must emit a typed expected invariant (for example, appointment status=confirmed, draft remains unsent, reminder exists with exact time). After execution, a separate perception pass re-reads the authoritative surface—browser tab/session for web state, AppleScript/read-only route for Mac state—and stores a signed verification record alongside the existing receipt. If the invariant is false, ambiguous, or the tab/session changed, mark the job “unverified” rather than successful, stop retries, push a pendant alert with the observed value, and offer an explicit recovery/undo job. Use the same operation key for retries and require compare-before-commit when possible.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops hearing “done” when a click timed out, a site rejected a field, or the wrong tab was active. They get a truthful result grounded in the resulting state, plus the exact observed discrepancy and a recovery choice. This works without Accessibility for AppleScript/browser-readable surfaces and degrades honestly for GUI-only actions.
args.effort: Medium: define invariant and verification schemas, add read-only adapters for existing Mac and browser surfaces, extend receipt storage/UI, and add pendant result states. One or two weeks for a narrow set of actions; broader semantic verification is incremental.
args.risk: A site may update asynchronously or expose stale cached text, causing a false unverified result; use bounded polling with timestamps and show evidence. Verification must never itself mutate state. If the verifier crashes, preserve the receipt as executed-but-unverified and allow manual inspection; do not automatically retry irreversible work.
args.cost_impact: Roughly one cheap read/verification model call only for semantic invariants ($0.001–$0.02), otherwise deterministic selectors/AppleScript. Additional browser/Mac round trips add modest bandwidth and relay storage.
args.latency_impact: Adds approximately 0.5–5 s after execution depending on eventual consistency; pendant can say “checking” immediately. No added latency before approval or before the action starts.
args.security_impact: Store hashes and minimal redacted evidence rather than full page contents; bind verification to URL/tab/session and plan hash. Read-only verification can inspect private data on the Mac but must not export secrets. Access failures become unverified, never success.
depends_on: A typed action plan with expected postconditions
Existing job receipts and undo routes
Browser session/tab affinity and typed browser results
Mac read-only AppleScript or equivalent route coverage
A pending pendant result state; GUI-only verification remains blocked until the owner grants Accessibility/Screen Recording

args.user_asks: “Carry this request through all the dependent systems: if the private site accepts the change, update my Mac calendar and remind me; if it fails, leave everything untouched and tell me exactly where it stopped.”
args.why_useful: The owner cannot currently ask for a single dependable real-world outcome spanning a logged-in website and local Mac state. A browser action may succeed while the calendar step is skipped, or a retry may create duplicate reminders. This capability is a compensating transaction (a saga), not merely a queued click: it commits each step only after verifying the prior step, uses idempotency keys, and performs safe compensation for already-completed reversible steps. The pendant gives one concise outcome instead of forcing the owner to reconcile several surfaces.
surfaces: faculty-judgement turns the request into a dependency graph with commit points, allowed compensations, and a final success invariant
relay-realtime persists the graph and resumes it after disconnects or Mac sleep
browser-extension reads the authenticated page, performs the approved reversible/irreversible step, and returns authoritative evidence
mac-planner uses Calendar/reminder APIs or AppleScript to create the local follow-up only after the browser commit is verified
faculty-perception independently checks each resulting state and detects partial completion
pendant receives step-by-step progress and a final success, partial-success, or safely-rolled-back result
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for graph compilation and recovery classification; deterministic adapters perform known browser and Calendar operations. Reserve realtime for approval and concise progress, not orchestration.
args.latency_budget: Show the first plan on the pendant in under 2 seconds. Each dependent step may take seconds to minutes because sites can be eventually consistent; reconnect resumption must not restart a committed step. A stalled graph should become paused, not silently fail, after a bounded timeout.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.002–$0.03 per request, mostly one planning/recovery call; deterministic execution and verification dominate latency rather than API cost. Compensation avoids costly duplicate actions and support effort.
args.security_concerns: Require approval for the exact graph and every irreversible node; bind all nodes to the original plan hash and operation id. Keep private page contents on the Mac/bridge; send only redacted values and evidence hashes to relay/pendant. Never compensate by sending a message or canceling a purchase automatically. If compensation is unsafe, stop in partial-success state and ask the owner.
missing: A durable dependency-graph job format with node state, commit markers, idempotency keys, and compensation policy
Adapters that can verify authenticated browser outcomes and local Calendar/reminder outcomes without GUI permissions
A recovery worker that resumes paused graphs after reconnect and never replays committed nodes
A partial-success UI and explicit owner choices for unsafe compensation
A shared redacted evidence/receipt format across browser and Mac

args.change: Introduce a durable cross-surface saga coordinator rather than treating each Mac/browser action as an independent job. Persist a DAG of typed nodes with dependency barriers, commit markers, idempotency keys, expected postconditions, and explicit compensation policies. On reconnect, resume only the first uncommitted node; after each node, run a read-only verifier before releasing dependents. Expose partial-success and paused-for-owner states through the existing job and receipt APIs, and make unsafe compensation impossible to auto-run.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can ask for an outcome that crosses a private website and their Mac without manually checking whether half the work happened. A site rejection will not leave a misleading calendar reminder, and a dropped connection will not duplicate a booking or reminder. When full rollback is impossible, the owner gets an honest partial result and a precise next choice.
args.effort: High integration effort: schema and durable worker first, then browser and Calendar adapters, verifier contracts, recovery tests, and pendant progress states. Start with browser-booking-to-Calendar/reminder as a narrow vertical slice.
args.risk: Some external actions cannot be undone; the coordinator must stop before those nodes unless separately approved and must surface partial completion. Eventual consistency can make a successful node look absent, so use bounded verification and never retry an ambiguous irreversible node. Recover by leaving the graph paused with its evidence and operation key.
args.cost_impact: Small durable storage and queue cost; one cheap planning or recovery call per graph ($0.002–$0.03), with deterministic steps otherwise. Verification adds browser/Mac requests but prevents duplicate side effects.
args.latency_impact: Adds verification latency between dependent steps (typically 1–5 seconds, longer for eventually consistent sites); disconnect recovery becomes reliable rather than immediate. The pendant can stream node status so the owner is not left guessing.
args.security_impact: Keep credentials and full private content on the Mac/browser surfaces. Relay stores only encrypted/redacted plan values, hashes, state transitions, and receipts. Bind every node to the owner's approval, session/tab identity, and idempotency key; require fresh approval for any compensation or newly discovered irreversible node.
depends_on: A versioned plan/receipt schema that supports dependency graphs and postconditions
Durable relay job execution across Mac sleep and reconnect
Browser command queue with stable tab/session affinity
Read-only Calendar/reminder verification adapters
Pendant progress and partial-success states
Owner Accessibility/Screen Recording only where no AppleScript or browser-readable adapter exists

transcript.text:
Recorded two proposals:

1. **Cross-surface dependent transactions** — complete a private browser action and only then update Calendar/reminders, with verification, idempotency, recovery, and honest partial-success states.
2. **Durable saga coordinator** — persist dependency graphs across reconnects, resume only uncommitted steps, verify each result before continuing, and prevent unsafe automatic compensation.

They require a shared dependency-graph/receipt schema, durable recovery worker, browser and Calendar verification adapters, and pendant progress/partial-success states. GUI-only steps remain dependent on owner-granted Accessibility/Screen Recording.

args.body: Fresh gap beyond queued audio shipping: no action can run a repeatable end-to-end 24 kHz acceptance transaction and produce a receipt. Need Mac generates tagged test audio -> relay pipeline -> pendant decode/I2S -> ESP32/A2DP -> Mac-side return/packet telemetry, with per-hop timestamps, loss/underrun and cleanup. This is distinct from implementing audio path; lets judgement decide ship/reject on evidence.

args.user_asks: Run a 24 kHz audio path check and tell me exactly where quality or timing breaks.
args.why_useful: The owner can currently decide to ship the audio path but cannot obtain one trustworthy, end-to-end proof across the worn pendant, relay, Mac, and Bluetooth bridge. A tagged test run would distinguish codec, transport, I2S, resampling, and A2DP failures instead of reporting that a command merely queued.
args.model_tier: background/scheduled work on a cheaper model; use realtime only to explain the short spoken result
args.latency_budget: Start within 2 seconds; a 10–20 second test is acceptable. Spoken result under 3 seconds after the run ends.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per run, dominated by a small diagnostic transcript; most work is local counters and timestamps.
args.security_concerns: Test audio should be generated locally and contain no microphone content. Do not upload owner speech. Bluetooth device names and packet diagnostics may leave the Mac only if explicitly enabled. Require confirmation before any firmware flash, pairing change, or sustained speaker output.

A relay test-session mode that tags and correlates frames end to end

A signed, durable audio acceptance receipt with per-hop evidence
An owner-approved audio-path acceptance spec (the 24 kHz criteria request is still pending)

args.change: Build an end-to-end audio acceptance transaction that creates a local tagged test stream, correlates relay pipeline events with pendant decode/I2S counters and ESP32/A2DP telemetry, computes per-hop latency/jitter/loss/underruns, stores a signed receipt, and automatically tears down the test. It must fail closed when telemetry is missing rather than infer success from HTTP 200.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner asks whether the 24 kHz path works, they get a defensible answer naming the failing hop—or a verified pass—instead of a vague queued-job success. It prevents shipping a path that sounds acceptable in one segment but drops frames at the bridge.
args.effort: Medium-high: a relay correlation schema, a Mac diagnostic runner, firmware/bridge counters, and a receipt renderer. No Accessibility grant is needed; shell/AppleScript and existing pipeline routes suffice for orchestration.
args.risk: Diagnostics could generate audible output, consume radio/battery, or mis-correlate reused packet IDs. Use a unique run nonce, bounded duration, local-only synthetic audio, explicit teardown, and mark incomplete on any missing counter. Recovery is deleting the run receipt and stopping the pipeline; never flash automatically.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost for local tests; roughly $0.01–$0.05 if a model summarizes the receipt. Firmware flash/storage impact is small if counters are compact, but must be budgeted against 211,608 B application RAM and 1 MB flash.
args.latency_impact: Adds no production voice latency. Test startup under 2 s and test duration 10–20 s; receipt available within 3 s of teardown.
args.security_impact: Synthetic audio avoids microphone leakage. Receipts may reveal Bluetooth device identity and network timing; keep local by default and redact identifiers before relay upload. Require confirmation before pairing changes, firmware writes, or prolonged playback.
depends_on: An authoritative 24 kHz acceptance spec
A diagnostic counter/event schema on pendant, relay, and ESP32 bridge
A local Mac runner using existing run_shell/run_applescript and pipeline routes
Durable receipt storage and a dashboard/voice summary path

args.change: Replace the provisional ESP32 classic-A2DP bridge with a BLE Audio-capable bridge (or a production codec module) whose transport and sink can preserve a 24 kHz mono path, while retaining a compatibility SBC output mode. Keep the pendant's 24 kHz decode as the canonical sample rate and move any unavoidable conversion to one explicitly measured boundary.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The current bridge hard-locks classic A2DP to 44.1 kHz stereo, forcing an extra 31,250→44,100 resample after the pendant's 24 kHz decode. A 24 kHz-capable sink would reduce avoidable conversion artifacts and make the owner's request for a true 24 kHz path physically achievable, not just true inside the codec.
args.effort: High: select a supported BLE Audio/LC3 chipset and headphones, redesign the bridge firmware and power/audio board, then validate coexistence with the nRF9160 link. Keep the existing ESP32 as a fallback during migration.
args.risk: BLE Audio interoperability, pairing UX, and battery draw may regress; some headphones will only support SBC. Mitigate with dual-mode fallback, an A/B hardware harness, and the proposed tagged acceptance transaction before changing the daily path.
args.cost_impact: Prototype bridge roughly $20–$60 in parts plus new headphones if needed; modest additional power versus the current ESP32 bridge, exact draw requires measurement. No per-run API cost.
args.latency_impact: Potentially lower buffering than the current SBC/A2DP path, but BLE Audio scheduling may add 10–30 ms; require measured p50/p95 latency in acceptance receipts.
args.security_impact: New pairing keys and Bluetooth identifiers must remain local and be resettable. Do not auto-pair or replace the current sink without confirmation.

A written 24 kHz acceptance criterion
Hardware/audio compatibility study for the chosen BLE Audio sink

args.user_asks: If you’re interrupted halfway through something I asked you to do, tell me exactly what is finished and let me resume it from the pendant without repeating any completed step.
args.why_useful: Today a dropped Mac, browser bridge, or relay can leave the owner unsure whether an email, form, or file operation happened. This gives them a trustworthy recovery path: a spoken pendant status, an explicit next step, and continuation from the last verified checkpoint rather than accidental duplicate actions. It is genuinely cross-surface because the pendant is the interruption/status surface, the relay retains the job, the Mac/browser perform the work, and the action faculty turns receipts into the next executable step.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only for the short pendant interruption/status exchange; use a cheaper background model to reconcile journal/receipts and derive the next safe step, escalating to realtime only when the owner asks to resume or a high-consequence ambiguity remains.
args.latency_budget: Pendant should receive a compact interrupted/awaiting-verification status within 2 seconds when connected. Recovery reconciliation may take 5–20 seconds in the background; resuming an individual Mac/browser step should begin within 3 seconds after confirmation.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per interruption with a small background model; costs are dominated by rereading large browser evidence or screenshots, so persist compact step summaries and hashes rather than resending full context.
args.security_concerns: Do not claim completion from an intent or an attempted command. Store requested, attempted, witnessed, and confirmed states separately; require fresh owner confirmation before irreversible continuation; never replay a write whose receipt is ambiguous. Private URLs, page snippets, and local file paths remain on the authenticated Mac/bridge unless explicitly needed for the spoken summary.
missing: A durable, typed checkpoint record shared by Mac, browser bridge, relay, and faculty-action (step id, idempotency key, precondition, side-effect class, receipt, witness, expiry).
A resume endpoint that accepts a checkpoint id and executes only the next unverified step, with stale-session and changed-page guards.
Pendant-visible pending/interrupted/disputed events and a compact confirmation interaction.
Mac and browser readback adapters that can independently verify side effects after a crash or reconnect.

args.user_asks: When a website or Mac app changes while you’re carrying out my task, pause at the exact changed step, tell me what changed in plain language, and let me approve a corrected plan from the pendant instead of guessing or starting over.
args.why_useful: Real tasks fail at the moment a page adds a verification challenge, changes a price, moves a button, or an app opens a different dialog. The owner should get a small, actionable interruption—what was expected, what is now present, and what the proposed correction would do—while all already-completed safe work remains intact. This is different from a generic approval prompt: it is adaptive replanning at a verified divergence point.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model to compare precondition snapshots and classify the divergence; use the realtime model only to explain the delta and collect a short owner decision. Use vision only when structured DOM/accessibility or AppleScript state is insufficient.
args.latency_budget: Detect and pause within 1–2 seconds of a changed precondition. A concise pendant explanation should take under 3 seconds; after approval, resume the corrected step within 5 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Low for structured state diffs; roughly <$0.02 for an interruption, with vision/screenshot analysis the dominant cost and used only as fallback.
args.security_concerns: Never transmit full private page contents when a field-level diff is enough. Treat changed prices, recipients, permissions, account destinations, and security challenges as high-consequence divergence requiring explicit confirmation. Do not attempt to solve CAPTCHAs or MFA silently; display that the owner must take over.
missing: A precondition snapshot and semantic-diff schema for browser DOM, app state, and filesystem targets.
A divergence classifier that distinguishes harmless layout drift from changed intent, destination, amount, or authorization.
A pause-and-replan protocol that preserves completed steps and invalidates stale action leases.

args.change: Add a divergence-aware execution interlock between planning and action. Compile every step into a semantic precondition snapshot (recipient, amount, URL/origin, selected account, target file, permission state, and stable field identifiers). Before committing a step, compare the live Mac/browser state to that snapshot. If it differs, atomically pause the job, invalidate its action lease, store a minimal redacted diff plus the last safe checkpoint, and emit a pendant decision event with approve-corrected-plan, edit, cancel, or owner-takeover options. On approval, generate a new plan revision linked to the old one; never mutate the old plan or replay prior steps.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Unexpected UI or data changes become a clear one-sentence question instead of a silent failure, wrong click, duplicate submission, or lost progress. The owner can safely approve the correction while away from the Mac and continue from where the task actually stopped.
args.effort: High: semantic state adapters for browser DOM and AppleScript-accessible Mac apps, a diff/classification service, atomic job pause/lease invalidation, plan revision storage, and pendant event/response plumbing. Start with browser forms and Mail/Calendar before general GUI vision.
args.risk: Over-sensitive diffs could interrupt harmless layout changes; under-sensitive diffs could miss a changed destination or amount. Default to pause on uncertainty, classify only from stable semantic fields, and retain a human-takeover path. Expire approvals when the page/session changes again.
args.cost_impact: Small metadata storage per step; background diffs are cheap. Vision fallback for unstructured dialogs costs more and should be sampled only after structured adapters fail.

args.model_tier: Use a cheap local recovery model for classifying executor errors and proposing bounded repairs. Escalate to the expensive realtime model only when the repair changes the approved effect, encounters an unfamiliar security prompt, or needs a spoken decision.
args.latency_budget: Attempt recovery within 2–4 seconds after a recoverable mismatch; continue as a durable background job if the page/app is slow. Ask the owner promptly only for scope, identity, payment, or security changes.
args.cost_estimate: Usually one small recovery inference and a fresh compact observation; roughly $0.005–$0.03 per recovery. Screenshots and repeated page context dominate cost, so retain structured locators and hashes rather than replaying full transcripts.
args.security_concerns: A changed interface must not become permission to do a different thing. Keep an immutable approved effect envelope (account, recipient, amount, destination, content hash, and allowed mutations); require renewed approval if any envelope field changes. Treat MFA, CAPTCHA, payment, deletion, and external-send prompts as hard stops. Redact observations before relay logging.

transcript.text:
Recorded a new capability:

**“If the app or website changes while you’re doing it, recover and finish the approved task without making me start over.”**

For this to exist, the system needs:

- A shared error taxonomy for stale UI, session expiry, transport failure, changed content, and scope changes.
- A perception → judgement → action repair loop that re-observes the affected tab or app and proposes a bounded replacement step.
- An immutable approval envelope covering the account, recipient, amount, destination, and content.
- Post-action verification proving the intended state, rather than trusting that a click or keystroke was accepted.

Recovery could be automatic for harmless UI changes, but MFA, CAPTCHA, payment, deletion, external sends, or any changed approval field must stop and ask the owner again.

This would prevent a stale tab, wrong account, navigation race, or dropped connection from turning an intended action into a silent mistake. It is genuinely cross-surface: the pendant establishes presence, relay holds the lease, Mac/browser performs the act, and perception proves the postcondition.

args.why_useful: The owner cannot currently distinguish an executor's acknowledgement from a real-world completion. A browser can report a click while the server rejects it, a Mac can report a file write while sync fails, or a relay can lose the result. This gives the owner a trustworthy completion answer based on independent witnesses rather than another optimistic receipt. It is new beyond ordinary job status, receipts, or undo because completion requires correlated evidence from the action surface and a separate observer, with disagreement surfaced as uncertainty.

args.change: Introduce a Witness Quorum layer between execution and completion reporting. Every side effect gets an action hash and evidence envelope. Expose that classification through job status/receipts and prevent the relay from saying “done” when only the executor acknowledged. For safe operations, allow an explicitly classified retry; for non-idempotent operations, freeze and request owner review.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an honest answer about whether something actually happened, rather than a confident “done” that may mean only that a click or API call was attempted. args.risk: Independent observers can disagree or observe stale state; false disputes could annoy the owner, while weak independence could create false confidence. Enforce freshness windows, source independence metadata, explicit unknown outcomes, and never auto-retry irreversible actions.
args.cost_impact: One additional readback per action and small durable evidence records; cheap compared with the risk of an unverified external side effect.
args.latency_impact: Adds 1–10 seconds before declaring completion; the owner can hear “executor finished, verification pending” immediately.
args.security_impact: Evidence must be scoped to the target and redacted. Independent observers need narrowly scoped read access, never broad credential export. Action hashes and nonces prevent replay or cross-job evidence substitution.

Idempotency classification for retry policy

transcript.text:
I discovered the current action surface and recorded a new cross-surface capability plus integration change:

**“Finish the prepared action.”**  
The system should:

1. Show the exact pending browser/Mac changes.
2. Accept approval through a deliberate pendant interaction.
3. Execute ordered steps with idempotency keys and checkpoints.
4. Survive a dropped voice connection.
5. Reconcile ambiguous outcomes instead of retrying blindly.
6. Report what was dispatched, verified, not completed, or remains unknown.

This extends the existing `/plan`, `/execute`, job receipts, browser bridge, Mac actions, pipeline audio, and journal routes rather than duplicating them.

### What is still needed

- A durable relay-side action-bundle/checkpoint store.
- Stable idempotency keys and typed side-effect proof from both Mac and browser workers.
- Pendant approval and pending-state transport.
- Reconnect delivery for the final spoken receipt.
- Dashboard timeline showing each step’s evidence and status.
- Fault-injection tests for disconnects, duplicate delivery, and unknown outcomes.

The pendant currently has **one button and one LED**, so approval and pending state must be designed around those constraints. Its audio path also shares one full-duplex I²S peripheral, so action receipts must not interfere with the 24 kHz playback path.

I do not need another permission request this round; the remaining firmware/audio access and acceptance-criteria requests are still unresolved upstream.

args.latency_budget: Routine checks can run on a minutes-to-hours cadence. An exception should reach the pendant within one polling interval; spoken escalation under 2 seconds once connected.
args.cost_estimate: Low background inference and storage per monitored case; cost is dominated by authenticated page reads and occasional local-agent calls. Realtime usage occurs only for unresolved exceptions.

Store state fingerprints and provenance rather than private page bodies where possible. If authentication expires or evidence conflicts, pause and notify rather than improvising.

args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can delegate the ongoing management of a messy situation without granting open-ended autonomy. transcript.text:
Round 78 produced two new records:

- **24 kHz audio conformance sentinel:** a synthetic pendant test that measures capture rate, Opus profile, packet loss, jitter, decode rate, underruns, and CPU headroom across pendant → relay → Mac. It reports the exact failing stage and safely falls back when the path is unhealthy.
- **Owner capability:** “Before my next call, verify that my pendant audio is healthy; if not, fix what you can and tell me exactly what failed.”

A significant current mismatch is now recorded: the prototype captures at **15,625 Hz**, uplinks Opus at **16 kHz**, but plays back at **24 kHz** through a **31,250 Hz** bridge clock. There is no verified end-to-end 24 kHz capture result yet.

I still need, but will not re-request this round:

1. The owner’s authoritative **24 kHz acceptance criteria**.
2. Permission to inspect/build the pendant firmware and connected serial/J-Link devices.
3. A pendant-local calibration test and counters.
4. A typed audio conformance receipt and relay-side profile validation/fallback.
5. A Mac-side audio/bridge health probe that does not open the microphone.

Accessibility and Screen Recording are not required for this audio work.

args.change: Replace the prototype audio front end with a native 24 kHz-capable capture and playback clock domain: use a microphone/codec path whose actual sample clock supports 24 kHz (or an integer-related clock with verified low-jitter conversion), add an independent audio DMA clock rather than deriving capture from the current 15,625 Hz path, and give the bridge a negotiated clock/profile contract. The firmware, Opus configuration, relay, and acceptance tests must all advertise measured rates rather than hard-coded labels.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets genuinely superwideband speech instead of a 16 kHz uplink being relabeled or reconstructed as 24 kHz on playback. Voices, environmental cues, and transcription quality improve, and the pendant remains reliable when the network changes because both ends agree on the real clock and profile.
args.effort: High: select and prototype a production audio codec or I2S microphone clocking scheme, revise the pendant/bridge PCB or carrier, update Zephyr drivers and DMA buffering, then requalify Opus, RF power, thermal behavior, and enclosure acoustics. This is a product-hardware change, not a simulator-only patch.
args.risk: A new clock tree can introduce drift, buffer overruns, RF interference, or higher power draw; the development kit must remain supported as a compatibility profile during migration. Recover with a negotiated 16 kHz mode and hardware-in-loop drift tests before deployment.
args.cost_impact: Prototype engineering plus roughly $8–$25 per production unit for codec/clock/audio components and PCB changes; likely tens of milliwatts additional draw depending on codec. API cost is negligible.
args.latency_impact: Potentially neutral or slightly lower once DMA is correctly clocked; initial buffering and resampling tests may add 10–30 ms until tuned.
args.security_impact: No new cloud data is required. Keep raw microphone samples local except during an explicitly active call; expose only negotiated profile and health metrics to the relay.
depends_on: Owner-defined 24 kHz acceptance criteria
Firmware inspection/build access and serial/J-Link hardware-in-loop testing
The previously proposed end-to-end conformance sentinel to prove the new clock path

transcript.text:
Recorded two proposals:

1. **Conditional actions with state-bound approval**  
   The owner could say, “If this exact situation occurs, do it,” with permission bound to specific facts, scope, expiry, and a one-time token. The system would re-check conditions immediately before acting and stop if anything changed.

2. **Cross-surface shadow execution**  
   Before acting across the Mac and browser, the system would simulate the plan against redacted state snapshots, show the predicted effects and conflicts, and refuse live execution if the world changed since approval.

These require a shared operation protocol, signed state snapshots, deterministic predicates, read-only Mac/browser adapters, and executors that enforce preconditions rather than trusting stale approvals.

args.change: Implement a contract-bound action transaction that sits between /plan, /execute, the job queue, Mac/browser runners, and pipeline events. Reject stale or mismatched steps. args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can trust “done” or “stopped” in a way they cannot today: a changed webpage, lost tab, stale plan, dropped pendant, or partial Mac failure cannot silently turn into an unverified action. args.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and state machine in relay, adapters in Mac/browser runners, postcondition verifier, receipt format, and pipeline event vocabulary; then failure-injection tests for expiry, duplicate delivery, tab replacement, and link loss.
args.risk: A strict verifier may pause work that would have succeeded, and old clients may omit contractHash. Roll out in shadow mode, accept legacy jobs as unverified, and provide an explicit retry with a newly compiled contract. Never auto-replay an irreversible step.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage/CPU for hashes and state; one extra lightweight verification/read per mutation. Background model cost remains low; no extra realtime call except the final concise status.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms for lease and local digest checks, plus native time for a postcondition read. Failures become earlier pauses instead of long silent retries.
args.security_impact: Improves replay and confused-deputy resistance by binding every mutation to a short-lived, user-approved contract and tab/session. Keep evidence redacted/minimal and avoid storing private page bodies by default.

args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can know that an action is waiting, paused, or truly finished even in a noisy room, while walking, or when playback is unavailable. It makes the device an honest physical hand instead of assuming a spoken message was heard.
args.effort: Medium hardware/firmware work: prototype a vibration driver and button on the next board, add BLE/cellular state messages, and test tactile patterns against clothing and battery conditions. Do not modify or flash the current unconnected development kit without approval.

args.latency_impact: Local state feedback is near-instant and continues through a short relay/audio interruption; it does not add server latency.
args.security_impact: No sensitive content is exposed; only abstract state codes are delivered. Button events must carry a nonce/contract hash so stale acknowledgements cannot authorize another job.

When a job stops after step n, derive a bounded recovery graph from each completed step's declared compensation (for example, restore a draft field or move a file back), distinguish safe compensation from irreversible external effects, and present the owner a spoken/inspectable choice: leave as-is, compensate selected reversible steps, or resume from the exact checkpoint after a fresh precondition check. args.user_asks: “When I walk away from my Mac, put my private work into a safe state; when I come back, restore exactly what I was doing.”
args.why_useful: The owner gets automatic, presence-bound privacy and continuity: sensitive browser sessions can be locked or obscured when the pendant leaves, while non-sensitive work remains recoverable. Returning to the desk restores the prior workspace without requiring them to remember a security ritual.
surfaces: The pendant emits a rotating, privacy-preserving proximity nonce over BLE and gives a local tactile cue when the protection boundary changes
The Mac bridge measures authenticated proximity, captures an encrypted workspace manifest, locks or masks designated applications and private browser tabs, and later restores only the recorded state
The browser extension labels tabs by sensitivity and can replace private pages with a local lock screen while preserving tab/session identity
The relay stores only the encrypted manifest and receives presence transitions, surviving a Mac sleep or temporary link loss
faculty-judgement selects the policy and asks once which applications/tabs are protected; faculty-action executes the transition and reports a compact result to the pendant
args.model_tier: Use a small/background model only to classify workspace sensitivity and reconcile restoration conflicts; proximity transitions and lock/mask actions must be deterministic local code. Realtime is unnecessary except for an optional spoken warning.
args.latency_budget: Protection should begin within 2 seconds of confirmed departure and restoration within 3 seconds of return. If confidence is ambiguous, leave the workspace protected rather than oscillating.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost during normal use; occasional background classification is roughly $0.001–$0.01 per workspace change. Main cost is engineering and modest encrypted manifest storage.
args.security_concerns: The pendant must not broadcast a stable owner identifier or location. Use rotating authenticated nonces, local key agreement, replay protection, and a grace period for brief signal loss. Never transmit page contents or credentials to the relay. Restoration must require the same pendant identity and a fresh nonce; if the pendant is lost, the owner can revoke its key from the Mac. Sensitive browser pages should be masked or locked, not closed or reloaded, to avoid data loss.
missing: A product pendant with authenticated BLE proximity and a secure key store
A Mac-local presence daemon integrated with lock/mask APIs and sleep/wake handling
Browser-extension sensitivity labels and a tab-preserving lock surface
An encrypted workspace-manifest store with key revocation and conflict handling
Owner-configurable protected application/tab policy and a clear local override

args.user_asks: “If I hold the pendant button, revoke this device and stop anything acting as me everywhere.”
args.why_useful: Provides a fast, physical kill switch when the owner suspects a lost pendant, exposed screen, or runaway automation. It can stop queued Mac/browser work and revoke the pendant’s authority even when the owner cannot reach the Mac or speak safely.
surfaces: The pendant detects a deliberately long press locally, shows a distinct LED/tactile pattern, and sends a signed emergency-revoke event when connectivity exists
The relay immediately marks the pendant key revoked, cancels queued jobs, invalidates action leases, and fans out the event to all reachable surfaces
The Mac bridge locks the session, terminates or freezes agent-owned processes, and removes temporary credentials and browser bridge authorization
The browser extension closes or locks designated authenticated tabs and invalidates its command channel without deleting user data
faculty-action returns only a terse revoked/partially-revoked status and retains a durable incident receipt for later owner review
args.model_tier: Deterministic firmware and relay control path; no model call is needed for activation or propagation. Use a cheap background model only later to summarize what was stopped and what could not be reached.
args.latency_budget: Local revoke cue immediately; relay fan-out under 1 second when connected; unreachable surfaces remain revoked at the relay and must fail closed when they reconnect.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible per event; one signed event and small receipt. Engineering cost is concentrated in credential scoping, cancellation, and fail-closed reconnect behavior.
args.security_concerns: Require a long press plus a clearly different local cue to reduce accidental activation, but do not require speech or network access. Protect the revoke key in secure device storage, prevent replay, and make revocation monotonic. Since a panic action can destroy unsaved work, lock/freeze before termination and preserve only minimal diagnostic metadata. Re-enrollment must require deliberate owner action on a trusted surface.
missing: Secure per-pendant revoke key and monotonic revocation registry
Firmware long-press handling that works offline
Relay fan-out and fail-closed reconnect protocol
Mac process/credential quarantine and browser bridge invalidation hooks
Owner-controlled re-enrollment and incident review UI

Recorded a new capability:

### Presence-bound privacy handoff

The owner should be able to say:

> “When I walk away from my Mac, put my private work into a safe state; when I come back, restore exactly what I was doing.”

This does not exist today. It would require:

- A pendant with authenticated, rotating BLE proximity credentials.
- A Mac-local presence daemon that detects departure and return.
- Sensitivity-aware browser tabs and an authenticated browser lock surface.
- An encrypted workspace manifest preserving tab/application state without sending page contents to the relay.
- Relay-side key revocation and conflict handling.
- Deterministic local protection and restoration; no model call should control the security transition.

I also recorded a second capability for a **physical emergency revoke switch** on the pendant. It was accepted as connective work but flagged as close to existing action-stop ideas; the genuinely missing pieces are the secure offline revoke key, fail-closed reconnect behavior, and credential quarantine across Mac and browser.

args.user_asks: “Handle this end to end, and keep me in control.” The system should carry out a reversible multi-step task across my logged-in browser and Mac, pause only at irreversible steps, and let me approve, cancel, or resume it from the pendant.
args.why_useful: Today the mind can decide a goal but execution is fragmented: browser commands can time out, Mac jobs can continue without the pendant knowing whether they are safe to resume, and a spoken approval is not a durable transaction boundary. This gives the owner one honest action state: what was planned, what precondition was checked, what changed, what is waiting for approval, and how to undo it. It is genuinely cross-node: the relay persists the job, the browser supplies private web state, the Mac performs local actions, and the pendant provides a physical cancel/approve affordance.

args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; produce a plan in 2–5 seconds; execute reversible steps asynchronously with progress updates. Never wait indefinitely on an offline browser: mark blocked after a bounded timeout and offer resume rather than retrying blindly.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly one realtime turn plus 1–3 cheap background turns per task; dominant cost is private-page extraction and any vision loop, not the state machine. Persist compact step records and hashes rather than resending full context.
args.security_concerns: Private URLs, page text, and local file paths leave their originating surface only as narrowly scoped evidence. Encrypt persisted evidence and expire it. Sending mail, deleting files, purchases, form submission, and other irreversible effects require explicit approval tied to the exact before/after summary. A physical pendant cancel must revoke the lease immediately; stale approvals and duplicate retries must be rejected.

A relay-to-pendant push channel for progress plus a local button/LED state machine for cancel, approve, and blocked/offline states
A single executor that can route each step to browser or Mac, verify typed results, and reconcile receipts before advancing

args.change: Implement a relay-owned Action Transaction Coordinator between the existing /execute, Mac jobs, and browser command queue. It should compile a goal into typed steps (surface, effect class, idempotency key, preconditions, approval requirement, lease expiry), dispatch one step at a time, correlate browser result or Mac receipt by the same step ID, and advance only after proof matches the precondition/postcondition. args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets reliable “it was done once” behavior instead of duplicated browser submissions, ambiguous Mac jobs, or a false completion after a timeout. args.effort: Medium-high: relay schema/state machine, adapters for existing Mac receipts and browser typed results, and tests for duplicate delivery, timeout, reconnect, approval expiry, and partial undo. No new model is required for enforcement.
args.risk: A bad proof adapter could advance without real completion, or an overly strict one could strand work. Default closed on missing/contradictory evidence; retain receipts and offer manual resume. Never auto-retry effect=write unless the step declares an idempotency key and the target confirms it.
args.cost_impact: Small D1 write/read overhead per step and one cheap background planning call; no material realtime cost. Evidence should be hashes/snippets with short retention, not full pages by default.
args.latency_impact: Adds tens to hundreds of milliseconds per step for persistence and verification; avoids the much larger cost of blind 45-second browser retries.
args.security_impact: Improves security by making approval scoped to an exact step and expiring it with the lease. Private evidence remains surface-local where possible; transaction IDs and hashes cross the relay, not secrets.

I recorded a new cross-node capability: **Deferred Intent with semantic verification**. A request would receive an expiry-bound lease, idempotency key, allowed surfaces, approval class, and explicit postcondition. The relay could resume it after reconnecting, Mac/browser agents could execute bounded steps, faculty-perception would verify the result, and the pendant would eventually receive a concise success/failure/unknown receipt.

What I still need:

The current stack can execute commands and retain receipts; the missing piece is the reliable, verified handoff between “a command ran” and “the owner’s goal was accomplished.”

args.user_asks: “Pause that job here and let me resume it from the exact next step on whichever device is available, with a compact explanation of what already happened and what will happen next.”
args.why_useful: Today long-running work is tied to the device and execution job that started it. A sleep, reconnect, or handoff can force the owner to repeat context or guess whether a step already happened. A portable checkpoint would make the hive act like one continuous worker: the Mac can stop after a verified boundary, the relay can preserve the checkpoint, the browser can reattach its session, and the pendant can resume or cancel without replaying completed side effects.
args.model_tier: Use a small background model to summarize checkpoints and select the next eligible step; use realtime only for the owner’s resume/pause voice interaction.
args.latency_budget: Pause acknowledgement under 1 second. Resume briefing under 3 seconds, then execution proceeds asynchronously. Checkpoint writes must be atomic before any next side effect.

- Explicit predicates and branches
- Time limits, spending/action limits, destinations, and expiry

- Fresh confirmation for irreversible or out-of-policy steps
- Receipts tied to both the triggering evidence and policy version

args.security_impact: Reduces unsafe retries and silent partial changes. Checkpoints must be encrypted or local-only by default, with redaction before relay notification; policies cannot authorize sends, purchases, deletion, or publication.

- Relay and pendant support for reporting conflicts and collecting the owner’s choice.

This is not a silent retry or ordinary undo: it prevents stale automation from overwriting newer changes made elsewhere.

args.why_useful: Today an approval can become stale or detached from the exact operation after a long workflow, a page refresh, a changed tab, or a handoff between agents. This protects the owner from sending to the wrong person, paying the wrong amount, modifying the wrong account, or approving a broader action than they requested without forcing confirmation for every harmless step.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to normalize and compare structured intent fields. Use realtime only to ask the owner a short clarification when a material mismatch is detected; deterministic hashes and policy rules should handle ordinary matches.
args.latency_budget: No noticeable delay for reversible steps. For an irreversible step, compare the final parameter capsule in under 500 ms; if ambiguous, pause and ask one concise question rather than executing.
args.cost_estimate: Usually a small structured comparison with negligible model cost; one realtime turn only for genuine mismatches. The dominant cost is extracting final fields from an unstructured page when typed browser evidence is unavailable.
args.security_concerns: Store a minimized intent capsule rather than raw speech or page contents, with sensitivity labels and expiry. Bind confirmation to the exact normalized parameters, session/tab identity, and destination. A changed recipient, amount, or scope invalidates approval. Never silently broaden an action because an agent inferred more context.
missing: A canonical intent capsule schema shared by judgement, action, Mac, and browser
Field-level semantic diffing with materiality policies by action type
A mandatory pre-commit hook that can pause every executor, including AppleScript and browser commands
Final-state extraction for recipients, amounts, attachments, and scopes from each supported app

args.change: Implement an intent-drift firewall at the final-commit boundary. Faculty-judgement emits a canonical, expiring intent capsule with typed fields (actor, recipient, destination, amount, object, scope, attachments, side effects, and allowed alternatives). args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets protection against a subtle but costly failure: the system completes the workflow it inferred rather than the action the owner actually authorized. They see only a short exception when something materially changed, not repetitive approval prompts.

args.risk: Overly strict comparison may interrupt legitimate edits, while weak extraction may miss drift. Default uncertain cases to ask-owner for irreversible effects, allow only explicitly safe alternatives, and retain a human-readable before/after diff for recovery.
args.cost_impact: Small persistent capsules and deterministic comparisons; occasional cheap semantic-model calls and rare realtime clarification. No hardware cost.
args.latency_impact: Sub-second for typed fields; roughly 1–3 seconds when semantic extraction is required, before an irreversible commit.
args.security_impact: Reduces replay, confused-deputy, wrong-recipient, and stale-approval risk. Capsules must be encrypted or minimized, expire quickly, and exclude raw private page content unless needed for the diff.

transcript.text:
Round 102 findings:

- No new grants or tools appeared; the granted category is empty.
- Mac bridge is online, but no pendant is currently connected. Chrome/browser bridge is offline.
- Action receipts and undo are implemented, but they explicitly have **no approval gates, preconditions, or refusal checks**.
- The pendant prototype has one button and one LED. Historical TTS reaches the relay at 24 kHz, but there is no live playback-completion or button-confirmation signal.

I recorded two new proposals:

1. **Wearable approval capability:** speak a bounded action preview, then approve it with a deliberate pendant long press. Execute only on an exact, short-lived plan hash and report the receipt.
2. **Approval-lease protocol:** connect relay, pendant, Mac, and browser with one-time nonces, expiry, replay protection, precondition checks, and receipt linkage.

What is still needed:

- Pendant button-event uplink and device identity.
- Approval lease/nonce routes shared by relay, Mac, and browser.
- Executor and browser precondition gates that fail closed if the plan changes.
- Live pendant telemetry: preview delivery, playback start/finish, underruns, and button ACK.
- A connected pendant for end-to-end verification.

args.user_asks: Make sure this actually happened: after you perform an action on my Mac or in a logged-in browser, independently verify the real-world postcondition and keep working until it is true or tell me exactly what prevented it.
args.why_useful: Today the system can execute an action and produce a receipt, but a receipt only says what the executor attempted or observed. The owner needs closure: for example, not merely 'calendar event created,' but confirmation that it appears in the authoritative calendar; not merely 'form submitted,' but a confirmation number or changed account state. A separate perception pass prevents the acting agent from certifying its own mistake and lets the relay deliver a concise success/failure outcome to the pendant.
args.model_tier: Cheap background/local models for polling and comparing structured postconditions; realtime only for the owner's final spoken result or an urgent failure.
args.latency_budget: Reversible local actions: verify within 5 seconds. Browser/account changes: retry with bounded backoff for up to 10 minutes, then deliver a failure explanation and the last evidence. Never keep retrying an irreversible action; only verify or use an explicitly approved compensating action.
args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 per workflow because verification uses structured API/DOM evidence and local comparison; cost is dominated by any authenticated browser reads and optional realtime notification.
args.security_concerns: Verification must be read-only by default and scoped to the same account/session and target named in the plan. Store redacted evidence (URL, timestamp, field names, hashes, confirmation IDs where safe), not page secrets. Do not treat a visually similar page or stale cache as proof. args.user_asks: “Stop everything now.”
args.why_useful: The owner needs a physical, immediate escape hatch when the Mac or browser is acting unexpectedly—without finding the dashboard or speaking a longer explanation. A deliberate pendant gesture would revoke the active execution lease across the relay, Mac, and browser, cancel queued reversible work, and prevent an approval-gated step from being released. It is a new cross-surface emergency control, not merely an activity log or ordinary undo.
args.model_tier: No expensive model is needed: firmware and relay perform the stop deterministically. Use a cheap background model only to summarize what was halted after the fact; realtime speaks a brief acknowledgment if the link is live.
args.latency_budget: Local haptic/LED acknowledgment in under 100 ms; relay cancellation propagation under 500 ms when connected; persist the stop locally and apply it when connectivity returns.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible per invocation, under $0.001 for event storage and optional summary. Hardware cost is zero if the existing button/LED can support a guarded long press.
args.security_concerns: A false trigger could interrupt useful work, so require a deliberate 1.5–2 second hold plus distinct vibration/LED confirmation. Cancellation must fail closed: once stopped, no queued irreversible action may run until a new explicit intent. Store only job ID, step ID, and cancellation reason; never speak private page contents.
missing: Pendant firmware gesture and durable local stop latch that survives link loss
Relay-wide revocable execution leases understood by Mac and browser workers
Cancellation propagation and acknowledgement in the Mac/browser action protocols
Dashboard view showing exactly which steps stopped, completed, or remain untouched

args.change: Implement a hardware-level emergency-stop latch on the pendant: a guarded long press (for example, 2 seconds) sets a persistent stop bit, emits a distinct vibration/LED pattern, and transmits a signed stop event whenever LTE reconnects. The relay treats that event as a global revocation for the owner's active execution leases; Mac and browser workers poll/subscribe to lease revocations and must abort before their next side effect. Clearing the latch requires a separate deliberate gesture and a fresh owner intent.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can halt an unexpected automation immediately from the device in their hand, even when speech, Safari, the dashboard, or the network is unavailable. It prevents a queued action from continuing silently after the owner has lost trust in the run.
args.effort: Medium: firmware button state machine and persistence, authenticated event type, relay lease registry, cancellation hooks in both executors, and an end-to-end fault-injection test for link loss and reconnect.
args.risk: Accidental stops interrupt work; use a long press and unmistakable feedback. A worker that fails to receive revocation could still act, so every side-effecting action must validate a short-lived lease immediately before execution. Recovery is to inspect receipts, clear the latch intentionally, and start a new transaction.
args.cost_impact: Near-zero API cost; approximately 1–4 KB firmware flash/RAM plus a few bytes of nonvolatile state. No new hardware cost if the existing button and LED are sufficient.
args.latency_impact: Local stop feedback is immediate; network-connected cancellation should occur within 0.5–2 seconds, with fail-closed checks at each subsequent action.
args.security_impact: Requires authenticated, replay-protected stop events and owner/device binding. The stop bit should reveal only job identifiers and status, not private browser or Mac data.
depends_on: A signed pendant event format and reconnect queue
Relay execution leases with revocation and expiry
Mac and browser executors checking the lease before every side effect
A dashboard receipt that distinguishes cancelled, completed, and never-started steps

Typed compensating actions with preconditions and postcondition verification for files, app state, and authenticated page fields
A dependency-aware rollback planner that stops when a later mutation depends on an earlier one

args.user_asks: “If this condition happens, carry out the bounded plan I gave you and tell me exactly what changed.” For example: if my authenticated travel page reports a cancellation, find an option under my stated limits, prepare it, and only commit automatically if every constraint and freshness check still passes; otherwise wake me on the pendant with the exact decision needed.
args.why_useful: Today the owner can ask for a check or a one-off action, but cannot safely leave a conditional, bounded plan running across a private browser session, their Mac, and an always-awake relay. This turns interruptions and changing external events into useful action without granting the system an open-ended standing mandate.
args.model_tier: background for polling/event normalization and constraint evaluation; planner only when the event requires multi-step option generation; realtime only to wake the owner and handle the live approval conversation.
args.latency_budget: Event ingestion under 30 seconds when a watch changes; option preparation under 2 minutes; owner wake-up is immediate when a constraint is ambiguous or a commit boundary cannot be met.
args.cost_estimate: Usually deterministic/background: roughly 1–3 cheap model calls per event (about $0.01–$0.08 depending on page extraction and option count). Planner escalation dominates cost only for ambiguous multi-site workflows.
args.security_concerns: The contract must be scoped to named accounts/tabs, allowed vendors, maximum amount/time, and an expiry. Private page contents leave the browser only as minimized fields and cited evidence. No irreversible commit may occur without a fresh exact-constraint proof; if evidence is stale, a session changes, or the Mac/browser disappears, the system pauses and asks. Every attempted mutation needs an immutable receipt and replay protection.
missing: conditional-action contract and durable trigger state (distinct from a passive page watch)
constraint evaluator that produces a machine-verifiable commit predicate
event-to-action idempotency and lease ownership across relay, Mac, and browser
fresh authenticated-page evidence capture immediately before commit
pendant-resume approval bound to the exact contract revision and evidence hashes

args.change: Create a durable conditional-action contract layer between page watches/events and executors. A contract stores a normalized trigger predicate, allowed action graph, hard limits (amount, destination, time window, account/session), expiry, and an owner-selected consequence policy. On each watch/event update, the relay evaluates the predicate deterministically, asks a background model only to extract candidate fields from cited page evidence, and emits either a no-op, a prepared action, or a pendant escalation. Immediately before any mutation it re-reads the authenticated source, recomputes the predicate, and requires the executor receipt to reference the same contract revision and evidence hashes. This is not a passive watch or a generic job runner: it is the missing connective control plane that converts an external event into a constrained, auditable action.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can leave a narrowly defined contingency in place—rather than repeatedly noticing a change and manually restarting the whole workflow—while retaining hard limits and a clear wake-up when reality falls outside them.
args.effort: High: contract schema/versioning, event deduplication, predicate evaluator, private-page extraction adapters, scheduler/expiry handling, and policy/receipt integration across relay, browser, and Mac.
args.risk: A mistaken predicate could authorize an unwanted consequence. Default new contracts to prepare-only, require explicit opt-in per consequence class, enforce maximum spend and destination allowlists in deterministic code, and halt on missing/stale evidence. Contract revisions are immutable; revocation must be immediate and tested during network partitions.
args.cost_impact: Background polling/extraction adds modest relay and browser costs; deterministic predicate checks are negligible. Planner escalation is reserved for candidate generation and should be uncommon.
args.latency_impact: Adds one authenticated re-read before commit (typically 1–5 seconds); event detection remains watch cadence-limited. No realtime model is needed unless waking the owner.
args.security_impact: Contracts contain sensitive account/action policy and must be encrypted/access-controlled. Store field hashes and citations rather than raw private pages where possible; bind execution to session identity, contract revision, and one-time action nonce to prevent replay.
depends_on: authenticated page-watch/event normalization
typed action schemas and receipts
fresh evidence/provenance capture
owner policy and expiry model
pendant notification/resume channel

args.why_useful: Today judgement can choose an action but action execution is fragmented: browser may be offline, the Mac may be busy, and a receipt can exist without a way to stop an in-flight job. A durable, owner-visible baton makes long-running work safe and comprehensible: the relay stays awake, the Mac/browser performs the step that has reach, and the pendant remains the immediate cancel/status surface.
args.model_tier: gpt-5.6-luna for planning/recovery decisions; deterministic relay/local executors for leases, retries, receipts, and cancellation; gpt-realtime-2.1 only for the short spoken update.
args.latency_budget: Immediate spoken acknowledgement under 500 ms; lease/state updates under 2 s; execution may run for minutes without holding the voice turn open. Reconnect reconciliation within 10 s.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per multi-step task depending on planner retries; deterministic state/receipt traffic dominates neither tokens nor compute. No model call for cancel, status, lease expiry, or reconciliation.
args.security_concerns: The relay must never receive private page contents or credentials; owner-private browser legs remain on the authenticated Safari/Chrome bridge. Use a short-lived, audience-bound lease and idempotency key; reject stale workers and duplicate commits. Pendant cancel should be available without speech. Require explicit confirmation before irreversible browser/Mac actions; retain only hashes, field-level before/after evidence, and configurable audio/job retention.
missing: A single durable action-baton state machine shared by relay, Mac agent, browser bridge, and dashboard (queued/claimed/running/paused/cancel-requested/cancelled/committed/failed/expired).
Lease claim/renew/revoke and exactly-once commit endpoints with worker identity, fencing token, idempotency key, and heartbeat timeout.
Pendant event/push mapping for status, pause, and cancel, including offline event spool and replay (the requested offline_intent_spool and physical_action_confirmation skills are still absent).

args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can feel that a requested Mac/browser action was accepted, is waiting, or failed while walking, in a noisy room, or with audio muted. transcript.text:
Discovered and recorded:

- **Cross-surface action baton:** durable ownership, leases, pause/cancel, reconnect reconciliation, and receipts across relay, Mac, browser, and pendant.
- **Tactile action feedback:** proposed a haptic actuator and button patterns for accepted, pending, failed, and cancel states.
- **Live defect:** Mac action jobs are failing at the executor boundary with errors such as “requires `appName`/`command`/`script`,” despite those values appearing in the recorded action objects. The browser bridge is offline with **11 pending commands**, while the Mac bridge is online.
- Sent judgement the required **24 kHz audio receipt fields**: correlation ID, codec/rate/frame details, packet gaps, underruns, playback timestamps, device identity, local acknowledgement, and partial/failure states.

What I still need:

1. An implemented shared action schema/normalizer between `/execute`, `mac_run_actions`, and the local executor.
2. A durable lease/cancellation state machine and pendant event path.
3. A real pendant connection for haptic/audio validation; none is currently online.
4. The previously requested 24 kHz acceptance criteria and audio-path probe results.
5. Owner decisions on confirmation policy, retention, and timezone; those requests remain unanswered, so I will not assume them.

Accessibility and Screen Recording remain unavailable, but these proposals do not depend on those grants.

args.user_asks: “That partly failed—repair it without repeating anything that already happened.” After a Mac, browser, or relay action is interrupted, inspect the real state across the relevant surfaces, identify the exact boundary reached, and safely complete or roll back only the missing reversible work. Return a proof of the repaired final state, not merely a retry log.
args.why_useful: Today a failed multi-surface task leaves the owner to guess whether anything happened. Retrying can duplicate a message, appointment, file, or browser submission; undo is often unavailable once the worker or connection disappears. State-based repair would turn ambiguous failures into safe recovery, especially when the pendant goes offline after the Mac has already acted.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background planner for state diff and repair-plan generation; deterministic typed probes and action receipts establish facts; reserve realtime for the short owner-facing explanation and confirmation when a repair could change external state.
args.latency_budget: Initial failure classification under 2 seconds; read-only reconciliation under 10 seconds; any repair requiring approval waits indefinitely for the owner rather than timing out into execution.
args.cost_estimate: Usually $0.01–$0.05 per incident, dominated by one background planning call and surface reads; deterministic retries and receipt comparison are negligible.
args.security_concerns: Never infer completion from a timeout. Read private browser state only through the authenticated bridge and keep credentials on-device. Repairs that send, submit, delete, purchase, or alter external records require fresh confirmation with a precise diff. Store hashes and provenance rather than page contents; expire sensitive evidence.
missing: A state-invariant and reconciliation protocol: each action declares its expected postcondition and an idempotent observation method.
Cross-surface read probes that can verify those postconditions after worker loss, including authenticated browser state and Mac filesystem/app state.
A repair planner that produces a minimal diff from observed state, with explicit safe-to-repeat and must-not-repeat steps.
A durable incident record linking the original intent, every receipt, observed state snapshots, repair approval, and final proof.
Per-action compensation adapters for effects that are reversible but lack a current undo implementation.

args.user_asks: “Tell me the private part only when it is safe.” Route sensitive results and confirmations to the owner’s pendant only when the paired device proves it is present; otherwise leave a redacted notification on the Mac/dashboard and wait. This should cover logged-in browser findings, account alerts, and action receipts without exposing their contents to nearby people or an unattended speaker.
args.why_useful: The system can reach private browser sessions and produce speech, but it has no owner-presence boundary: a spoken account balance, message preview, or approval payload can be overheard when the pendant is elsewhere. Presence-bound disclosure lets the owner use the hive in shared spaces without choosing between privacy and usefulness.
args.model_tier: No model call for presence, pairing, sensitivity labels, or redaction. Use a background model only to summarize after the policy gate; realtime speaks only after an authenticated presence grant.
args.latency_budget: Presence decision under 200 ms from a valid pendant heartbeat/button nonce; redacted fallback under 1 second. Never speak sensitive content while presence is uncertain.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost for gating; roughly a few hundred bytes of authenticated telemetry per heartbeat and event. Optional background summarization costs less than $0.01 per briefing.
args.security_concerns: Use mutually authenticated device keys and short-lived proximity/session proofs, not Bluetooth name or network address alone. Treat browser contents, messages, financial data, and action diffs as sensitive by default. Do not send raw private content to the relay when a local redacted route is possible. Require explicit owner policy for categories and provide an immediate pendant mute/lock gesture.
missing: A paired-device cryptographic presence protocol with freshness and replay protection.
Sensitivity labels propagated from browser extraction through planner, receipt, TTS, and dashboard rendering.
A relay policy gate that refuses sensitive TTS/upload when the presence proof is absent or stale.
Local redaction templates and a dashboard review queue for withheld content.
Pendant firmware support for secure presence nonce, lock/mute gesture, and offline policy cache.

transcript.text:
Recorded two capabilities:

1. **State-based repair after partial failure**  
   The owner should be able to say, “That partly failed—repair it without repeating anything.” The system needs postconditions, cross-surface state probes, minimal repair plans, compensation adapters, and proof of the final state.

2. **Presence-bound private disclosure**  
   Sensitive browser findings, account alerts, and action receipts should be spoken only when the paired pendant proves the owner is present. Otherwise, the system should provide a redacted Mac/dashboard notification and wait. This requires cryptographic presence proofs, sensitivity propagation through TTS and receipts, and a relay disclosure gate.

Both were passed to `propose_capability`; they are now recorded.

args.change: Add a cross-surface execution contract between faculty-judgement and faculty-action. Every dispatched plan carries typed steps {target surface, preconditions, intended effect, proof obligation, confirmation class, idempotency key, expiry}. faculty-action may execute reversible steps autonomously, but must return a structured receipt only after satisfying the proof obligation (for example: reminder ID exists, file hash matches, browser field value is observed after reload); otherwise it reports blocked/unknown rather than success. The relay persists the contract and checkpoints, routes each step to Mac AppleScript, browser bridge, or relay, and resumes only uncompleted idempotency keys after disconnect/restart. Irreversible steps stop at the existing confirmation boundary. This is intentionally narrower than a generic durable runner: it prevents the mind from saying 'done' when an action merely dispatched.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner says 'handle it,' they get a trustworthy answer: completed with evidence, waiting for their decision, or genuinely unable—not a confident success message after a dropped browser or half-finished Mac action.
args.effort: Medium-high: shared contract schema, relay persistence/checkpointing, adapters for existing Mac and browser receipts, and planner/action tests for duplicate delivery and missing proof.

args.change: Introduce a resumable cross-surface workflow contract: every delegated browser/Mac step emits a redacted checkpoint containing workflow ID, tab/session identity, precondition hash, side-effect status, next step, and one optional owner decision schema. Recorded three new items:

- **Attention boundary:** the owner can say “I’m busy,” and the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser pause non-urgent work and suppress interruptions until explicitly released.
- **Decision-point delegation:** the system handles a long browser/Mac workflow until it reaches a decision only the owner can make, asks one constrained question on the pendant, then resumes the exact step.

They require shared attention-state semantics, durable resumable workflow checkpoints, constrained pendant question/answer transport, tab reattachment, and fail-closed page precondition validation.
