transcript.text:
This round I recorded three capabilities and one firmware change:

1. **Pendant-confirmed actions** — the system prepares a Mac/browser action, shows a nonce-bound pending state on the pendant, and commits only after a physical button press. This is the most important missing action path: voice can decide, but the worn device authorizes irreversible work.
2. **“Save what I’m looking at”** — capture the active authenticated Safari tab into an encrypted handoff capsule containing URL, title, selected/salient text, timestamp, and a short label, then make it available later as a note or spoken queue item.
3. **Safe receipt-aware undo** — resolve “undo the last thing,” verify that the post-action state has not changed, and execute an exact inverse only when the receipt and state proof are valid.
4. **USB tether confirmation firmware** — while the chips are attached to the Mac, use nonce-tagged serial commands, LED pending/accepted/expired states, debounced button events, monotonic sequence numbers, and fail-closed expiry. This makes the pendant useful before LTE registration.

The recorder noted that the first capability is close to an existing “prepare on Mac/browser, confirm on pendant” proposal, so the genuinely new part is the **local USB-tether implementation and nonce/state-proof protocol**, not the general confirmation concept.

What I still need:

- A local USB device registry or serial transport exposing `/dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658*` and `/dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA` to the Mac bridge.
- Pendant firmware support for button events, LED state, nonce validation, and durable ACK delivery.
- A planner/action schema carrying operation digest, expiry, preconditions, and inverse descriptors.
- Active Safari tab identity and extraction support for the handoff capsule.
- Reconciliation of an important status conflict: live discovery reports **no registered pendant**, although the system says both chips are physically connected over USB. Until that is resolved, the system must explicitly distinguish “locally tethered pendant” from “relay-registered pendant.”

args.user_asks: Lock my private Mac and browser when I walk away, and unlock them only when my pendant is back with me and I tap its button.
args.why_useful: The owner's browser contains authenticated accounts and the Mac holds private notes, mail, and files. A wearable presence-and-tap authorization would protect those surfaces without relying on remembering to lock them, while avoiding the dangerous behavior of unlocking from voice alone.
args.model_tier: No expensive model for presence or locking; realtime only for exceptional spoken status questions.
args.latency_budget: Lock within 5 seconds of confirmed absence; unlock within 1 second of a valid local tap and presence proof.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero API cost. Hardware/security integration dominates.
args.security_concerns: Never use proximity alone to unlock. Require a cryptographic pendant identity, recent local button tap, replay-resistant challenge, and owner-configured grace period. Revoke the device credential when lost; keep private page contents off the relay.
missing: secure pendant identity storage or secure element
BLE/UWB or equivalent presence signal in addition to USB tethering
Mac login/session-lock integration and browser tab redaction/locking
credential rotation and lost-device revocation route
owner-visible audit log of lock/unlock events

args.user_asks: Read whatever is currently in front of me on the Mac, one short piece at a time, and let me skip or revisit pieces with the pendant button.
args.why_useful: The owner could consume a long email, private webpage, terminal result, or document while walking, cooking, or unable to look at the screen. The Mac has reach into private sessions and the pendant supplies an always-available physical navigation control.
args.model_tier: Cheap extraction/chunking model for ordinary text; realtime only for spoken control and ambiguous references.
args.latency_budget: First chunk in under 2 seconds; next/previous controls under 300 ms locally once queued.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.002–$0.02 per document depending on OCR and summarization; cache chunks by document fingerprint.
args.security_concerns: Read only the explicitly foreground source; never sweep unrelated tabs or hidden fields. Keep extracted text on the Mac unless the owner asks for relay delivery, encrypt the queue, and expire it after playback.
missing: foreground-app and selection extraction across Safari, Notes, Mail, terminal, and PDFs
pendant playback queue with next/previous/repeat button events
text-to-speech output path and interruption handling
screen-reading permission or equivalent accessibility-free adapters
source boundary and sensitive-field redaction

args.user_asks: If my pendant is lost or stolen, revoke it immediately, stop it receiving queued audio or commands, and tell me the last trustworthy place and time it was seen.
args.why_useful: A wearable is an authorization device as well as an audio endpoint. The owner needs a single emergency action that prevents a found device from replaying private queued material or approving work, even when the pendant is offline.
args.model_tier: Deterministic security workflow; no model needed except a short spoken explanation.
args.latency_budget: Credential revocation and queue quarantine within 2 seconds when the Mac or relay is reachable; apply the quarantine on the pendant's next connection.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost; durable credential and event storage dominate.
args.security_concerns: The emergency command must be available from the authenticated Mac/dashboard and require strong owner authentication, but must not reveal the bike-lock secret or other sensitive memories. Last-seen data must be coarse by default and tamper-evident.
missing: device credential lifecycle and revocation list
pendant-side boot-time quarantine and queue wipe
last-seen attestation with trustworthy clock/source
a Mac/dashboard emergency control and recovery enrollment flow
separate recovery credential that does not depend on the lost pendant

args.change: Add a small secure-element-backed identity and presence subsystem to the pendant: per-device signing key, monotonic anti-replay counter, challenge-response over USB today and BLE/UWB presence later, plus a tamper-evident lost-device quarantine flag. Keep private audio and page data out of the secure element; it stores only keys, counters, and state.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant can become a trustworthy personal key for privacy and recovery, rather than merely another unauthenticated serial endpoint. If it is lost, the owner can revoke it without exposing queued commands or private audio.
args.effort: High: board revision or secure-element daughterboard, bootloader integration, Mac/relay credential lifecycle, and recovery UX. Prototype over the existing USB serial chips before committing to a board change.
args.risk: Bad provisioning or a corrupted counter could permanently strand the owner. Include an offline recovery credential, atomic counter updates, factory-reset enrollment, and a clearly documented replacement flow.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $2–$8 per device for a secure element and supporting parts; negligible runtime API cost and low power draw.
args.latency_impact: Challenge response adds tens of milliseconds locally; presence decisions depend on BLE/UWB sampling and should not block ordinary audio.
args.security_impact: Substantially improves resistance to replay, stolen-pendant use, and forged confirmation packets; requires careful key backup policy so private keys never leave the device.
depends_on: a defined device credential lifecycle
Mac and relay lock/revoke endpoints
pendant firmware update and bootloader path
owner recovery enrollment and audit UI

transcript.text:
Recorded four proposals:

- **Presence-bound privacy lock:** lock private Mac/browser sessions when the owner leaves; unlock only after cryptographic pendant presence plus a fresh physical tap.
- **Pendant-controlled read-aloud mode:** read the foreground Safari page, document, terminal result, or email in short chunks, with next/previous/repeat controlled physically from the pendant.
- **Lost-pendant emergency quarantine:** revoke credentials, stop queued audio and commands, quarantine pending actions, and report the last trustworthy seen time.
- **Hardware-backed pendant identity:** secure-element-backed keys, anti-replay counters, challenge-response, and a tamper-resistant quarantine state.

The key changes required are not ordinary model work: secure pendant identity, presence sensing beyond USB, Mac session-lock integration, foreground-content extraction, a pendant playback/navigation queue, credential revocation and recovery enrollment, and an auditable security control surface.

transcript.text:
Recorded four new capabilities and one stack change:

1. **Privacy departure lockdown** — “I’m leaving” safely pauses notifications/media, hides or closes allowlisted sensitive apps and browser sessions, reports completion through the pendant, and leaves an undo receipt.
2. **Focus session with exact restoration** — “Hold my focus for an hour” snapshots Mac/browser state, enters quiet mode, provides a pendant emergency escape, and restores only what it changed.
3. **Pendant capture-to-action packets** — a distinct button gesture captures the frontmost app, selected text/clipboard, active Safari tab, and timestamp for later continuation without re-explaining context.
4. **Emergency help gesture** — a physical pendant gesture sends an owner-approved message to a configured contact, retries until delivery is verified, and exposes cancellation/status.
5. **Cross-surface action saga coordinator** — joins relay jobs, Mac receipts, browser request IDs, and pendant serial sequence numbers into one timeline with verified prepared/committed/failed states instead of trusting a generic success response.

What is still needed:

- A distinct pendant gesture and local emergency event path, separate from conversation start/end.
- Offline event spooling and cancellation behavior on the pendant.
- A relay delivery adapter with bounded retries and delivery receipts for emergency alerts.
- Owner-configured emergency contact, message, location-consent, and privacy-lockdown policies.
- Mac adapters for Focus state, notification control, frontmost app, selected text, clipboard, and Safari tab metadata.
- A durable job runner and cross-surface receipt coordinator; the existing pieces are present, but they do not yet form a verified transaction.
- Signed USB serial gateway telemetry from the physically connected pendant/ESP32, without treating telemetry as authorization.

The physically tethered pendant and audio bridge are usable for testing now, but the LTE device remains unregistered.

args.user_asks: “Run presentation mode.” While I present, let the pendant’s button advance or go back through Keynote/PowerPoint/browser slides, let me ask the mind to jump to a named slide or display speaker notes on the Mac, and give a clear LED/audio acknowledgement for every transition.
args.why_useful: The owner gets a discreet, wearable presentation remote that can also recover from a wrong slide without touching the laptop. It combines a physical control, Mac application state, browser content, and optional audio feedback in a way no single node can provide.
args.model_tier: Deterministic button commands for next/previous; a cheaper planner for slide-name lookup; realtime only for ambiguous spoken corrections.
args.latency_budget: Button-to-slide transition under 250 ms; spoken slide lookup under 2 s.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.01 per session; mostly local AppleScript/browser actions.
args.security_concerns: Bind control to the explicitly selected presentation window and session; do not capture microphone audio or slide contents unless requested. Require a clear start/stop gesture and show the active presentation target.
missing: Presentation-session binding for Keynote, PowerPoint, and browser slides
A pendant button gesture/state distinct from conversation control
Low-latency Mac event channel with ordered acknowledgements and recovery when the presentation app changes

args.user_asks: “Fill this out without exposing my private data.” Have the Mac and authenticated browser inspect the form, fetch only the minimum matching values from local sources, fill reversible fields locally, and show me a field-by-field provenance and redaction report before anything leaves the Mac or is submitted.
args.why_useful: The owner can use logged-in services without handing the relay a copy of their identity, financial, or health data. The browser can reach the private form while the Mac remains the privacy boundary and the pendant can announce that review is waiting.
args.model_tier: Background extraction/classification model on the Mac; realtime only for owner questions about a field.
args.latency_budget: Form inspection under 5 s; review report under 10 s; zero network transmission of protected values.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.01–0.05 per form; dominated by local structured extraction and optional semantic matching.
args.security_concerns: Treat all field values as sensitive by default. Keep raw values on the Mac, send only field labels, redacted previews, and hashes to the relay/dashboard, and require explicit approval for each sensitive field or a narrowly scoped batch.

args.change: Add a local privacy kernel between the Mac agent and browser bridge: classify every outgoing field, clipboard value, screenshot region, and page extraction as public, personal, or secret; enforce a deny-by-default export policy; perform matching, redaction, and hashing locally; and return verifiable proofs that the relay saw only the permitted projection.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask the system to act on private websites and documents without trusting that the cloud model received their passwords, identity numbers, or financial details. Privacy becomes an enforced behavior rather than a promise in a prompt.
args.effort: High: local classifier, browser protocol changes, policy UI, test corpus, and fail-closed integration across every Mac/browser route.
args.risk: Over-redaction can make tasks fail; recover by showing the blocked field category and allowing a narrowly scoped, time-limited local approval. Misclassification must never export a secret by default.
args.cost_impact: Moderate local CPU/RAM; small relay storage for policy decisions and hashes, with no raw sensitive payloads.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms for structured fields and more for screenshots; no added latency when an action contains only allowlisted metadata.

args.user_asks: “Protect me if the pendant disappears.” If the worn device is unexpectedly disconnected or its heartbeat stops, lock the Mac, pause private browser work, revoke only the sessions I have configured as high-risk, and notify me through another channel; distinguish a planned USB unplug from a loss and let me recover safely when the pendant returns.

args.model_tier: Fully deterministic heartbeat and policy engine; no expensive model required.
args.latency_budget: Detect unexpected loss within 5 s; lock/pause within 2 s after detection; recovery status when the pendant reconnects.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible per event; persistent heartbeat telemetry and occasional notification fees dominate.

args.security_concerns: Never persist passwords, payment fields, tokens, or unrestricted page HTML. transcript.text:
Recorded four new action proposals:

1. **Pendant-held authorization for consequential actions**  
   Prepare Mac/browser work, but execute only while the owner physically holds the pendant button. Releasing it or unplugging the pendant aborts pending steps.

2. **Physical attention beacon**  
   A deliberate pendant gesture starts a short, escalating Mac/ESP32 audio-and-LED beacon to help locate a nearby phone, bag, or person. It automatically times out and can be stopped from the pendant.

3. **Walk-away handoff**  
   A pendant tap snapshots the current browser/Mac task—tabs, selected text, files, pending jobs, and next step—so the owner can leave and later resume only after reviewing the stale-state checks.

4. **Pendant-bound job completion channel**  
   Durable Mac/browser job outcomes become signed, redacted receipts delivered as a pendant LED/audio notification, including queued delivery after reconnection and deduplication.

What I still need:

- A defined serial protocol for button gestures, LED state, acknowledgements, and disconnect events on the connected nRF9160/ESP32 hardware.
- A firmware-side physical-presence/gesture event; the pendant is physically connected to the Mac but is still not relay-registered.
- Durable relay outbox semantics for queued notifications and action leases.
- Browser snapshot/resume primitives with stable tab identity and hash-based stale-state validation.
- The owner’s explicit policy for which action classes may use “button held” consent versus requiring a separate confirmation.
- The owner must still manually grant Accessibility/Screen Recording if true GUI automation is needed; I did not re-request the denied permission.

args.user_asks: If I hold the pendant's emergency gesture, start a timed safety check: alert me locally, notify my chosen contact with my last confirmed location/status, and escalate only if I do not cancel. Let me cancel from the pendant even if the Mac or voice session is unavailable.
args.why_useful: A wearable should be able to summon help when the owner cannot reach a phone or speak. The pendant, relay, Mac, and browser/phone surfaces together can provide a resilient escalation path rather than a cloud-only panic button.
args.model_tier: Deterministic firmware and relay state machine; no expensive model during the emergency. Realtime model is used only if the owner speaks afterward and asks for explanation.
args.latency_budget: Local alert under 250 ms; relay notification under 2 seconds; escalation window configurable from 15 seconds to 10 minutes.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost; SMS/push delivery and relay storage dominate, roughly cents per activation.
args.security_concerns: Require an intentional gesture, an unmistakable countdown, explicit contact configuration, encrypted status, and no location sharing outside the configured escalation chain. Test mode must be impossible to confuse with a real alert.
missing: device-local emergency gesture and cancel latch
relay emergency state machine with authenticated device identity
location/status source and a configured notification provider
owner-configured contacts, escalation delay, and test mode

args.user_asks: Move an active private browser task between my Mac and another trusted device without copying passwords: package the exact task state and a short-lived capability, let me approve the transfer with the pendant, and reopen it on the destination with secrets remaining in the destination's authenticated browser.
args.why_useful: The owner can leave the Mac, continue on another trusted surface, and return without losing a half-finished private task or exposing credentials to the relay. The pendant supplies a physical, human-visible handoff rather than an invisible session clone.
args.model_tier: Deterministic state packaging and cryptographic capability transfer; a cheap model summarizes the task state, while realtime handles only spoken approval.
args.latency_budget: Package in under 2 seconds; destination becomes resumable within 5 seconds; capability expires quickly if not redeemed.
args.cost_estimate: Under $0.01 per transfer for summarization; storage and encrypted relay transport dominate.
args.security_concerns: Never export cookies, passwords, or raw session tokens. Bind the short-lived capability to both devices, a task hash, and the pendant gesture; revoke on mismatch or expiry. Require explicit approval for any resumed mutation.
missing: cross-device trusted-pair registry
browser task-state export/import that excludes credentials
relay-encrypted one-time capability exchange
destination-side reattachment and stale-state validation

args.change: Add a low-power tactile/haptic actuator and a secure element to the pendant, with firmware-managed patterns for countdown, success, failure, waiting-for-approval, and cancelled states. The secure element should attest the device and protect a monotonic event counter without exposing private keys to the Mac or relay.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets unmistakable private feedback in a noisy or socially inappropriate environment and a trustworthy physical identity for approvals, transfers, and emergency actions. They can understand whether the system is waiting, finished, or cancelled without opening a screen.
args.effort: High: enclosure/board revision, driver and power-budget work, secure-element provisioning, firmware protocol, and relay verification.
args.risk: Extra power draw, uncomfortable vibration, or actuator failure could hide state. Use bounded patterns, a hardware mute, watchdog fallback to LED, and manufacturing-time key recovery procedures.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $4–$12 in components and assembly at low volume; roughly 5–20 mA during haptic pulses and negligible idle draw, plus engineering and provisioning cost.
args.latency_impact: Local state feedback can begin below 100 ms; attestation adds tens to hundreds of milliseconds before a remote action is accepted.
args.security_impact: Improves resistance to forged USB events and replayed approvals, but key provisioning and device replacement become security-critical. No private key should leave the secure element.
depends_on: A defined pendant event/state protocol
Relay verification of device attestation and monotonic counters
Owner-approved tactile patterns and emergency behavior
A hardware revision compatible with the existing nRF9160 enclosure and battery

transcript.text:
Recorded:

- **Credential-free private task transfer between trusted devices**  
  The owner should be able to move an active authenticated browser task from the Mac to another trusted surface using a short-lived pendant-approved capability, without exporting cookies, passwords, or session tokens. This requires a trusted-device registry, credential-free browser state export/import, encrypted one-time relay capabilities, destination reattachment, and stale-state validation.

  The owner should receive unmistakable private haptic status—waiting, approved, succeeded, failed, cancelled—and use the pendant as a cryptographically attested physical approval device. This requires a low-power haptic actuator, secure element, monotonic event counter, firmware state protocol, relay attestation verification, and a hardware revision compatible with the current enclosure and battery.

transcript.text:
Recorded six proposals this round:

- One-button pendant capture that saves the current Mac app/browser context as a note, reminder, or idea.
- Resume the last unfinished task by reopening exact files/tabs and reporting completed, failed, and blocked steps.
- Pause reversible work when the pendant disconnects and offer safe continuation after reconnect.
- A context-capture broker joining pendant events, Mac state, browser state, and `/capture`.
- A resumable task-bundle manifest spanning files, browser tabs, receipts, and pending decisions.
- A presence-scoped execution controller with disconnect checkpoints and reconnect diffs.

What I still need:

1. **Pendant event transport** — authenticated button and link-presence events over today’s USB serial path, later reusable for LTE.
2. **Context snapshot APIs** — active Mac app/window and current browser tab, with local redaction before anything reaches relay storage.
3. **Step-level execution semantics** — typed checkpoints distinguishing completed, attempted, paused, and safe-to-resume actions.
4. **Browser reattachment guarantees** — stable session/tab IDs and read-only restoration before any mutation.
5. **Audio acknowledgment path** — a verified way to send the short confirmation/status response to the pendant.
6. **Owner approval for the eventual firmware/toolchain work** — I can specify and test the protocol, but will not build, flash, or modify hardware without the separate approval already noted.

The largest remaining unknown is the exact pendant serial event protocol: until button and connection-state events are defined, the Mac and relay cannot reliably know that an intentional physical capture or safe resume request occurred.

args.security_concerns: Define a deny-by-default field policy for credentials, tokens, health/financial identifiers, and message bodies. transcript.text:
Round 126 produced four new records:

1. **Possession-bound approval** — a fresh, expiring action nonce bound to the exact planned action, approved by a physical pendant interaction before execution.
2. **Partial-success reconciliation** — inspect actual post-action state before retrying, repair only missing steps, and report exactly what changed.
3. **Checkpointed workflows** — Mac/browser perform safe steps while the pendant pauses the workflow for risky-step confirmation or local cancellation.
4. **Cross-surface armed-state indicator** — relay, Mac, browser, and pendant show the same pending action, target, hash, and expiry, disarming on mismatch.

The recorder confirmed these are connective gaps between existing routes, not repetitions of a single existing feature.

What I still need:

- A **pending-action ledger** carrying action hash, one-time nonce, target, expiry, and approval state.
- A **cross-surface receipt/postcondition ledger** linking browser tab identity, Mac job, resulting object, and evidence.
- A **USB-serial pendant bridge** for confirmation/cancellation that works today while LTE registration is absent.
- A **durable checkpoint workflow state machine** with pause, resume, timeout, cancel, and repair semantics.
- The owner’s explicit **risk policy** for which actions may be auto-executed versus requiring physical confirmation.
- A verified **pendant identity and button/LED protocol**; the device is physically attached, but still not registered with the relay.
- The previously requested build/device inspection and audio-path acceptance criteria remain unavailable.

args.user_asks: “Move this appointment to the best available time, but don’t cancel the current one unless the replacement is confirmed.”
args.why_useful: The owner gets safe multi-system transactions instead of brittle sequences that can leave them with no appointment, duplicate bookings, or a missing reservation. The system can negotiate a replacement, hold it, and commit only when the complete transition is evidenced.
args.model_tier: A cheaper background planner searches and compares options; deterministic transaction orchestration handles holds, commit ordering, compensation, and timeouts. Realtime is used only for presenting the choice and receiving a final preference.
args.latency_budget: Show viable options within 60 seconds where the site permits; commit confirmation within 2 seconds after the owner’s pendant approval; retain the old booking until the replacement has a durable confirmation.
args.cost_estimate: $0.02–$0.15 per transaction, dominated by authenticated-page extraction and any negotiation/planning calls.
args.security_concerns: Never expose booking credentials or commit without explicit approval. Bind every hold and commit to the exact account, appointment, timezone, and expiry. If a site cannot guarantee holds, stop rather than simulate atomicity. Missing today: a saga/compensation coordinator, reservation-hold abstraction, and cross-site transaction policy.
missing: cross-service transaction coordinator with compensation steps
reservation/hold and expiry model
commit proof requirements for each supported service

args.user_asks: “When I leave my desk, keep the task alive and tell me on the pendant only when I need to make a decision that cannot wait.”
args.why_useful: The owner can hand off long tasks without keeping a Mac screen open or listening continuously. The relay filters routine progress, while the pendant delivers only deadline-bearing decisions with enough context to act from anywhere.
args.model_tier: Background model summarizes progress and classifies urgency; a cheap deterministic scheduler handles deadlines and quiet hours; realtime is reserved for the brief spoken interruption and response.
args.latency_budget: Decision alerts delivered within 3 seconds of detection; routine work may continue for minutes or hours without conversation turns.
args.cost_estimate: $0.005–$0.03 per task-hour depending on polling and summarization; most idle time uses no model calls.
args.security_concerns: Only send minimum necessary information to the pendant; redact private page content and require a physical confirmation for consequential decisions. Offline delivery needs a bounded local queue and expiry so stale prompts cannot commit anything. Missing today: urgency/deadline policy, durable decision inbox, and pendant notification protocol.
missing: durable decision inbox with deadline and escalation semantics
quiet-hours and urgency policy
pendant notification/acknowledgment transport

args.user_asks: “Give me a private, spoken handoff when I arrive home: what changed while I was away, what decisions are waiting, and what I can safely approve now.”
args.why_useful: This creates a useful boundary between unattended work and owner control. Instead of a noisy stream of alerts or a generic morning briefing, the owner receives a compact, current handoff that separates completed work, blocked work, and actions ready for approval.
args.model_tier: A background model compiles the handoff from receipts, deadlines, and pending decisions; realtime speaks it when the owner requests it. Deterministic filtering excludes stale, already-resolved, or low-priority items.
args.latency_budget: Generate within 5 seconds on request; spoken handoff under 60 seconds by default, with drill-down on demand.
args.cost_estimate: $0.005–$0.04 per handoff, mostly summarization; receipt collection and filtering are deterministic.
args.security_concerns: Require owner presence/physical pendant acknowledgment before reading sensitive titles aloud; support a silent LED/vibration summary and explicit “details” command. Never infer completion from absence of an error. Missing today: a cross-surface handoff compiler, privacy-aware audio policy, and presence/arrival signal.
missing: handoff compiler over jobs, browser sessions, and decisions
privacy-aware spoken disclosure policy
arrival/presence trigger or explicit pendant request path

transcript.text:
Recorded three new capabilities:

- **Safe cross-service appointment/reservation moves** using holds, explicit commit ordering, and compensation if the replacement fails.
- **Away-from-desk decision delivery** where long-running work continues and the pendant interrupts only for urgent, expiring decisions.
- **Private arrival handoff** summarizing completed work, blocked work, and approvals waiting when the owner returns.

These require new transaction coordination, durable decision/handoff queues, privacy-aware pendant delivery, and presence/arrival signaling—not merely wiring existing routes together.

transcript.text:
Round 127 findings:

- Mac bridge is online and relay-reachable.
- Safari extension is online with three tabs, but the active tab currently failed to open.
- Computer-use vision loop is disabled; vision upload consent is false.
- Accessibility and Screen Recording remain unavailable, while AppleScript automation remains granted.
- No new orchestrator grants appeared this round.

I recorded four new proposals:

1. **Physical-confirmed transactions:** complete a booking or purchase across authenticated browser tabs, but require a short-lived pendant button press immediately before final submission, then provide an immutable receipt.
2. **USB-tethered pendant controls:** use the physically connected pendant button and LED for one-press capture, double-press urgency, and hold-to-cancel while the Mac is reachable.
3. **Cross-surface action timeline:** unify spoken intent, browser evidence, proposed mutations, pendant confirmation/refusal, execution result, and undo/receipt links into one auditable record.
4. **“Save this page to my project”:** extract the useful content from the current private Safari tab and create a versioned local project artifact with provenance.

What I still need:

- A Mac serial harness for `/dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658*` and a defined pendant event/confirmation protocol.
- A relay confirmation gate that binds a physical button nonce to one specific browser job.
- Browser extraction that can detect and explain inaccessible frames, with a top-level-page fallback.
- An atomic Mac project-artifact writer with source manifests and versioning.
- For full GUI automation only, the owner must manually grant Accessibility and Screen Recording to **AI Pendant Agent**; I will not re-request those denied permissions.

args.user_asks: “Close out my last meeting.”
args.why_useful: The owner gets the work after the meeting, not merely a calendar briefing: the Mac finds the latest meeting note and related email, the browser supplies any private follow-up context, the system extracts decisions and owners, creates reminders, and prepares clearly separated follow-up drafts for review. The pendant gives a concise spoken recap while the Mac keeps the evidence packet.
args.model_tier: Use a background text model for note/email extraction and task clustering; use realtime only for the spoken command and short recap. Deterministic Mac actions create reminders and drafts but never send them.
args.latency_budget: Return an initial meeting artifact in 10 seconds and finish extraction in under 30 seconds; pendant recap under 5 seconds after completion.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.06 per meeting, dominated by summarizing several notes/messages; reminder and draft creation are deterministic.
args.security_concerns: Meeting notes, mail, and private tabs may contain sensitive information. Keep source content on the Mac, pass only bounded excerpts to the model, preserve citations and confidence, and never send follow-ups automatically. Require review for every external draft.
missing: A unified meeting-time correlation across Calendar, Notes, Mail, and browser tabs
A structured decision/action extractor with source spans and owner attribution
A Mac writer that creates grouped reminders and review-only drafts with provenance

args.user_asks: “Make a safe-to-share version of this private page and put it in my project.”
args.why_useful: The owner can turn sensitive authenticated material into a redacted artifact without manually hunting for passwords, account numbers, tokens, or personal details. The browser provides the private source, a background model proposes redactions with highlighted evidence, the Mac writes a separate version, and the pendant reads a short disclosure summary before any sharing step.
args.model_tier: Cheap background model for candidate entity detection and redaction suggestions; deterministic pattern scanners for credentials and identifiers; realtime only for the owner’s request and disclosure recap.
args.latency_budget: Candidate scan in under 8 seconds for a normal page; redacted artifact and side-by-side change list under 20 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.04 per artifact; local deterministic scanning should handle most secrets and keep model usage low.
args.security_concerns: The unredacted source must remain local. Never upload raw page contents by default. Write a separate output, preserve a non-sensitive source hash, show every proposed removal, and require explicit approval before export or sharing. False negatives must be called out rather than implied safe.
missing: A local redaction scanner for browser text and screenshots
A provenance-preserving artifact/diff writer
A share-safety policy that distinguishes local save, clipboard, email attachment, and external upload

args.change: Add a pendant-led interruption and resumption contract for delegated work: every long-running Mac/browser operation publishes a compact next-step capsule (goal, current checkpoint, required owner input, expiry, and safe cancellation state). A button gesture or spoken “resume that” retrieves the capsule and resumes only from the last verified checkpoint, rather than replaying earlier actions.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can walk away from a task, return hours later, and continue without remembering which tab, form, or step was in progress. The pendant communicates waiting/error/completed states without opening the Mac, while stale or ambiguous work stops safely instead of silently repeating an action.
args.effort: High: define checkpoint semantics across browser and Mac jobs, persist capsules in the relay, implement pendant status gestures, and make every executor idempotent at checkpoint boundaries.
args.risk: A bad checkpoint could skip a prerequisite or duplicate a mutation. Require explicit checkpoint receipts, short leases for irreversible steps, and default to reopening for review when proof is missing. Recovery is a visible paused state with raw job links.
args.cost_impact: Small durable-state cost; background summarization is optional and inexpensive. No realtime model call is needed for status or resume routing.
args.latency_impact: Button acknowledgement under 200 ms; resume decision under 2 seconds; no added latency to ordinary actions.
args.security_impact: Capsules may reveal private task names and URLs. Encrypt relay storage, minimize contents, expire them, and require the same owner/device pairing for resume.
depends_on: A stable operation/checkpoint identifier shared by Mac jobs, browser sessions, and relay state
A pendant event channel and local status/acknowledgement protocol
Idempotent browser and Mac execution at checkpoint boundaries

transcript.text:
Recorded three new proposals:

- **“Close out my last meeting.”** Extract decisions and action items from Calendar, Notes, Mail, and relevant private browser context; create attributed reminders and review-only follow-up drafts, then give the owner a spoken recap.
- **“Make a safe-to-share version of this private page.”** Detect credentials and personal information locally, produce a separate redacted artifact with a complete change list, and require approval before export or sharing.

args.user_asks: “Only interrupt me when it is genuinely urgent; let me acknowledge it from the pendant.”
args.why_useful: The relay can watch Mac/browser sources while the owner is away from the screen, but the pendant is the only surface that can deliver a compact interruption and receive a physical acknowledgment. It prevents both missed urgent changes and notification spam.
args.model_tier: background classifier on relay; realtime only for the owner's follow-up conversation
args.latency_budget: Urgent event to pendant under 10 seconds; routine events are batched. Acknowledgment should be recorded under 2 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Low: event filtering and one short notification per true urgent event; dominated by relay wakeups and occasional Mac/browser polling, not LLM calls.
args.security_concerns: Private browser/calendar/mail facts must remain on the relay/Mac path and only a redacted category plus short summary should reach the pendant. Require explicit per-source opt-in and never expose account contents on the LED/audio channel without an owner request.
missing: event subscriptions from Mac Calendar/Mail and authenticated browser watches
a relay-to-pendant push transport for the currently USB-attached device and later LTE
pendant acknowledge/quiet-mode protocol
urgency policy and deduplication state

args.user_asks: “Pin what I’m looking at right now so I can ask about it later.”
args.why_useful: A physical pendant gesture would capture the owner's fleeting context before a tab, selection, or app changes. The later question can be answered from a time-stamped capsule instead of guessing which page or text they meant. This is especially useful today because the pendant is USB-connected to the Mac even without relay registration.
args.model_tier: cheap local extraction and hashing on the Mac; realtime model only when the owner later asks a question about the capsule
args.latency_budget: Create a capsule in under 1 second after the button gesture; later retrieval under 3 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Low: local metadata/selection capture and compact text hashing; model cost only for later semantic retrieval or explanation.
args.security_concerns: Capsules may contain private page text. Store encrypted locally by default, retain only a short TTL, show a visible LED acknowledgment, and require an explicit command before syncing content to the relay. Do not silently capture microphone audio or passwords.
missing: an accessibility-free active-selection bridge (AppleScript/browser extension fallback where available, with honest unknown-selection state)
pendant USB gesture and capsule-status protocol
encrypted capsule schema with URL, foreground app, selected text, screenshot/hash, timestamp, and provenance
cross-surface retrieval endpoint

args.change: Add a unified wearable event envelope shared by pendant USB today and relay/LTE later: event_id, source, severity, expiry, redacted payload, acknowledgment state, and provenance pointer. Mac/browser jobs, watch notifications, and action receipts publish into it; the pendant renders only the compact envelope and returns ack/snooze/dismiss events. Deduplicate by event_id across reconnects.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets one dependable way to hear about urgent changes and know whether the system actually delivered them, rather than separate silent queues on the Mac, browser, and relay.
args.effort: Medium-high: protocol, USB serial transport, relay queue, reconnect semantics, and pendant firmware/UI; can be prototyped over the live USB-connected chips without flashing by using the Mac bridge.
args.risk: A malformed or duplicated event could annoy the owner or hide an urgent one. Use bounded queues, expiry, replay tests, and a Mac dashboard fallback; never let notification delivery mutate the source account.
args.cost_impact: Small relay storage and bandwidth; negligible model cost because envelopes are produced by existing jobs/classifiers.
args.latency_impact: Adds one queue hop, typically tens to hundreds of milliseconds over USB and under a few seconds over LTE.
args.security_impact: Redaction and provenance indirection reduce sensitive data on the pendant, but event metadata still reveals activity; encrypt transport and make source subscriptions explicit.
depends_on: relay-to-pendant transport over USB, then LTE
pendant acknowledgment firmware
event producers for browser/Mac watches
durable deduplication/TTL storage

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

args.user_asks: “Tell me what is waiting for my review, in order, and let me dismiss or reopen one from the pendant.”
args.why_useful: Long-running Mac and browser work currently finishes into separate job, receipt, and briefing surfaces. A wearable review queue gives the owner one truthful list while away from the screen, with enough identity to resume the exact item rather than starting over.
args.model_tier: no model for aggregation; use a cheap background summarizer only to compress stale receipts, reserving realtime for spoken follow-up
args.latency_budget: Queue refresh under 3 seconds after reconnect; one spoken item under 2 seconds; dismiss/reopen acknowledgment under 1 second.
args.cost_estimate: Very low: existing job/receipt records plus short summaries; occasional summarization is the only model cost.
args.security_concerns: The pendant must receive titles and redacted status, never raw private page contents or account tokens. Reopening an item should deep-link to the authenticated Mac/browser session, and any irreversible continuation must remain behind the existing review/approval surface.
missing: a cross-surface queue projection joining jobs, receipts, browser sessions, briefings, and capture capsules
pendant list navigation and dismiss/reopen commands over USB/LTE
stable deep links from a queue item to its Mac or browser session
TTL and privacy classification for displayed summaries

args.subject: Live context gaps confirmed
args.body: Fresh discovery: /observe exposes foreground app (Claude), running apps, permissions; /machine-context inventory/timezone/automation. /browser/inspections is live but empty. Devices list sees Safari (3 tabs) and Mac bridge online, but no registered pendant/LTE. Active selection and evidence locators remain unexposed.

transcript.text:
Discovered and recorded four new capabilities/changes:

1. **Urgent interruption channel** — relay/Mac/browser classify meaningful events, send a redacted alert to the pendant, and accept acknowledge/snooze/dismiss.
2. **Physical context pinning** — a pendant gesture captures the current Mac/browser context for later retrieval, without opening the microphone.
3. **Unified wearable event envelope** — common USB/LTE event protocol for notifications, acknowledgments, expiry, deduplication, and provenance.
4. **Wearable review queue** — pending jobs, receipts, briefings, and browser tasks become one ordered queue that can be reviewed or dismissed from the pendant.

What I still need:

- An active-selection/evidence-locator surface. `/observe` provides the foreground app and running applications; `/machine-context` provides inventory and automation details, but neither exposes the selected text, DOM locator, or current browser element.
- A relay-to-pendant transport. The Mac bridge is online, but the device registry still shows no registered pendant/LTE device.
- Pendant-side protocols for gesture input, compact notifications, acknowledgment, queue navigation, and reconnect/deduplication.
- A cross-surface queue projection joining jobs, receipts, browser sessions, briefings, and journal records.
- A privacy-preserving capsule schema for pinned context, including TTL, encryption, redaction, timestamp, URL, and provenance.

The most immediately testable item is context pinning over the physically connected USB pendant and Mac bridge, once the active-selection fallback behavior is defined.

args.user_asks: “Put the whole hive in private mode now, and tell me when no pending capture or upload still contains private data.”
args.why_useful: A wearable owner needs an immediate, physical privacy boundary that covers the Mac, authenticated browser, relay queues, and pendant—not merely muting one application. This gives a trustworthy way to stop context collection before entering a sensitive situation and receive a verifiable cleanup result.
args.model_tier: Deterministic policy engine; no model needed except optional natural-language explanation.
args.latency_budget: Local Mac/browser capture stops within 500 ms; relay revocation and purge receipt within 5 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Low storage and queue-scan cost; no routine model spend.
args.security_concerns: Private mode must fail closed on uncertain connectivity, revoke future uploads, quarantine already queued payloads, and show exactly what could not be deleted. It must not claim deletion from third-party browser/server history that it cannot control.
missing: signed privacy-mode command from pendant
shared capture/upload gate across Mac, browser, and relay
queue inventory with deletion receipts and honest unknown states
visible pendant confirmation and recovery path

args.user_asks: “Before you use a logged-in account, prove to me which account and identity you are about to act as.”
args.why_useful: The owner may have multiple accounts or stale authenticated tabs. The system should not infer identity from whichever tab happens to be open; it should bind the planned action to an explicitly displayed account, domain, tab, and freshness proof across the browser and Mac.
args.model_tier: Deterministic account/session binding and cryptographic challenge; use the model only to explain ambiguity.
args.latency_budget: Identity check under 2 seconds for an open session; stale or conflicting sessions pause before any mutation.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost; small metadata and challenge storage.
args.security_concerns: Never transmit cookies or credentials. Bind only to extension-reported origin, account label, tab/session identifier, and a nonce; if the browser cannot prove identity, report unknown rather than guessing.
missing: authenticated account identity reporting from the browser bridge
freshness and origin attestation for tabs
pendant-readable identity summary
a pre-action gate that consumes the attestation

args.user_asks: “When I say I’m leaving, package exactly where I was across the Mac and browser so I can continue from the pendant or another device.”
args.why_useful: Today a task can be split across an active app, private tabs, drafts, and queued jobs, but losing the Mac session loses the owner's place. A portable, privacy-scoped handoff would preserve the unfinished intent, evidence pointers, and safe next step without copying secrets or requiring the original screen.
args.model_tier: Cheap background state summarization; realtime only when the owner asks to resume or resolve ambiguity.
args.latency_budget: Create handoff in under 3 seconds; resume summary under 2 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Low: compact encrypted metadata and provenance pointers; occasional summarization cost per handoff.
args.security_concerns: Never replicate cookies, passwords, or full private page bodies by default. Encrypt the capsule, scope it to the owner's device/session, expire it, and make every included tab, draft, and queued action visible before transfer.
missing: portable encrypted handoff format
browser/Mac task-state and draft extraction with secret redaction
relay storage and device-to-device retrieval
resume validator that checks tabs and data are still fresh

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

1. **A physical whole-system privacy mode**  
   The owner should be able to put the pendant, Mac, browser bridge, and relay into a fail-closed private state and receive a truthful deletion/quarantine receipt.  
   **Required changes:** signed pendant command, shared capture/upload gate, queue inventory, purge receipts, and explicit reporting of anything unreachable or undeletable.

2. **Account-identity proof before logged-in actions**  
   Before acting, the system should identify the exact domain, account, tab/session, and freshness state it is using instead of trusting whichever authenticated tab is open.  
   **Required changes:** browser account attestation, origin/session freshness, pendant-readable identity summary, and a pre-action gate that blocks ambiguous identity.

3. **Portable encrypted task handoff**  
   The owner should be able to say “I’m leaving” and preserve their exact unfinished state—intent, evidence pointers, drafts, and safe next step—for later continuation from the pendant or another device.  
   **Required changes:** encrypted handoff format, secret-redacted Mac/browser state extraction, relay storage, and a resume validator that checks freshness before continuing.

args.user_asks: “During a meeting, when I tap the pendant, mark that moment and remember what was being discussed; afterward, give me a sourced action list and draft follow-ups.”
args.why_useful: The pendant is the only always-with-me, low-friction marker. It lets the owner capture decisions without touching the Mac, while the Mac/browser can add agenda, document, and participant context afterward.
args.model_tier: Realtime model only for the tap/short acknowledgment; background model for transcript segmentation, document lookup, and follow-up drafts.
args.latency_budget: Tap acknowledgment under 300 ms; post-meeting synthesis within 2 minutes of the meeting ending.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.03–$0.15 per meeting depending on audio duration; transcription and synthesis dominate.
args.security_concerns: Meeting audio and private documents leave the device to the relay/Mac pipeline. Require explicit meeting-mode start, visible recording indicator, local retention limit, and approval before any draft is sent or calendar/task is changed.
missing: A device-side tap marker event carrying monotonic timestamp and meeting-mode state
A Mac audio/transcript segmenter that can align marker timestamps to speech
A cross-surface evidence bundle linking transcript spans, browser sources, and generated drafts

args.user_asks: “I’m leaving my desk—make sure the document or page I was working on is ready to continue later, and tell me on the pendant exactly where I left off.”
args.why_useful: This turns an interruption into a recoverable handoff instead of lost context: the Mac records the active work state, the browser preserves the authenticated tab, and the pendant gives a concise resumption cue while walking away.
args.model_tier: Cheaper background model for summarizing and indexing the work state; realtime model only if the owner asks a follow-up by voice.
args.latency_budget: Capture state within 5 seconds of the trigger; spoken resumption cue within 10 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Under $0.02 per handoff for local metadata and a short summary; model cost scales with page/document text.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated URLs, document snippets, and unsaved text are sensitive. Never transmit full page contents by default; store an encrypted local pointer plus minimal excerpt, and require confirmation before reopening or sharing anything.
missing: A reliable desk-away trigger (pendant button pattern or Mac idle/lock event)
A browser/Mac active-work snapshot schema with unsaved-buffer detection
A pendant playback queue for short resumption cues

args.change: Add a physical, offline-capable panic/abort gesture to the nRF9160 pendant: a long press emits a signed high-priority abort event over USB serial (and LTE when registered), flashes the LED distinctly, and is idempotently consumed by the relay to cancel all owner-scoped Mac/browser jobs that have not reached an irreversible checkpoint. The event must queue locally if disconnected and expire after a short TTL.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can stop an automation immediately with the device in their hand, even when the voice link or Mac UI is stuck—preventing an unwanted send, purchase, or other external action.
args.effort: Medium-high: firmware gesture/state machine, signed event framing, relay cancellation fan-out, and job-runner cancellation semantics.
args.risk: False triggers could cancel useful work; use a deliberate 2–3 second hold plus LED/audio confirmation. A queued abort must not cancel a later unrelated job, so bind it to an owner/session epoch and TTL. Recovery is simply rerun the canceled job after review.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; roughly 1–2 KB firmware flash and well under 2 KB RAM. No new hardware if the existing button/LED are usable.
args.latency_impact: Local LED indication under 100 ms; USB cancellation target under 500 ms, LTE path dependent on network.
args.security_impact: Abort events need authenticity and replay protection; never accept a bare serial byte as a global cancel. Keep payload to owner/session/job epoch, not content.
depends_on: A stable pendant-to-Mac serial event protocol
Durable job cancellation propagation through /jobs/:jobId/cancel and browser command deletion
An irreversible-action checkpoint contract in the Mac/browser runners

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

args.user_asks: “When I double-tap the pendant, let me speak a quick thought while I’m away from the Mac; turn it into the right note, task, or reminder and read back what you captured.”
args.why_useful: The owner can capture ideas hands-free without opening a laptop or leaving a Mac microphone on. The pendant/bridge supplies the physical input, while the Mac can place the result in the correct project or reminder system.
args.model_tier: Realtime model for endpointing and a brief read-back; cheaper background model for classification, deduplication, and filing.
args.latency_budget: Start recording within 200 ms of the double-tap; read-back within 5 seconds after speech ends.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per capture; audio transcription dominates.
args.security_concerns: Audio is private and may contain bystanders. Show a recording LED, require a deliberate gesture, encrypt queued audio, auto-delete raw audio after transcription, and ask for confirmation when classification would create an external or high-impact task.
missing: A pendant/ESP32 button-to-record event and local audio framing protocol
An offline queue for captures when the pendant is only USB-attached or temporarily disconnected
A classifier that maps text to Notes, Reminders, project journal, or a review inbox with confidence and provenance

The connective routes already exist; the missing work is the contracts between them.

args.user_asks: “Before you send, buy, publish, delete, or change anything important, ask me to press the pendant; only that physical press should authorize this exact operation.”
args.why_useful: A physical cryptographic gesture is harder to trigger accidentally than voice and does not expose approval secrets in speech. It gives the owner one consistent, device-bound authorization across browser sessions, Mac apps, and relay jobs.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap deterministic verifier for the signed challenge; reserve the realtime model for explaining the pending operation in plain language.
args.latency_budget: Challenge and pendant acknowledgment under 500 ms over USB; under 2 seconds when relayed over LTE.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost; approximately 1–2 KB per authorization receipt and occasional relay storage.
args.security_concerns: The challenge must bind to exact action arguments, target account, expiry, and session; prevent replay and downgrade to voice approval. Losing the pendant needs revocation. Show a human-readable summary before the press and retain an auditable receipt.
missing: A cryptographic challenge-response protocol between pendant and Mac/relay
Action intents that expose a canonical hash of all irreversible arguments
A browser/Mac executor gate that refuses execution without a matching unexpired physical authorization

args.user_asks: “If my Mac, browser, or relay goes offline while something is in progress, tell me exactly which step completed, which did not, and what is safe to retry—on the pendant when it reconnects.”
args.why_useful: Today a disconnected multi-surface action can leave the owner unsure whether an email, form, or booking happened. A cross-surface reconciliation report prevents duplicate actions and turns partial failure into a safe next step.
args.model_tier: Deterministic event reconciliation first; a cheaper model summarizes the resulting state. Realtime is only needed for the short reconnect announcement.
args.latency_budget: Persist every step before execution; produce a recovery state within 3 seconds of reconnection.
args.cost_estimate: Low: event metadata is a few KB per job; model cost is under $0.02 for a short recovery summary.
args.security_concerns: Receipts may contain private URLs or account details. Encrypt them, minimize payloads, bind them to an owner/job epoch, and never infer success from a timeout. Mark unknown explicitly and require review before retrying irreversible steps.
missing: A durable cross-surface step event schema with pre/post state and idempotency keys
A reconciliation worker that compares Mac, browser, and relay receipts after partition
A compact reconnect notification and safe-retry presentation on the pendant

args.change: Add a cross-surface 'intent lease' protocol: every action the judgement faculty hands to faculty-action carries an owner, scope, expiry, and allowed side effects. The relay displays the lease state, the Mac/browser executors enforce it at every step, and the pendant can renew or revoke it with a deliberate gesture. Expired leases halt before the next external mutation and report the exact boundary.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Long-running automation will stop being a runaway process. The owner can safely say 'continue for the next ten minutes' or revoke authority from the pendant, even if the original conversation has ended.
args.effort: High: shared lease schema, enforcement middleware in both executors, relay persistence, and pendant gesture/state UI.
args.risk: Clock skew, lost renewals, or an overly short lease could interrupt benign work. Use server-issued monotonic expiries, checkpoint only between steps, and make paused jobs resumable rather than silently failed.
args.cost_impact: Tiny metadata overhead and negligible API cost; no new hardware if the current button/LED can signal lease state.
args.latency_impact: One local verification per action step; renewal under 500 ms on USB and a few seconds over LTE.
args.security_impact: Strongly improves least-privilege and revocation. Lease tokens must be signed, audience-bound, non-replayable, and exclude raw credentials.
depends_on: Canonical action intents and preconditions
Durable job checkpoints and receipts
A pendant gesture/event transport

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

args.user_asks: “If I set a check-in deadline and then become unreachable, try the pendant, my Mac, and my approved contact channels in order; only escalate after showing that each attempt failed.”
args.why_useful: The wearable is the one surface that can follow the owner away from the Mac. A transparent escalation chain could provide real safety value during travel, illness, or a solo activity without requiring the owner to keep a phone conversation open.
args.model_tier: Deterministic scheduler and delivery receipts for escalation; a background model may summarize failures, but no model should decide whether to escalate or who receives a message.
args.latency_budget: Heartbeat and deadline evaluation within 30 seconds; each escalation attempt gets a bounded timeout and a final status within 2 minutes.
args.cost_estimate: Low scheduled-job cost plus SMS/email/channel fees; roughly $0.01–$0.20 per escalation attempt depending on channel.
args.security_concerns: This is safety-critical and can expose location or distress information. Require explicit setup, named contacts, a test mode, clear cancellation, signed delivery receipts, no inferred medical claims, and confirmation of the exact message and data shared before arming.
missing: A durable deadline/heartbeat contract spanning pendant, relay, and Mac
LTE/device registration and a low-power pendant heartbeat path
A verified contact-channel adapter with delivery receipts and a prominent armed/disarmed state

transcript.text:
Recorded three new proposals:

1. **Physical authorization for irreversible actions**  
   The owner presses the pendant to authorize the exact purchase, send, deletion, or publication. This requires signed challenge-response between pendant, relay, Mac, and browser, plus executor-side enforcement.

2. **Cross-surface failure reconciliation**  
   After an outage, the system reports precisely which steps completed, which are unknown, and what is safe to retry. This requires durable step events, idempotency keys, reconciliation across Mac/browser/relay receipts, and pendant reconnect notifications.

3. **Deadline-based safety check-ins**  
   If the owner misses an explicitly armed check-in, the system tries the pendant, Mac, and approved contact channels in sequence, showing every failed attempt before escalation. This requires a heartbeat protocol, registered LTE path, durable deadlines, verified contact adapters, and clear armed/disarmed controls.

I still need the underlying cross-surface protocols: signed pendant events, durable action checkpoints, lease/expiry enforcement, device registration, and verified delivery receipts.

args.user_asks: “I’m stepping away—lock everything down.”
args.why_useful: One physical command would immediately protect an unattended laptop: close or suspend private browser sessions, stop queued Mac work, mute the audio path, and leave a reversible audit trail. It uses the worn object as the trusted trigger instead of relying on a voice phrase that could be overheard.
args.model_tier: Realtime interprets the short intent; deterministic relay policy and the Mac agent execute the bounded lockdown; no background model is needed.
args.latency_budget: LED acknowledgement within 300 ms; local Mac/browser changes within 3 s; relay receipt within 10 s.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.01 per invocation; dominated by one realtime intent turn, not device operations.
args.security_concerns: A false trigger could interrupt work, so require a deliberate long press plus a nonce LED pattern and keep restore reversible. No page contents leave the Mac; relay stores only session IDs, timestamps, and action receipts. Closing tabs must never delete data.
missing: Pendant long-press event over the current USB serial bridge
A named privacy-lock policy spanning Mac jobs and browser sessions
A restore operation that reopens only the sessions closed by this lock

args.user_asks: “Bookmark exactly where I am; I’ll continue later.”
args.why_useful: A wearable bookmark would turn an interruption into a resumable work state: the Mac records the frontmost app and reversible document context, the browser bridge records the relevant tab URLs/titles and scroll anchors, and the relay makes a compact spoken resume card. On return, one button or voice command reopens the right tabs and presents the next unfinished step instead of forcing the owner to reconstruct it.
args.model_tier: A cheap background planner normalizes the captured state; realtime is used only when the owner asks for the spoken resume card.
args.latency_budget: Capture acknowledgement under 1 s; resume card under 15 s; restoration may take up to 30 s and must report partial success.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.02 per bookmark, mostly one small background summarization; storage is a few KB of metadata plus no copied page secrets.
args.security_concerns: Persist opaque tab/session references and local document paths, not page bodies or clipboard contents. Private tabs must be opt-in. Reopening a tab is reversible and must not submit forms or trigger mutations.
missing: A serial bookmark event and timestamped LED confirmation on the pendant
Mac APIs for frontmost app/document context without screenshots
Browser extraction of per-tab URL/title/scroll anchor with session binding
A resume-card schema and idempotent restore job

args.user_asks: “The action failed—figure out what went wrong and get me to a safe retry.”
args.why_useful: Instead of a vague failure, the hive would collect a bounded failure packet: the Mac agent's typed step results and stderr, browser tab identity and last safe page state, relay job timeline, and pendant connectivity/LED state. It would classify whether retry is safe, prepare a minimal repair action, and speak one clear next step. This is especially valuable when the owner is away from the Mac and cannot inspect logs.
args.model_tier: A cheaper background model summarizes and clusters failures; realtime only delivers the short spoken diagnosis when requested.
args.latency_budget: Failure detection under 5 s; evidence packet under 20 s; no automatic retry of irreversible steps.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.03 per failed job; the dominant cost is background diagnosis, with evidence retained locally where possible.
args.security_concerns: Redact tokens, cookies, message bodies, and secret command arguments before relay storage. The repair plan is advisory until the owner confirms; retries must begin from a recorded idempotent checkpoint and never replay a send/purchase/delete step.
missing: A typed failure envelope shared by Mac, browser bridge, relay, and pendant
Automatic secret redaction for stderr and DOM evidence
Checkpoint metadata distinguishing safe replay from irreversible completion
A pendant error-event endpoint and a dashboard failure timeline

args.change: Add a cross-surface failure envelope and recovery coordinator. Every Mac/browser step emits a typed checkpoint with action class (replayable, inspect-only, irreversible), redacted evidence pointers, and an idempotency key. The relay joins those events with job receipts and pendant connectivity, freezes only the unsafe suffix after a disconnect or error, and exposes one repair/continue decision rather than allowing a whole workflow to replay.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When something breaks, the owner gets a trustworthy answer—what completed, what did not, and the one safe way forward—instead of duplicated messages, half-filled forms, or guessing whether a retry is dangerous.
args.effort: Medium-high: shared schema in local-agent and relay, browser adapter changes, recovery state machine, redaction tests, and dashboard timeline.
args.risk: A bad checkpoint classification could either replay an irreversible action or unnecessarily stop work. Default unknown steps to frozen; preserve current receipts and allow manual recovery. Roll out in observe-only mode first.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; small D1 event volume and a few KB per failed job.
args.latency_impact: Adds under 100 ms per step for event emission; diagnosis is asynchronous.
args.security_impact: Positive if redaction is correct: fewer raw logs in relay. Requires strict filtering of cookies, authorization headers, DOM secrets, and shell arguments.
depends_on: typed action result schema in the Mac agent
browser command IDs and tab affinity
redaction library shared by relay and Mac
owner-confirmed policy for unknown/irreversible steps

transcript.text:
Round 131 produced four new records:

1. **Pendant-triggered privacy lockdown** — a deliberate long-press closes/suspends private browser sessions, cancels queued Mac work, mutes audio, and leaves a reversible receipt.
2. **Cross-device resumable work bookmark** — the pendant bookmarks the current Mac app/document and browser tabs, then later restores the context and produces a concise resume card.
3. **Safe failure diagnosis and retry** — failed Mac/browser jobs produce a redacted evidence packet, identify what completed, freeze unsafe steps, and prepare a safe retry plan.
4. **Cross-node failure-envelope coordinator** — typed checkpoints classify steps as replayable, inspect-only, or irreversible, preventing dangerous whole-workflow replays.

What I still need:

- A pendant USB-serial event for long-press/bookmark/error signals.
- A restore policy for privacy lockdown and work bookmarks.
- A shared checkpoint schema identifying replayable versus irreversible actions.
- Secret redaction for stderr, DOM evidence, cookies, tokens, and shell arguments.
- A safe recovery state machine that defaults unknown steps to frozen rather than retrying them.

args.user_asks: “Move the information from this logged-in page into my local project, but do not send the page contents through the relay.”
args.why_useful: The owner could safely combine private browser data with local Mac work: the browser extracts only explicitly named fields, transfers them over the authenticated Mac bridge, and the relay receives only a redacted receipt. Today the system can inspect browser pages or act on the Mac, but cannot enforce this private, field-scoped boundary across both.
args.model_tier: A local Mac planner handles field selection and transformation; realtime is unnecessary except for the owner's initial command.
args.latency_budget: Preview in 5 seconds; local transfer and receipt in 15 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.02 per invocation; local processing dominates and relay traffic is metadata only.
args.security_concerns: Require an explicit field allowlist, local-only encryption, and a preview before writing. Never expose cookies, surrounding page text, or credentials to the relay; reject selectors that broaden beyond the approved fields.
missing: Field-scoped browser extraction with a local-only destination
A Mac/browser encrypted handoff channel with relay-blind payloads
A redaction and provenance receipt proving which fields moved
Local destination adapters for project files, Notes, and editor buffers

args.user_asks: “Keep my plan true, not merely recorded.”
args.why_useful: The hive would maintain a declared desired state across services—for example, a calendar appointment, a local project checklist, and a logged-in reservation—and periodically reconcile observed state. It could repair harmless drift automatically, prepare changes for review, and tell the owner when an external change makes the plan impossible. Current routines and watches report activity, but they do not maintain a cross-device invariant.
args.model_tier: Background model evaluates drift and proposes repairs; deterministic adapters perform only explicitly permitted reversible updates; realtime is reserved for spoken escalation.
args.latency_budget: Routine reconciliation within 10 minutes of a change; urgent contradiction surfaced within 60 seconds when a session is online.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.05 per reconciliation cycle, dominated by authenticated page reads and occasional background reasoning.
args.security_concerns: Desired states need scopes, expiration, and per-field permissions. Never silently change external commitments, send messages, or purchase; retain before/after evidence and require confirmation for consequential repairs.
missing: A desired-state schema spanning browser entities and Mac files/apps
Cross-surface identity matching and conflict resolution
A drift detector that distinguishes external change from stale observation
Repair policies with field-level approval and expiration

args.user_asks: “Tell me when the thing I started has actually reached the outside world.”
args.why_useful: For actions spanning the Mac and browser, the owner should receive a final, externally verified outcome rather than a local success message: the relay records the commit receipt, the browser re-reads the resulting confirmation page or message status, and the pendant gives a short completion signal. This closes the dangerous gap between 'the click happened' and 'the service accepted it.'
args.model_tier: Deterministic verification first; a cheap background model interprets ambiguous confirmation pages. Realtime only speaks the final one-sentence result.
args.latency_budget: Verification within 10 seconds of commit; ambiguous cases escalated within 30 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.03 per action, mainly one authenticated re-read; no model call for structured confirmations.
args.security_concerns: Verification must be read-only and bound to the same tab/session and idempotency key. Do not infer success from a toast alone. Store hashes/snippets rather than full private pages and require owner confirmation if the result is ambiguous.
missing: Post-commit verification contracts per browser action
A service-side correlation ID visible in receipts and confirmation pages
Read-only browser reattachment after a mutation
Pendant completion/error event protocol

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

- **Private browser-to-local transfer:** move only explicitly approved fields from a logged-in page into a local Mac project, without sending page contents through the relay.
- **Cross-device desired-state maintenance:** declare “keep this plan true,” then detect drift across browser services, Calendar, and local files and propose or perform permitted repairs.
- **Externally verified completion:** after a browser/Mac action, re-read the resulting service state and tell the owner whether it was actually accepted—not merely clicked locally.

They require field-scoped encrypted handoff, desired-state and conflict schemas, post-commit verification contracts, correlation IDs, read-only browser reattachment, and a pendant completion/error event protocol.

args.why_useful: This is the system’s highest-value action loop: the owner does not have to describe a URL, copy text, or choose a surface. The worn button/voice establishes intent, Safari supplies private context, the Mac executes reversible work, and the pendant confirms what actually happened. It turns “I’m looking at it” into useful action while preserving the send/buy/delete boundary.
args.model_tier: Realtime model only for the short intent and confirmation exchange; a cheaper background planner performs page extraction and reversible steps, with the browser harness enforcing an explicit irreversible checkpoint.
