args.user_asks: “Do this on my Mac, and keep trying safely until you can prove it worked—or tell me exactly what is unknown.”
args.why_useful: This would turn the system from a fire-and-forget remote control into a truthful executor: faculty-judgement can stage a multi-step plan, faculty-action can execute it across Mac and browser, and faculty-perception independently verifies each postcondition. If a step fails, the relay can retry only idempotent steps or run a declared compensation; the owner gets a single result of verified, safely rolled back, or unknown instead of a misleading success.
args.model_tier: background for planning and reconciliation; realtime only for the short spoken confirmation and urgent cancellation
args.latency_budget: 1–3 seconds to stage; ordinary steps may take up to 60 seconds; never claim completion before independent verification
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per workflow, dominated by planner/reconciliation model calls; verification and receipts are local/HTTP reads
args.security_concerns: Action summaries, not secrets or page contents, go to the pendant. Irreversible or ambiguous steps require the existing physical approval latch. Retries need idempotency keys, deadlines, and a visible unknown state; compensation must never be guessed.
missing: A workflow executor that persists step dependencies, idempotency keys, compensation policy, and verified/unknown terminal states
A relay fan-in that correlates mac_run_actions/browser_run_actions receipts with verify_operation_step results
Owner-configured risk policy for which classes may retry or compensate

args.user_asks: “When the pendant is plugged into my Mac, make it work as a real local voice terminal automatically; if the cable disappears, continue through LTE or queue safely without losing my turn.”
args.why_useful: The hardware is physically present over USB today while LTE registration is not. A tether-aware session would make the wearable useful now: button, microphone, speaker and Mac bridge form a low-latency local path, while the relay preserves conversation identity and hands off to LTE when available. The owner should not have to know which transport is carrying a turn or repeat a request after a cable/link transition.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the active voice turn; a cheap background worker reconciles transport handoff, queued audio, and receipts
args.latency_budget: USB local audio acknowledgement under 150 ms; transport handoff under 2 seconds; queued turns must survive arbitrary disconnects
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero incremental model cost for transport selection; $0.001–$0.02 per deferred turn for background transcription/summarization, dominated by audio retention and STT
args.security_concerns: The Mac bridge must authenticate the serial device and bind a session to a device nonce; never accept arbitrary serial input as owner speech. Local recordings remain ephemeral unless upload fails, following the existing failure-only SD rule. Handoff must reject duplicate turn IDs and replayed audio.
missing: A production serial daemon implementing the nRF9160/ESP32 framing, HELLO and CRC negotiation, with reconnect and backpressure
Relay transport/session handoff keyed by device identity and monotonic turn cursor
An explicit local-vs-LTE routing policy and a user-visible indicator of queued versus delivered turns

args.name: last_response_replay_cursor
args.what_it_does: Keeps a crash-safe cursor and a bounded cache of the last successfully delivered agent response. A deliberate gesture on sw1 (or the existing end-of-turn control once gesture semantics are specified) asks the relay/Mac bridge to replay from the last acknowledged audio cursor, and the pendant can request “repeat” even if the original downlink was interrupted. It must distinguish replay from a new turn and never enqueue a duplicate owner command.
args.why_not_server_side: The pendant is the only surface that knows the owner missed audio at the moment it happened and the only one that remains available during a USB/LTE transition. A local cursor survives a dropped link and prevents the owner from having to reconstruct a request by voice.
args.trigger: A dedicated sw1 gesture or a relay push indicating an interrupted downlink; do not overload sw0 active-edge behavior without changing the firmware gesture contract.
args.inputs: Downlink response ID, Opus frame sequence/cursor, delivery acknowledgements, interruption reason, and an optional owner gesture. No secrets or page contents.
args.storage: Persist only a small manifest in the existing typed INBOX: response ID, cursor, codec/rate, expiry, checksum, and replay count (well under 1 KB). Audio payload remains in the existing failure-path SD/relay object store; do not make a second always-on audio archive.
args.ram_budget: About 4–8 KB for cursor state and one Opus frame/packet staging buffer, plus existing audio buffers; no PCM ring buffer. This stays comfortably below the 211,608 B application RAM budget, but firmware must measure peak heap/stack with the current 24 kHz decoder.

args.change: Add a sealed low-power ERM/LRA haptic motor and a second tactile switch to the wearable revision, with a tiny driver controlled by a dedicated GPIO. Keep the current sw0 active-edge path unchanged; assign sw1 to deliberate gestures (repeat, cancel, or approval) and use haptic patterns for pending, accepted, cancelled, and link-lost states. The firmware should expose the same event envelope over USB/LTE so the relay remains the authority.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can operate and safely confirm actions in public or noisy places without putting private audio on the speaker, and a second button removes the current ambiguity between instant talk and deliberate approval/replay gestures.
args.effort: Moderate hardware revision: board layout, enclosure, driver, current draw characterization, firmware gesture/state machine, and manufacturing prototype.
args.risk: Added motor noise can leak into the microphone and false gestures can be dangerous. Require debounce, a physically distinct switch, conservative defaults, and preserve the existing approval latch semantics. If the motor fails, LED/audio cues remain available.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $1–$4 BOM increase in volume, plus PCB/enclosure NRE. Typical haptic pulse is tens of mA for under 200 ms; negligible average draw if used only for state transitions, but LTE battery impact must be measured.

Recorded four proposals this round:

1. **USB-tethered local control mode** — use the physically connected pendant and Mac bridge even without LTE, with authenticated serial framing, local allowlists, and receipt replay.
2. **“Undo the last thing”** — resolve the latest committed transaction, select a safe inverse, execute it on the correct Mac/browser surface, and independently verify the result.
3. **Truthful offline outcome reporting** — bind approval, execution, browser command, and verification to one transaction nonce so reconnects report *verified*, *failed*, *partially completed*, or *unknown* rather than implying success.
4. **Firmware implementation for USB control** — framed CBOR transport, pairing, monotonic IDs, crash-safe queues, fail-closed behavior, and pendant status signaling.

- Mac/browser acknowledgment hooks that expose fresh state for verification.
- Owner-defined local allowlist and approval policy for tethered actions.

args.user_asks: “Use what I’m looking at and handle this: save the selected text to my notes, add a reminder for tomorrow, and tell me when it is actually done.”
args.why_useful: The pendant becomes a physical 'act on this exact thing' control instead of forcing the owner to repeat URLs, titles, or snippets. It joins wearable intent, the Mac's focused app/browser state, execution, and independent verification into one dependable action—the most useful everyday action surface.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the short spoken intent; a cheaper background planner executes the multi-step workflow and faculty-perception verifies each postcondition.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 s; capture focused context in under 2 s; complete typical note+reminder flow in 10–30 s, with spoken progress if longer.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per workflow, dominated by planner/verifier model calls; context hashes and selected text stay on the Mac unless needed for the requested action.
args.security_concerns: Focused text may be private or secret. The Mac must classify sensitivity, send only the minimum excerpt/hash, redact secrets, and require the existing physical approval latch before external side effects. Never transmit passwords or page contents to the pendant.
missing: A Mac bridge primitive that atomically snapshots focused app, URL, selection, and sensitivity label
A typed context-handoff envelope consumed by planner/action
A resolved postcondition verifier route with operation and step correlation

args.user_asks: “If I lose the Mac link while you’re doing that, keep the job safe: tell me exactly whether it ran, is waiting, or was cancelled when I reconnect.”
args.why_useful: A dropped link currently forces the owner to guess whether a real-world action happened. This gives the pendant a truthful recovery conversation: durable intent state, no duplicate execution after reconnect, and a clear verified/unknown outcome across the wearable, relay, Mac, browser, and perception nodes.
args.model_tier: Relay state machine and Mac executor are deterministic; use a cheap background model only to summarize the state in natural language.
args.latency_budget: Persist state before dispatch; reconnect status available within 2 s of the Mac or pendant returning, with no requirement to keep a model session alive.
args.cost_estimate: Under $0.005 per job for durable state and a short summary; storage and receipts dominate, not inference.
args.security_concerns: Replay protection and idempotency keys are mandatory. A lost receipt must produce UNKNOWN, never SUCCESS. Sensitive action details remain on the Mac; the pendant receives only a redacted human summary and state token.
missing: Durable operation state shared by relay and Mac executor
Idempotency-key enforcement at every side-effecting executor
Reconnect status query and compact pendant status vocabulary

args.change: Add a 'context pin' gesture on sw1: while the owner is viewing a Mac/browser item, one deliberate press captures a short-lived, sensitivity-labeled reference (app, URL, selection hash, title) and gives it a visible LED/audio confirmation. The next spoken request explicitly binds to that pin; it expires after 10 minutes or on completion.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can point at a thing without reading it aloud or remembering where it lives, then speak naturally while walking away. It prevents the common failure where an assistant acts on the wrong tab or stale document.
args.effort: Medium: firmware gesture/event, Mac bridge context snapshot, relay envelope and expiry, planner binding, and perception checks.
args.risk: A stale or sensitive pin could be misapplied. Use short expiry, sensitivity-based redaction, explicit confirmation for side effects, and show the title/domain back to the owner before execution. Recovery is simply discard and repin.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a small relay record per pin. Firmware storage is a few hundred bytes if offline buffering is needed.
args.latency_impact: About 1–2 s to snapshot and acknowledge; no added latency after the pin is resolved.
args.security_impact: Improves security by binding actions to a concrete context, but selection text must not reach the pendant or relay unless explicitly required; use hashes and local redaction.
depends_on: Mac bridge focused-context snapshot API
Use sw1 (sw0 has active-edge semantics and no gesture headroom)
Existing physical_transaction_approval_latch for consequential actions

args.user_asks: “Watch this open browser page for the condition I named, and when it becomes true, do the prepared Mac action—but ask me if the page changes or the evidence is ambiguous.”
args.why_useful: The owner gets a durable, supervised bridge from browser state to real-world Mac action instead of repeatedly checking pages. It combines a browser session the relay cannot access, a Mac executor, perception of fresh evidence, and the pendant as an interruption/approval channel.
args.model_tier: Cheap scheduled/background polling and deterministic selectors first; realtime model only when the owner speaks or ambiguity needs a short clarification.
args.latency_budget: Polling cadence configurable from 30 s to 15 min; notify within one cadence plus 2 s; action starts only after fresh evidence and required approval.
args.cost_estimate: Low: browser polling is local; occasional compact perception calls cost under $0.01 per check, with model use only for changed/ambiguous pages.
args.security_concerns: Page content can include private account data. Keep observation local to the browser extension, send hashes/minimal snippets, freeze the prepared action if DOM identity or URL changes, and require physical approval for consequential side effects. Never silently act on a changed page.
missing: A durable browser watch with selector/URL identity, cadence, expiry, and change detection
A cross-surface trigger event from browser-extension to relay and Mac planner
A fresh-evidence gate that binds the action to the exact observed page revision

transcript.text:
Recorded three new proposals:

1. **Context pin from the pendant** — press sw1 while viewing an item on the Mac/browser, then speak naturally about that exact item. It uses a short-lived, sensitivity-labeled reference rather than transmitting private page contents.

2. **Safe reconnect status for interrupted jobs** — durable, idempotent operation state that reports `pending`, `cancelled`, `verified`, or `unknown` after a Mac/browser/pendant link drop, never falsely claiming success from a missing receipt.

3. **Supervised browser watches** — monitor a specific page condition and prepare the associated Mac action, but halt if the URL/DOM changes or evidence is ambiguous, with physical approval still required for consequential actions.

What I still need:

- A real Mac focused-context snapshot API: app, URL, title, selection hash, and sensitivity label.
- Durable cross-surface operation state with idempotency enforcement and reconnect queries.
- Browser watch primitives with URL/DOM identity, expiry, cadence, and revision-bound triggers.
- A resolved independent verifier: `verify_operation_step` is granted but currently unresolved.
- A real hardware audio probe: `audio_path_probe` currently resolves only to `/observe`, so it cannot perform the measurements its schema promises.
- Owner policy for which watched conditions and action classes may proceed automatically; I will not invent that policy.

args.user_asks: “Take this as far as you can, and if you hit a login, 2FA, CAPTCHA, or approval screen, tell me exactly what I need to do; then continue the same job without starting over.”
args.why_useful: Today an agent either stops at an authentication boundary or risks asking for secrets. This lets the browser extension retain the live session while the pendant gives the owner a precise, minimal handoff. The owner completes only the private step, and faculty-action resumes the original operation with evidence that the page did not change underneath it.
args.model_tier: Deterministic browser boundary detection and state machine; use realtime only for the short spoken handoff and a cheap background model to summarize non-sensitive instructions.
args.latency_budget: Detect a blocked boundary within 2 s; speak instructions within 1 s; resume within 3 s after the owner completes it.
args.cost_estimate: Under $0.02 per interrupted workflow, dominated by one compact perception/summary call. Secrets and authentication codes remain entirely on the owner's browser/device.
args.security_concerns: Never request passwords, OTPs, recovery codes, or CAPTCHA answers through the relay or pendant. Bind the continuation to the same tab, origin, and pre-boundary state; expire it after a short timeout and abort on navigation or account change. Require approval before the resumed side effect.
missing: A typed auth-boundary event containing origin, tab identity, safe human instructions, and continuation token
Browser-side detection of challenge completion without exposing secret fields
Continuation validation against pre- and post-boundary page identity

args.user_asks: “Handle this private form, but keep every secret field on my Mac and show me exactly which fields you filled before anything is submitted.”
args.why_useful: The owner could delegate tedious forms without handing the AI passwords, payment numbers, or medical identifiers. The browser holds the values locally; faculty-action fills by opaque field handles, produces a redacted field-level diff, and submits only after the owner confirms the intended non-secret values.
args.model_tier: Local deterministic field mapping and redaction; a small planner model interprets labels and summarizes the diff. Realtime is only for confirmation dialogue.
args.latency_budget: Preview in 3–8 s for ordinary forms; no submission until the owner confirms. Local secret filling should add less than 500 ms.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.03 per form, primarily label interpretation; no secret data leaves the browser.
args.security_concerns: Opaque handles, origin binding, field-type allowlists, and redaction are mandatory. The relay must never receive field values. Submission requires the existing physical approval mechanism and independent postcondition verification.
missing: Browser-local secret-field handles and fill operation
Redacted field-diff preview protocol
Origin- and form-version-bound submit token

args.change: Introduce a resumable action checkpoint protocol at every external boundary: persist a compact, redacted checkpoint containing tab/app identity, intended side effect, completed substeps, idempotency key, and the next safe operation. On retry, faculty-action must reconcile the checkpoint with fresh Mac/browser state before issuing any new mutation, rather than replaying the whole plan.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A browser crash, login interruption, or dropped connection would no longer force the owner to repeat a long workflow or risk duplicate purchases, messages, or submissions. The assistant can continue from the last proven safe point and explain precisely what remains.
args.effort: Medium-high: executor instrumentation, relay persistence, browser identity checks, and perception integration.
args.risk: A stale checkpoint could cause an incorrect continuation. Expire checkpoints, require fresh state reconciliation, and return UNKNOWN when reconciliation is inconclusive; recovery is manual restart from a newly prepared plan.
args.cost_impact: Small storage and hashing overhead; negligible model cost except when reconciliation is ambiguous.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–2 s at each external boundary, but avoids much longer retries and duplicate side effects.
args.security_impact: Checkpoints must contain hashes and labels, never form secrets or page contents; encrypt sensitive metadata at rest and bind records to the operation nonce.
depends_on: A resolved independent postcondition verifier
Executor-wide idempotency keys
Browser tab/origin identity exposed to the Mac harness

transcript.text:
Recorded three proposals:

1. **Authentication-boundary handoff** — the system drives a browser task until login, 2FA, CAPTCHA, or approval is required; the pendant tells the owner exactly what to do without receiving secrets, then the same operation resumes after validating the tab and origin.

2. **Private-form execution with local secrets** — passwords, payment data, and other sensitive values remain in the browser. The owner receives a redacted field-level preview and must physically approve before submission.

3. **Resumable action checkpoints** — every external side effect records a redacted checkpoint, idempotency key, completed steps, and next safe operation. After crashes or link loss, the system reconciles fresh state instead of replaying the entire workflow.

These require browser-local secret handles, authentication-boundary events, tab/origin and form-version binding, durable executor checkpoints, universal idempotency keys, and a resolved independent postcondition verifier.

args.user_asks: "Test the pendant and audio bridge end to end, and tell me exactly what passed."
args.why_useful: The hardware is physically attached to the Mac today, but there is no owner-facing way to turn that into a trustworthy health result. This would exercise both serial devices, button/LED paths, the ESP32 I2S bridge, and the already-accepted 24 kHz path, then return a receipt instead of a vague 'connected'.
args.model_tier: background for deterministic diagnostics; realtime only to explain failures conversationally
args.latency_budget: 15–60 seconds for a full fixture; under 3 seconds for a cached connection check
args.cost_estimate: <$0.01 per run; almost all cost is local serial and fixture time, not model tokens
args.security_concerns: No microphone capture and no flashing. Serial output may contain identifiers, so redact device IDs by default. Require explicit confirmation before any firmware write or reset.
missing: A typed Mac diagnostic operation that enumerates the two known serial ports and returns exit code, stdout/stderr, and timestamps
A read-only pendant/bridge test protocol with a versioned receipt
A relay route to persist the diagnostic receipt and expose it to faculty-perception

args.user_asks: "Make this a safe, resumable job: if the Mac loses connection halfway through, continue when it comes back and don't repeat anything that already happened."
args.why_useful: Long tasks currently span a wearable, relay, Mac, and browser, but a link drop can leave the owner unsure whether a side effect happened. A resumable step ledger with idempotency keys, postcondition verification, and a physical resume/cancel gesture would let the system finish real work without duplicate sends or silent partial completion.
args.model_tier: background for planning and reconciliation; realtime only for immediate owner questions
args.latency_budget: Immediate local acknowledgement; reconciliation within 5 seconds of Mac/browser return
args.cost_estimate: <$0.03 per job, dominated by a small planning/reconciliation call; storage and verification are local
args.security_concerns: Never replay an irreversible step from an ambiguous receipt. Store hashes and action IDs, not page secrets. Resume requires the existing deliberate pendant confirmation for risky steps; unknown outcomes are surfaced as unknown.
missing: A durable per-step idempotency/lease record shared by relay and Mac
A narrow executor receipt schema with actionId/attemptId and explicit unknown outcome
Integration of verify_operation_step into commit decisions, not merely post-hoc display
A reconnect handshake between pendant and relay for pending jobs

args.user_asks: "When I am interrupted, give me one short wearable summary and let me defer it without opening the Mac."
args.why_useful: The pendant is the only surface continuously available, while the Mac and browser know the actual context. This would have the relay combine urgency, active Mac app/browser state, and owner quiet-hours policy into a privacy-minimized spoken/LED card; a button gesture defers it and records the exact reminder, so interruptions become actionable instead of lost.
args.model_tier: small background model for ranking and summarization; realtime only when the owner asks follow-up
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds from event to a compact wearable notification; deferred item durable immediately
args.cost_estimate: <$0.01 per event with local state extraction and short summaries; batch low-priority events to reduce calls
args.security_concerns: Send only coarse app/site labels and event metadata to the relay, never page contents by default. Suppress private-window and secure-input context. Deferral is reversible; any external action still requires confirmation.
missing: A push event contract carrying urgency, expiry, and privacy classification
A pendant notification queue that can distinguish unread, deferred, expired, and acknowledged items
A Mac/browser context projection limited to labels rather than content
A two-button gesture mapping for acknowledge versus defer

args.user_asks: "Let me use the assistant on private Mac and browser data without raw page contents, messages, or documents leaving the Mac unless I explicitly allow it."
args.why_useful: Today the relay can coordinate the Mac, browser, and wearable, but the owner cannot express a durable, inspectable rule for what private content may cross that boundary. A local data firewall would make the system useful for sensitive work rather than forcing an all-or-nothing trust decision.

args.latency_budget: Under 300 ms for known patterns; under 2 seconds for an unfamiliar document with a preview
args.cost_estimate: <$0.01 per request when local; occasional background classification dominates
args.security_concerns: The firewall itself must run before relay serialization, fail closed on uncertainty, and emit only policy-safe hashes/labels. The owner needs an inspectable transfer log and one-time override; secret values must never be included in previews or model prompts.

args.user_asks: "When I ask for help with a sensitive document, show me exactly which facts the assistant used and let me revoke that access later."
args.why_useful: The owner needs more than an action receipt: they need provenance for reasoning over personal files and a way to withdraw future access. This creates a user-visible, time-bounded evidence capsule linking the pendant request, Mac/browser sources, extracted facts, and downstream actions without copying the entire source document to the relay.
args.model_tier: Background model for local evidence extraction and summarization; realtime only for a spoken provenance query
args.latency_budget: Initial capsule within 5 seconds; revocation takes effect before the next relay dispatch
args.cost_estimate: <$0.05 per sensitive task, dominated by local extraction and a compact encrypted index
args.security_concerns: Evidence capsules must contain hashes, locators, sensitivity labels, and minimal snippets by default—not source contents. Revocation must prevent future reuse but honestly cannot erase copies the owner explicitly exported; that limitation must be displayed.
missing: A Mac-local evidence capsule/index with source hashes and retention expiry

args.model_tier: Background model for clustering approved outcomes and drafting routine candidates; realtime only for preview questions
args.latency_budget: Draft after 3–5 approved repetitions; preview under 2 seconds; no automatic execution until explicit review
args.cost_estimate: <$0.05 per candidate routine; storage and clustering dominate, not realtime inference

A routine-diff/preview editor with parameter sensitivity labels
A promotion workflow from candidate to enabled routine

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

1. **Local privacy firewall** — use private Mac/browser data while ensuring raw contents stay local unless explicitly authorized. Requires a Mac-local egress interception point, typed data-sharing policies, fail-closed redaction, and an auditable transfer log.

2. **Revocable evidence capsules** — show exactly which facts and sources informed an answer or action, with time-bounded access and later revocation. Requires local provenance indexing, relay authorization checks, and a pendant-readable provenance surface.

3. **Outcome-based routine learning** — learn recurring workflows only from approved outcomes, then present an editable routine draft before automation. Requires safe training data separation, routine diffs, rejection signals, and explicit promotion to an enabled routine.

The shared missing layer is not more execution routes; it is **policy and provenance between existing planning, execution, browser inspection, and receipt routes**.

args.user_asks: “Use my pendant as a physical presence key: only while it is connected and I deliberately approve, allow a sensitive browser or Mac action; otherwise stage it.”
args.why_useful: A stolen/unattended Mac session would not be enough to send messages, submit forms, or expose secrets. The owner gets a security boundary they can carry and revoke simply by unplugging or withholding the gesture.
args.model_tier: background for policy/risk classification; realtime only for the spoken request; deterministic firmware/relay verification for the key challenge
args.latency_budget: Presence check under 300 ms; approval feedback under 1 s; no model call on the critical verification path.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.01 per use; dominated by relay requests, not inference.
args.security_concerns: The pendant must sign only a nonce/challenge and never receive page contents, passwords, or form data. Unplug, timeout, replay, counter rollback, and serial spoofing must fail closed. Sensitive action still requires the existing physical transaction approval latch.
missing: A live USB-serial pendant identity/attestation route (the device is physically connected but absent from the relay device table)
A Mac bridge watcher that exposes connect/disconnect and challenge-response without treating serial text as identity
Policy data naming which risk classes require presence, owner-confirmed later

args.user_asks: “Give me an undo button for the last safe Mac or browser action: if I press the pendant within the grace period, reverse it and tell me whether the reversal was verified.”
args.why_useful: The owner can recover from an accidental move, rename, draft edit, or browser navigation without finding the original app. It makes proactive automation tolerable because correction is physical, fast, and explicit.
args.model_tier: Deterministic action ledger and inverse planner first; background model only to derive an inverse for unfamiliar reversible operations; realtime for the brief spoken confirmation.
args.latency_budget: Undo staging immediately; physical undo dispatch under 1 s; verification within 3 s or report unknown rather than claiming success.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.02 for an unusual inverse; ordinary actions use existing ledger and no model call.
args.security_concerns: Only actions classified reversible may enter the undo capsule. Store minimal before-state hashes or safe identifiers, not secrets. Expiry, single-use nonce, and verification are mandatory; deletion, external sends, and irreversible submissions are never auto-undone.
missing: A first-class inverse/compensation schema in the existing action ledger
A pendant command for selecting the most recent undo capsule and returning a signed decision
Verifier support for inverse postconditions plus a visible unknown outcome

args.user_asks: “When I press the pendant, freeze a tiny handoff of what I’m currently doing—foreground Mac app, active browser page, and the next obvious step—so I can resume it later by asking.”
args.why_useful: The owner can leave a task mid-stream and recover it without remembering which tab, document, or draft mattered. It joins wearable intent, Mac state, browser sessions, and relay memory into a usable personal continuity feature.
args.model_tier: Realtime only to name the handoff when asked; background/cheap model summarizes the captured state; deterministic collectors gather app/tab metadata.
args.latency_budget: Capture under 2 s; spoken confirmation under 1.5 s; later retrieval under 2 s.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.01 per capture and retrieval when metadata-only; vision is invoked only if the owner explicitly asks for visual context.
args.security_concerns: Default payload is metadata and owner-supplied label, excluding page text, clipboard, passwords, and private fields. Sensitive pages require explicit confirmation before capture. Retention and deletion must be visible in the dashboard.
missing: A durable handoff object and retrieval route (distinct from browser inspection and job receipts)
A pendant press event bridge while the pendant is USB-attached but not relay-registered
A policy for private-tab/app redaction

args.user_asks: “If an action gets stuck or the page changes underneath you, stop safely, tell me exactly what blocked it on the pendant, and let me resume from that checkpoint after I answer—without starting the whole task over.”
args.why_useful: Today a multi-step task can leave the owner guessing whether it ran, partially ran, or needs repeating. A checkpointed recovery path turns failures into a short clarification instead of duplicate sends, lost drafts, or abandoned work.
args.model_tier: Deterministic executor checkpoints and postcondition verifier first; cheap background model summarizes the failure; realtime only handles the owner’s clarification.
args.latency_budget: Detect and checkpoint within 2 s of failure; spoken blocker summary within 3 s; resume within 5 s after clarification.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.02 per recovery, mostly one small summarization call; ordinary successful actions add no model cost.
args.security_concerns: Checkpoint must contain redacted locators and hashes by default, never passwords or full page contents. An uncertain postcondition must block retries until verification or explicit owner choice. External sends remain staged behind the existing physical approval latch.
missing: A durable checkpoint schema linking operation, step, executor receipt, and verifier evidence
A resume route that can safely replay only the uncompleted suffix
A pendant notification/event path while the hardware remains USB-attached but relay-unregistered

args.change: Add a local USB-pendant adapter in the Mac bridge: watch /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA, parse only the firmware's framed button/status/telemetry messages, attach a bridge-held monotonic sequence and device-session nonce, and emit signed relay events. Expose connect/disconnect and last-seen state to the action and checkpoint services, without claiming LTE registration.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The physically connected pendant becomes useful today instead of invisible: presses can approve, cancel, bookmark, or acknowledge a Mac/browser task while the owner is wearing it, and the UI can truthfully say when the device is absent.
args.effort: Medium: serial framing adapter, reconnect handling, schema tests, and a local diagnostic panel; no firmware flash required.
args.risk: Malformed or spoofed serial input could authorize actions. Fail closed on framing, session changes, counter rollback, and disconnect; require the existing physical approval latch for consequential actions. Recover by disabling the adapter and falling back to Mac-only staging.

args.user_asks: “Before you make a consequential change across my Mac and browser, show me one compact commit card—exact destination, fields or files affected, and side effects—and let one deliberate pendant approval commit the whole batch atomically, or leave everything untouched.”

transcript.text:
This round I recorded three capabilities:

1. **Verified, physically approved action execution**  
   Stage a Mac/browser action, show a redacted summary on the pendant, require deliberate physical approval, execute it, independently verify the postcondition, and report success, rollback, or unknown.

2. **Resumable multi-step jobs**  
   Let long Mac/browser workflows checkpoint after each step, pause safely for approval, and resume from the exact unfinished step after the owner returns or the connection recovers.

3. **USB-local pendant action bridge**  
   Since the pendant and ESP32 are physically attached to the Mac today—even without LTE registration—use an authenticated serial protocol for approval/cancellation, progress, and receipts. This makes the physical safety boundary usable now rather than waiting for cellular deployment.

What I still need:

- **Owner policy:** which risk classes may execute after physical approval, and which must always remain staged for explicit confirmation.
- **A transport-neutral operation envelope:** action ID, attempt ID, digest, expiry, monotonic counter, approval state, verification provenance, and unknown/rollback outcome.
- **The serial framing contract:** message types, device identity, replay protection, reconnect behavior, and fail-closed semantics for `/dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658*` and `/dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA`.
- **Exact pendant revision/button behavior:** the current hardware inventory says one `sw0` button, while earlier firmware notes referenced two buttons. I will not design gesture semantics until that conflict is resolved.
- **Perception’s required verification provenance:** I’ve asked `faculty-perception` which fields and locators it needs to bind verification receipts to an action attempt.

No hardware modification or flashing is required for the USB bridge proposal.

args.user_asks: "Keep these things consistent everywhere": when I change a real-world commitment, update every dependent surface—calendar, messages, files, and browser forms—as one coordinated operation, and stop with a precise list of what changed if any surface cannot be made consistent.
args.why_useful: Owners routinely make commitments that span applications. Today the Mac agent can act in individual surfaces, but cannot guarantee that a calendar change, notification, and related document either agree or are safely reconciled. This would prevent contradictory schedules and half-completed updates.
args.model_tier: Background model derives dependency graph and compensation plan; realtime model is used only for ambiguity or owner-facing confirmation.
args.latency_budget: Plan under 5 s; each mutation may take seconds; owner receives a progress event within 1 s of each committed or compensated step.
args.cost_estimate: $0.02–$0.10 per coordinated operation, dominated by cross-app perception and compensation planning.
args.security_concerns: Never send private contents to the relay or pendant. Each mutation needs a bounded scope, idempotency key, and an explicit compensation policy. If compensation is unsafe, stop before the next mutation and report a partial state rather than guessing.
missing: A dependency-graph representation for related app/browser artifacts
Cross-surface idempotency and compensation primitives
A durable consistency receipt that records each surface's before/after digest
Owner-configurable rules for which compensations are allowed automatically

args.user_asks: "Teach you this once": let me perform or correct a multi-surface workflow, then save the demonstrated sequence as a private, parameterized playbook that I can invoke by voice later—with approval boundaries preserved and a preview of every step that can affect another person or account.
args.why_useful: The owner cannot currently turn a corrected one-off action into a reliable personal procedure. A playbook would make the hive mind improve from interaction rather than repeatedly rediscovering the same workflow, while keeping risky steps explicit instead of silently learning authority.
args.model_tier: Background model extracts and generalizes the workflow; realtime model handles the demonstration conversation and disambiguates parameters.
args.latency_budget: Capture corrections inline; later invocation should produce a preview in under 3 s and execute each step with normal surface latency.
args.cost_estimate: $0.01–$0.08 per invocation; extraction costs occur once per newly taught playbook, with storage and verification dominating thereafter.
args.security_concerns: Playbooks must store selectors, parameter schemas, risk classes, and redacted examples—not credentials, page contents, or private message bodies. Any changed UI or account context invalidates the affected step and requires re-perception. Owner can revoke a playbook and inspect its history.
missing: A private playbook store with versioning and revocation
Demonstration-to-parameter extraction and selector generalization
A policy-preserving compiler from playbook steps to existing action risk/approval modules
Regression tests that replay steps against fresh perception without performing mutations

args.change: Create a cross-surface commitment graph owned by the owner: represent a commitment (event, person, deadline, artifact, and communication obligations) as a private semantic object, then have judgement and action resolve all linked calendar, message, file, and browser records before proposing a mutation. Perception periodically detects drift and presents only the affected edges; action can repair them through explicit, per-edge approvals.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner could say “move the launch to Thursday” once and get a trustworthy answer about every affected commitment, rather than manually remembering which calendar entry, document, form, and person now disagree.
args.effort: High: private graph schema, entity resolution across Mac/browser surfaces, drift detection, owner correction UI, and integration with action approval and verification.
args.risk: Incorrect linking could cause unrelated records to be changed. Default to read-only suggestions, require per-edge confirmation for ambiguous links, retain reversible history, and allow one-command graph freeze/revoke.
args.cost_impact: Low steady API cost for local metadata; occasional model cost for entity resolution and drift explanation. No new hardware cost.
args.latency_impact: Initial graph construction is minutes in the background; an individual query should answer in a few seconds, with mutations remaining explicitly staged.
args.security_impact: Graph contains highly sensitive relationship and schedule metadata. Keep raw contents on the Mac, send only hashes/labels to relay, encrypt at rest, and make sharing/export impossible by default.

Cross-surface entity-resolution model
Independent perception of calendar, files, browser, and messages
The coordinated-operation capability and owner approval policy

2. **Truthful bounded recovery** — execute, independently verify, retry only idempotent steps, switch surfaces when safe, and report “unknown” rather than claiming success.
3. **Cross-surface handoff capsules** — bind pendant capture, planning, execution, approval, and verification into one resumable chain with operation/action/attempt IDs, hashes, freshness, and evidence receipts.

The proposals were recorded. The recovery idea was flagged as close to existing execution/verification infrastructure, so its real novelty is the missing connective controller: retry budgets, idempotency enforcement, and alternate-surface policy.

args.why_useful: The owner gets protection against forgotten promises rather than another passive reminder. The pendant hears the commitment, the always-awake relay watches for drift, and the Mac/browser can assemble a repair using the real account context. No single node can provide this end to end.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for commitment extraction, deadline-risk scoring, and periodic reconciliation; reserve realtime for the brief warning and any owner clarification.
args.latency_budget: Capture acknowledgement under 2 seconds. Reconciliation can run hourly and on relevant email/calendar/browser events; urgent risk warnings should reach the pendant within 30 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.01–$0.08 per commitment per day, dominated by email/calendar summarization; local Mac and browser reads add no model cost.
args.security_concerns: Commitments may contain sensitive work or relationship information. Keep raw messages on the Mac where possible, send only extracted facts and hashes to the relay, and never contact anyone or alter a calendar entry without physical approval. args.cost_estimate: About $0.02–$0.10 per negotiation, dominated by thread parsing and occasional replanning; browser and calendar operations are local.
args.security_concerns: Outbound messages and calendar details are consequential. Show recipient, proposed times, and a short draft digest on the pendant; require a fresh physical approval for every send. Do not expose mailbox contents or session tokens to the pendant or relay.

The planner sends the Mac a typed operation with selectors, predicates, and a redacted summary; the Mac resolves private values inside the authenticated app, performs only the approved operation, and returns hashes plus minimal proof. args.user_asks: Before changing anything, let me ask “what would happen if you did this?” and receive a concrete preview of the resulting file, calendar, message, or browser changes—including conflicts and side effects—without mutating the Mac or browser.
args.why_useful: Today a plan is still an abstraction; the owner cannot inspect the exact proposed diff across private browser and Mac state from the pendant. A cross-surface shadow run would make consequential automation understandable before approval.
args.model_tier: Background model for shadow planning and diff explanation; realtime only to answer the short spoken preview.
args.latency_budget: Preview in under 10 seconds for ordinary tasks; never mutate while previewing.
args.cost_estimate: $0.02–$0.10 per preview depending on browser/Mac inspection and diff generation.

args.user_asks: Fill a sensitive form for me without telling the model the secret: use the browser session or Mac keychain locally, show me only the non-secret fields and destination, then let me physically approve the exact submission.
args.why_useful: The owner could automate tedious logins, payment, and personal forms while keeping passwords, card numbers, and one-time codes out of model context and out of pendant audio.
args.model_tier: Realtime for destination/field confirmation; deterministic local executor for secret retrieval and insertion; background model only for non-secret field mapping.
args.latency_budget: Field preparation under 5 seconds; submission only after physical approval.
args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.02, dominated by non-secret page interpretation; secret retrieval is local.
args.security_concerns: Secrets never cross the relay or model boundary. Use one-use capability tokens scoped to origin, field, and expiry; redact screenshots, logs, receipts, and spoken output. Refuse unexpected origins or extra fields.

Browser and Mac executors that accept opaque secret handles rather than values

args.why_useful: The owner cannot currently delegate a private, ongoing follow-up that spans browser and Mac sessions without polling or leaving an automation running blindly. This turns asynchronous waiting into a bounded personal assistant behavior.
args.model_tier: Cheap background watcher and classifier; realtime only when a material event crosses the owner’s threshold.
args.latency_budget: Detect material changes within 1 minute; speak an alert within 2 seconds of classification.
args.cost_estimate: $0.01–$0.05 per monitored day, dominated by polling and occasional classification; use hashes/diffs to avoid model calls.
args.security_concerns: Watchers must be explicitly scoped to app, account, thread, and expiry. Keep message bodies local, send only minimal event summaries, and provide a physical cancel gesture and automatic expiration.

transcript.text:
Recorded three new capabilities:

1. **Cross-surface shadow previews** — preview exact file, calendar, browser, or message changes without mutating anything. Requires mutation-free Mac/browser execution and a redacted diff format.

2. **Secret-preserving form completion** — use local Keychain/browser secrets through opaque handles, while keeping values out of model, relay, logs, and pendant audio. Requires scoped secret-provider adapters and proof that secrets were not exported.

3. **Bounded asynchronous watch** — monitor a specific Mail, Messages, or browser condition, suppress routine changes, and alert the owner only when a material event occurs. Requires durable scoped watches, incremental private diffs, expiry, and an owner-editable materiality policy.

args.user_asks: “I’m walking into my next meeting—prepare me.”
args.why_useful: The worn interface turns calendar context into a ready-to-use workspace: it finds the next event, gathers the linked notes/files and relevant browser pages on the Mac, creates a private meeting scratchpad, and reads a 20-second spoken brief back to the owner. It is genuinely cross-surface: the pendant supplies urgency and confirmation, relay coordinates, Mac and browser hold the authenticated data, and perception confirms the workspace actually opened.
args.model_tier: background for calendar/document retrieval and summarization; realtime only for the brief and follow-up conversation
args.latency_budget: Under 10 seconds to announce the meeting and start preparation; under 30 seconds for the complete packet. Never block the owner on a slow browser tab.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per preparation, dominated by summarization and browser/page extraction; calendar and local Mac operations are negligible.
args.security_concerns: Meeting titles, notes, and browser content remain on the authenticated Mac/browser surfaces where possible; the relay receives only the minimum structured event and brief. External sending or editing source documents must be staged and require the existing physical transaction approval latch. If links or permissions fail, report partial preparation rather than claiming success.
missing: A meeting-prep orchestrator that resolves the next event and its links
A private scratchpad creation action with an idempotency key
A compact spoken-brief response path from relay to the pendant
A verifier recipe for calendar selection, opened resources, and scratchpad file state

args.user_asks: “Privacy shield.” (a deliberate pendant gesture)
args.why_useful: One physical gesture immediately moves the owner's Mac into a known private state while they are away from the keyboard: pause browser polling, hide or lock sensitive windows, mute notification previews, and mark the session as privacy-armed. A second deliberate gesture restores the prior state. This is useful in a café, office, or when handing the laptop to someone, and unlike a software hotkey it remains available when the screen is obstructed or the owner is carrying the machine.
args.model_tier: No large model for the hot path; deterministic policy and local Mac actions. Use the realtime model only to explain status if the owner asks by voice.
args.latency_budget: Visible privacy state within 2 seconds of the confirmed gesture; restoration within 3 seconds. If any surface cannot be secured, the pendant must say which one remains exposed.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero API cost; primarily local action execution and one small relay event per arm/disarm.
args.security_concerns: The pendant receives only an opaque state/nonce, never window titles, page contents, or secrets. The Mac agent must use an allowlisted privacy profile, record exactly what changed, and verify each postcondition independently. Do not close tabs or discard unsaved work; lock/hide/mute only, with a bounded undo record. Arming should be allowed proactively only if the owner chooses that policy; default to confirmation for disarm.
missing: A first-class privacy profile with reversible, allowlisted actions across macOS and the browser bridge
A pendant gesture/event route that works while LTE is absent but the pendant is USB-attached
A fail-closed aggregate status beacon when one surface cannot be secured
An independent verifier mapping for hidden/locked windows, browser pause, and notification state

args.user_asks: “I’m leaving now—save my place.”
args.why_useful: A deliberate pendant gesture creates a durable, private continuity card for the owner's current work: active project, unsaved-document warnings, relevant files, browser session URLs/titles, and the last action state. It then lets the owner resume from the pendant or Mac later instead of reconstructing context. The Mac/browser do the observation and persistence; the relay stores the signed handoff; the pendant gives an immediate receipt even when disconnected.
args.model_tier: Deterministic capture first; a cheap background model may summarize the card. Realtime is only for a spoken confirmation or resume query.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the gesture in under 1 second, capture local state in under 5 seconds, and sync opportunistically. Never wait for cloud connectivity before writing the local handoff.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for capture; about $0.005–$0.02 when a model summarizes a large work context. Storage is small JSON plus hashes, not document copies.
args.security_concerns: Do not upload document bodies or page secrets by default; retain titles/paths/URLs only when their sensitivity policy allows. Redact password-manager and private browsing surfaces. The card must be encrypted at rest, expire by policy, and show provenance for every item. Resume must reopen or edit only after explicit owner intent, with verification that the target file/page still matches its recorded hash.
missing: A cross-surface continuity-card schema and encrypted relay store
A Mac/browser snapshot operation that returns a structured, sensitivity-labelled state rather than screenshots
A pendant offline acknowledgement and later delivery tied to the existing typed OUTBOX
A resume planner that treats stale hashes as warnings instead of silently acting

args.user_asks: “Before you send anything outside my Mac, show me exactly what will leave and stop if it contains a secret.”
args.why_useful: The owner gets a trustworthy outbound-data firewall rather than hoping an action planner noticed a credential, private URL, or personal identifier. It intercepts browser submissions, email/message sends, uploads, and clipboard-to-web actions; computes a field-level redaction/diff preview; speaks a short summary through the pendant; and requires the existing physical approval latch only for the risky fields. Safe local actions continue without friction.
args.model_tier: Deterministic local classifiers and policy engine on the Mac for the hot path; a cheaper background model may explain ambiguous fields. No realtime model is needed unless the owner asks for a spoken explanation.
args.latency_budget: Intercept and classify in under 300 ms for ordinary forms; preview in under 2 seconds. Fail closed on classifier uncertainty for external transmission, but never destroy the draft.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.01 per intercepted action when local classifiers resolve it; occasional model explanation costs roughly $0.01–$0.03.
args.security_concerns: Raw secrets must remain on the Mac/browser; the relay and pendant receive hashes, sensitivity labels, and a human-readable summary only. The firewall itself must be unbypassable by a planner, log an immutable decision receipt, and distinguish a user-approved exception from an automatic pass. It must never claim a message was sent until the independent verifier checks the postcondition.
missing: A Mac/browser interception hook for all external writes, not just planner-generated actions
A field-level outbound payload inspector with secret/PII policy labels
A safe redaction preview protocol that can be rendered as short pendant audio
A verifier postcondition for the exact approved payload digest

args.user_asks: “Only interrupt me for something I must answer today; hold everything else.”
args.why_useful: The owner gets a true cross-device interruption filter: Mac and browser notifications are classified against calendar, deadlines, sender identity, and the owner's current focus; urgent items are summarized privately on the pendant, while everything else is held in a digest with a promised delivery time. A button can promote the currently held item without opening the laptop. This is more useful than blanket Do Not Disturb because it preserves the few interruptions that actually matter.
args.model_tier: Cheap background classification with deterministic deadline/sender rules; realtime only for an urgent spoken summary or the owner’s reclassification command.
args.latency_budget: Classify new notifications within 1 second; urgent pendant alert within 3 seconds. Digest generation can be deferred to the next quiet boundary.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.001–$0.01 per notification batch, dominated by classification; local rules handle most events without API calls.
args.security_concerns: Notification bodies stay on the Mac/browser whenever possible; the relay gets only urgency, source, deadline, and a short encrypted summary. Private banking, health, and authentication notifications must never be spoken or relayed without explicit policy. Every suppression needs an expiry and an accessible audit trail so nothing silently disappears.
missing: A unified notification/event feed across macOS and authenticated browser sessions
Owner-editable urgency and sensitivity policies with per-sender and per-calendar exceptions
A durable held-item queue with expiry, deduplication, and pendant promotion gestures
Independent verification that an urgent item was delivered and a suppressed item remains retrievable

args.user_asks: “Give my accountant access to these three documents until Friday, and take it back automatically.”
args.why_useful: The owner can make a bounded external commitment without manually hunting through sharing dialogs: the Mac identifies exactly the named files, the browser handles the authenticated sharing service, the relay tracks expiry, and the pendant confirms the final recipient/scope/duration. At expiry it revokes access and independently verifies revocation, turning risky ad-hoc sharing into a reversible delegation.
args.model_tier: Background model for resolving “these documents” and recipient identity; deterministic policy for scope, expiry, and revocation. Realtime only for the concise approval prompt.
args.latency_budget: Prepare a scope preview within 10 seconds; execute after physical confirmation within 5 seconds; revoke at the deadline with retry and a truthful unknown state if the provider is unavailable.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per delegation, mostly document/recipient resolution; scheduled revocation and verification are low-cost.
args.security_concerns: Never send document contents to the relay. The approval envelope contains only recipient identity, file IDs/hashes, permission level, and expiry. Default to least privilege and no resharing. If revocation cannot be verified, alert the owner and keep retrying; never report success from an API acknowledgement alone. Provider-specific permanent links and inherited folder permissions require explicit refusal or a stronger confirmation.
missing: Provider-neutral share/revoke adapters for browser-authenticated services
A scope resolver that proves file identity before any share action
A scheduled revocation worker with retry and independent postcondition verification
An approval summary that is short enough for the pendant but includes recipient, files, permission, and expiry

args.user_asks: When I say “make this safe to share,” have the pendant identify the exact file or browser draft, the Mac/browser create a redacted copy, and return a side-by-side confirmation that no recipient, hidden metadata, or private fields remain before I send it.
args.why_useful: Prevents the most dangerous everyday mistake: sending the right-looking document with private content or metadata still embedded. It requires the worn device for intent, the Mac for filesystem/metadata access, the browser for authenticated compose context, and perception for independent verification.
args.model_tier: background for metadata/content inspection; realtime only to disambiguate the owner's spoken target
args.latency_budget: Initial inventory 2–5 s; redaction preview under 10 s; never send automatically without the existing physical approval latch.
args.cost_estimate: Usually $0.01–$0.08 per invocation; dominated by document extraction/inspection, with browser and Mac actions otherwise local.
args.security_concerns: Private document content must stay on the Mac/browser where possible; send only hashes, field labels, and minimal snippets to the model. Require physical approval for any outbound send. Preserve original read-only and make a new copy.

Browser action support for attaching the generated copy and exposing recipient/draft fields to verification
A policy rule defining which metadata classes count as private

args.user_asks: Let me say “I’m driving” or press the pendant’s focus gesture: pause non-urgent relay notifications, set the Mac to a safe focus mode, and restore everything automatically when I say “I’m parked,” with a visible countdown and an emergency override.
args.why_useful: A wearable is uniquely positioned to change interruption policy at the moment the owner needs it, while the Mac and relay control different notification sources. Automatic restoration prevents the common failure where focus mode stays on for hours and important messages are missed.
args.model_tier: background/rules engine; realtime only for spoken state changes
args.latency_budget: Engage in under 1 s from button or voice intent; restore in under 2 s after explicit parked signal. No model call is needed for known phrases.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero API cost after setup; a small classification call only for ambiguous spoken variants.
args.security_concerns: Do not infer driving from location or microphone continuously. Store only focus-state timestamps. Emergency contacts and emergency-call notifications must bypass suppression. Restoration must be idempotent and verified against Mac state.
missing: Pendant focus gesture firmware/state event (sw1 is the candidate)
Relay notification policy with durable TTL and emergency bypass
Mac DND/Focus read-write plus postcondition verification
Owner-configurable safe phrases and emergency allowlist

args.user_asks: After any multi-step request, tell me one honest sentence: “done,” “partly done,” or “unknown,” naming the exact step that still needs me; if the Mac or browser disconnects, resume from the last verified step instead of repeating or guessing.
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful reliability behavior: the owner can trust that a request involving files, apps, and authenticated tabs either completed or clearly stopped. It makes the pendant a dependable hand, not a source of duplicate sends or silent failures.
args.model_tier: background state machine; realtime only to summarize the final status aloud

args.user_asks: “Take care of this dispute until it is actually resolved.” Let the system manage a long-running case across email, web portals, documents, and calendar: gather the case facts privately, prepare each proposed communication, obtain a deliberate pendant approval before sending, watch for replies, schedule follow-ups, and stop only when an independently verified resolution or an explicit owner decision exists.
args.why_useful: Today the owner can ask for one browser click or one draft, but must personally remember every later reply, deadline, and escalation. This would turn a vague real-world outcome—refund, support case, insurance claim, cancellation—into a supervised process that survives days and interruptions without silently sending anything.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for case extraction, deadline tracking, and draft preparation; use realtime only for the owner's approval conversation and exceptions. Use deterministic policy for send/stop rules.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge intake in 2 s; produce the first case plan within 30 s; monitor replies on a scheduled cadence; require no continuous session. Approval prompts should reach the pendant within 2 s of a proposed outbound action.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.05–$0.50 per case over its lifetime, dominated by document/reply extraction and occasional vision checks; polling and storage are minor.
args.security_concerns: Browser credentials and message contents remain on their native Mac/browser surfaces; the pendant gets only a redacted summary and approval digest. Every outbound message or form submission requires a fresh, scoped physical approval. Expired cases, changed facts, unknown sender identity, and irreversible commitments stop rather than retry. Keep an append-only case audit with deletion controls.
missing: A durable case state machine with deadlines, reply correlation, and escalation rules
A native watcher for new email/browser responses that can wake a sleeping relay without scraping secrets into model context
Scoped approval envelopes that bind the exact outbound text, recipients, attachments, and expiry
Independent verification of receipt/acceptance and a clear owner-facing 'resolved versus waiting versus unknown' state

args.user_asks: “Show me exactly what will happen before you do it.” For any high-impact Mac or browser action, produce a reversible preview of the external effect—recipient, fields, files, money, permissions, and resulting page diff—then let me approve that exact digest on the pendant; if reality differs, abort instead of adapting silently.
args.why_useful: The owner currently has to trust a plan or inspect a screen unaided. A preflight simulation makes approval meaningful: the physical gesture authorizes one concrete effect, not an evolving agent interpretation.
args.model_tier: Cheap deterministic extraction for fields and diffs, with a stronger model only when the action's consequences are ambiguous; realtime speaks the short summary.
args.latency_budget: Preview in under 5 s for ordinary forms/files and under 15 s for multi-page workflows; no side effect before approval.
args.cost_estimate: $0.01–$0.10 per preview, mostly browser inspection and document diffing.
args.security_concerns: Never execute a 'preview' by submitting or triggering an irreversible endpoint. Redact secrets from the pendant summary. Bind approval to a canonical digest of exact values, recipients, attachments, and scope; any DOM or file change invalidates it.
missing: A dry-run/sandbox contract for Mac and browser action types
Structured consequence extraction and human-readable diff rendering
Approval envelopes that carry the exact preview digest and invalidation conditions
A fail-closed detector for side effects that cannot be simulated

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

1. **Long-running supervised case management** — handle disputes, refunds, cancellations, or claims across days until independently verified resolved.
2. **Preflight consequence previews** — show the exact recipients, fields, files, money, permissions, and page changes before approval; abort if reality differs.
3. **Temporary bounded delegation** — let the owner grant narrowly scoped, expiring authority such as routine scheduling while prohibiting spending or external communication.

They require durable case state, dry-run contracts, exact approval digests, typed policy enforcement, reply/watch mechanisms, and fail-closed behavior across relay, Mac, browser, perception, and the pendant.

- The Mac agent is fully ready: Accessibility and Screen Recording are now granted, full-control and vision loops are enabled, and the browser bridge is online with 9 Safari tabs.

- **Watchdog events:** normalized heartbeat, deadline, stalled, and “needs decision” signals from Mac/browser executors.
- **Continuation semantics:** pause/resume support, exactly-once delivery, expiry, and a reconnect handshake reporting whether a job is still safely mutable.
- **Pendant integration:** the relay device table still does not show the physically connected pendant as registered. Registration/identity and the serial control protocol are still required for remote physical approvals and queued follow-ups.

No owner action was executed this round; discovery and capability recording only.

transcript.text:
Round 181 discovery is complete.

**Live findings**
- Mac agent is online with full-control planning enabled.
- Safari browser bridge is online with 9 tabs; the active tab is X.
- Computer-use loop is enabled, but vision upload consent is currently false.
- Device inventory still does not show a registered pendant, despite the prototype hardware specifications being available.

**Three proposals recorded**
1. **Context firewall** — spoken choices such as “public only,” “selected tabs,” or “this tab,” enforced across planner, browser, relay, and executor.
2. **Tamper-evident action receipts** — concise spoken records of what changed, where, what evidence verified it, and what remains unknown.
3. **Pause/resume checkpoints** — long-running tasks stop at ambiguity or link loss and resume only after fresh precondition verification, without replaying side effects.

I also recorded an integration change making context grants immutable, scoped, expiring, and one-use.

**What I still need**
- A real resolvable postcondition-verifier route; `verify_operation_step` is granted but currently unresolved.
- Durable operation/step/attempt IDs shared by planner, executor, browser bridge, and receipts.
- Browser sensitivity labels and opaque tab/session identifiers for the context firewall.
- Pendant firmware/relay challenge-response integration for hardware-backed presence approval.
- Confirmation of the actual pendant hardware revision and button count.
- Pendant registration and device keys if these workflows must work untethered over LTE.

args.user_asks: Before carrying out a consequential request, tell me the strongest plausible way your interpretation could be wrong, what would happen if it were wrong, and the one fact that would disambiguate it. Let me answer that fact once from the pendant, then proceed or refuse.
args.why_useful: The owner gets an adversarial safety check rather than a confident guess. This catches wrong recipients, similarly named files, stale browser accounts, and ambiguous purchases before anything leaves the machine.
args.model_tier: A separate inexpensive critique pass for ordinary actions; realtime only presents the concise risk and asks the single clarifying question. High-risk actions may use an independent model with no shared hidden context.
args.latency_budget: 2–5 seconds before execution; never more than one clarification round unless the owner asks for detail.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.02–$0.12 per consequential action, dominated by the independent critique model or visual inspection.
args.security_concerns: The critic must see only the minimum task and target metadata, not secrets. It must not invent certainty or silently widen scope. If critics disagree, fail closed and stage the action. Preserve the critique and answer as an auditable preflight record.
missing: An independent critique route with separate context isolation
A structured ambiguity/risk schema shared by judgement and action
Fresh target disambiguation from Mac/browser state
A compact pendant interaction for answering one fact without exposing private page content

args.user_asks: Rewrite this outgoing message to reveal the least personal information needed to accomplish its purpose, show me the private details you removed as categories rather than quoting them, and let me approve the redacted version from the pendant before sending.
args.why_useful: The owner can ask the system to communicate without accidentally disclosing home addresses, health details, private names, or unrelated conversation context. It is more useful than merely warning that a draft is sensitive: it produces a safer usable draft.
args.model_tier: A cheaper structured redaction model produces the candidate and classified removals; realtime reads a short summary; deterministic diffing ensures the sent bytes equal the approved draft.
args.latency_budget: 3–8 seconds to produce a candidate; under 2 seconds to approve and send.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.02–$0.10 per draft, depending on classification and whether browser form state must be inspected.
args.security_concerns: Raw private content must remain on the Mac/browser whenever possible. The pendant receives categories and a redacted preview, never the removed secrets. No automatic send after rewriting; require explicit approval for external communication. Keep the original and candidate in separate encrypted stores with short retention.
missing: A local redaction/classification service with stable entity categories
Byte-exact draft diff and approval binding so the sent text cannot change after approval
Browser and Mail/Message adapters that expose draft state without leaking content to the relay
A policy defining categories that are never allowed to leave the Mac

args.user_asks: When you tell me a personal fact or recommendation, let me ask “why do you believe that?” and hear a short provenance chain: which Mac file, calendar event, browser page, or conversation supplied it, when it was observed, what may be stale, and what you inferred rather than directly saw.
args.why_useful: The owner can detect stale or misattributed personal information before it drives an action. This makes the hive trustworthy without reading private documents aloud and distinguishes observed facts from model guesses.
args.model_tier: Deterministic provenance graph and freshness calculation; a low-cost model compresses the chain into speech. Realtime is only needed for the conversational explanation.
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for an existing fact; under 10 seconds if fresh Mac/browser inspection is required.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for indexed provenance; $0.01–$0.05 for summarization or a fresh inspection.
args.security_concerns: Speak source types and minimal titles by default, not document contents. Require a deliberate request before revealing sensitive source names. Hash source snapshots, enforce retention, and mark inferred links as uncertain rather than presenting them as evidence.
missing: A provenance graph that records source locator, observation time, transformation, and confidence for every claim
Instrumented Mac/browser reads that emit provenance events rather than only final text
Freshness and contradiction rules across calendar, files, browser, and conversation state
A privacy-preserving spoken provenance formatter

transcript.text:
Recorded three new owner-facing capabilities:

1. **Adversarial preflight**  
   Before consequential actions, the system identifies the strongest plausible interpretation error, its consequence, and one clarifying fact. It proceeds only after that fact is answered.

2. **Privacy-preserving message rewriting**  
   The system rewrites outgoing messages to disclose the minimum necessary, reports removed information by category, binds approval to the exact resulting bytes, and only then sends.

3. **Spoken provenance for personal facts**  
   The owner can ask “why do you believe that?” and hear the source type, observation time, freshness, inference chain, and uncertainty without having private documents read aloud.

What must change:

- Add an independent critique route with isolated context.
- Add structured ambiguity and risk records to planning and execution.
- Add local redaction/classification and byte-exact approval binding.
- Instrument Mac and browser reads to emit source, timestamp, transformation, and confidence metadata.
- Add freshness, contradiction, and provenance graph rules.
- Add privacy-preserving pendant summaries for risks, redactions, and sources.
- Keep all three fail-closed when evidence is stale, critics disagree, or the approved content changes.

transcript.text:
Recorded four proposals:

1. **Cross-surface transactional workflows** — execute Mac/browser steps as one operation, compensate reversible steps after failure, stop at irreversible boundaries, and require fresh perception verification rather than trusting executor receipts.
2. **Set-down privacy curtain** — use the owned IMU to mute private speech and invalidate pending actions when the pendant is placed down; pickup requires an explicit sw1 resume gesture.
3. **Context-rich physical bookmarks** — capture a redacted active-app/browser/session snapshot with each bookmark tap. This is close to an existing context-card idea, so it should be treated as an amendment rather than expanded into a separate feature.
4. **Firmware haptic and gesture service** — enable the already-owned LSM6DSOX and DRV2605L, classify set-down/pickup locally, and provide haptic pending/success/failure/unknown states with signed monotonic events.

I also notified `faculty-perception` about operation/step/attempt correlation for compensation verification and `relay-realtime` about the privacy-curtain hooks.

What I still need:

- **Firmware integration and bench validation:** enable `i2c2`, add IMU/haptic drivers, and test over the currently connected USB devices. Building, flashing, and provisioning remain approval-gated.
- **Relay/Mac pause semantics:** a defined contract for muting speech, pausing jobs, and invalidating pending approvals when the pendant is set down.
- **Transaction compensation schema:** per-step idempotency keys, pre/postconditions, rollback actions, and explicit `verified`, `unknown`, and `committed` states.
- **Owner policy:** timeout and sensitivity rules for the privacy curtain and which action classes may be compensated automatically. I will not invent those defaults.

Recorded three additional capabilities:

1. **Outbound data firewall**  
   The owner should be able to send files, messages, and forms only after the Mac/browser locally identifies the exact destination, account, payload, attachments, and detected secrets, then presents a hash-bound redaction approval on the pendant.  
   **Required changes:** local outbound interception, on-device secret/PII detection and redaction, payload-hash-bound approval, and post-submit verification. Unredacted content must never reach the relay.

2. **Account and workspace identity guard**  
   Before any browser mutation, the system should verify not just the URL but the active account, organization, workspace, permission level, and environment. It should block personal/work, test/production, or similarly named-account mistakes.  
   **Required changes:** per-domain identity expectations, browser-side account fingerprinting, a pre-mutation identity gate, and a narrowly scoped physical override bound to the inspected tab.

3. **Commitment follow-through**  
   The owner should be able to make a promise conversationally and later receive a grounded follow-up draft when the relevant meeting, deadline, or email context arrives—never sent automatically.  
   **Required changes:** durable commitment records with provenance, calendar/mail watchers, local evidence retrieval, deduplicated draft generation, and a pendant inbox supporting approve, dismiss, and snooze.

args.latency_budget: Policy check under 100 ms locally; boundary warnings within 1 second; no cloud model call for ordinary steps

args.security_concerns: The relay must fail closed when it cannot classify a field. Secrets must never be placed in job receipts, prompts, pendant audio, or screenshots.
