args.user_asks: Do the task, and don't tell me it succeeded unless you independently checked the result; if it failed safely, fix it or tell me exactly what remains.
args.why_useful: This would make the system's central promise trustworthy across the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser: judgement plans, faculty-action executes, faculty-perception verifies fresh postconditions, and only then does the pendant announce success. Safe reversible failures can be retried automatically; irreversible or ambiguous outcomes stop with a truthful unknown state instead of a false success.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to clarify the owner's request and narrate the result; use the cheaper background/local planner for decomposition, execution, retries, and evidence comparison.
args.latency_budget: 2-5 seconds for a simple Mac action, 10-30 seconds for a browser or multi-step task; verification must happen before the success beacon, even if that adds one round trip.
args.cost_estimate: Low-to-moderate: one planning call plus local execution and a small verification call; the dominant cost is model reasoning for recovery, not the read-only verifier or receipts.
args.security_concerns: Postcondition evidence must be sensitivity-labeled and default to hashes/minimal snippets. Never send page secrets or form contents to the pendant. A failed verification must not trigger an unbounded retry loop; irreversible actions require the existing physical transaction approval latch and an unknown result must be surfaced rather than guessed.
missing: A first-class orchestration contract linking operation_id, step_id, executor receipt, verifier provenance, retry budget, and final outcome across POST /plan and POST /execute.
A recovery policy that classifies a failed postcondition as retryable, needs approval, or unknown without inventing owner policy.

args.user_asks: Save this thread so I can continue it later on my Mac, exactly where we left off.
args.why_useful: A spoken conversation should become a resumable work item rather than disappearing into audio history. A deliberate pendant bookmark captures the current turn; the relay creates a compact encrypted continuation capsule containing the transcript cursor, unresolved decision, active operation, and relevant Mac/browser session handles. Later, the Mac or browser can reopen the right context without replaying private audio or making the owner repeat themselves.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to identify the bookmark boundary and state the one-sentence continuation summary; use a cheaper background model/local code to assemble, index, expire, and retrieve capsules.
args.latency_budget: Bookmark acknowledgement under 500 ms on the pendant; capsule persistence within 2 seconds; resume in 3-8 seconds once the Mac/browser is reachable.
args.cost_estimate: Low: one short summary generation per bookmark and otherwise storage/lookup; transcript and private page contents should not be re-sent when a stable handle or digest is sufficient.
args.security_concerns: Capsules must be encrypted, scoped to the owner, expire by default, and contain opaque references rather than passwords, cookies, full browser pages, or raw microphone audio. Resuming an action must re-check current state and use the existing physical approval latch for consequential steps. The owner needs a way to list and delete capsules.
missing: A continuation-capsule schema with transcript cursor, operation/job references, browser session handle, expiry, sensitivity labels, and a redacted human summary.
A pendant bookmark-to-relay event that binds the bookmark to the active conversation/session without storing a second audio copy.
A resume endpoint that rehydrates only the minimum context and invokes fresh perception before action.

args.user_asks: Don't interrupt me while I'm busy; hold anything non-urgent and tell me at the first safe moment.
args.why_useful: The wearable can know that an alert was delivered, while the Mac can observe foreground work and the browser can report an active session. Together they can defer non-urgent spoken interruptions instead of talking over a meeting or typing session, then deliver a compact queue at a natural pause with a haptic cue. Urgent items bypass the queue, and every deferral is visible rather than silently lost.
args.model_tier: Use local rules for urgency, quiet hours, active foreground app, and queueing; use a cheaper background model to compress deferred items. Reserve realtime for the owner's explicit request or an urgent alert.
args.latency_budget: Observe and classify within 1 second of an attempted delivery; urgent alerts under 2 seconds; deferred digest under 5 seconds after a safe delivery opportunity.
args.cost_estimate: Low: mostly route reads, queue operations, and one small summarization call for a batch. No continuous model streaming is needed.
args.security_concerns: Foreground app names and browser session metadata are sensitive; retain only coarse categories and short-lived timestamps. Never infer availability from an absent heartbeat. An urgent classification must be explainable and configurable by the owner, with conservative defaults. Do not use the pendant microphone to monitor conversations.
missing: A durable interruptibility policy with owner-set urgency classes, quiet windows, expiry, and a safe-default unknown state.
A delivery arbiter that combines /observe, /browser/status, scheduled jobs, audio playback acknowledgements, and current conversation state without treating stale presence as current availability.
A pendant queue presentation that distinguishes urgent, deferred, expired, and failed delivery using the existing outcome beacon.

transcript.summary: This round produced three non-duplicate capabilities. The highest-value one is an end-to-end truthful executor: faculty-action runs the plan, faculty-perception independently verifies fresh postconditions, and the pendant announces success only after evidence; safe failures can recover, ambiguous ones remain unknown. I also proposed resumable conversation-to-work capsules (bookmark on the pendant, encrypted relay handoff, fresh Mac/browser context on resume) and an attention-safe delivery arbiter that defers non-urgent interruptions until the Mac/browser indicate a safe moment. What I still need is implementation of the missing orchestration contracts: operation/step IDs joined to executor receipts and verifier provenance, a redacted continuation-capsule schema and resume endpoint, and an owner-editable interruptibility/urgency policy. I also still need a real source for Mac lock/wake state; until then availability must remain unknown, not inferred.
transcript.biggest_unknown: Whether the owner wants the first policy defaults for retries, capsule expiry, urgency, and safe delivery chosen conservatively by the system or explicitly configured before these capabilities are built.

args.user_asks: Freeze everything you are doing right now, everywhere, and make sure nothing queued can continue until I explicitly unlock it.
args.why_useful: Today there is no single physical emergency stop spanning relay jobs, Mac execution, browser commands, and deferred work. A pendant gesture should revoke the system's authority immediately, cancel cancellable work, prevent queued work from starting, and leave irreversible in-flight work marked unknown for later verification. This gives the owner a trustworthy escape hatch when a device is lost, a task looks wrong, or they simply change their mind.
args.model_tier: Use device firmware and relay code for the immediate signed revocation; use local deterministic enforcement on Mac/browser. A background model may summarize what was stopped, but must not decide whether the kill switch applies.
args.latency_budget: Pendant acknowledgement under 300 ms locally; relay propagation under 2 seconds when connected; every surface must fail closed while the revocation epoch is newer than its authority token.
args.cost_estimate: Low API cost; the work is protocol and enforcement. Storage is a small monotonic epoch plus bounded receipts. Hardware uses existing buttons/LED or haptic path, with no new parts required.
args.security_concerns: The stop gesture must be unambiguous and available offline. Revocation records need monotonic counters, signatures, replay protection, and crash-safe persistence. It must not claim that an already-submitted external action was undone; it reports cancelled, stopped, or unknown. Unlock must require a deliberate physical gesture and never happen merely because connectivity returns.
missing: A global authority-epoch protocol accepted by relay, Mac executor, and browser extension.
A cancellation interface that maps each running job/action to safe cancellation or unknown, rather than pretending all work is reversible.
A firmware gesture and local fail-closed state machine that survives link loss and reboot.

args.user_asks: Show me exactly what information you sent to each device or website while doing that, and let me revoke anything that should not remain.
args.why_useful: The owner currently gets action receipts, but not a comprehensible, cross-surface account of data movement. A provenance ledger would answer which transcript fragments, files, form fields, and derived summaries crossed the relay, Mac, browser, or third-party boundary, with hashes and destinations rather than copying secrets into a new report. It would make privacy inspectable after the fact and support targeted deletion or credential/session revocation where possible.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic instrumentation and hashing for collection and joins; use a cheaper model only to render a plain-language explanation. Realtime is unnecessary unless the owner asks during an active task.
args.latency_budget: No more than 100 ms added per action for event capture; an on-demand report in 2-5 seconds; revocation requests may take longer but must show pending versus completed.
args.cost_estimate: Low-to-moderate storage and hashing cost, with small summarization calls only when requested. The dominant engineering cost is adding data-boundary events to every executor and browser adapter.
args.security_concerns: The ledger must not become a second secret store: default to field names, classifications, sizes, destination identities, and salted hashes; retain raw values only under explicit owner policy. Reports need access control and expiry. Deletion must distinguish local erase, remote deletion requested, and impossible-to-recall exposure.
missing: A canonical data-flow event schema linking operation/step, source classification, destination, transformation, retention, and deletion status across relay, Mac, and browser.
Instrumentation hooks in POST /execute and browser commands that emit those events even on failure.
A user-facing revocation/deletion workflow that can invalidate browser sessions, remove local artifacts, and report limits honestly.

result.builtFrom: 7 of 8 pieces you named are already known to this system. The rest are not in what anyone here has observed yet: /approve. That is not proof they do not exist — no agent has inventoried every surface — so check before treating them as the gap.

args.user_asks: Handle this for the next hour, but do not spend money, contact anyone, or use files outside this folder; stop and show me what you found when the limit is reached.
args.why_useful: The owner needs useful autonomy without granting an all-purpose agent. A bounded delegation contract would travel with the task across relay, Mac, and browser: allowed destinations, files, action classes, time, number of attempts, and external side effects are enforced mechanically. The system can research, draft, and prepare work unattended, then stop at a declared boundary instead of silently escalating its authority.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic policy enforcement and local planners for limits; use a cheaper background model for research and drafting. Realtime only handles clarification or a boundary decision that the owner explicitly asks to resolve.
args.latency_budget: Contract validation under 100 ms before each action; ordinary work proceeds at current latency; a boundary stop and pendant notification within 2 seconds of reaching a limit.
args.cost_estimate: Low per invocation once policy enforcement exists; storage is a compact signed contract and counters. Model spend becomes predictable because token, time, step, and retry budgets are hard ceilings.
args.security_concerns: The contract must default-deny unspecified capabilities, bind to a specific operation and expiry, and be checked locally even if the relay is unreachable. Browser cookies and Mac credentials remain inaccessible unless explicitly named as an allowed capability. Exceeded budgets produce a stopped/unknown result, never an automatic extension.
missing: A signed, portable delegation-contract schema with allow/deny rules for paths, domains, action classes, time, spend, token and step budgets.
Enforcement hooks in Mac shell/AppleScript, browser actions, relay jobs, and queued retries, with counters that survive crashes.
A compact owner-facing preview and post-run report showing each consumed budget and the exact boundary that stopped the task.

args.why_useful: The owner can preserve the meaning of a fleeting moment without stopping to explain which app, page, or document was on screen; the worn button supplies time-local intent while the Mac supplies context the pendant cannot see.
args.model_tier: background for note assembly; realtime only to acknowledge capture
args.latency_budget: haptic acknowledgement under 300 ms; context snapshot under 3 s; filing may finish asynchronously
args.cost_estimate: Low: one small realtime event plus a cheap background summarization call; storage and Mac/browser reads dominate, not model tokens.
args.security_concerns: Context may include private page text or secrets. Default to app name, URL, document title, selection hash, and a short user-approved snippet; never upload passwords or page bodies by default. Filing a note is reversible and may be proactive; external sharing is never implied.
missing: A typed cross-surface moment record schema linking pendant event ID, Mac observation, browser session, and resulting note
A Mac/browser context snapshot route that returns provenance without requiring Screen Recording

args.user_asks: If I say “do it” after asking you to change something, execute the staged action only if the exact app, account, target, and final state still match what I approved; otherwise keep it pending and tell me what changed.
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful action capability: it turns conversational intent into dependable real-world completion without silently acting on a stale tab, wrong account, or changed form. It combines the pendant's deliberate confirmation with independent postcondition truth.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the short approval exchange; deterministic routes and a cheap verifier for execution and commit
args.latency_budget: Approval feedback under 500 ms; preflight under 2 s; execution may take minutes but must expose progress and final truth
args.cost_estimate: Low-to-moderate: mostly deterministic Mac/browser calls; one verifier/model call only when the UI is ambiguous. Cost is dominated by long-running browser workflows.
args.security_concerns: The pendant receives only an opaque transaction summary, digest, expiry, and outcome—not secrets or page contents. args.user_asks: While I am walking or moving, keep risky computer actions staged; let me approve harmless actions, but require me to be still and deliberate before sending messages, buying, deleting, or changing security settings.
args.why_useful: The pendant is worn in motion and a pocket press, stumble, or accidental contact should not approve a consequential action. Using motion as a safety signal makes the physical approval boundary fit daily life rather than assuming a desk posture.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for sensor/event classification; deterministic policy for gating and action routing
args.latency_budget: Motion classification under 200 ms; haptic explanation immediately; safe actions continue without perceptible delay, risky actions wait for stillness
args.cost_estimate: Low: IMU sampling and local thresholds are cheap; no model call is needed for ordinary still/moving classification. Firmware integration and calibration dominate.
args.security_concerns: Motion is a safety signal, not consent. Never use stillness alone as approval; combine it with the existing nonce-bound deliberate gesture. Keep raw IMU local, transmit only coarse state and confidence, fail closed on sensor/link faults, and allow an emergency cancel gesture.

transcript.text:
Round 229 produced three actionable directions:

1. **Verified target-bound execution** — “Do it” proceeds only if the app, browser session, account, recipient/resource, and final-state digest still match the approved plan. Any mismatch pauses for re-approval.
2. **Motion-aware physical safety gate** — Integrate the owned LSM6DSOX so movement can delay risky actions. Motion is only a safety signal; it can never substitute for deliberate physical approval.
3. **Moment capture with context** — A physical bookmark should bind the pendant’s audio/event timestamp to the Mac foreground app, browser session, URL, and a privacy-filtered context snapshot, then file one searchable note.

I also sent the remaining requirements to judgement and perception:

- Canonical risk classes and approved-plan digest fields.
- Rules for actions when motion is unknown or the owner is moving.
- Stable, fresh locators for app, account, recipient/resource, and final-state verification.
- Explicit `unknown` results whenever perception is stale or ambiguous.

What I still need from the system:

- A commit coordinator joining the physical approval latch, action attempt ID, target digest, execution receipt, and `verify_operation_step`.
- Stable browser account/session identity metadata.
- Firmware integration of the owned LSM6DSOX (`i2c2` currently disabled), with local calibration and fail-closed motion states.
- A privacy-bounded Mac/browser context snapshot schema for moment capture.

I will not request the already-denied Accessibility permissions again.

args.user_asks: Let me say “prepare this for later” and have the system carry the task across the relay, Mac, and browser until the exact prerequisites are true, then ask me once—without losing the page, draft, files, or reasoning if any device sleeps or disconnects.
args.why_useful: Today a task that spans a logged-in browser, local files, and a later human decision is fragile: a dropped link or sleeping Mac forces the owner to reconstruct it. This would make the system a durable personal handoff rather than a one-shot command runner.
args.model_tier: Background model for decomposition and resumption; realtime only for the final concise prompt and physical confirmation
args.latency_budget: Capture and acknowledgement under 1 s; resumption within 10 s of prerequisites becoming true; no requirement that all devices be online simultaneously
args.cost_estimate: Moderate: durable state and periodic cheap checks dominate; use the expensive model only when a prerequisite or plan meaningfully changes.
args.security_concerns: Persist only encrypted references and redacted summaries, never browser secrets or page contents in the relay. Bind every resume to the original plan, expiry, account, and target digest. Require fresh verification and approval before external or destructive effects.
missing: A durable cross-surface task object with checkpoints, prerequisite predicates, expiry, and resumable artifacts
Atomic handoff/import/export between relay, Mac planner, and browser session
A scheduler/event watcher that wakes only on relevant prerequisite changes
A human-readable recovery view showing exactly what is ready, blocked, or stale

args.user_asks: Give me a private “show me only what I need” mode: when a task involves sensitive browser or Mac content, let the browser keep the real values local while the pendant and relay receive only structured facts, redacted previews, and a one-line action summary.
args.why_useful: The owner can use the hive for banking, health, work, and private communications without putting page contents or secrets into the relay or spoken audio. This is a usable privacy boundary, not merely a promise not to log data.
args.model_tier: Local deterministic extraction first; a small background model may classify/redact; realtime model receives only the sanitized projection
args.latency_budget: Redaction and projection under 300 ms for ordinary fields; complex pages under 2 s; never delay an emergency cancel
args.cost_estimate: Low-to-moderate: local extraction is cheap; occasional background classification for unknown fields. Storage and encryption dominate.
args.security_concerns: Default-deny transmission for unknown fields; typed sensitivity labels for normal/private/secret; secrets remain in the browser process. Redaction must be fail-closed, with hashes or opaque handles instead of guessed masking. Owner can inspect and revoke each projection.
missing: A browser-side typed redaction engine that understands form fields, account identity, message bodies, and payment/security secrets
A capability-based projection token so relay actions can refer to a local value without receiving it
End-to-end audit records proving what left the browser and which model saw it
A pendant vocabulary for saying “withhold details” versus “read details aloud”

args.user_asks: When the system cannot finish a multi-device task, hand me a precise recovery card: what step completed, what remains uncertain, what I can safely retry, and what must not be repeated—available by voice on the pendant and as a full view on the Mac.
args.why_useful: A truthful partial failure is more useful than “something went wrong.” The owner can recover from a dropped connection, browser navigation, or Mac sleep without duplicate purchases, messages, or edits.
args.model_tier: Deterministic receipt/state synthesis; cheap background model only to compress the explanation into one spoken sentence
args.latency_budget: Recovery status under 2 s after a failure; pendant summary under one spoken sentence; detailed Mac view can load asynchronously
args.cost_estimate: Low: mostly existing receipts and verifier results; model cost is limited to wording ambiguous recovery summaries.
args.security_concerns: Do not speak sensitive values aloud. Use opaque step IDs and redacted target labels. The retry recommendation must be derived from idempotency and verified state, never guessed. Require confirmation for any retry with external side effects.
missing: A structured partial-completion state machine with per-step idempotency and retry safety
A receipt synthesizer that distinguishes completed, failed, unknown, cancelled, and never-started
A cross-surface recovery-card protocol and compact haptic/voice encoding
A user-facing history that retains the card until acknowledged or superseded

transcript.text:
Recorded three new capabilities:

1. **Durable cross-device task handoff**  
   The owner should be able to say “prepare this for later,” with the task surviving relay, Mac, and browser disconnects while preserving checkpoints and local artifacts.  
   **Needed:** a durable task object with prerequisites, expiry, resumable checkpoints, atomic handoff between surfaces, and an event-driven resumption service.

2. **Private projection mode**  
   Sensitive browser and Mac values should remain local while the relay and pendant receive only typed facts, redacted previews, hashes, and safe action summaries.  
   **Needed:** browser-side fail-closed redaction, capability tokens referring to local values without exposing them, end-to-end disclosure auditing, and explicit voice/haptic controls for whether details may be revealed.

3. **Precise multi-device recovery cards**  
   After a partial failure, the owner should hear and see exactly what completed, what is unknown, what is safe to retry, and what must not be repeated.  
   **Needed:** per-step idempotency and retry state, structured receipt synthesis, compact pendant encoding, and persistent recovery history.

These require new coordination and privacy primitives—not merely more model capability—and cannot be obtained reliably from today’s independent job receipts and device-local state.

args.user_asks: Stop the thing you just started—immediately, everywhere.
args.why_useful: A long-running Mac or browser action can become unsafe or simply wrong after it starts. Today the owner has no pendant/voice-level kill path that propagates to every executor and produces a truthful stopped-versus-unknown result. A single abort command would be the most useful action safety capability: it beats waiting for a browser timeout or trying to regain GUI control.
args.model_tier: Realtime only to interpret the explicit stop utterance; cancellation propagation and receipt updates should be deterministic code, not an expensive model.
args.latency_budget: Abort signal fan-out under 300 ms; each executor must acknowledge cancellation or report unknown within 2 s.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost after intent recognition; one small relay event and bounded receipt writes dominate.
args.security_concerns: Stop is fail-safe and must never approve a pending action or start a compensating action. Bind cancellation to the active operation ID, not the most recent job text; if identity is ambiguous, cancel nothing and ask. Mac/browser workers must checkpoint and refuse new steps after the cancel token. If an external side effect already committed, report committed/unknown rather than claiming rollback.
missing: A relay-wide cancellation token endpoint keyed by operation ID
Mac and browser executors that poll/subscribe to cancellation between steps and return a terminal stopped/committed/unknown receipt
Pendant rendering of an active-operation abort acknowledgement (the existing outcome beacon can render the result)

args.user_asks: Take the value from the logged-in website and paste it into the desktop app, but do not show me the secret or send it through the model.
args.why_useful: The browser may hold an authenticated token, recovery code, address, or other sensitive field that the Mac app cannot reach. Today the owner must manually copy it, exposing it to screens, clipboard history, or the model. A sealed browser-to-Mac handoff lets the owner bridge those two otherwise separate surfaces while preserving a no-secret-to-model boundary.
args.model_tier: The model only selects the already-bound source field and destination locator from typed metadata; a deterministic encrypted channel transfers the bytes. Use the realtime tier only if the owner is speaking live; no background model call is needed.
args.latency_budget: 2–5 seconds including a physical approval gesture; never wait indefinitely for a stale browser session.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero inference cost; encrypted payload transfer and two receipts dominate. No plaintext should enter model context or ordinary logs.
args.security_concerns: R2 secret disclosure: require an explicit physical approval using the existing transaction latch, show only site/app names and field labels—not values—and bind source tab, destination app/window, operation digest, expiry, and one-use nonce. The browser extension must redact values from snapshots; relay stores ciphertext only; Mac types directly without clipboard persistence, then independently verifies destination field presence without returning its contents. Refuse cross-origin or unbound destination changes.
missing: A typed secret-handoff command in the browser bridge and Mac agent
An ephemeral encrypted payload channel with memory-only handling and zeroization
A verifier postcondition that can prove destination acceptance without exposing the value

args.user_asks: Prepare this form everywhere, and tell me exactly which fields still need my eyes.
args.why_useful: Many real tasks span a browser session and a desktop app: gather known values, fill only low-risk fields, stop at ambiguity, and return a compact checklist of unresolved fields. This would turn the system from a single-surface clicker into a safe preparation handoff while keeping final judgment with the owner.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model to map typed field metadata and identify missing/ambiguous values; use realtime only for the owner's spoken request. Execution and field checks are deterministic.
args.latency_budget: Initial inventory under 5 seconds; fill each bound field within 1 second; stop immediately on ambiguity or navigation.
args.cost_estimate: One small planning call per form, then deterministic browser/Mac actions. Cost is dominated by screenshots only when a typed DOM/AppleScript locator is unavailable.
args.security_concerns: Never submit, send, purchase, or disclose a sensitive value as part of preparation. Every write is risk-classified; private fields are not echoed. Revalidate URL, account/session identity, and field labels immediately before each write. Return a digest and unresolved-field list, not raw page contents, and require the existing physical approval latch for any final commit.
missing: A shared typed form model that can represent fields across browser and desktop app
Cross-surface target binding and drift detection between preparation and final approval
A compact pendant-readable unresolved-field summary

args.change: Add a cancellation state machine to the pendant protocol: accept only a signed, operation-bound abort envelope, persist its nonce and monotonic counter in the existing inbox, reject expired/replayed/mismatched envelopes, and render an unmistakable cancel acknowledgement through the accepted tactile_action_outcome_beacon. The firmware must never treat a cancel packet as approval, and it must fail closed if the operation ID is absent.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner says stop, the pendant gives a dependable local acknowledgement even if the Mac/browser link is briefly delayed; a mistaken or stale packet cannot silently approve anything.
args.effort: Medium: protocol schema, bounded inbox record, replay protection, and integration with the existing outcome renderer; no new hardware, but i2c2/DRV2605L is needed if the accepted haptic implementation is not yet wired.
args.risk: A malformed or stale packet could create false confidence. Mitigate with signed envelopes, expiry, operation binding, and a distinct unknown pattern. Recovery is to show unknown and leave the executor in its existing fail-safe state.
args.cost_impact: Negligible runtime cost; tens of KB firmware/storage at most, no component purchase. Haptic driver adds minimal I2C/power use only while rendering.
args.latency_impact: Local acknowledgement under 100 ms after receipt; no effect on audio path.
args.security_impact: Improves safety by adding a non-approving abort path; replay and cross-operation injection must be rejected.
depends_on: A relay cancellation-token route and executor cancellation polling
Existing physical_transaction_approval_latch envelope/monotonic-counter conventions
Existing tactile_action_outcome_beacon firmware integration

Include provenance, timestamps, operation/step digests, and verified versus unknown states; never infer success from a missing error. Exporting externally is R2 and needs physical approval.

A bounded capture/export route with sensitivity labels and retention expiry
Owner-visible report retrieval and deletion controls

args.user_asks: Show me every pending action that could still affect the outside world, in one short queue, and let me cancel selected ones without opening the Mac.

Resume must fail closed if the browser session, target identity, or relevant file state has changed. The pendant receives only redacted step labels and status, never credentials or page contents. Expire abandoned checkpoints and make cancellation auditable.

args.change: Add an owner-visible cross-surface circuit breaker keyed to the Mac's observed foreground app and secure-input state. args.why_useful_to_owner: The system stops doing the wrong thing merely because the owner switched windows, opened a different tab, entered a password field, or let the browser session go stale. args.risk: False pauses when harmless background apps or tab IDs change; recover by showing the exact changed field and letting the owner deliberately resume. A stale observation must be treated as unknown and pause, never as permission. No action is undone automatically.
args.cost_impact: Near-zero API cost; two local GETs per mutating step and a few hundred bytes of journal metadata. No new hardware required.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 50–200 ms per mutating step locally; approval/resume may take human time, intentionally.
args.security_impact: Improves safety by binding execution to the context the owner approved and by treating secure input and stale browser state as a hard stop. The observation payload must be redacted before relay/pendant delivery.

args.user_asks: Before you send, upload, or paste anything outside my devices, show me exactly what data is leaving, who receives it, and what was redacted; let me approve the transfer from the pendant.
args.why_useful: Today an action can be approved as a whole while the owner cannot inspect its actual outbound payload. This gives the owner a practical privacy boundary for browser forms, email/messages, uploads, and relay calls: a compact semantic manifest and content digest expose the transfer without putting the sensitive content into the pendant or model context.
args.model_tier: Local deterministic classifier and hashing for ordinary payloads; a slower background model may produce a human-readable field summary. Realtime is used only to answer the owner's spoken question and read back the compact manifest.
args.latency_budget: Under 500 ms for hash/field inventory and under 2 s for a staged summary. Never delay low-risk local-only actions; external transfer stays staged until the owner approves or it expires.
args.cost_estimate: Usually pennies or less: hashing and schema inspection are local; model cost only applies when a payload needs semantic labeling. No payload bytes need leave the Mac for the normal path.
args.security_concerns: The manifest must not copy secrets, full message bodies, passwords, card numbers, or private page content to the relay or pendant. Use typed categories, byte counts, destination/origin, redaction counts, and a digest. Approval binds to the exact payload digest, destination, action, and expiry; any mutation invalidates it. Unknown classification is a hard stop, not permission.
missing: A data-flow interception seam covering browser commands, POST /execute actions, relay uploads, and message/mail automation.
A typed redaction-and-manifest format with sensitivity enums and stable payload digests.
A policy engine that classifies local-only, private, and external transfers and routes the manifest to the physical approval latch.
A receipt verifier that proves the committed payload matched the approved digest without retaining its contents.

args.change: Add a pendant-originated global revoke epoch, distinct from per-operation cancel. A deliberate two-button gesture (or the forthcoming wheel plus button) increments a monotonic revoke counter locally and signs it; relay, Mac planner, browser bridge, and queued jobs reject every staged or not-yet-committed external action with an older epoch. When the link is down, the pendant stores the revoke event in the existing typed outbox and renders a persistent revoked state; on reconnection the relay fans it out before accepting any queued work. Already-verified irreversible results remain reported honestly as completed, while unknown operations are quarantined for perception rather than silently retried.
args.why_useful_to_owner: One physical gesture gives the owner an emergency stop for the entire system—useful if the pendant is lost, a browser session looks wrong, or they suddenly realize several queued actions should not happen. They do not need to find and cancel jobs one at a time, and a disconnected pendant still records the intent safely.
args.effort: High: signed epoch storage in pendant firmware, relay fan-out and ordering, Mac/browser admission checks, and a durable quarantine state. It needs careful race tests around commit versus revoke.
args.risk: A mistaken gesture can pause useful work; recovery is an explicit new epoch and fresh approval, never automatic replay. A revoke racing with a commit may yield unknown, which must be surfaced rather than falsely labeled cancelled. Protect the gesture from accidental presses and rate-limit repeated epochs.
args.cost_impact: Low API/storage cost: one small monotonic record per revoke and a few bytes on each queued operation; implementation and race testing dominate.
args.latency_impact: No cost on local-only actions. External action admission adds a local epoch lookup; propagation after reconnection is sub-second when relay and bridge are online.
args.security_impact: Creates a system-wide emergency containment boundary that does not depend on Mac Accessibility, browser page content, or a live microphone. It must use anti-replay counters and never expose secrets to the pendant.
depends_on: Existing typed OUTBOX/INBOX durability on the pendant
physical_transaction_approval_latch as the gesture/nonce boundary
Relay durable jobs and browser command queue
An operation journal carrying the current revoke epoch
A single admission check shared by POST /execute and browser command dispatch

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

args.change: Add a soldered secure element (for example, an ATECC608-class device) to the production pendant and use it as the non-exportable signing root for approval, global-revoke epochs, and device pairing. Provision an owner-controlled recovery key on the Mac/relay during enrollment; the relay stores only the public key and key version. Firmware must reject software-only fallback keys, expose attestation/key-version metadata, and support rotation by an explicit physical ceremony.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a pendant whose approvals and emergency revokes remain trustworthy after firmware updates, a stolen Mac session, or a replacement relay. A replacement pendant can be enrolled without silently inheriting an attacker’s identity, while the old pendant can be revoked globally.
args.effort: High hardware and firmware change: add I2C wiring and secure-element provisioning, define recovery ceremony and manufacturing flow, update relay pairing and key rotation, and test reset/rollback/lost-device cases.
args.risk: Provisioning mistakes or lost recovery material can strand the owner; provide a clearly documented offline recovery ceremony and a second recovery copy under the owner's control. Added silicon and I2C failure can make the pendant unavailable, so firmware should fail closed for approvals but retain ordinary local recording. Never print private keys or recovery secrets.
args.cost_impact: Roughly $1–$3 BOM increase plus PCB/enclosure revision; a few mA only during signing, negligible idle draw. Engineering/provisioning cost is substantial.
args.latency_impact: Signing adds tens to hundreds of milliseconds to approval/revoke gestures, acceptable because these are deliberate security actions.
args.security_impact: Strongly improves the physical approval boundary and prevents relay/database compromise from minting pendant approvals. Requires secure provisioning, anti-rollback handling, and public-key pinning across relay, Mac, and browser bridge.
depends_on: A canonical signed envelope shared by pendant, relay, Mac, and browser
The global revoke epoch and physical transaction approval latch
Owner-approved recovery policy and key rotation UX
Production PCB access to the pendant I2C bus

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

transcript.text:
Recorded three additional proposals:

1. **Outbound data manifest and approval** — Before anything leaves the Mac, browser, or relay, the owner sees a redacted summary of what is being sent, where, and a digest of the exact payload. Approval becomes invalid if the payload changes.

2. **Global pendant revoke epoch** — One deliberate pendant gesture invalidates every queued or staged external action across the relay, Mac, and browser, including while temporarily offline. Unknown in-flight operations are quarantined rather than retried.

3. **Secure-element identity for the production pendant** — A hardware-backed signing root protects approvals, revoke events, pairing, recovery, and key rotation. This requires a production PCB revision, provisioning ceremony, and relay/Mac/browser support for attestation and recovery.

These are not available today because the system lacks a unified outbound-data interception layer, system-wide revoke admission checks, and hardware-backed pendant identity.

args.user_asks: “Do the whole browser-and-Mac task, but keep me in control: show me exactly what will change, let me approve it on the pendant, execute it, and tell me whether the final state is verified.”
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful missing behavior: one spoken request can cross the browser’s logged-in session and Mac apps without pretending that an executor receipt proves success. The relay coordinates planning, the Mac/browser hands perform the steps, the pendant is the out-of-band approval boundary, and faculty-perception independently verifies the postconditions. It turns 'I asked you to do it' into a truthful, recoverable transaction rather than a pile of disconnected actions.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the short conversational clarification and final spoken status; use the local planner/vision loop for execution and a cheaper background model for plan normalization and receipt summarization.
args.latency_budget: Preview in 2–4 seconds; physical approval immediately; execution normally under 15 seconds, with an explicit pending state for longer work. Never claim completion until verification returns.
args.cost_estimate: Usually one realtime turn plus local Mac/browser execution; roughly $0.02–$0.10 depending on clarification and vision steps. Verification is primarily local and should not add a model call when structured state is available.
args.security_concerns: The preview must contain canonical target, fields, risk, reversibility, deadline, and affected surfaces but never page secrets or form contents on the pendant. Approval binds to a digest and expiry. Executor receipts are not completion; verification evidence is sensitivity-labeled and defaults to hashes/minimal snippets. High-risk irreversible steps remain staged unless the owner changes policy.
missing: A single cross-surface transaction envelope shared by relay, Mac, browser, pendant, and verifier (transaction ID, plan digest, step IDs, deadlines, reversibility).
An action-runner that can hand one transaction between mac_run_actions and browser_run_actions while preserving step IDs.
An amendment to verify_operation_step carrying actionId/attemptId and the canonical transaction digest.
A pendant rendering for a compact multi-step preview, not only the existing outcome beacon.

args.user_asks: “Privacy shield on.” / “Privacy shield off.”
args.why_useful: A wearable assistant is always near conversations, screens, and logged-in sessions. The owner needs one unmistakable physical way to stop the mind, not merely mute audio: stop new microphone/audio ingestion, cancel or freeze pending browser/Mac work, prevent new screenshots and page-body transfer, and show when the shield is actually active. The pendant can trigger this offline over the existing button path; the relay, Mac agent, and browser extension enforce it at their own boundaries.
args.model_tier: No model for enforcement. Use deterministic relay/device state transitions; use the cheap background tier only to summarize what was suppressed after the owner explicitly asks.
args.latency_budget: Local pendant acknowledgement under 100 ms; relay and Mac/browser enforcement under 1 second when connected. If disconnected, the pendant must remain shielded locally and queue only the state transition, never captured content.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero API cost during enforcement; a small background summary costs cents only when requested.
args.security_concerns: Fail closed: an unacknowledged OFF command never disables the shield. Shield state must be monotonic per device counter, authenticated, and visible as a distinctive haptic/audio pattern. It must revoke pending transaction leases, stop browser polling/results, block screen capture and microphone forwarding, and scrub transient uncommitted context. It cannot claim that already-sent data was recalled; the owner gets a truthful boundary timestamp.
missing: A firmware-local privacy-shield state and button/wheel gesture that works without LTE.
A relay-wide deny gate checked by every audio, capture, browser, and action route.
Mac/browser hooks that refuse new capture and discard already queued commands when the signed shield epoch advances.
A durable, owner-visible audit record of shield-on timestamp, enforcement acknowledgements, and the exact boundary of data that had already left the device.

args.user_asks: “Fill this form with my saved details, but do not send the values to the assistant; show me the field names and final total, then ask for pendant approval before submitting.”
args.why_useful: This makes the browser extension a real private hand rather than a remote screen. Logged-in forms, addresses, payment details, and health fields stay inside the browser/OS vault; the relay and Mac planner see only field labels, validation state, and a redacted digest. The owner can complete tedious forms by voice while retaining both data minimization and a deliberate physical submit boundary.
args.model_tier: Use a small local deterministic field classifier for labels/types and validation. Use realtime only for the owner’s conversational disambiguation; never send field values to a model. Use the background tier to summarize the redacted result if requested.
args.latency_budget: Inspect and produce a redacted preview in 2 seconds; local fill in under 3 seconds; submission waits for pendant approval. If a field cannot be classified confidently, leave it untouched and ask.
args.cost_estimate: Usually no model cost beyond one short realtime clarification; browser-side DOM and vault operations dominate latency.
args.security_concerns: The extension must enforce an allowlist of field types and origins, never expose values through snapshots, logs, receipts, URLs, or error text, and bind approval to origin + form structure digest + redacted field summary + expiry. Payment, identity, health, and irreversible submissions require explicit approval; a changed DOM invalidates the digest. Verification returns only submitted/failed/unknown and safe provenance.
missing: A browser-local vault/autofill adapter that can fill approved fields without returning values to the relay or Mac planner.
A browser snapshot/redaction contract that guarantees secrets cannot enter browser_inspect, browser_result, logs, or model context.
A form transaction digest and post-submit verifier that checks the target submission without recording sensitive values.
Pendant preview vocabulary for redacted fields and a distinct 'ready to submit' confirmation pattern.

Please avoid treating these as already implemented.

args.user_asks: “Pause this until tomorrow, then bring me back exactly where we stopped, explain what changed, and let me continue only after I approve the new plan.”
args.why_useful: Today a multi-step task that hits a login, a changed webpage, a sleeping Mac, or an owner interruption becomes an opaque half-finished job. The owner should be able to suspend it for hours or days and resume safely: preserve the human-readable intent and completed-step evidence, re-observe the live Mac/browser state on resume, show only the differences, invalidate stale approvals, and continue from the first unverified step rather than repeating or guessing.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to normalize the paused intent and summarize state differences; use the realtime tier only when the owner asks a conversational clarification. Deterministic state comparison and approval expiry must not depend on a model.
args.latency_budget: A pause acknowledgement should be immediate. Resume should produce a changed-state summary within 5 seconds and wait indefinitely for approval; execution proceeds in normal step latency.
args.cost_estimate: Low: one background summary on resume and local state probes. The dominant cost is only incurred when the live state materially changed and clarification is needed.
args.security_concerns: Never reuse an old approval after expiry, browser-origin change, form digest change, or Mac account/session change. Preserve only redacted intent and evidence, not secrets or page bodies. A paused action must have an owner-visible deadline and cancellation path; if state cannot be reconciled, report unknown instead of retrying blindly.
missing: A durable paused-work record with completed step IDs, evidence hashes, intent digest, expiry, and the exact resume predicate.
A re-observation/diff protocol spanning Mac app state and browser session state, with a formal 'changed/unchanged/unknown' result.
A resume planner that starts at the first unverified step and requires a fresh physical approval whenever material state changed.
Pendant controls for compact pause/resume/cancel status and a way to select among multiple paused tasks once the rotary input exists.

args.user_asks: “Before I commit to this, check my calendar, open commitments, and the relevant browser page; tell me exactly what conflicts, and draft the least-disruptive option without sending or accepting anything.”
args.why_useful: The assistant today can act on one surface at a time, but cannot reliably protect the owner from commitments that collide across Calendar, Mail, reminders, and logged-in web services. This capability makes the mind a pre-commitment guardian: it gathers current facts from each surface, identifies time/resource conflicts, proposes alternatives, and leaves every external commitment untouched until the owner explicitly chooses one.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic calendar/time overlap and deadline rules first; use a cheaper background model to summarize conflicts and rank alternatives. Realtime is reserved for the owner’s final conversational choice.
args.latency_budget: Initial conflict report in under 5 seconds for local apps and one browser session; longer research is staged with a truthful pending status. No external write occurs during analysis.
args.cost_estimate: Usually one short background summarization call; local AppleScript/browser reads dominate. No cost for deterministic overlap checks.
args.security_concerns: Read only by default. Browser pages and mail may contain private data, so pass field-level redacted facts rather than full bodies to models. Every proposed change must include source, timestamp, timezone, confidence, and whether it is reversible. Never infer an acceptance from a draft or preview.
missing: A unified commitment schema joining Calendar events, reminders, mail deadlines, and browser transaction dates while retaining provenance.
A conflict engine that distinguishes hard overlaps from soft constraints such as travel, preparation, focus blocks, and response deadlines.
A redacted cross-surface evidence view the owner can inspect on the pendant or Mac before choosing an option.
A separate write phase with fresh verification so drafts, replies, and calendar changes cannot occur during the read-only check.

args.user_asks: “Forget everything from that conversation and prove where it was deleted; keep only an anonymous receipt that the deletion happened.”
args.why_useful: A wearable mind accumulates audio, transcripts, browser results, Mac logs, job receipts, and offline SD artifacts in different places. Today the owner cannot issue one deletion request and know whether every copy—including queued or disconnected copies—was removed. This capability gives them a bounded, verifiable right to erase a selected conversation or artifact across pendant, relay, Mac, and browser while retaining only a non-content deletion receipt.
args.model_tier: No model is needed for deletion or proof. Use deterministic object manifests, cryptographic hashes, and deletion acknowledgements; use the cheap background tier only to explain the receipt in plain language after deletion.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge scope immediately; delete online copies within 10 seconds and queue signed deletion tombstones for disconnected devices. Do not claim completion until every reachable store acknowledges and unreachable stores have an explicit pending state.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model/API cost. Storage scans and authenticated deletion acknowledgements dominate.
args.security_concerns: Deletion must be scoped (conversation, artifact, date range, or all), authenticated by the owner, idempotent, and resistant to replay. The receipt must not reveal deleted content or reconstruct it from hashes. Browser caches, Mac logs, relay D1 records, pipeline audio, and pendant failure-path SD objects need separate acknowledgements. If a third-party site retains a submitted value, report that boundary honestly instead of promising erasure.
missing: A cross-surface data lineage manifest mapping each audio/transcript/action/browser artifact to its storage copies and retention class.
Signed, idempotent deletion tombstones that survive relay and pendant link loss and are applied before queued replay.
Deletion hooks for Mac logs/jobs/context graph, relay D1/pipeline objects, browser command/result caches, and pendant SD outbox/inbox.
A verifier that proves absence or states the exact remaining/unreachable boundary without exposing content.

transcript.text:
This round I recorded three proposals:

1. **Deferred, checkpointed cross-surface workflows**  
   A spoken “handle this later” survives a disconnected pendant, resumes when the Mac/browser return, executes one step at a time, and stops unless each postcondition is independently verified. Irreversible steps still require the existing physical approval latch.

2. **Wearable fault-to-bug-report pipeline**  
   “File this bug” would collect bounded, redacted UART/bridge diagnostics, correlate them with audio and job receipts, draft an issue locally, and require review before anything leaves the Mac.

3. **Jewellery-style rotary crown and confirmation input**  
   The encoder would provide selection, repeat, cancel, and navigation without overloading recording gestures. I noted that this overlaps somewhat with prior encoder proposals, so it should be treated as an implementation refinement rather than a wholly separate feature.

What I still need:

- **A registered pendant** for real LTE delivery testing. The live inventory currently shows the Mac bridge online but no pendant; USB remains bench-only.
- **A durable workflow/checkpoint record** linking intent, step IDs, retries, expiry, idempotency keys, and verifier receipts.
- **A structured, read-only UART diagnostic operation** with bounded output, exit status, device identity, and secret redaction.
- **An owner policy** specifying which action-risk classes may resume unattended versus requiring approval.
- **Mechanical decisions** for the rotary crown and second button, plus firmware integration of the already-owned IMU and DRV2605L on `i2c2`.
- **A local issue-draft destination and send policy** for bug reports; I would keep raw diagnostics local and require explicit review before upload.

I also asked faculty-perception, mac-terminal, and relay-realtime for additional non-duplicate gaps; their responses are pending.

args.user_asks: Let me say “use the private browser session to do this, and leave no sensitive trace.” The pendant should carry only an opaque task token, the relay should never receive page contents, the Mac/browser should perform the task in a temporary isolated workspace, and I should receive proof that drafts, downloads, clipboard contents, and temporary files were either retained by my instruction or erased.
args.why_useful: Today the browser can reach logged-in private sessions, but the owner cannot ask for a sensitive task with a strong, inspectable confidentiality boundary spanning pendant, relay, Mac, and browser. This would make high-value actions possible without treating the relay or model context as a second browser.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles only the short command and confirmation. Local Mac/browser execution and deterministic secret-scrubbing do the work; use a background model only to classify whether requested output is sensitive.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; establish the isolated workspace in under 3 seconds; return a cleanup receipt within 2 seconds after completion.
args.cost_estimate: Typically under $0.01 per task; local isolation, hashing, and cleanup dominate rather than inference.
args.security_concerns: The system must fail closed if the browser cannot guarantee session isolation or cleanup. Never send page text, form secrets, cookies, clipboard contents, or downloaded files to the relay. A cleanup receipt must distinguish erased, retained by instruction, and unknown. Sensitive sends and irreversible actions still require explicit approval.
missing: A browser command mode that returns structured success and cleanup attestations without exposing page contents
A Mac sandbox/temp-workspace lifecycle with clipboard and download quarantine
A redaction-and-retention contract shared by relay, browser, Mac, and verifier
An owner-visible policy for which sensitive operations are permitted

args.user_asks: Let me say “for the next hour, calendar changes are okay, messages are never okay, and purchases always need me.” The system should issue a temporary, visible action policy that applies across the relay, Mac, browser, and pendant, expires automatically, and can be revoked with one safe gesture.
args.why_useful: The owner currently cannot express a short-lived exception without relying on an unspecified permanent policy. A bounded policy lease makes proactive automation practical while preventing an old approval from silently widening into a different action class.
args.model_tier: Realtime parses the spoken policy; deterministic policy evaluation executes it. No expensive model should sit in the authorization path.
args.latency_budget: Policy acknowledgement and haptic confirmation within 1 second; every action consults the lease synchronously before execution; expiry and revocation take effect within one action poll.
args.cost_estimate: Well under $0.01 per policy lease; cryptographic signing and local policy checks dominate.
args.security_concerns: A lease must be signed, scoped to exact action classes and destinations, have an absolute expiry, and default to deny on clock uncertainty or link loss. The pendant should display only a compact policy ID and risk pattern, never secrets. Revocation must be safe and idempotent.
missing: A canonical cross-surface policy-lease schema and evaluator
A monotonic/absolute expiry strategy that remains safe across relay, Mac, and pendant clock differences
A way for each executor to prove which policy lease authorized a step
Firmware handling for policy-expired and policy-revoked outcomes

args.user_asks: Let me say “remind me when I start walking.” The pendant should detect only the transition from still to walking locally, send a tiny signed event without audio or location, and have the relay deliver the reminder once—then forget the motion trace.
args.why_useful: This gives the owner a genuinely wearable reminder trigger without GPS, phone presence, or continuous cloud sensing. It uses the pendant's owned IMU while preserving privacy: the relay receives one transition, not a movement history.
args.model_tier: A tiny deterministic firmware classifier handles still→walking; the relay and Mac use existing reminder/routine machinery. No model inference is needed for the trigger.
args.latency_budget: Detect the transition within 1–2 seconds; deliver the reminder within 5 seconds when connected; queue one event safely if disconnected.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible inference cost; firmware work and small authenticated event storage dominate.
args.security_concerns: Do not infer identity, location, gait, or health. Store only a coarse event type, monotonic event ID, and expiry. Require explicit opt-in per reminder, rate-limit false triggers, and provide a pendant cancel gesture. Motion data must never leave the device.
missing: An IMU firmware classifier and calibration flow using the owned LSM6DSOX on enabled i2c2
A signed, deduplicated motion-transition event in the existing typed outbox
A reminder trigger condition supporting device events rather than only wall-clock schedules
A way to inspect, disable, and expire active motion-triggered reminders

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

- **Private browser execution with verifiable cleanup** — sensitive tasks stay inside an isolated Mac/browser workspace; the relay receives only an opaque token and a cleanup attestation.
- **Temporary cross-surface action-policy leases** — spoken rules such as “calendar is okay for one hour, messages are never okay” become signed, expiring, revocable policy data.
- **Motion-transition reminders** — “remind me when I start walking” is detected locally from the owned IMU, sending only a signed one-time event rather than location or motion history.

What must change:

- Browser and Mac execution need a **sandbox/retention contract** covering page data, clipboard, downloads, temporary files, and cleanup evidence.
- Relay, Mac, browser, and pendant need a **shared expiring policy-lease schema**, including clock-safe expiry, revocation, and authorization evidence.
- Firmware needs an **LSM6DSOX still-to-walking classifier** and signed event emission; reminders need to accept device-event triggers rather than only schedules.
- The existing components must be wired together with explicit fail-closed semantics. The proposal recorder noted these are connective gaps between existing routes, not entirely absent primitives.

args.why_useful: A dropped or locked Mac should not turn a safe delegated task into either a silent failure or an unsafe blind retry. The relay can hold the intent, the Mac can wait for unlock, browser can reattach, and faculty-perception can independently revalidate every precondition before faculty-action continues.
args.model_tier: background for queue supervision and revalidation; realtime only for the owner's short resume/cancel exchange
args.latency_budget: Immediate pendant acknowledgement; resume within 5 seconds of a fresh Mac heartbeat, otherwise remain staged
args.cost_estimate: Low: mostly event/state checks and one cheap planner turn only when revalidation differs; dominant cost is browser/Mac evidence capture

args.user_asks: “There are several things waiting for my approval. Let me turn the pendant wheel to choose exactly one, tell me its short summary, and approve or cancel only that one.”
args.why_useful: The current approval latch can safely queue decisions, but a single button/LED cannot let the owner distinguish multiple pending actions. A rotary selector makes the wearable a real control surface: the owner can disambiguate a browser submission from a file move without exposing page secrets or reaching for the Mac.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the terse spoken summary and haptic interaction; background for queue maintenance
args.latency_budget: Wheel-to-summary under 300 ms; approval result delivered within 2 seconds when connected; queue remains usable offline
args.cost_estimate: Low per interaction; realtime tokens dominate, with compact signed queue records under 1 KB each

args.user_asks: “When I say ‘send this to the team’, use the note I just spoke, the file or page I am looking at, and the right logged-in destination to prepare one reviewable draft everywhere—but do not send anything.”
args.why_useful: This turns the pendant into a bridge between fleeting speech and the owner's actual working context. The Mac can identify the foreground document, the browser can supply the authenticated destination, and the relay can preserve one provenance-linked draft; the owner gets a coherent draft instead of manually copying between surfaces, with sending still impossible until separately approved.
args.model_tier: Background planner for extracting and formatting; realtime only to capture the spoken note and confirm the target audience
args.latency_budget: Capture immediately; draft package in under 15 seconds; no mutation beyond draft creation without explicit confirmation
args.cost_estimate: Moderate: one planning turn plus Mac/browser reads; avoid realtime for composition and reuse extracted context across destinations
args.security_concerns: Default to draft-only. Never transmit passwords, hidden fields, or unrelated page text. Require explicit target resolution when multiple team destinations exist; show source provenance and redact sensitive snippets before the draft leaves the Mac. Sending is a separate high-risk transaction with physical approval.
missing: A typed cross-surface context capsule joining pendant audio, foreground Mac document, and browser session without copying whole pages
A draft-only multi-destination action primitive with per-destination previews and independent cancellation
A policy resolver for ambiguous audience names and private/public destinations

result.builtFrom: 7 of 8 pieces you named are already known to this system. The rest are not in what anyone here has observed yet: verify_operation_step. That is not proof they do not exist — no agent has inventoried every surface — so check before treating them as the gap.

transcript.text:
Proposed three new capabilities:

1. **Lock-aware, verified action resumption**  
   Resume staged Mac/browser work after unlock, but only after fresh app, file, account, and browser-state verification. Unknown state remains stopped.

2. **Pendant pending-action selector**  
   A future rotary wheel lets the owner browse multiple pending approvals, hear a short redacted summary, and approve or cancel exactly one item. This extends—not duplicates—the physical approval latch.

3. **Spoken note → multi-surface draft package**  
   “Send this to the team” captures the spoken note plus the current Mac document/browser context, prepares reviewable drafts at the resolved destinations, and never sends without a separate approval.

What I still need:

- A trustworthy Mac lock/unlock or login-session event source; `/observe` does not currently provide one.
- The rotary encoder and additional button in the jewellery enclosure, plus firmware integration and a compact haptic/audio interaction vocabulary.
- Typed cross-surface context records joining pendant audio, foreground Mac state, and browser session without leaking unrelated or secret page data.
- Durable resume/precondition records and a relay API for selecting one pending action atomically.
- A policy for ambiguous recipients and private/public destinations before the draft-package capability can safely operate.

args.change: Add a signed Mac session-state provider to the local agent. It should publish login-session transitions (locked, unlocked, logged-out, asleep, awake), session generation, and observation age through a read-only route and event stream. The provider must use the host's native session APIs, not Accessibility or Screen Recording, and must never expose usernames, window contents, or credentials. On every unlock, emit a new generation so deferred faculty-action work cannot reuse pre-lock browser/file evidence.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask the pendant to finish work after stepping away without risking execution against a changed or unattended Mac. Actions can wait for a real unlock event and then re-check their targets instead of guessing from a stale heartbeat.
args.effort: Medium: native macOS session-state helper, signed event plumbing, route schema, and integration with the existing job/resume and verification records.
args.risk: A missed or spoofed transition could resume the wrong work; recover by treating stale, contradictory, or unknown state as locked and requiring fresh verification plus the existing physical approval. No automatic unlock or credential handling.
args.cost_impact: Negligible runtime/API cost; small always-on helper and event storage.
args.latency_impact: Unlock-to-resume decision under one second when the agent is online; no polling burden.
args.security_impact: Improves safety by making lock state explicit. Events must be authenticated, minimal, retained briefly, and never include account secrets or page content.
depends_on: A durable deferred-action record containing precondition fingerprints and invalidation reasons
A resume coordinator that consumes session-generation changes and calls independent postcondition verification before execution

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

args.user_asks: “If I change the page or file myself while you are working, stop before overwriting me, tell me exactly what conflicted, and let me choose whether to keep mine or yours.”
args.why_useful: Today an agent can have a stale plan while the owner edits the same document or browser tab. Cross-surface conflict detection would make delegation safe in the way a human assistant is safe: owner work wins by default, and the system explains the precise divergence instead of silently applying an old action.
args.model_tier: Cheap deterministic fingerprints and event comparison first; background model only to explain the conflict in plain language
args.latency_budget: Detect before each mutating step, under 500 ms for normal file/browser state; spoken/haptic warning immediately
args.cost_estimate: Low to moderate; hashes and typed state dominate, with model cost only for ambiguous human-readable summaries
args.security_concerns: Compare hashes, field identities, and structural metadata rather than exporting private content. Never merge secrets or submit after a conflict. Require explicit owner choice, with cancel as the default and physical approval for resuming a mutation.
missing: A shared version vector spanning Mac files, browser tabs/fields, and relay action steps
Pre-mutation snapshots and typed conflict records consumable by faculty-perception
A pendant conflict interaction that distinguishes cancel, keep-owner-state, and retry-against-new-state

transcript.text:
Recorded two additional proposals:

- A native Mac session-state provider for trustworthy lock/unlock, sleep/wake, and login-generation events, enabling safe deferred execution.
- Cross-surface conflict detection that stops before overwriting the owner’s concurrent edits and lets them choose whether to cancel or retry.

The owner cannot have these today because the system lacks a trustworthy lock-state source and a shared version/conflict model across Mac files, browser state, relay jobs, and pendant interaction.

args.user_asks: “Continue the operation that was interrupted, but only if the world is still in the state you expected.”
args.why_useful: A dropped link, app restart, or browser reload currently leaves the action facet with an ambiguous half-run. This capability turns that ambiguity into a safe, useful recovery: perception re-checks every unfinished step, action resumes only from a verified boundary, and the owner gets one plain-language explanation instead of a duplicate submission or silent abandonment. It is the single most useful action capability because it makes long tasks trustworthy rather than merely executable.
args.model_tier: background for journal reconciliation and cheap local checks; realtime only when the owner asks what is happening
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for a resume decision when cached postconditions are available; up to 10 seconds for fresh browser/Mac verification
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per recovery; dominated by one small judgement call, not by the Mac/browser checks
args.security_concerns: Never replay a mutation from an executor receipt alone. Each unfinished step needs a fresh faculty-perception verification with locator and provenance; private/secret evidence stays as hashes or minimal snippets. If a step is not provably complete, stop and require the existing physical transaction approval before retrying. The relay must expire recovery leases and deduplicate operation/step IDs.
missing: A recovery coordinator that consumes executor receipts and verifier results and computes a resumable boundary
An additive operation_id/attempt_id correlation field on verify_operation_step and action receipts
A durable, user-readable recovery explanation in the dashboard and a compact outcome event for the pendant

args.user_asks: “Tell me exactly what changed on my Mac and in my open browser since I last left, and let me undo only the changes I choose.”
args.why_useful: The owner can ask the pendant for a trustworthy return-to-work briefing instead of reconstructing tabs, files, drafts, and app state from memory. It is more than presence: it correlates a baseline with current state, separates the agent's mutations from outside changes, and offers targeted undo without rolling back unrelated work.
args.model_tier: background for state hashing/diffing; realtime only to summarize the selected diff in conversation
args.latency_budget: 3 seconds for a normal diff; 10 seconds if browser snapshots or file manifests must be refreshed
args.cost_estimate: <$0.01 for hash-based diffs; LLM cost only for summarization and selected undo planning
args.security_concerns: Baselines must be content-addressed and encrypted; default evidence is names, metadata, and hashes, never file contents or form secrets. Browser fields marked private/secret are represented only by redacted change markers. Undo is per mutation, requires an action receipt and fresh postcondition verification, and must fail closed when an outside edit makes reversal unsafe.
missing: A durable per-owner baseline/checkpoint store with explicit checkpoint creation and expiry
A provenance-aware diff service that joins Mac action ledger entries, browser command results, and fresh observations
A selective undo planner that can present candidate reversals without treating all changes as agent-owned

args.user_asks: “Repeat your last answer.” (turn the pendant wheel one click toward me)
args.why_useful: A missed answer is not a failed download: every byte may have arrived while the owner was distracted. A physical, low-attention replay control lets the owner recover without saying the wake word again or forcing the realtime model to guess which answer they mean. It is especially valuable in noise, while walking, or when the link has just recovered.
args.model_tier: No new model call when the artifact is still cached; otherwise background retrieval, with realtime only for a short spoken confirmation
args.latency_budget: Start playback within 300 ms for a cached response; within 3 seconds after a cellular retry
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for cached replay; one small retrieval/metadata call when the artifact is absent
args.security_concerns: The wheel must address an opaque response ID, never arbitrary history. Replay only audio artifacts delivered to this owner and within a bounded expiry; require a deliberate two-click or press-and-hold for private/secret responses. Persist only response ID, cursor, codec/rate, expiry, checksum, replay count, and interruption status—not transcript or audio by default. Deduplicate replay requests and never treat replay as a new instruction.
missing: A rotary encoder input and debounce/gesture firmware integration (the owner has requested this product direction; current bench buttons are already assigned)
A compact INBOX manifest field identifying the last replayable audio artifact and its expiry
A relay verb that fetches/resumes a specific delivered artifact without invoking the model or re-executing its underlying action

transcript.summary: Recorded three capabilities. The strongest is resumable execution: after a dropped link or restart, faculty-action must resume only at a boundary independently re-verified by faculty-perception, never from executor receipts alone. I also recorded a private “what changed since I left?” diff with selective, provenance-checked undo, and owner-controlled replay of the last delivered audio through the future rotary input. The recorder flagged the latter two as close to existing backlog ideas, so they should be treated as narrow amendments rather than broad new primitives.

Without those, I can specify safe behavior but cannot implement a trustworthy continuation or replay path.
