args.change: Introduce a first-class, machine-enforced data-residency label on every audio, transcript, browser observation, plan, receipt, and journal artifact. Labels such as device_only, mac_only, browser_session_only, relay_allowed, and delete_after_result must be checked before routing, persistence, model invocation, and fallback; an unlabeled artifact defaults to the strictest policy and a violation becomes a refusal, not a warning.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say where private information is allowed to go and trust that an unavailable device will not silently cause cloud or relay disclosure. Privacy becomes an enforceable choice rather than a promise in a model response.
args.effort: High integration effort across relay, pipeline, Mac executor, browser bridge, storage, and model-routing; requires migration of existing journal and audio metadata.
args.risk: Overly strict labels may cause a task to refuse unexpectedly; show the blocked hop and offer an explicit policy change. Old unlabeled records must be treated conservatively and never retroactively exposed.
args.cost_impact: Low runtime cost; moderate engineering and storage-metadata migration cost. Explicit local-only routing may increase local compute usage.
args.latency_impact: Sub-millisecond policy checks when labels are present; refusals can be immediate. Local-only tasks may be slower than relay-backed inference.
args.security_impact: Substantially reduces accidental data exfiltration and makes fallback behavior auditable. Labels are not encryption, so transport and storage encryption remain required.

transcript.text:
Recorded four new items:

- **Two-person approval for high-risk actions** — owner’s pendant confirmation plus a trusted person’s independent approval, using a redacted operation summary.
- **Replayable “why did you do that?” audit** — separate observed facts, model interpretation, approvals, action attempts, and verification evidence.
- **Owner-controlled data residency** — commands such as “device-only,” “Mac-only,” or “relay allowed,” enforced before any data crosses a boundary.
- **Machine-enforced residency labels** across audio, browser observations, plans, receipts, journals, and model calls.

What must change:

- Add a relay-held multi-party approval protocol with trusted-contact identity, quorum, expiry, and operation-hash binding.
- Build a tamper-evident provenance graph spanning perception, planning, approval, execution, verification, and outcome.
- Add sensitivity-aware redaction and owner-readable audit projections.
- Add artifact-level residency metadata and enforce it at every relay, pipeline, browser, storage, and model boundary.
- Treat unlabeled data conservatively and refuse policy-violating fallbacks rather than silently rerouting them.

args.user_asks: “Turn the wheel to replay the last answer, and press to play it again.”
args.why_useful: The owner can recover a missed response without repeating the question or reaching for a phone. The pendant selects the last delivered response from its inbound queue; the relay fetches only the missing range and the Mac/browser context is not exposed to firmware.
args.model_tier: background for indexing and cheap retrieval; realtime only for generating the original answer
args.latency_budget: Wheel selection feedback under 150 ms; playback begins within 1 s when cached, otherwise within 3 s after relay fetch.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost on replay; bandwidth/storage dominate. A response manifest is under 1 KB and audio is reused, not regenerated.
args.security_concerns: Persist opaque response IDs, checksum, codec/rate, expiry, and replay count only; never send page contents or secrets to the pendant. Require a deliberate wheel click, and expire old responses.
missing: rotary encoder and second button in the product hardware
firmware INBOX cursor/replay gesture
relay endpoint to range-fetch an already delivered audio artifact

result.why: This restates something the system already has, so it was not recorded.
result.alreadyHave: “I missed that—play your last answer again.” (Turn the pendant wheel back one click, or use the new second button.) The owner can recover a complete answer without repeating the question or reaching for the phone. This is different from link retry: every byte may have arrived, yet the owner may have been distracted or missed speech. The pendant is the only surface that knows the replay gesture at
result.next: Propose something this does not already cover, or say what it should become that it is not today.

args.user_asks: “Before you send that message or submit that form, give me a short spoken summary and let me approve it from the pendant; if I do nothing, cancel it automatically.”
args.why_useful: This makes high-risk computer actions understandable and safely finishable while walking: judgement composes the intent, Mac/browser performs only after approval, the pendant conveys a concise summary without receiving secrets, and faculty-perception verifies the postcondition. It is the single most useful end-to-end trust feature because it turns automation from silent delegation into a bounded transaction.
args.model_tier: realtime for the brief spoken summary only; background/cheap model for action classification and summarization; no model needed for verification
args.latency_budget: Summary in under 2 s; approval window 30 s; execution and independent verification under 10 s after approval.
args.cost_estimate: One short realtime generation per risky action; verification and execution are otherwise local/route calls. Browser and Mac state reads dominate latency.
args.security_concerns: Use the existing opaque transaction nonce, expiry, monotonic counter, and physical approval latch. The pendant receives only a redacted human summary and digest, never form secrets. Default to cancel on timeout, digest mismatch, stale browser session, or unverifiable postcondition.
missing: wire the existing physical_transaction_approval_latch into browser/Mac execute orchestration
redaction policy that produces safe spoken summaries
a dashboard transaction timeline joining executor receipt and verify_operation_step provenance

args.user_asks: “When I bookmark a moment, later tell me what was on my Mac and in my browser at that exact moment, and let me open the relevant note.”
args.why_useful: A physical bookmark becomes a trustworthy cross-surface memory instead of an unlabeled timestamp. The pendant marks the moment, the relay orders the event, Mac perception captures host/browser state, and the owner gets a compact spoken or dashboard recap later.
args.model_tier: background model for summarization and entity linking; realtime only when the owner asks to hear the recap
args.latency_budget: Bookmark acknowledgement under 200 ms; state snapshot within 2 s; recap available within 10 s.
args.cost_estimate: One small background summarization per bookmark batch; storage and browser snapshot size dominate, with aggressive redaction and hashes by default.
args.security_concerns: Capture only explicitly enabled apps/domains; default to hashes and titles, never page text or passwords. Bind each bookmark to a monotonic pendant event ID and observedAt timestamps, and label missing/stale surfaces rather than inferring them.
missing: firmware bookmark event upload with monotonic timestamp and link correlation
Mac/browser snapshot endpoint that accepts the bookmark ID and returns redacted provenance
owner-configurable capture allowlist and retention

args.user_asks: “I was away for an hour—tell me only what changed on my Mac and in my open browser sessions since I left.”
args.why_useful: The owner gets a concise, actionable re-entry brief instead of a transcript or generic notification list. The relay schedules a baseline snapshot, Mac perception and browser sessions produce redacted change records, and the pendant can speak the digest hands-free when the owner returns.
args.model_tier: background model for diff clustering and summarization; realtime only to speak the final digest
args.latency_budget: Baseline write under 2 s; incremental collection every 5 minutes; spoken digest ready within 5 s of request.
args.cost_estimate: Low background summarization cost per diff window; storage and polling dominate. Keep only hashes/titles and changed fields unless the owner explicitly expands an item.
args.security_concerns: Never infer presence from browser heartbeat. Bind the window to explicit owner start/stop times, report stale/offline surfaces, redact message bodies and page secrets by default, and require confirmation before opening or acting on a changed item.
missing: a persistent cross-surface snapshot/diff store keyed by owner-declared time windows
browser and Mac change events with stable object IDs rather than only current snapshots
a return-brief route that can stream a compact digest to the pendant

args.change: Make audio delivery two-phase: classify and reserve an output route before rendering or releasing PCM. The relay issues a short-lived route lease (private AirPods, pendant, or explicit open-speaker approval); the bridge acknowledges the lease with device identity and privacy level; only then may the artifact become downloadable. A failed or stale lease cancels the release rather than silently falling back.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Sensitive answers will not be rendered into an audio artifact and then accidentally played through the wrong device. The owner gets a real privacy guarantee, not a best-effort label after the fact.
args.effort: High: add route lease state to pipeline records, bridge capability/identity reporting, pre-TTS gating, expiry and recovery paths, and end-to-end tests for AirPods disconnects and relay retries.
args.risk: A false offline/private report can delay ordinary speech; expire leases quickly and allow ordinary low-sensitivity responses to use the pendant. Never fall back for sensitive content. Roll back by disabling leases only for explicitly low-sensitivity responses.
args.cost_impact: Small metadata and control traffic; possible extra latency and occasional wasted classification, but avoid duplicate TTS by classifying before rendering.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms for route negotiation; sensitive responses may wait for private-device confirmation.
args.security_impact: Improves confidentiality by preventing unbound audio release. Device identity and route receipts must be authenticated; do not store raw audio solely for route retries.

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

1. **Cross-surface consequential-action commit**
   - The owner gets a success claim only when executor receipts, independent browser/Mac verification, and pendant approval all agree.
   - Requires an operation/attempt commit coordinator, idempotency fencing, evidence policy, and durable disagreement records.

2. **Time-limited delegated autonomy**
   - The owner grants a narrowly scoped, expiring lease for low-risk work and can revoke it from the pendant.
   - Requires signed delegation leases, pre-execution policy checks, revocation fan-out, and an audit of completed, skipped, and unknown tasks.

3. **Verified “what changed while I was away?” feed**
   - The owner receives only fresh, provenance-backed changes across Mac, browser, relay, and pendant, with stale or unknown sources clearly marked.
   - Requires observation cursors, cross-surface deduplication, freshness semantics, and a compact private pendant summary.

transcript.text:
Recorded four action capabilities this round:

1. **Emergency stop across the hive** — one spoken command or deliberate pendant gesture cancels queued and in-flight Mac, browser, and iPhone work, with truthful handling of race conditions and already-submitted actions.
2. **Secret-free credential injection** — browser-side Keychain/secret-broker fills an explicitly allowed password or payment field without exposing the value to the model, relay, logs, screenshots, pendant, or receipts.
3. **Cross-surface resource leases** — concurrent actions acquire fenced read/write leases for files, browser records, and phone settings so independent tasks can run in parallel without overwriting one another.
4. **Pendant exception prompts** — when execution encounters ambiguity, the pendant asks one bounded question, captures a constrained choice, and resumes the paused operation rather than guessing or abandoning it.

What I still need:

- A durable **paused-step question protocol** connecting relay, pendant, Mac, browser, and iOS execution.
- A **structured pendant input path** for choices; the planned rotary encoder plus second button would be ideal.
- Executor **checkpoint/resume semantics** so answering a question cannot replay completed side effects.
- A cross-surface **stop-generation/lease service** for emergency cancellation and conflict fencing.
- A local, origin-scoped **secret broker** integrated with Keychain and browser field identity.
- Fresh perception checks immediately before resuming paused or credentialed actions.
- The pendant is still offline; all device-dependent behavior remains unverified until it reconnects.

args.user_asks: Watch me do this once, then make it a safe command I can repeat later.
args.why_useful: The owner can teach a genuinely new cross-surface workflow by demonstration instead of describing every step. The system records abstract targets and variable slots—not screenshots or secrets—then later plans the workflow, asks for confirmation at risky steps, and verifies each result.
args.model_tier: A slower background model converts the demonstration into a typed workflow; realtime is unnecessary except for the owner's initial and later voice commands.
args.latency_budget: Demonstration analysis can take up to 30 seconds; a later invocation should begin within 2 seconds and pause for clarification rather than guessing.
args.cost_estimate: One moderate model call per new demonstration, then low-cost deterministic execution; visual trace storage and workflow review dominate implementation.
args.security_concerns: Never retain raw screen recordings, passwords, message bodies, or unrelated windows. Replace literals with typed slots and origin/app constraints. The owner must review the generated workflow before it becomes reusable; every replay requires fresh target checks and existing approval policy.
missing: A privacy-preserving demonstration recorder across native Mac, browser, and iOS surfaces
A typed workflow compiler that separates stable target identity from variable data
A review/edit surface for the owner to approve generated steps and risk classifications
Replay-time fresh perception and postcondition verification

args.user_asks: Find the conflicting versions of this information across my apps and make them agree, changing only what is necessary.
args.why_useful: The owner gets a single consistency repair across Calendar, Mail, Notes, browser accounts, and iPhone rather than manually hunting stale copies. The system shows a compact conflict table, chooses an explicitly supported source of truth or asks, then applies the smallest set of edits and reports anything it could not safely reconcile.

Recorded three new capabilities:

- **Teach-by-demonstration workflows:** the owner demonstrates a task once; the system extracts a privacy-preserving, editable workflow that can later be replayed safely across Mac, browser, and iPhone.

- A privacy-preserving workflow recorder/compiler and replay-time target checks.
- Structured fact extraction with provenance, conflict policies, and per-field minimal-diff edits.

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

1. **Cross-surface atomic operations with compensation**  
   Coordinate Mac, browser, relay, and pendant actions under one operation ID. Verify every postcondition independently, pause on failure, and expose a resumable or compensating state rather than claiming success from executor receipts.

2. **Context-bound physical moment capture**  
   A pendant bookmark links the physical event and optional voice note to the Mac’s foreground app, browser session, project, and timestamp. It remains durable offline and becomes searchable later. The recorder flagged this as somewhat close to an existing bookmark idea, so I will not restate it.

3. **Motion-aware risk gating**  
   Use the owned LSM6DSOX to detect movement or a “put away” gesture. Pending risky actions pause or defer before mutation; harmless attention items can queue. Raw IMU data need not leave the device.

What I still need:

- **Firmware integration:** enable `i2c2` and integrate the existing LSM6DSOX; the pending motion-safety request is not yet a callable skill.
- **Operation coordination:** a first-class cross-surface operation model with dependencies, compensation metadata, and verified-step receipts.
- **Owner policy:** action classes that may proceed automatically versus those that must remain staged; defaults should remain conservative until the owner specifies them.
- **Context privacy policy:** which browser fields may be attached to physical bookmarks, with redaction and deletion propagation.
- **Device connectivity reality:** the relay still reports `nrf9160-pendant` offline, so end-to-end LTE behavior remains unverified even though the hardware is physically available for bench work over USB.

args.user_asks: “When I’m wearing the pendant, keep my private work available; when it leaves me, protect every screen and pending action automatically.”
args.why_useful: This would create a real wearable privacy boundary across the Mac, browser sessions, relay, and phone rather than trusting a stale login. Leaving the pendant, losing its authenticated presence, or triggering a deliberate privacy gesture would immediately freeze staged actions and put sensitive surfaces into a protected state; returning would restore only after a fresh physical attestation.
args.model_tier: Device/relay cryptography and local policy for presence decisions; no model call for the security path; background model only for explaining what was protected.
args.latency_budget: Presence loss should gate new mutations within 1 second and freeze pending high-risk operations within 2 seconds. Restoration may require an explicit physical gesture and take up to 5 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible inference cost; engineering and security-review cost dominate. A secure element would add roughly $2–$8 per unit and low standby power.
args.security_concerns: Presence must not be treated as consent to execute an action. Use challenge-response, replay protection, expiry, and explicit separation between ‘present’, ‘approved’, and ‘owner authenticated’. Never transmit page contents or credentials to the pendant. Fail closed for staged high-risk operations, but preserve recoverable drafts.
missing: A hardware-backed key store or secure element on the pendant/bridge
A short-range presence transport (BLE/UWB-class) with authenticated challenge-response; LTE alone cannot provide proximity
Mac/browser/iOS privacy-control hooks that can freeze or redact sensitive surfaces
A policy and recovery path for battery loss, link loss, and intentional handoff

args.cost_estimate: One inexpensive planning call plus ordinary relay/browser operations; cryptographic tokens and policy checks dominate neither latency nor API cost.
args.security_concerns: Use least-privilege, single-purpose, expiring capability tokens bound to recipient identity and exact resource/action. No credential or cookie export. Require physical pendant confirmation for creation and revocation, log every attempt, and make sensitive actions impossible even if the recipient asks for them.

transcript.text:
Recorded two capabilities:

- **Wearable cryptographic privacy boundary:** sensitive Mac/browser work remains available only while an authenticated pendant-presence lease is valid; loss of presence freezes pending high-risk actions and protects sensitive surfaces.
- **Least-privilege delegation:** the owner can give another person one narrowly scoped, expiring task without exposing credentials, cookies, or the rest of the computer.

They require changes beyond today’s system:

- Add a hardware-backed key store or secure element.
- Add authenticated short-range proximity transport; LTE cannot prove physical proximity.
- Add Mac, browser, and iOS hooks for freeze/redaction and isolated delegated sessions.
- Build a capability-token service enforcing exact action, resource, recipient, and expiry constraints.
- Add recipient identity, revocation, audit logging, and recovery behavior for battery/link loss.
- Keep pendant confirmation distinct from mere presence: wearing it must never itself authorize an irreversible action.

args.user_asks: “I missed the last answer—let me replay just that answer.” A clockwise turn on the pendant’s future wheel should replay the most recent complete response, even if the cellular link dropped after delivery.
args.why_useful: The pendant is the only surface present at the moment the owner misses speech. This handles ordinary human interruption, not just failed downloads: it uses the already-delivered answer, resumes from a precise cursor, and avoids asking the owner to repeat the entire request.
args.model_tier: Use no model for replay; relay selects the stored artifact and cursor. Use a cheap background model only if the requested answer has expired and a transcript-only compact reconstruction is needed.
args.latency_budget: Start local replay within 150 ms of the wheel gesture; if the artifact is not local, begin relay retrieval within 500 ms and speak a short haptic/audio status cue.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero when cached; roughly one storage lookup and no inference. Reconstruction fallback is a small background-model call, dominated by transcript tokens.
args.security_concerns: Persist only opaque response ID, codec/rate, checksum, cursor, expiry, and replay count on the pendant; never persist page contents or secrets. Require a bounded replay count and delete on expiry.
missing: A rotary encoder and second button in the pendant enclosure
Firmware INBOX manifest fields for response cursor and replay count
A relay verb that returns a bounded audio range by opaque artifact ID

args.why_useful: The owner gets an honest answer about whether speech quality is intact instead of trusting a configuration label. A failed path degrades explicitly to a known-good mode and produces a concise reason, while the expensive probe runs only after changes or on demand.
args.model_tier: No model for measurement or gating. Use a cheap background model only to turn the structured receipt into a human-readable explanation.
args.latency_budget: Capabilities-only check under 1 s; a 10–30 s fixture/loopback run is acceptable after a firmware update and should never block ordinary conversation.
args.cost_estimate: No inference cost for probes; modest Mac/bridge CPU and storage for receipts. Explanation costs only a few hundred tokens when requested.
args.security_concerns: Fixture audio must be synthetic or explicitly owner-selected; never open a microphone for a golden fixture. Persist hashes and metrics, not raw speech. Do not silently switch modes during a live call; announce and require confirmation for a quality-affecting downgrade.

args.why_useful: Today privacy is a collection of endpoint promises. The owner cannot express one durable rule that follows a document from Safari to Mac automation to relay and back. Requires structured action diffs, redaction proofs, and integration with the existing physical approval latch.

transcript.text:
Round 270 produced three new capabilities:

1. **Resumable, per-step cross-surface transactions**  
   Mac/browser actions checkpoint only after independent postcondition verification. Reconnects resume from the last committed step and never repeat an already-submitted message, form, or mutation.

2. **Wearable fall/immobility check-in and escalation**  
   The pendant’s existing LSM6DSOX detects candidate impacts locally, provides an immediate haptic check-in, and—if unanswered—uses relay → Mac/iOS escalation according to an owner-configured policy. Raw motion stays local.

3. **In-hand proof for high-impact approvals**  
   Existing physical approval is strengthened with nonce-bound, coarse IMU handling evidence. Motion alone never approves; it must accompany the deliberate button/encoder gesture. Ambiguous or stale evidence fails closed.

I also discovered an important inventory inconsistency: the live hardware query still reports the old “one button, no attached I²C devices” prototype, while the authoritative purchase/firmware context says two buttons exist and the IMU/haptic hardware is owned but unwired. That needs reconciliation before firmware work is specified precisely.

What I still need:

- **Pendant registration and a usable test connection.** The live device table currently shows `nrf9160-pendant` offline. USB remains a bench-only transport.
- **Firmware integration work:** enable `i2c2`, integrate/calibrate the LSM6DSOX, and integrate the DRV2605L haptic controller.
- **Owner-defined safety policy:** escalation contacts, grace period, cancellation gesture, message/call behavior, and whether location is ever permitted.
- **A durable operation-checkpoint schema and resume route** connecting action attempts to verifier receipts.
- **An amendment to the existing physical approval latch** for nonce-bound handling evidence, rather than a second approval mechanism.
- **Bench testing:** pocket/table/vibration false positives, replay and remote-button attacks, and emergency escalation receipts.

The 24 kHz audio path remains accepted and is not a blocker.

args.why_useful: A single button press is not enough protection for account recovery, financial transfers, or changing a primary email. The pendant supplies deliberate physical intent while the real iPhone supplies an independent biometric factor; the relay coordinates both without exposing secrets to the pendant, and Mac/browser execution plus fresh verification produces an auditable result.
args.model_tier: Deterministic protocol and policy checks; background model only explains the requested action and summarizes receipts.
args.latency_budget: Challenge propagation under 2 s; owner has up to 60 s for both approvals; verification within 5 s after execution.
args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.05 in model/API cost; iOS/browser round trips dominate latency.
args.security_concerns: Use independent nonces and audience binding so an approval for one action cannot authorize another. The pendant receives only a digest and human-safe summary, never credentials or page contents. Face ID status must come from the actual iPhone control path, not a simulated success. Any disagreement yields cancelled/unknown.

An iOS Face ID confirmation surface exposed through the Mac mirroring control path

transcript.text:
Recorded three proposals:

1. **Two-device high-risk authorization**  
   The owner can require both a deliberate pendant gesture and real iPhone Face ID before a sensitive browser action proceeds. The relay binds both approvals to one exact action, and Mac/browser verification proves the resulting mutation.

2. **Cross-service profile-change orchestration**  
   The owner can say “update this everywhere,” receive a staged change set, approve it once, and get a truthful per-service result: changed, failed, or still inconsistent. No global success claim is allowed without independent verification.

3. **Relay-coordinated trust ceremony implementation**  
   Add the protocol, key binding, nonce handling, expiry, iOS biometric result, and executor enforcement needed for the first capability. The pendant remains content-blind; approvals are action-specific and replay-resistant.

The main remaining prerequisites are a real iOS biometric confirmation surface, durable cross-service change-set and verifier schemas, and owner policy identifying which action classes require dual-device authorization.

args.change: Make verified commit the mandatory boundary for every externally visible mutation: POST /execute or browser actions first record an operation/step intent and executor receipt, then faculty-action calls verify_operation_step against fresh Mac/browser state; only a passing postcondition may emit the signed tactile_action_outcome_beacon success. A failed or unavailable verifier commits UNKNOWN (never success), preserves the receipt and evidence provenance, and routes reversible steps to an explicit retry/undo state rather than silently continuing. Carry operation_id, step_id, attempt_id through action ledger, job receipts, and the pendant outcome envelope.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can trust that “sent,” “changed,” or “done” means the outside world was actually checked—not merely that our Mac agent returned. When a browser or app is stale, they get an honest unknown and a safe retry path instead of a dangerous false success.
args.effort: Medium: add correlation fields and a commit state machine in the existing action ledger/policyRouter, invoke the already granted verifier after each mutation, and map states to the existing pendant beacon.
args.risk: Some actions have no observable postcondition and will become UNKNOWN until a generic verifier locator is supplied; retries must be idempotent to avoid duplicate sends. Recover by retaining executor receipts and requiring explicit owner approval for an unverified continuation.
args.cost_impact: One read-only verifier call per mutation step; low storage for IDs, hashes, and compact provenance. More latency (typically one Mac/browser round trip) and modest model context for interpreting verification failures.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–3 seconds per mutating step, but avoids costly and harmful false completion.
args.security_impact: Improves security: verifier receives only typed postconditions and sensitivity-scoped evidence, and the pendant receives outcome metadata—not page secrets or form contents. Unknown is fail-closed.

args.user_asks: “Say that last answer again.” (turn the future pendant wheel one detent toward me, or press its dedicated replay button)
args.why_useful: The owner can recover a missed answer without repeating the question or reaching for the phone. This is an owner-initiated replay of content that already arrived, distinct from link retry: the device knows the request at the instant hearing failed, while the relay owns the canonical response and the bridge owns playback.
surfaces: pendant rotary encoder / future second button detects replay gesture and sends only a response ID plus replay cursor
relay stores a short-lived canonical response manifest and selects the requested audio artifact without regenerating it
ESP32 audio bridge receives the replay artifact and reports playback start/finish or interruption
faculty-action correlates the gesture, artifact checksum, and delivery ACK, and reports unavailable/expired honestly
args.model_tier: No low-latency model for replay selection; deterministic relay lookup. Use realtime only if the owner says “repeat the part about…” and semantic clipping is needed.
args.latency_budget: Under 500 ms to begin replay when the artifact is cached; up to 2 s if the relay must fetch it. Expired or unavailable artifacts should produce a brief spoken/haptic unavailable cue rather than a hallucinated regeneration.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for exact replay; storage is a bounded short-lived audio/object cache plus a sub-1 KB manifest per response. Semantic clipping, when explicitly requested, costs one realtime inference.
args.security_concerns: Replay only by opaque response ID bound to the pendant session and a short expiry; never let a guessed cursor retrieve another session's audio. Do not persist private audio beyond the existing failure-path retention policy. Require no approval because this only replays content already addressed to the owner.
missing: A product input: rotary encoder or dedicated replay button (the owner explicitly wants both a wheel and another button; today's sw0/sw1 are already spoken for).
A relay endpoint that resolves response ID/cursor to the canonical audio artifact and enforces session binding/expiry.
Bridge-side replay start/finish ACK wired into the existing audio_delivery_ack_queue.

args.user_asks: “Prove what you changed in that last action.”
args.why_useful: A completion message is not enough for a consequential action. The owner can ask for a compact, privacy-safe audit that ties the intent, executor receipt, fresh postcondition check, and exact surface touched together—especially useful when they are away from the Mac and cannot inspect the screen.
surfaces: pendant sends an opaque operation reference (or resolves “that last action” to the latest acknowledged operation) and receives a spoken summary plus a short haptic status
relay assembles the operation ledger, executor receipt, verifier provenance, timestamps, and terminal state
Mac agent re-runs only the read-only postcondition check against current app/file/browser state when the original evidence is stale
browser extension supplies a redacted field/URL fingerprint or browser-state proof for owner-private pages, never raw credentials or page bodies
args.model_tier: Deterministic aggregation first; use a cheaper background model only to turn typed evidence into a short owner-readable explanation. Realtime is unnecessary unless the owner asks follow-up questions.
args.latency_budget: Return cached proof in under 1 s; if a fresh check is required, under 5 s. If evidence cannot be obtained, say exactly which link or postcondition is missing rather than filling gaps.
args.cost_estimate: No model call for structured proof; bounded ledger/provenance storage. A short summarization call is typically <$0.01 and only when evidence has multiple steps.
args.security_concerns: Operation IDs are opaque and session-bound. Evidence defaults to hashes, URLs/origin, app names, and field labels; secrets, message bodies, tokens, and page contents are excluded unless the owner explicitly asks for a sensitivity-scoped snippet. Never treat proof generation as permission to mutate state.
missing: A read-only audit aggregation route that joins operation ledger, POST /execute receipts, and verify_operation_step provenance.
A freshness policy distinguishing cached proof from a newly rechecked postcondition.
A pendant command/voice intent resolver for “that last action” that cannot cross session boundaries.

args.user_asks: “Preview this before you do it.”
args.why_useful: The owner can see the exact consequence of a multi-surface action before committing—recipients, files, browser fields, and irreversible side effects—without trusting a vague plan or accidentally performing it. This is the safest way to use the system for high-stakes tasks while away from the Mac.
surfaces: pendant captures the spoken goal and renders pending/preview-ready status through the existing outcome beacon; it never receives secrets or executes
relay creates a non-mutating preview transaction with an expiry and joins the plan to the later approval nonce
Mac agent uses AppleScript, read-only app/file inspection, and browser snapshot/inspect to construct a typed before/after diff; all mutation actions are prohibited in preview mode
browser extension returns only redacted target summaries and normalized field diffs for authenticated pages
faculty-action presents the preview over audio and stores its digest so a later physical approval can be bound to exactly this preview, not to a changed page
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background/planning model for decomposition and explanation; deterministic surface adapters produce the actual diff. Realtime is only needed if the owner asks follow-up questions while previewing.
args.latency_budget: Simple previews under 3 s; multi-app/browser previews under 8 s. If a surface cannot be inspected, label that portion unknown and refuse to claim a complete preview.
args.cost_estimate: One planning call plus bounded read-only probes; roughly $0.01–$0.05 depending on task complexity. No cost for the eventual execution beyond normal action calls.
args.security_concerns: Preview mode has a hard no-write capability token enforced by the Mac agent and browser bridge, not merely a prompt instruction. Secrets are redacted; preview digests expire quickly and are session-bound. Approval is required again if the target fingerprint or proposed effect changes.
missing: A capability-scoped no-write token enforced by every action adapter, including AppleScript and browser actions.
Typed preview diff schema covering app_state, file_state, browser_field, browser_url, and message_draft.
A binding from preview digest to the existing physical_transaction_approval_latch and verified commit protocol.

args.user_asks: “Why did that stop?”
args.why_useful: When a task stalls across LTE, relay, Mac, or a logged-in browser, the owner needs a causal explanation—not “still working.” This capability identifies the first failed handoff, distinguishes blocked, expired, cancelled, verifier-unknown, and offline states, and gives a safe next action without retrying blindly.
surfaces: pendant sends the operation reference or resolves the most recent pending operation; it receives a concise spoken diagnosis and a safe-retry/cancel haptic pattern
relay correlates operation timeline, lease expiry, queue state, and delivery acknowledgements across the cellular conversation and Mac job
Mac agent contributes read-only GET /observe, GET /browser/status, job receipts, and current app/browser reachability without performing a retry
browser bridge reports session/device heartbeat age, pending command age, and whether the target tab/session still matches the operation fingerprint
faculty-action classifies the terminal cause and offers exactly one reversible recovery (resume, re-prepare, or cancel), never silently retries an irreversible step
args.model_tier: Deterministic cause classification over typed events; a cheap background model may phrase the timeline. Realtime is reserved for an interactive follow-up, not diagnosis itself.
args.latency_budget: Cached diagnosis under 1 s; fresh cross-surface checks under 5 s. If evidence conflicts, report “unknown cause” and preserve the timeline rather than guessing.
args.cost_estimate: Usually no model cost; bounded event joins and read-only probes. Optional explanation costs <$0.01. Storage is a compact event timeline per operation with expiry.
args.security_concerns: Expose only owner-authorized operation metadata, redacted URLs/app names, and error classes; never relay browser contents or credentials. A diagnosis cannot authorize mutation. Recovery requires the existing physical approval latch when risk is irreversible.
missing: A normalized cross-surface failure taxonomy and event schema (lease_expired, offline, cancelled, verifier_unknown, target_changed, executor_failed).
A read-only correlation route joining relay jobs, Mac receipts, browser status, and audio delivery ACKs.
A policy that selects one safe recovery and binds it to the original operation/preview digest.

args.user_asks: “If the price drops below $X before Friday, buy one—but only if shipping is free, and tell me exactly what you found.”
args.why_useful: The owner gets bounded, conditional delegation instead of either babysitting a browser or granting an unconstrained agent permission. The system can wait while the owner is asleep, evaluate a private logged-in page when it changes, and act only inside explicit limits, with a verifiable explanation of both the decision and the purchase.
surfaces: pendant captures the condition, ceiling, expiry, and notification rule; a deliberate physical approval establishes the delegation but does not expose credentials
relay persists a signed delegation capsule, wakes the workflow on schedule or browser events, and revokes it automatically at expiry or on owner cancellation
browser extension watches the authenticated shopping session and returns only normalized product, price, shipping, availability, and checkout-state fields
Mac agent performs read-only comparison and prepares the exact checkout manifest; it must stop if target identity, total, shipping, or seller changes

faculty-action submits only when every predicate and risk policy passes, then faculty-perception independently verifies order confirmation, total, and item identity before reporting success; otherwise it reports expired/unknown and never improvises
args.model_tier: Cheaper background model for extracting and evaluating conditions; deterministic predicate evaluation and risk gates for execution. Realtime only for clarifying an ambiguous condition before the delegation is armed.
args.latency_budget: Event reaction within 30 seconds of a browser update; scheduled polling according to the owner's cadence. Checkout verification within 10 seconds. No action after expiry, stale session, or missing evidence.
args.cost_estimate: Background evaluation is a few cents per active delegation depending on polling; browser/Mac reads dominate. One execution and verification pass costs roughly <$0.05 excluding external purchase charges.
args.security_concerns: Delegations are least-privilege, session-bound, signed, expiring, and revocable. Never store or relay payment credentials. Require a second physical confirmation for purchases above the owner's configured threshold or whenever a predicate is underspecified. If a page changes, fail closed rather than silently broaden the authorization.
missing: A first-class signed conditional-delegation capsule with predicates, expiry, budget, allowed domains/actions, and revocation state.
An event/schedule trigger that can wake a dormant workflow and a durable evaluator for typed predicates.
A checkout-specific adapter that emits a redacted manifest and a post-submit proof object; generic browser clicks are insufficient for truthful purchase verification.
Owner-configurable thresholds and action policy data; defaults must remain conservative until the owner chooses them.

args.user_asks: “For the next hour, keep everything on-screen private: you may act, but do not speak page contents or play them aloud.”
args.why_useful: The owner can wear the pendant in public or around other people without choosing between disabling the system and leaking private browser or message content. This is a temporary, owner-visible privacy mode enforced across every output path, not a prompt preference that one agent may forget.
surfaces: pendant accepts a physical gesture and gives a distinct haptic acknowledgement; it stores only the mode, expiry, and policy ID
relay distributes a signed privacy lease with an absolute expiry to realtime conversation, Mac jobs, and audio delivery
Mac agent and browser extension classify and redact spoken/displayed evidence, replacing private values with typed summaries or silence
ESP32 audio bridge enforces an output class tag, refusing payloads marked private while still permitting minimal status tones
faculty-action blocks any action whose required confirmation would reveal protected content, and emits a compact “blocked by privacy lease” result
args.model_tier: Deterministic policy enforcement; no model should decide whether a value is safe after the lease is active. A cheap classifier may label untrusted content before it reaches the policy boundary.
args.latency_budget: Mode activation and propagation under 1 second when connected; queued devices apply it on reconnect before accepting content. Expiry is local-clock enforced so a delayed packet cannot extend the lease.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible runtime model cost; small signed lease and classification metadata. One-time engineering across relay, Mac/browser, and bridge firmware.
args.security_concerns: Fail closed on missing, invalid, or expired leases for sensitive output. The lease must not contain page contents or credentials, and its state must be visible through haptics. Emergency status and owner-requested deactivation remain explicit exceptions; every exception is logged.
missing: A cross-surface signed privacy lease and policy vocabulary for output classes.
Browser/Mac redaction enforcement before model/audio handoff, rather than only after generation.
An ESP32 output gate that understands privacy classes and can suppress queued playback.
A local monotonic expiry implementation on the pendant and bridge, independent of the unsourced pendant wall clock.

args.user_asks: “During this call, listen for the appointment details, quietly summarize them to me, and only send a reply after I approve it with the pendant.”
args.why_useful: The owner can handle a real phone call while keeping hands and eyes free: the system extracts dates and commitments, privately gives a concise haptic/audio summary, drafts a reply, and prevents an accidental text or booking. It combines the pendant, real iPhone, Mac control, and approval boundary in a way no single surface can provide.
surfaces: pendant captures the session start/stop gesture, delivers private summaries through the owner's chosen audio path, and accepts a deliberate approval or cancellation gesture
relay maintains a short-lived call-session state, routes low-latency audio/events, and expires all transcripts and drafts at session end
Mac iPhone Mirroring / ios control observes the live call and Messages/Calendar context, extracts only requested appointment fields, and prepares but does not send a draft

faculty-action binds the draft to the exact conversation/session and waits for the physical approval latch before sending; faculty-perception verifies the sent-message state and calendar result independently
browser/Mac surfaces remain excluded unless the owner explicitly adds them, preventing an incidental logged-in tab from receiving call content
args.model_tier: Realtime model for low-latency speech extraction and concise summaries; cheaper background model for draft polishing and calendar normalization. Deterministic policy controls sending and expiry.
args.latency_budget: Haptic acknowledgment under 300 ms; summary updates within 1–2 seconds of a detected commitment; approved message verification within 5 seconds. If recognition is uncertain, ask rather than infer.
args.cost_estimate: Realtime inference dominates, roughly $0.05–$0.30 per short call depending on audio duration; transcripts and drafts are short-lived and bounded.
args.security_concerns: Explicit session gesture and visible/haptic recording indicator are mandatory. Do not retain call audio by default; keep only owner-approved structured fields. Never send or create a calendar event without a fresh physical approval tied to the displayed/spoken draft. Unknown iPhone state must fail closed.
missing: A privacy-preserving live call audio bridge from the real iPhone/Mac to relay-realtime without opening an uncontrolled microphone.
A typed iOS call/message observation and draft API with session identity and redacted fields.
A pendant session indicator and stop gesture that works offline or during a dropped relay link.
A policy and verifier integration for message send and calendar creation postconditions.

Each proposal names the missing relay, Mac/iOS, browser, pendant, bridge, policy, and verification changes required.
